title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
河南鄉試錄序
嘉靖乙卯歲在賔興乃河南
當天下文明之中際
聖主萬年之運被服儒術之士以
鴻漸之翼戢于草野延頸而
瞻俯肩而奮盱衡而趨彬彬
蒸蒸何其盛也先是巡按監
察御史蔡〔汝 楠〕展采錯事旣脩
===
旣戒會
請告
上特命御史李〔初 元〕來代之〔初 元〕
旣受
命唯謹趲程而進至則屬士風揚
德意靡夙靡夜風采振肅經畫精
punctuated:
河南鄉試錄序

嘉靖乙卯歲在賔興，乃河南當天下文明之中，際聖主萬年之運，被服儒術之士，以鴻漸之翼戢于草野，延頸而瞻，俯肩而奮，盱衡而趨，彬彬蒸蒸，何其盛也！先是，巡按監察御史蔡〔汝 楠〕展采錯事，旣脩旣戒，會請告，上特命御史李〔初 元〕來代之。〔初 元〕旣受命，唯謹趲程而進，至則屬士風，揚德意，靡夙靡夜，風采振肅，經畫精
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Henan Provincial Examination

In the yimao year of Jiajing [1555], the time came to honor and recommend worthy men. Henan occupies the center of the realm’s cultural refinement and enjoys the age of our sage sovereign’s enduring reign. Scholars steeped in Confucian learning, their wings poised for gradual ascent like wild geese yet folded away in the countryside, stretched their necks to look expectantly, bent their shoulders to exert themselves, and raised their brows to hasten forward. Refined and flourishing—how splendid their numbers!

Previously, Cai Runan, the Regional Inspector serving as Investigating Censor, had discharged his duties and arranged affairs, completing preparations and issuing admonitions, when he happened to request leave. His Majesty specially commanded Censor Li Chuyuan to come and replace him. Having received the command, Chuyuan hastened on his journey with utmost care. Upon arriving, he fostered the scholars’ ethos [?] and proclaimed the sovereign’s benevolent intentions, laboring early and late. His bearing inspired awe and discipline, and his planning was meticulous…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
密期於得真賢濟實用以上
慰
聖明側席籌釋之懷是時巡撫右
副都御史今陞户部右侍郎
鄒〔守愚〕夙著勳猷人文丕煥
巡撫右副都御史張〔烜〕保釐
方新聲教允達總理河道工
===
部右侍郎兼右僉都御史曾
〔鈞〕撫治鄖陽右副都御史劉
〔伯躍〕耀威寧宇邇遠無恐巡
鹽御史曹〔光〕李〔禎〕督馬御史
徐〔紳〕苟〔頳〕肅脩風紀振揚文
教咸相與協衷以共
熙典秋八月至期御史遴選百
punctuated:
密，期於得真賢、濟實用，以上慰聖明側席籌釋之懷。是時，巡撫右副都御史、今陞户部右侍郎鄒〔守愚〕，夙著勳猷，人文丕煥；巡撫右副都御史張〔烜〕，保釐方新，聲教允達；總理河道工部右侍郎兼右僉都御史曾〔鈞〕、撫治鄖陽右副都御史劉〔伯躍〕，耀威寧宇，邇遠無恐；巡鹽御史曹〔光〕、李〔禎〕，督馬御史徐〔紳〕、苟〔頳〕，肅脩風紀，振揚文教，咸相與協衷，以共熙典。
秋八月，至期，御史遴選百
translation_en:
…meticulous, aiming to obtain truly worthy men capable of practical service, thereby consoling His Sagely Majesty, who sits expectantly awaiting the worthy and longs for relief from his cares [?]. At this time, Zou Shouyu, Grand Coordinator and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, now promoted to Right Vice Minister of Revenue, had long distinguished himself through meritorious achievements and judicious plans, and cultural accomplishment shone resplendently. Zhang Xuan, Grand Coordinator and Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, had newly undertaken the task of bringing order to the region, and his moral influence and instruction reached throughout it. Zeng Jun, Director-General of River Conservancy, Right Vice Minister of Works, and concurrently Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, together with Liu Boyue, Right Vice Censor-in-Chief charged with pacifying and administering Yunyang, displayed their authority and secured the realm, leaving those near and far without fear. The Salt-inspecting Censors Cao Guang and Li Zhen, and the Horse-inspecting Censors Xu Shen and Gou Cheng, rigorously upheld official discipline and promoted literary learning and moral instruction. All united their purposes to bring this splendid undertaking to fruition.
In autumn, in the eighth month, when the appointed time arrived, the Censor carefully selected the various…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
執事以從而諸校官胥以聘
至乃以學正袁〔階〕教諭何〔子〕
〔顯〕蕭〔謙〕朱〔褒〕程〔汝昌〕劉〔澤〕吳
〔朝周〕吳〔守蒙〕分經而校而屬
〔斉欽〕與教諭胡〔直〕使總其事
曰學以徵業也文以徵志也
眞才是庸罔敢弗虔以左布
===
政使鄭〔綱〕右叅政裴〔紳〕司提
調按察使張〔渙〕副使雷〔賀〕司
監試分職而按而屬右布政
使岑〔萬〕左叅政周〔大禮〕左叅
議曹〔忭〕孟〔養性〕副使焦〔璉〕扈
〔永通〕寇〔陽〕僉事李〔燧〕許〔彥忠〕
楊〔延相〕朱〔舜民〕與署都指揮
punctuated:
執事以從，而諸校官胥以聘至。乃以學正袁〔階〕、教諭何〔子〕〔顯〕、蕭〔謙〕、朱〔褒〕、程〔汝昌〕、劉〔澤〕、吳〔朝周〕、吳〔守蒙〕分經而校，而屬〔斉欽〕與教諭胡〔直〕使總其事，曰：「學以徵業也，文以徵志也。眞才是庸，罔敢弗虔。」
以左布政使鄭〔綱〕、右叅政裴〔紳〕司提調，按察使張〔渙〕、副使雷〔賀〕司監試，分職而按，而屬右布政使岑〔萬〕、左叅政周〔大禮〕、左叅議曹〔忭〕、孟〔養性〕、副使焦〔璉〕、扈〔永通〕、寇〔陽〕、僉事李〔燧〕、許〔彥忠〕、楊〔延相〕、朱〔舜民〕與署都指揮
translation_en:
…functionaries to attend him, while all the school officials arrived by invitation. The subprefectural school instructor Yuan Jie and the county school instructors He Zixian, Xiao Qian, Zhu Bao, Cheng Ruchang, Liu Ze, Wu Chaozhou, and Wu Shoumeng were assigned to evaluate the papers, with responsibility divided by Classic. Qi Qin and the county school instructor Hu Zhi were entrusted with overall direction. The charge was: “Learning provides evidence of scholarly accomplishment; writing provides evidence of aspiration. Employ only genuine talent, and let none dare to be less than conscientious.”
The Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Zheng Gang and the Right Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner Pei Shen were assigned to serve as Proctors, while the Provincial Surveillance Commissioner Zhang Huan and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Lei He were assigned to supervise the examination, each exercising oversight within his allotted duties. Responsibilities were also entrusted to the Right Provincial Administration Commissioner Cen Wan; the Left Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner Zhou Dali; the Left Provincial Administration Assistant Commissioners Cao Bian and Meng Yangxing; the Surveillance Vice Commissioners Jiao Lian, Hu Yongtong, and Kou Yang; the Surveillance Assistant Commissioners Li Sui, Xu Yanzhong, Yang Yanxiang, and Zhu Shunmin; together with the acting Regional Military…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
僉事陳〔惟喬〕程〔宣繼〕呂〔隆〕各
嚴其防範曰簾以內毋出也
簾以外毋入也祗奉
憲章罔敢不慎比鎖院乃又申誓
之合提學副使徐〔霈〕所取士
約二千有奇三試而拔尤異
者得士八十人并刻其文以
獻〔賫〕〔敎〕謹稽首序曰〔賫〕〔敎〕聞之
===
昔者周之盛代也明良康乂
泰和流於宇宙然始未嘗不
以賓賢斂才為先務故其時
歌之曰藹藹王多吉士惟君
子使媚于天子又曰藹藹王
多吉人惟君子使媚于庶人
punctuated:
僉事陳〔惟喬〕、程〔宣繼〕、呂〔隆〕，各嚴其防範，曰：「簾以內毋出也，簾以外毋入也。」祗奉憲章，罔敢不慎。比鎖院，乃又申誓之。合提學副使徐〔霈〕所取士，約二千有奇，三試而拔尤異者，得士八十人，并刻其文以獻。〔賫〕〔敎〕謹稽首序曰：〔賫〕〔敎〕聞之：

昔者周之盛代也，明良康乂，泰和流於宇宙，然始未嘗不以賓賢斂才為先務。故其時歌之曰：「藹藹王多吉士，惟君子使，媚于天子。」又曰：「藹藹王多吉人，惟君子使，媚于庶人。」
translation_en:
…Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Chen Weiqiao, Cheng Xuanji, and Lü Long each strictly enforced their security precautions, declaring: “Those inside the curtain must not go out; those outside the curtain must not enter.” They reverently observed the statutes, none daring to be negligent. When the examination compound was locked, the injunctions were reiterated to them. The candidates selected by Xu Pei, the Education Intendant and Vice Commissioner, numbered somewhat over two thousand in all. Through three examination sessions, the most outstanding were selected, yielding eighty successful candidates; their essays were also printed for presentation. Ji 賫 and Jiao 敎 [names uncertain] respectfully bow their heads and write this preface: We have heard the following:

In the flourishing age of the Zhou, an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers brought peace and good order, and great harmony spread throughout the universe. Yet from the outset they invariably made honoring worthy men as guests and gathering talent their foremost task. Thus the songs of that time said: “In great numbers are the king’s many worthy officers; it is gentlemen whom he employs, dear to the Son of Heaven.” They also said: “In great numbers are the king’s many worthy men; it is gentlemen whom he employs, dear to the common people.”

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
周之稱爲上爲德爲下爲民
樹勳名而耀龍光者宜蔑以
逾於此矣光嶽氣完賢哲並
毓聖作物覩實維其期是以
修思皇之譽崇蒸髦之美故
其歌曰周王壽考遐不作人
龍興而雲虎嘯而風豈其機
===
則然乎我
國家之興也變夷而華撥亂而
治功超萬古比於開闢之一
初視周則過之我
聖祖創垂鴻烈
列祖纘和茂勳至于我
皇上以
punctuated:
周之稱，爲上爲德，爲下爲民，樹勳名而耀龍光者，宜蔑以逾於此矣。光嶽氣完，賢哲並毓，聖作物覩，實維其期。是以修思皇之譽，崇蒸髦之美。故其歌曰：「周王壽考，遐不作人。」龍興而雲，虎嘯而風，豈其機則然乎？
我國家之興也，變夷而華，撥亂而治，功超萬古，比於開闢之一初，視周則過之。我聖祖創垂鴻烈，列祖纘和茂勳，至于我皇上以
translation_en:
…As for the acclaim accorded to Zhou—for those above, for virtue; for those below, for the people [?]—surely nothing could surpass this in establishing meritorious renown and displaying imperial glory. The vital energies of the great mountains and rivers were whole; worthy and wise men were nurtured together. A sage arose, and all beings beheld him: this was indeed the appointed time. Thus they cultivated the reputation of having abundant eminent men and exalted the excellence of their many outstanding talents. Hence their song says: “May the king of Zhou enjoy long life! Does he not nurture men of talent?” When the dragon rises, clouds gather; when the tiger roars, winds arise. Could the impulse behind this work in just such a way?
When our dynasty arose, it transformed barbarism into Chinese civilization and brought order out of chaos. Its achievements surpassed those of all antiquity, comparable to the very first opening of heaven and earth; measured against Zhou, it exceeded it. Our Sagely Founder established and bequeathed magnificent achievements; successive imperial ancestors continued his splendid accomplishments in harmony, down to our present Emperor, who, by…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
大聖人之德體仁履義經文緯武
涵漸而化成之功實並於
天地泰和之氣燁燁乎真與盛周
比隆矣夫山以嶽爲尊嵩宅
中而鎮水以濆爲長河繞地
而抱降神儲精環四履而疆
也於茲土獨先焉爾多士之
===
生也豈其徒哉矧我
皇上右文弘化彝倫式敘
至道汾穆
湛恩洪鬯
德至于
天而慶雲見甘露降
德至于地而靈芝生嘉禾秀乃茲
punctuated: 大聖人之德，體仁履義，經文緯武，涵漸而化成之功，實並於天地。泰和之氣燁燁乎，真與盛周比隆矣！夫山以嶽爲尊，嵩宅中而鎮；水以濆爲長，河繞地而抱。降神儲精，環四履而疆也，於茲土獨先焉。爾多士之生也，豈其徒哉？矧我皇上右文弘化，彝倫式敘，至道汾穆，湛恩洪鬯。德至于天，而慶雲見、甘露降；德至于地，而靈芝生、嘉禾秀。乃茲
translation_en:
…the virtue of a great sage, embodying benevolence and practicing righteousness, weaving together civil and military accomplishments. His work of nurturing transformation truly equals that of Heaven and Earth. The radiance of supreme harmony indeed rivals the flourishing Zhou! Among mountains, the sacred peaks are most exalted: Mount Song occupies the center and stands guard. Among waters, the river [?] is foremost: the Yellow River winds around and embraces the land. In the descent of divine powers and the accumulation of vital essence throughout the territory within the four boundaries, this land holds a singular precedence. Could the birth of you many scholars here be without purpose?

Moreover, our Emperor honors literary culture and extends its transforming influence; the enduring human relationships are duly ordered. The supreme Way is harmonious and majestic [?], and his profound grace spreads abundantly. His virtue reaches Heaven, and auspicious clouds appear and sweet dew descends; his virtue reaches Earth, and numinous fungi spring up and auspicious grain flourishes. Now, at this…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
歲逢兔而長生星見丙而呈
瑞熙
鴻號而受
長曆
萬壽無疆之頌正在
今日又我
國家所未有之盛者此與周之
壽考作人者絜功較德不啻
===
矣昔人有言不養士而求賢
譬如不琢玉而求文采也乃
若多士漸濡于
大聖人之世也雲蒸雷動斯蓋其
時矣其又不爲幸耶〔賓 敎 受〕
其文而竊觀之憲聖稽賢淵
punctuated:
歲逢兔而長生星見，丙而呈瑞，熙鴻號而受長曆，萬壽無疆之頌正在今日，又我國家所未有之盛者。此與周之壽考作人者絜功較德，不啻矣。
昔人有言：「不養士而求賢，譬如不琢玉而求文采也。」乃若多士漸濡于大聖人之世也，雲蒸雷動，斯蓋其時矣，其又不爲幸耶？〔賓 敎 受〕其文而竊觀之，憲聖稽賢，淵
translation_en:
…the year encounters the Hare and the Star of Longevity appears; at bing, auspicious signs manifest [?]. The august title is glorified, and a long span of rule is received. Praise of boundless longevity belongs precisely to this day: this is a flourishing such as our dynasty has never before enjoyed. Measured in achievement and virtue against the Zhou dynasty’s longevity and cultivation of men of talent, it more than equals them.
Someone of old said: “To seek worthy men without nurturing scholars is like seeking beautiful markings in jade without polishing it.” As for the many scholars steeped in the influence of this age of the great Sage, now surely is their time to rise like gathering clouds and stir like thunder. Is this not also their good fortune? 〔“Guest; instruction; receive” [?]〕Receiving their compositions [?], I have ventured to examine them: they take the sages as models and consult the worthies, profound…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
源道貞則性命之奧摛藻紓
英文質並茂則和順之光經
務成化揚推古今則彌綸之
業吉辭勁氣砥節厲心則忠
直之操上之可以黼黻
帝猷下之可以康濟民欲蓋皆贊
世之
===
國華挺時之民望也斯亦周時
楨國常吉之朋矣〔資　固〕〔敎　日〕
月以冀也藉是以少逭於戾
其曰惟爾多士其或異時文
斐而用疎靜言而庸違行汙
而寄治詭正而翼姦褊陋而
志弗昌嗇縮而氣弗振夸詐
punctuated:
源道貞，則性命之奧；摛藻紓英，文質並茂，則和順之光；經務成化，揚推古今，則彌綸之業；吉辭勁氣，砥節厲心，則忠直之操。上之可以黼黻帝猷，下之可以康濟民欲，蓋皆贊世之國華、挺時之民望也。斯亦周時楨國常吉之朋矣。〔資　固〕〔敎　日〕月以冀也，藉是以少逭於戾。
其曰：「惟爾多士，其或異時文斐而用疎，靜言而庸違，行汙而寄治，詭正而翼姦，褊陋而志弗昌，嗇縮而氣弗振，夸詐
translation_en:
…rooted in the Way and steadfast [?], revealing the mysteries of human nature and destiny; displaying literary embellishment and unfolding brilliance, with refinement and substance flourishing together, revealing the radiance of harmony and concord; managing affairs and accomplishing transformation, expounding upon antiquity and the present, achieving work that comprehensively orders the world; employing auspicious words and vigorous expression, tempering integrity and strengthening resolve, demonstrating loyal and upright conduct. Above, they can embellish the Emperor’s grand designs; below, they can bring well-being to the people and satisfy their needs. All are ornaments of the state who assist their age, outstanding men of their time upon whom the people set their hopes. They too belong among those companions of the Zhou era who were pillars of the state and ever auspicious. 〔資　固〕〔敎　日〕 [Annotations and their connection to the following text are unclear.] This is what I hope for month by month [?], trusting thereby to escape some measure of blame.
The admonition runs: “You many scholars: should you in future possess elegant writing but little practical ability, speak fine words in repose but act contrary to them in office, be entrusted with government despite sullied conduct, distort what is right and abet wickedness, be narrow and shallow with aspirations that fail to flourish, be timid and constrained with spirits that fail to rise, be boastful and deceitful…”

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
而事非乘遽條而節非立恐
諛而職非脩技害而心非廓
有一於此其流將何所不至
哉士之蠹也斯所謂實弗中
聲虛名而寡效者
國家亦何賴於此乎〔賁敎〕又緣
是而夙夜以憂也將亦不免
===
是懼亦曰惟爾多士於乎爾
多士敬之哉語不云乎唐虞
之際於斯爲盛士蓋無負於
周矣孰謂爾多士也顧不比
於鳶飛魚躍獨有負於
大聖人之世者耶研慮攄力勉卒
景行〔賁敎〕第觀之是役也右
punctuated:
而事非乘，遽條而節非立，恐諛而職非脩，技害而心非廓，有一於此，其流將何所不至哉？士之蠹也，斯所謂實弗中聲、虛名而寡效者，國家亦何賴於此乎？〔賁敎〕又緣是而夙夜以憂也，將亦不免是懼。亦曰：「惟爾多士！」於乎！爾多士敬之哉！語不云乎：「唐虞之際，於斯爲盛。」士蓋無負於周矣，孰謂爾多士也，顧不比於鳶飛魚躍，獨有負於大聖人之世者耶？研慮攄力，勉卒景行，〔賁敎〕第觀之是役也。

右
translation_en:
…yet their conduct is improper [?]; hasty and disorderly [?], yet without established integrity; fearful and flattering, yet neglectful of their duties; spitefully injurious [?], yet without breadth of mind. If even one of these faults is present, to what extremes might its consequences not lead? Such men are a blight upon the scholars. These are what are called men whose substance does not match their reputation, whose names are vaunted but whose accomplishments are few. What could the state possibly gain from relying on them? I, 〔Benjiao〕, am therefore troubled day and night, and cannot escape this apprehension. Again I say: “You, the many scholars!” Alas! You scholars, be reverent! Do not the Analects say, “Between the age of Tang and Yu and this time, talent was most abundant now”? The scholars surely did not fail the Zhou. Who could say that you scholars, unlike the soaring kite and leaping fish, would alone fail the age of the Great Sage? Think deeply, exert your strength, and strive to carry your noble conduct through to the end. I, 〔Benjiao〕, shall watch for this in the present examination.

The Right …

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
叅議李〔多〕僉事王〔之誥〕以入
賀行右叅政董〔德明〕僉事陳〔夢鶴〕以兵賦出始事鈞勞所不
可泯保定侯梁〔繼璠〕安鄉伯
張〔鐸〕兵科給事中曹〔禾〕戶部
主事沈〔應乾〕劉〔效祖〕中書舍
人謝〔朝錫〕行人司行人祝〔堯〕
===
煥〕金〔應奎〕蕭〔九成〕以奉使至
雅意崇尚又咸喜中土人文
之盛而樂觀厥成云
陝西西安府同州儒學學正
史〔資教〕謹序
punctuated:
叅議李〔多〕、僉事王〔之誥〕以入賀行，右叅政董〔德明〕、僉事陳〔夢鶴〕以兵賦出，始事鈞勞，所不可泯。保定侯梁〔繼璠〕、安鄉伯張〔鐸〕、兵科給事中曹〔禾〕、戶部主事沈〔應乾〕、劉〔效祖〕、中書舍人謝〔朝錫〕、行人司行人祝〔堯〕煥〕、金〔應奎〕、蕭〔九成〕以奉使至，雅意崇尚，又咸喜中土人文之盛，而樂觀厥成云。
陝西西安府同州儒學學正史〔資教〕謹序。
translation_en:
…Assistant Administration Commissioner Li Duo and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Wang Zhigao departed to offer congratulations at court; Right Administration Vice Commissioner Dong Deming and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Chen Menghe went out on military levy business. All shared equally in the work at the outset, and their efforts must not go unrecorded. Liang Jifan, Marquis of Baoding; Zhang Duo, Earl of Anxiang; Cao He, Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for War; Shen Yingqian and Liu Xiaozu, Secretaries in the Ministry of Revenue; Xie Chaoxi, Drafter in the Secretariat; and Zhu Yaohuan [?], Jin Yingkui, and Xiao Jiucheng, Messengers in the Office of Transmission, arrived on official missions. They held literary learning in high esteem, and all rejoiced in the flourishing of cultural accomplishment in the Central Plain and gladly witnessed the successful completion of this examination.
Preface respectfully written by Shi Zijiao, Instructor of the Confucian School of Tongzhou, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi.

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
子曰志於道據於德依於仁游於藝
溥博如天淵泉如淵
禮之實節文斯二者是也樂之實樂斯二
者樂則生矣生則惡可已也惡可已則
不知足之蹈之手之舞之
易
乾元者始而亨者也利貞者性情也乾始
===
能以美利利天下不言所利大矣哉大
哉乾乎剛健中正純粹精也
惠我德大得志也
是以君子將有爲也將有行也問焉而以
言其受命也如嚮无有遠近幽深遂知
來物非天下之至精其孰能與於此
有天道焉有人道焉有地道焉
書
天敘有典勑我五典五惇哉天秩有禮自
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

子曰：「志於道，據於德，依於仁，游於藝。」

溥博如天，淵泉如淵。

禮之實，節文斯二者是也；樂之實，樂斯二者。樂則生矣，生則惡可已也？惡可已，則不知足之蹈之，手之舞之。

易

乾元者，始而亨者也；利貞者，性情也。乾始能以美利利天下，不言所利，大矣哉！大哉乾乎！剛健中正，純粹精也。

惠我德，大得志也。

是以君子將有爲也，將有行也，問焉而以言，其受命也如嚮，无有遠近幽深，遂知來物。非天下之至精，其孰能與於此？

有天道焉，有人道焉，有地道焉。

書

天敘有典，勑我五典五惇哉！天秩有禮，自…
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

The Master said: “Set your resolve on the Way, hold firmly to virtue, rely on humaneness, and find recreation in the arts.”

Vast and all-embracing like Heaven; deep and ever-flowing like an abyss.

The substance of ritual lies in regulating and adorning these two things. The substance of music lies in taking delight in these two things. With delight, they grow; once they grow, how can they be stopped? When they cannot be stopped, one unwittingly begins to dance with one's feet and wave one's hands.

Book of Changes

The primal power of Qian is that which initiates and brings things to fulfillment; its beneficial steadfastness is its inherent nature and disposition. Through its initiating power, Qian benefits all under Heaven with excellent benefits, without declaring what it benefits. How great it is! Great indeed is Qian! Firm and vigorous, central and correct, it is pure, unalloyed, and quintessential.

“They cherish my virtue” means that one's aspirations are greatly fulfilled.

Thus, when the gentleman is about to undertake something or take action, he consults it in words. It receives his request like an echo; whether things are distant or near, obscure or profound, he thereby knows what is to come. Were it not the most refined thing under Heaven, what could participate in this?

Within it are the Way of Heaven, the Way of humanity, and the Way of earth.

Book of Documents

Heaven has established an order with constant norms; it charges us to make our five constant relationships each substantial. Heaven has established ranks with rites; from…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
我五禮有庸哉
惟臣欽若惟民從乂
貌曰恭言曰從視曰明聽曰聰思曰睿恭
作肅從作乂明作哲聰作謀睿作聖
道洽政治澤潤生民四夷左衽罔不咸賴
詩
羔裘晏兮三英粲兮彼其之子邦之彥兮
彼爾維何維常之華彼路斯何君子之車
戎車既駕四牡業業豈敢定居一月三
===
捷
適求厥寧適觀厥成
自今以始歲其有君子有穀詒孫子
春秋
秋齊侯宋公江人黃人會于陽穀〔僖公三年〕
楚人伐鄭〔宣公五年〕春晉趙盾衛孫免侵
陳〔宣公六年〕
宋師伐陳衛人救陳〔宣公十有二年〕夏楚
punctuated:
我五禮有庸哉！惟臣欽若，惟民從乂。貌曰恭，言曰從，視曰明，聽曰聰，思曰睿。恭作肅，從作乂，明作哲，聰作謀，睿作聖。道洽政治，澤潤生民，四夷左衽，罔不咸賴。

詩
羔裘晏兮，三英粲兮。彼其之子，邦之彥兮。彼爾維何？維常之華。彼路斯何？君子之車。戎車既駕，四牡業業。豈敢定居？一月三捷。適求厥寧，適觀厥成。自今以始，歲其有。君子有穀，詒孫子。

translation_en:
…let our five rites have their regular observance! Let ministers reverently comply, and let the people follow good order. In demeanor, there should be respect; in speech, compliance; in sight, clarity; in hearing, acuity; in thought, penetration. Respect produces seriousness; compliance produces order; clarity produces wisdom; acuity produces sound judgment; penetration produces sageliness. The Way prevailed and government was well ordered; beneficence nourished the people. Even the barbarians of the four quarters, who fastened their robes on the left, all benefited from it.

Book of Odes
How smooth the lambskin coat! How brilliant its three ornaments! That man is an outstanding talent of the state. What is that luxuriant bloom? It is the blossom of the cherry tree. What great chariot is that? It is the nobleman's carriage. The war chariot is harnessed, its four stallions imposing. How dare we settle down to rest? Three victories in a single month. Seek their peace; behold their accomplishment. From this time onward, may each year bring abundance. May the nobleman possess blessings and bequeath them to his descendants.

Spring and Autumn Annals
In autumn, the marquis of Qi, the duke of Song, and representatives of Jiang and Huang met at Yanggu. 〔Third year of Duke Xi.〕 Men of Chu attacked Zheng. 〔Fifth year of Duke Xuan.〕 In spring, Zhao Dun of Jin and Sun Mian [?] of Wei invaded Chen. 〔Sixth year of Duke Xuan.〕 The army of Song attacked Chen; men of Wei came to Chen's aid. 〔Twelfth year of Duke Xuan.〕 In summer, Chu…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
子伐宋〔宣公十有三年〕
盟于召陵〔僖公四年〕夏四月己巳晉侯齊
師宋師秦師及楚人戰于城濮〔僖公二十有八年〕
晉欒書帥師救鄭〔成公六年〕
夏五月甲午遂滅偪陽〔襄公十年〕
禮記
郊之祭也迎長日之至也大報天而主日
也兆於南郊就陽位也掃地而祭於其
質也器用陶匏以象天地之性也於郊
故謂之郊牲用騂尚赤也用犢貴誠也
故樂者天地之命中和之紀人情之所不
能免也
昔者聖人建陰陽天地之情立以爲易
志之所至詩亦至焉詩之所至禮亦至焉
禮之所至樂亦至焉
===
第貳場
論
仁智合一於聖
punctuated:
子伐宋〔宣公十有三年〕。
盟于召陵〔僖公四年〕。夏四月己巳，晉侯、齊師、宋師、秦師及楚人戰于城濮〔僖公二十有八年〕。
晉欒書帥師救鄭〔成公六年〕。
夏五月甲午，遂滅偪陽〔襄公十年〕。

禮記
郊之祭也，迎長日之至也，大報天而主日也。兆於南郊，就陽位也。掃地而祭，於其質也。器用陶匏，以象天地之性也。於郊，故謂之郊。牲用騂，尚赤也。用犢，貴誠也。
故樂者，天地之命，中和之紀，人情之所不能免也。
昔者聖人建陰陽天地之情，立以爲易。
志之所至，詩亦至焉；詩之所至，禮亦至焉；禮之所至，樂亦至焉。

第貳場
論
仁智合一於聖。
translation_en:
…the ruler of Chu attacked Song. 〔Thirteenth year of Duke Xuan〕

A covenant was concluded at Shaoling. 〔Fourth year of Duke Xi〕 In summer, in the fourth month, on the jisi day, the Marquis of Jin and the armies of Qi, Song, and Qin fought against the men of Chu at Chengpu. 〔Twenty-eighth year of Duke Xi〕

Luan Shu of Jin led an army to relieve Zheng. 〔Sixth year of Duke Cheng〕

In summer, in the fifth month, on the jiawu day, they thereupon destroyed Biyang. 〔Tenth year of Duke Xiang〕

Record of Rites (Liji)

The suburban sacrifice welcomes the arrival of lengthening days. It offers great thanksgiving to Heaven, giving the sun the principal place. Its site is marked out in the southern suburb to occupy the position of yang. The ground is swept and the sacrifice performed there, expressing simplicity. The vessels are of earthenware and gourds, symbolizing the nature of Heaven and Earth. Because it takes place in the suburbs, it is called the suburban sacrifice. A reddish ox is used as the sacrificial victim because red is esteemed. A calf is used because sincerity is prized.

Thus music is the ordinance of Heaven and Earth, the ordering principle of balance and harmony, and something human feelings cannot do without.

In antiquity, the sages established the essential workings of yin and yang and of Heaven and Earth, setting them forth as the Changes (Yijing).

Where the aspirations reach, poetry also reaches; where poetry reaches, ritual also reaches; where ritual reaches, music also reaches.

Second Session

Discourse

Benevolence and wisdom unite as one in the sage.

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢舉賢良方正直言極諫之士詔〔文帝二年〕
擬唐以陸贄爲翰林學士誥〔建中四年〕
擬宋以杜衍同平章事兼樞密使謝表〔慶曆四年〕
判語〔五條〕
官員赴任過限
檢踏災傷田糧
===
丁夫差遣不平
詐欺官私取財
脩理橋梁道路
第叁場
策〔五道〕
問大學一書帝王脩齊治平之要道與典
謨訓誥相爲表裏宋儒眞德秀著爲衍
義其綱領條目無非羽翼聖經敷陳治
道君人者所宜留意焉者夫何陳之當
punctuated:
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢舉賢良方正直言極諫之士詔〔文帝二年〕。
擬唐以陸贄爲翰林學士誥〔建中四年〕。
擬宋以杜衍同平章事兼樞密使謝表〔慶曆四年〕。

判語〔五條〕
官員赴任過限。
檢踏災傷田糧。
丁夫差遣不平。
詐欺官私取財。
脩理橋梁道路。

第叁場
策〔五道〕
問：大學一書，帝王脩齊治平之要道，與典謨訓誥相爲表裏。宋儒眞德秀著爲衍義，其綱領條目，無非羽翼聖經，敷陳治道，君人者所宜留意焉者。夫何陳之當
translation_en:
Edicts, proclamations of appointment, and memorials 〔One topic from among these [?]〕
Compose an edict in the manner of the Han dynasty calling for the recommendation of men who are worthy and good, upright and correct, and capable of frank speech and forthright remonstrance. 〔Second year of Emperor Wen’s reign〕
Compose a proclamation in the manner of the Tang dynasty appointing Lu Zhi as Hanlin Academician. 〔Fourth year of Jianzhong〕
Compose a memorial of thanks in the manner of the Song dynasty, on behalf of Du Yan, for his appointment as Chief Councilor and concurrently Military Affairs Commissioner. 〔Fourth year of Qingli〕

Legal judgments 〔Five items〕
Officials exceeding the time limit for reporting to their posts.
Inspecting disaster-damaged farmland and its grain-tax assessment.
Inequitable assignment of laborers to service.
Fraudulently obtaining government or private property.
Repairing bridges and roads.

Third Session
Policy questions 〔Five questions〕
Question: The Great Learning sets forth the essential Way by which emperors and kings cultivate themselves, regulate their families, govern the state, and bring peace to the realm. It complements the canons, counsels, instructions, and proclamations of the Book of Documents. The Song Confucian scholar Zhen Dexiu composed the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning; its organizing principles and detailed divisions all serve to support the sage’s classic and expound the Way of government. These are matters to which rulers ought to attend. Why, then, when it was presented at the time …

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
時多悅而不繹而傳之後世亦未有深
知而篤好者也洪惟我
太祖高皇帝甫定天下即銳志講學因冞源之
請
命左右大書衍義於兩廡朝夕諦觀以代丹青
即盤銘豆觴之遺意也時與侍臣議論
聖謨洋洋具載典策不識諸士子亦有所聞與
我
皇上受
===
天明命丕振
中興益懋
聖德維時輔臣首請以大學衍義
進講
皇上欣然嘉納乃
默契化源
親揮
宸翰因賦五言古詩十韻
命二三輔臣賡相倡和萃而輯之名曰
punctuated:
時，多悅而不繹，而傳之後世，亦未有深知而篤好者也。洪惟我太祖高皇帝甫定天下，即銳志講學，因冞源之請，命左右大書衍義於兩廡，朝夕諦觀，以代丹青，即盤銘豆觴之遺意也。時與侍臣議論，聖謨洋洋，具載典策。不識諸士子亦有所聞與？
我皇上受天明命，丕振中興，益懋聖德。維時輔臣首請以《大學衍義》進講，皇上欣然嘉納，乃默契化源，親揮宸翰，因賦五言古詩十韻，命二三輔臣賡相倡和，萃而輯之，名曰：
translation_en:
…at the time, many took pleasure in it but did not explore its meaning; and when it was transmitted to later generations, there were likewise none who understood it deeply and cherished it devotedly. We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao, as soon as he had pacified the realm, firmly resolved to pursue learning through lectures and discussion. At the request of Mi Yuan [?], he ordered his attendants to write out the Extended Meaning in large characters on the two side galleries. He examined it attentively morning and evening, using it in place of paintings. This carried forward the intent of the ancient inscriptions on basins, sacrificial vessels, and drinking cups. From time to time he discussed it with his attendant officials; his abundant sagely counsels are fully recorded in the official books. We wonder whether you candidates have also heard of these things?
Our reigning Emperor received Heaven’s luminous mandate, grandly advanced the restoration, and further cultivated his sagely virtue. At that time, his senior ministers first requested that the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning (Daxue yanyi) be expounded in imperial lectures. The Emperor gladly approved and accepted their proposal. In silent accord with the source of transformation, he personally wielded the imperial brush and composed an ancient-style poem in five-character lines with ten rhymes. He commanded several senior ministers to compose matching poems in response. These were gathered and compiled into a collection entitled…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
翊學詩心學淵源與
聖祖先後一轍猗與盛哉傳播海內諸士子誦
而習之蓋有年矣請明著於篇以觀對
揚之懿
問治曆明時作樂崇德大有關于治道在
儒者所必講也以帝舜之聖而首察璣
衡以后夔之賢而專職音樂則其事亦
有未易言者漢而下論曆律者代有其
人據其說果足以被之琴瑟管絃而克
舉乎保章馮相之職與唐一行論氣朔
推步者凡七議曆數者十有二其詳可
得聞與元郭守敬曆法或者謂太衍莫
過焉果何所取衷與宋蔡元定律呂證
辨者凡十論本原者十有三其說可悉
數與黃鍾分寸或者執含少之說以疑
之抑自有見與夫曆莫重于曆元而其
要在候氣律莫首于黃鍾而其要在定
管制作之方諸家必有可憑者即欲聞
punctuated:
《翊學詩》。心學淵源，與聖祖先後一轍，猗與盛哉！傳播海內，諸士子誦而習之，蓋有年矣。請明著於篇，以觀對揚之懿。
問：治曆明時，作樂崇德，大有關于治道，在儒者所必講也。以帝舜之聖，而首察璣衡；以后夔之賢，而專職音樂，則其事亦有未易言者。漢而下，論曆律者代有其人，據其說，果足以被之琴瑟管絃，而克舉乎保章、馮相之職與？唐一行論氣朔推步者凡七，議曆數者十有二，其詳可得聞與？元郭守敬曆法，或者謂太衍莫過焉，果何所取衷與？宋蔡元定律呂，證辨者凡十，論本原者十有三，其說可悉數與？黃鍾分寸，或者執含少之說以疑之，抑自有見與？夫曆莫重于曆元，而其要在候氣；律莫首于黃鍾，而其要在定管。制作之方，諸家必有可憑者，即欲聞
translation_en:
…Poems in Aid of Learning (Yixue shi). The origins and transmission of his learning of the mind follow precisely the same course as those of the sagely ancestral emperor, though they lived at different times. Ah, how magnificent! These poems have circulated throughout the realm, and scholars have recited and studied them for years. Please set this out clearly in your essay, so that we may see the excellence of your response in extolling the imperial achievement.
Question: Regulating the calendar to clarify the seasons and creating music to exalt virtue have great bearing on the way of government; scholars of the Confucian tradition must investigate them. Even with Emperor Shun’s sagacity, his first concern was to examine the celestial instruments; even with Hou Kui’s worthiness, he was charged specifically with music. These matters are therefore not easily discussed. From the Han onward, every age has had men who discussed calendrical science and pitch standards. Are their theories really sufficient to be applied to zithers, pipes, and strings, and to enable the duties of the Baozhang and Fengxiang astronomical officials to be fulfilled?
The Tang scholar Yixing presented seven discussions of calculating solar terms and new moons and twelve discussions of calendrical reckoning. May we hear their details? Regarding the calendrical methods of Guo Shoujing of the Yuan, some say that the Taiyan [?] could not surpass them. What, precisely, did he take as his standard? In his work on pitch standards, Cai Yuanding of the Song provided ten discussions of evidence and disputed points and thirteen discussions of fundamental principles. Can you enumerate all his explanations? Regarding the dimensions of the Huangzhong, or Yellow Bell, pitch pipe in inches and tenths of an inch, some invoke the theory of “containing the lesser” [?] to cast doubt on them. Did they perhaps have insights of their own?
In calendrical science, nothing is more important than the calendrical epoch, and the key lies in observing the seasonal qi. Among pitch standards, nothing takes precedence over Huangzhong, and the key lies in fixing the dimensions of the pipe. Among the methods of construction proposed by the various authorities, there must be some on which one can rely. We now wish to hear…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
局求人以專斯業爾多士豈無義獎之
選乎願有以先告我也
問昔之君子所以垂世而不朽者曰道德
曰功業曰文章是三者非判然不相須
也惟兹中土雅號多賢若格天奕業降
嶽楨時詩啓二毛學傳一貫于斯三者
亦秉之矣自是以降代不乏人雖才器
不同而顯微可述有智爲帝師功成高
蹈者有外寛內明士民歸心者有攬轡
===
澄清願爲容接者有平心化盜私謚文
範者有舉親却敵鬧捷不動者有望高
一時器與三蘇者有忠義報國矢志恢
復者有十事要說排時自慶者有決獄
有聲急流勇退者有唱名奏瑞竟安社
稷者有大節難奪彥博並稱者有杖策
一言遂定大計者有孤城抗賊保全江
淮者有德量難測人稱顏子者其于古
人之功業有相彷彿否與有陳至言而
punctuated:
局求人以專斯業，爾多士豈無義獎之選乎？願有以先告我也。

問：昔之君子所以垂世而不朽者，曰道德，曰功業，曰文章。是三者非判然不相須也。惟兹中土，雅號多賢，若格天奕業、降嶽楨時、詩啓二毛、學傳一貫，于斯三者亦秉之矣。自是以降，代不乏人，雖才器不同，而顯微可述。有智爲帝師、功成高蹈者，有外寛內明、士民歸心者，有攬轡澄清、願爲容接者，有平心化盜、私謚文範者，有舉親却敵、鬧捷不動者，有望高一時、器與三蘇者，有忠義報國、矢志恢復者，有十事要說、排時自慶者，有決獄有聲、急流勇退者，有唱名奏瑞、竟安社稷者，有大節難奪、彥博並稱者，有杖策一言、遂定大計者，有孤城抗賊、保全江淮者，有德量難測、人稱顏子者。其于古人之功業，有相彷彿否與？有陳至言而
translation_en:
…[a bureau?], seeking men to devote themselves to this undertaking. Among you many candidates, are there none worthy of selection and commendation for righteousness [?]? I hope you will first offer me some guidance.

Question: The means by which gentlemen of antiquity left a lasting legacy and achieved immortality were moral virtue, meritorious achievement, and literary accomplishment. These three are not sharply separated and independent of one another. This central region has long been renowned for its many worthies: those whose magnificent achievements reached Heaven; those born through the numinous power of the sacred mountains to serve as pillars of their age; the two Mao masters who opened up the meaning of the Poetry; and those who transmitted the learning of the single thread running through the Way. They too possessed these three qualities.

From that time onward, no age has lacked such men. Though their talents and capacities differed, their deeds, both manifest and obscure, can be recounted. There was one whose wisdom made him an emperor’s teacher and who withdrew to lofty seclusion once his work was accomplished; one who was outwardly lenient but inwardly discerning, winning the allegiance of scholars and commoners; one who took up the reins determined to cleanse the realm, and with whom others wished to be received into fellowship [?]; one who reformed robbers through evenhandedness and was privately given the posthumous name Wenfan, “Model of Culture”; one who recommended a relative and repelled the enemy, remaining unmoved amid the clamorous celebration of victory [?]; one whose reputation towered over his contemporaries and whose ability ranked with that of the three Su masters [?]; one who served his country with loyalty and righteousness, vowing to recover the lost territory; one who set forth essential arguments in ten points and, opposing his times, congratulated himself [?]; one renowned for deciding legal cases who courageously withdrew at the height of his career; one who announced a name and reported an auspicious sign, ultimately securing the state [?]; one whose integrity in great matters could not be shaken and who was ranked alongside Yanbo; one who came bearing his staff and, with a single utterance, settled a major plan; one who resisted rebels in an isolated city and preserved the Jiang–Huai region; and one whose virtue and magnanimity were unfathomable, whom people called Master Yan. Did their meritorious achievements bear comparison with those of the ancients?

There was one who presented words of utmost truth and…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
動主者有受易學而來歸者有進策治
安號通國體者有校正六經立碑大學
者有作申鑒以匡時政者有脩直史入
冊黃孤者有寢處百日指玄著論者有
仿佑六經斗山著望者有高潔工詩冲
濟可法者有賦二京兼精曆筭者有不
愧科名兄弟並美者有博覽洽聞類物
辨俗者其于古人之文章有相彷彿否
與其所謂功業文章果皆不詭于道與
===
道學初明眞儒挺出若其參造化關盛
衰今古賴之似又不可以一鄉論也諸
士子高山景行將誰與歸願詳述之以
觀尚友之學
問兵者所以明德除害也故舉得於外福
生於內三代而下談說經武要略無慮
數十百家今所存七書而已乃其攻討
克備貴謀多筭行之有順逆用之有巧
拙昭然可覩識矣遡觀古昔若滅竈會
punctuated:
動主者，有受易學而來歸者，有進策治安、號通國體者，有校正六經、立碑大學者，有作《申鑒》以匡時政者，有脩直史、入冊黃孤者，有寢處百日、指玄著論者，有仿佑六經、斗山著望者，有高潔工詩、冲濟可法者，有賦二京、兼精曆筭者，有不愧科名、兄弟並美者，有博覽洽聞、類物辨俗者。其于古人之文章有相彷彿否與？其所謂功業文章，果皆不詭于道與？道學初明，眞儒挺出，若其參造化、關盛衰，今古賴之，似又不可以一鄉論也。諸士子高山景行，將誰與歸？願詳述之，以觀尚友之學。

問：兵者，所以明德除害也。故舉得於外，福生於內。三代而下，談說經武要略，無慮數十百家，今所存七書而已。乃其攻討克備，貴謀多筭，行之有順逆，用之有巧拙，昭然可覩識矣。遡觀古昔，若滅竈會
translation_en:
…moved their ruler; some received instruction in the Book of Changes and came back; some presented proposals for orderly and peaceful government and were reputed to understand the essentials of governing the state; some collated and corrected the Six Classics and erected inscribed stelae at the Imperial University; some composed the Mirror of Admonitions (Shen jian) to rectify contemporary government; some compiled truthful histories and entered the registers of “Huang Gu” [?]; some remained in their quarters for a hundred days, expounding mysteries and composing treatises; some supported the Six Classics [?] and gained reputations as eminent as the Northern Dipper and Mount Tai; some were lofty and pure in character and accomplished in poetry, their equanimity and helpfulness worthy of emulation [?]; some composed rhapsodies on the two capitals and were also expert in calendrical calculation; some lived up to their examination honors, brothers alike distinguished; and some read widely and possessed comprehensive knowledge, classifying things and distinguishing customs. Did their literary achievements resemble those of the ancients? Were their so-called accomplishments in public service and letters indeed all consistent with the Way? When the Learning of the Way first became clear, true Confucian scholars emerged outstandingly. Insofar as they participated in the transforming and nurturing work of Heaven and Earth and affected flourishing and decline, both past and present have depended upon them: it seems that they cannot be assessed merely within the confines of one locality. You candidates look up to lofty mountains and follow the great road: whom, then, will you follow? Please explain in detail, so that we may observe your learning in seeking the friendship of worthy men of the past.

Question: Arms are the means by which virtue is made manifest and harm removed. Thus, when military undertakings abroad succeed, blessings arise at home. Since the Three Dynasties, writers discussing the essential principles of military affairs have numbered scores or hundreds; today only seven books survive. Their methods of attack, punitive campaigns, conquest, and defense [?], their emphasis on strategy and ample calculation, the favorable or adverse circumstances of their implementation, and the skill or clumsiness of their application can all be clearly discerned. Looking back into antiquity, consider such examples as extinguishing cooking fires and assembling [?]…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
竈之殊其形囊沙量沙之異其用百里
趨利則馬陵之斃軍志所戒也或曰兵
貴神速何與包原隰而陣則秭歸之役
宜爲人所乘也乃又褁氊深入何與魚
腹列陣誠三代才也而或謂運用之妙
存乎一心嚴飭部伍眞漢名將也而有
不擊刁斗者將才無出其右其故可得
聞與夜半奪關不踰易字多多益辦以
簡得之其義何所指與至於聚米指畫
===
虜在目中矣何以曰兵難遥度養虎遺
患敵固不可縱矣何以曰窮寇勿追背
水之陣與氷堅可渡者其指安在淮淝
之捷與赤壁之戰者其計安得夫掎角
之勢覆人之達計也奇正之變馭敵之
祕機也呼吸存亡於玆攸繫昔人所稱
微乎微矣孔子曰我戰則克其必有所
以矣諸士握機抱筭而來豈以是爲危
事而諱言之耶
punctuated: 竈之殊其形，囊沙量沙之異其用，百里趨利則馬陵之斃，軍志所戒也。或曰：「兵貴神速。」何與？包原隰而陣，則秭歸之役宜爲人所乘也，乃又褁氊深入，何與？魚腹列陣，誠三代才也，而或謂：「運用之妙，存乎一心。」嚴飭部伍，眞漢名將也，而有不擊刁斗者，將才無出其右，其故可得聞與？夜半奪關，不踰易字；多多益辦，以簡得之，其義何所指與？至於聚米指畫，虜在目中矣，何以曰：「兵難遥度」？養虎遺患，敵固不可縱矣，何以曰：「窮寇勿追」？背水之陣與氷堅可渡者，其指安在？淮淝之捷與赤壁之戰者，其計安得？夫掎角之勢，覆人之達計也；奇正之變，馭敵之祕機也。呼吸存亡，於玆攸繫。昔人所稱：「微乎微矣！」孔子曰：「我戰則克。」其必有所以矣。諸士握機抱筭而來，豈以是爲危事而諱言之耶？
translation_en:
…the stoves differed in their outward arrangement, while bagging sand and measuring sand differed in their uses. Racing a hundred li to gain an advantage led to destruction at Maling: this is what the military writings warn against. Yet some say, “In warfare, extraordinary speed is prized.” How is this reconciled? When troops encamped across uplands and lowlands, as in the campaign at Zigui, they deserved to have their vulnerability exploited. Yet there was also the advance deep into enemy territory wrapped in felt. How is this reconciled? He who arrayed troops at Yufu [?] truly possessed the ability of the Three Dynasties; yet someone said, “The subtlety of employing them lies wholly in the mind.” He who strictly ordered his units was truly a renowned Han general; yet there was another who did not strike the watch kettles, and whose ability as a commander none surpassed. May we hear the reasons for this? Seizing a pass at midnight did not go beyond the word “ease” [?]; the ability to handle ever greater numbers was achieved through simplicity. What do these statements mean?

As for piling up rice to indicate the terrain and explain a plan, the enemy was already before one’s eyes. Why, then, is it said that “military affairs are difficult to assess from afar”? Raising a tiger leaves trouble for the future: certainly an enemy must not be released. Why, then, is it said, “Do not pursue a cornered enemy”? What is the purport of the formation with its back to the water, and of the assertion that the ice was solid enough to cross? How were the plans for the victory at the Huai and Fei rivers and the battle of Chibi devised? A disposition that holds an enemy from the rear while attacking from the front is an effective plan for overthrowing him; transformations between irregular and regular operations are the hidden means of controlling him. Survival or destruction in the space of a breath depends upon these things. As men of old exclaimed, “Subtle indeed, how subtle!” Confucius said, “If I fought, I would win.” Surely he had grounds for saying this. You gentlemen have come with a grasp of the critical workings of warfare and plans in mind. Would you regard this as a perilous subject and shrink from discussing it?

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
問古者制民之產田以井受民安其生然
井田之中溝塗川澮疆理限隔設險之
義存焉故其時人樂爲善至比屋可封
後世阡陌久廢貧富不均易與爲姦乃
令河南所在平曠盜賊四起小行剽劫
大且嘯聚豈無能爲生耶抑地險不足
人懷恣睢也說者謂古昔能止盜者莫
善於漢言治盜者莫詳於宋今觀渤海
弄兵安之而治冀州起刺到部屛息有
===
三科募士而稱明朝歌有單車之職而
更生魚釜至於賈父清平歌興交趾朱
君良計戒於納降又人人殊矣而當時
所稱有謂簡別流民弱黨殲渠不勞而
定者豈確論與宋之名臣或謂縻用兇
險以消始禍或謂籠取豪猾使自歆利
其意同與至於歐陽四事太虛二弊固
禦盜之律令也而所謂折氣攜心尤爲
至計可得悉言其義與夫比追胥施刑
punctuated: 問：古者制民之產，田以井受，民安其生。然井田之中，溝塗川澮，疆理限隔，設險之義存焉。故其時人樂爲善，至比屋可封。後世阡陌久廢，貧富不均，易與爲姦。乃令河南所在平曠，盜賊四起，小行剽劫，大且嘯聚。豈無能爲生耶？抑地險不足，人懷恣睢也？說者謂古昔能止盜者莫善於漢，言治盜者莫詳於宋。今觀渤海弄兵，安之而治；冀州起刺，到部屛息；有三科募士而稱明朝歌，有單車之職而更生魚釜。至於賈父清平，歌興交趾；朱君良計，戒於納降，又人人殊矣。而當時所稱，有謂簡別流民，弱黨殲渠，不勞而定者，豈確論與？宋之名臣，或謂縻用兇險以消始禍，或謂籠取豪猾使自歆利，其意同與？至於歐陽四事、太虛二弊，固禦盜之律令也。而所謂折氣攜心，尤爲至計，可得悉言其義與？夫比追胥、施刑
translation_en:
Question: In antiquity, the people's livelihoods were regulated: fields were allotted according to the well-field system, and the people lived securely. Yet within those well-fields, the ditches, roads, waterways, drainage channels, boundaries, and partitions embodied the principle of establishing defensive obstacles. Thus people at that time delighted in doing good, to the point that household after household was worthy of enfeoffment. In later ages, the field paths had long fallen into disuse, wealth and poverty became unequal, and people were easily drawn into wrongdoing. Now Henan is everywhere flat and open, and bandits arise on all sides: in small groups they plunder and rob; in larger numbers they gather into armed bands. Is this because they cannot earn a living? Or is it because the terrain offers insufficient obstacles and people harbor unbridled impulses?

Commentators say that, among past dynasties, none surpassed the Han in stopping banditry, and none discussed its suppression more fully than the Song. Consider the armed disturbances in Bohai: reassurance restored order. In Jizhou, unrest [?] subsided as soon as the official arrived in his jurisdiction. One official recruited men in three categories and won praise for enlightened government in Zhaoge; another went to his post in a single carriage and gave new life to men who were like fish in a cauldron. As for Father Jia's peaceful and equitable government, it inspired songs in Jiaozhi; Lord Zhu's sound strategy cautioned against accepting surrender. Each man's approach differed. Yet among the measures praised at the time was selecting and distinguishing among displaced people, weakening the followers, and destroying the ringleaders, thereby restoring peace without exertion. Is this a sound assessment?

Among the eminent ministers of the Song, some advocated keeping violent and dangerous men in service to eliminate trouble at its inception; others advocated drawing powerful rogues into one's control so that they themselves would eagerly seek the benefits. Were their intentions the same? As for Ouyang's four measures and Taixu's two abuses, these are certainly guiding rules for guarding against bandits. But what is called breaking their spirit and dividing their loyalties is an especially effective strategy. Can you explain its meaning fully? As for setting deadlines for pursuit and searches [?], and imposing punishments…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
慶建樓置鼓義營賞告之法有司之已
事也能不廢格足矣採木銷萌達權握
筭必有出於是者何以告我而擇行之
punctuated: 慶、建樓置鼓、義營賞告之法，有司之已事也，能不廢格足矣。採木銷萌、達權握筭，必有出於是者，何以告我而擇行之？
translation_en: …rewards, erecting towers and installing drums, establishing militia camps [?], and rewarding informants: these measures are already the business of the responsible officials. It is enough that they should not neglect or obstruct their implementation. Yet in removing the roots and suppressing the first sprouts of trouble [?], adapting measures to circumstances, and commanding effective strategies, there must be approaches that go beyond these. What can you tell me, so that I may select and implement them?

The Master said: “Set your resolve on the Way, hold firmly to virtue, rely upon benevolence, and find recreation in the arts.”

Zhao Xian

Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: 〔In this topic, the Sage shows people the full scope of the work of learning. Most interpretations are tiresomely disjointed. By entering into it in due sequence, one comes close to attainment. Why is this so? For a scholar, nothing takes precedence over making his resolve clear, and the Way is the target of that resolve. title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
惑嚮至正以端向往之趣而凡念以從事者不
淆於似是之非夫固以天下之定理爲吾心之
定見而所入之途正矣夫道而曰志猶未得也
至於得之而爲德焉不有以守之可乎必也隨
吾踐履之所有益敦夫固執之功即吾力行之
所至恒懋夫秉持之力蓋有始終如一而日新
又新者矣夫德而曰據猶與我二也至於熟之
而爲仁焉不有以存之可乎必也奉帝則以周
旋而全體之不息順天理以游衍而成性之恒
===
存蓋有常變一致而終食不違者矣夫然則大
本已立而學亦至矣至若藝者又至理所寓而
日用所須也不有以游之亦非所以多識而畜
德矣是必朝與游焉旁通之以極義理之趣夕
與游焉博觀之以盡事物之情則應務有餘而
此心不放中之所養者益熟矣夫本與末而兼
該內與外而交養輕重不失先後有序謂非聖
脩之極乎雖然志也者聖學之所以成始而成
終者也是故始乎此志終乎此志一志立則道
punctuated: 惑，嚮至正以端向往之趣，而凡念以從事者不淆於似是之非。夫固以天下之定理爲吾心之定見，而所入之途正矣。夫道而曰志，猶未得也；至於得之而爲德焉，不有以守之可乎？必也隨吾踐履之所有，益敦夫固執之功；即吾力行之所至，恒懋夫秉持之力。蓋有始終如一而日新又新者矣。夫德而曰據，猶與我二也；至於熟之而爲仁焉，不有以存之可乎？必也奉帝則以周旋，而全體之不息；順天理以游衍，而成性之恒存。蓋有常變一致而終食不違者矣。夫然則大本已立，而學亦至矣。至若藝者，又至理所寓而日用所須也。不有以游之，亦非所以多識而畜德矣。是必朝與游焉，旁通之以極義理之趣；夕與游焉，博觀之以盡事物之情。則應務有餘而此心不放，中之所養者益熟矣。夫本與末而兼該，內與外而交養，輕重不失，先後有序，謂非聖脩之極乎？雖然，志也者，聖學之所以成始而成終者也。是故始乎此志，終乎此志，一志立則道
translation_en:
…confusion; turn toward what is supremely correct to set the direction of one’s aspirations aright, so that every thought brought to one’s undertakings is unconfused by errors that resemble truth. Thus one takes the fixed principles of all under Heaven as the settled convictions of one’s own mind, and the path upon which one enters is correct.

Yet to speak of “setting one’s resolve upon” the Way means that one has not yet attained it. Once one has attained it and it becomes virtue, can one dispense with the means of holding fast to it? Whatever one has achieved in personal practice, one must further strengthen the effort to maintain it firmly; wherever strenuous action has brought one, one must constantly exert oneself to sustain it. Thus one remains consistent from beginning to end, renewing oneself daily, and renewing oneself yet again.

Yet to speak of “holding firmly to” virtue means that it still stands apart from oneself. Once it has matured into benevolence, can one dispense with the means of preserving it? One must conduct oneself according to the Supreme Lord’s standards, embodying them fully without cease; one must move freely in accordance with Heaven’s principles, constantly preserving one’s perfected nature. Thus one remains consistent amid both ordinary circumstances and change, never departing from benevolence even for the duration of a meal. Then the great foundation is established, and learning too has reached its culmination.

As for the arts, these too are where ultimate principles reside and are necessary for daily use. Without the means of freely engaging in them, one cannot broaden one’s knowledge and nurture virtue. One must engage in them in the morning, comprehending their connections on every side to explore fully the purport of moral principles; one must engage in them in the evening, observing broadly to understand exhaustively the realities of affairs and things. Then one will have ample capacity to respond to affairs without letting the mind stray, and what is nurtured within will mature still further. Comprehending both root and branches, nurturing both the inner and the outer, properly distinguishing the weighty from the less weighty, and proceeding in due sequence—could this be called anything other than the pinnacle of sagely cultivation?

Nevertheless, resolve is what enables the learning of the sages to accomplish both its beginning and its completion. Thus one begins with this resolve and ends with this resolve. Once a single resolve is established, the Way…

translation_en:
…the Way can be fully realized, virtue made complete, benevolence brought to maturity, and the arts mastered. Otherwise, learning falls into neglect as resolve weakens, and there will be no means of bringing it to completion. The Record of Rites says, “For a scholar, resolve comes first”; and when Mengzi discusses the scholar’s task, he likewise sums it up as elevating one’s resolve. Can establishing resolve possibly be deferred? Ah! In recounting his own life, the Sage begins with setting his heart on learning; here, too, he begins with setting his resolve on the Way. Profound indeed is his meaning!

“Vast and broad like Heaven; deep and welling like an abyss.”
Chen Jiaming

Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor, comments: “Most precise and incisive in describing the fullness of abundant virtue. Only a scholar who has cultivated himself could achieve this.”

Associate Examiner He, Instructor, comments: “The topic concerns principle and human nature, making it difficult to find fitting words at short notice. This essay is wide-ranging without running thin, profound without being obscure: truly a work that surpasses the field.”

Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: “The explanation of the two occurrences of ‘like’ has vitality and force of expression.”

Examiner Shi, Instructor, comments: “Essays on the meaning of the Doctrine of the Mean like this one are exceedingly rare.”

In treating the virtue of the utmost sage, the Doctrine of the Mean employs two comparisons to convey its abundant fullness. The sage, above and below, moves in the same current as Heaven and Earth. Could one then say that the abundant fullness of his virtue is not like Heaven and like an abyss? In elucidating the Way of Heaven at this point, the Doctrine of the Mean seems to say: endowed with keen perception and sagacious understanding, the sage possesses the virtues of benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom. How abundant, indeed, must their fullness within him be! His nature establishes all that exists under Heaven [?], and pervades without…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
窮誠貫天下之道而廣大莫禦聖人之德固有
所謂溥博矣仰而觀之其如天矣乎蓋其冲漠
無朕積元氣以上浮渾闢無窮普貞觀以下濟
言天下之廣大者至天焉極矣而聖人之德如
之則是大心體物無一理之不備者即天之無
不覆幬也全體大極無一善之不該者即天之
無不包含也天也聖也固有異象而同體者矣
聖同天不其大乎至若寂然不動靜以涵萬化
之原湛然無欲虛以妙萬物之感聖人之德固
===
有所謂淵泉矣俯而察之其如淵矣乎蓋其山
下出泉而源之所發者深地中有水而流之所
達者遠言天下之靜深者至淵焉極矣而聖人
之德如之則是洗心以藏密而探之莫究其極
者即淵之渾淪而無涘也資深以逢原而取之
莫盡其量者即淵之涵蓄而不竭也淵也聖也
固有異形而同理者矣聖同淵不其深乎夫聖
德所積至於極盛如此由是而發見有不當其
可哉大抵有盛德必有大業如天如淵言聖德
punctuated: 窮，誠貫天下之道而廣大莫禦，聖人之德固有所謂溥博矣。仰而觀之，其如天矣乎？蓋其冲漠無朕，積元氣以上浮；渾闢無窮，普貞觀以下濟。言天下之廣大者，至天焉極矣，而聖人之德如之。則是大心體物，無一理之不備者，即天之無不覆幬也；全體大極，無一善之不該者，即天之無不包含也。天也，聖也，固有異象而同體者矣。聖同天，不其大乎？至若寂然不動，靜以涵萬化之原；湛然無欲，虛以妙萬物之感，聖人之德固有所謂淵泉矣。俯而察之，其如淵矣乎？蓋其山下出泉，而源之所發者深；地中有水，而流之所達者遠。言天下之靜深者，至淵焉極矣，而聖人之德如之。則是洗心以藏密，而探之莫究其極者，即淵之渾淪而無涘也；資深以逢原，而取之莫盡其量者，即淵之涵蓄而不竭也。淵也，聖也，固有異形而同理者矣。聖同淵，不其深乎？夫聖德所積，至於極盛如此，由是而發見，有不當其可哉？大抵有盛德必有大業，如天如淵，言聖德
translation_en: …without end; his sincerity pervades the Way of all under Heaven, vast and impossible to restrain. The sage’s virtue assuredly possesses what is called all-embracing breadth. Looking upward to contemplate it, is it not like Heaven? Empty and still, without perceptible trace, it gathers primordial qi to float aloft; opening out boundlessly, it universally manifests its constancy and extends its aid below [?]. Of all that is broad and vast in the world, Heaven is the utmost, and the sage’s virtue resembles it. Thus, his enlarging the mind to embody all things, with no principle lacking, is precisely like Heaven’s sheltering everything beneath it. His fully embodying the Supreme Ultimate, with no goodness left out, is precisely like Heaven’s encompassing everything. Heaven and the sage indeed differ in appearance but share the same substance. Since the sage is one with Heaven, is he not great? As for his being still and unmoving, in tranquility containing the source of all transformations, and being limpid and free of desire, in emptiness responding wondrously to the impulses of all things, the sage’s virtue assuredly possesses what is called the depth of a wellspring. Looking downward to examine it, is it not like an abyss? A spring emerges beneath a mountain, and the source from which it issues is deep; water lies within the earth, and the reach of its flow is far. Of all that is tranquil and deep in the world, the abyss is the utmost, and the sage’s virtue resembles it. Thus, his cleansing the mind to store what is hidden, so that no probing can reach its limit, is precisely like the abyss’s undivided expanse without a shore. His drawing deeply upon what he has acquired to encounter its source, so that no drawing upon it can exhaust its capacity, is precisely like the abyss’s inexhaustible reserves. The abyss and the sage indeed differ in form but share the same principle. Since the sage is one with the abyss, is he not deep? Now, when the sage’s accumulated virtue reaches such supreme fullness, could any manifestation proceeding from it fail to be fitting? In general, abundant virtue necessarily brings great achievements. To say “like Heaven” and “like an abyss” speaks of the sage’s virtue…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
之以天淵祓生民而淵之以淵參天地贊化育
固溥博淵泉之極功也豈特如之已哉雖然人
心本自廣大而自私者隘之人心本自淵深而
自蔽者淺之學者苟能從事於戒懼謹獨以復
其本然之體則至大至深而聖可幾矣
禮之實節文斯二者是也樂之實樂斯二
者樂則生矣生則惡可已也惡可已則
不知足之蹈之手之舞之
===

已夫禮樂不出乎所性之外也於孝弟而極中
和之妙則其本立矣禮樂之實不在茲乎此孟
子示人以盡性之學也蓋曰道不可以泛求學
banxin: 鄉試錄文　五　羅許
punctuated:
之以天，淵祓生民而淵之以淵，參天地，贊化育，固溥博淵泉之極功也，豈特如之已哉？雖然，人心本自廣大，而自私者隘之；人心本自淵深，而自蔽者淺之。學者苟能從事於戒懼謹獨，以復其本然之體，則至大至深，而聖可幾矣。

translation_en:
…with Heaven; “purifying the people” and “deepening them with the depths” [?]. To stand alongside Heaven and Earth and assist their transforming and nourishing work is indeed the ultimate achievement of expansive breadth and wellspring-like depth. How could it amount merely to resembling them? Nevertheless, the human mind is inherently broad and great, but selfishness constricts it; the human mind is inherently profound, but self-obscuration makes it shallow. If learners can devote themselves to vigilance and apprehension, and to watchfulness when alone, thereby restoring the mind’s original constitution, they can attain the utmost greatness and depth, and sagehood can be approached.
The substance of ritual is to regulate and embellish these two things; the substance of music is to delight in these two things. With delight comes growth; once it grows, how can it be stopped? When it cannot be stopped, one unconsciously begins to stamp one’s feet and dance with one’s hands.
Associate Examiner Xiao, Instructor, comments: 〔Writers addressing this topic generally resemble one another. This essay alone is dignified and orderly in form, and its treatment of principle is composed and expansive. Its author evidently studies principle [?]; it is selected for more than literary merit alone.〕
Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: 〔Both expression and reasoning are fully accomplished.〕
Examiner Shi, Instructor, comments: 〔Closely pertinent, precise, and substantial.〕
In examining the substance of ritual and music, the great worthy simply brings to their fullest realization the subtleties of equilibrium and harmony within filial devotion and respect for elder brothers. Ritual and music do not extend beyond what belongs to our inherent nature. When the subtleties of equilibrium and harmony are fully realized within filial devotion and respect for elder brothers, their foundation is established. Does not the substance of ritual and music lie here? This is how Mencius teaches people the learning through which they fully realize their nature. He is, in effect, saying: “The Way cannot be sought vaguely; learning …

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
英先於盡性仁義智之實固在於孝弟矣而禮
樂豈外是乎今夫禮嘉天下之會而儀文度數
特其華耳以言其實亦惟於孝弟節文之而已
蓋愛敬之用情勝則易流也必損過就中不使
之蕩焉而無節親長之事恩勝則易略也必釋
同增美不使之簡焉而無文天叙之惇本乎天
秩以爲之則藹然相愛之中固有截然而不紊
者矣人紀之脩本乎人文以爲之質井然有辨
之際固有燦然而可觀者矣斯則品節既極其
===
詳而推行曲當其可天下之大中在我矣舉而
措之以嘉天下之會禮可勝用哉樂以平天下
之情而聲容節奏特其文耳以言其實在樂乎
孝弟而已夫惟樂也吾見悅諸心而融諸慮天
性之由衷者既非勉強以從事則根於心而生
於色至情之活潑者自將隨感而即形由是心
和則氣和而日新月盛有欲罷不能者以達其
機也由是氣和則形和而足蹈手舞有不言而
喻者以彰其化也斯則和順積於中而神應妙
punctuated:
英先於盡性。仁義智之實固在於孝弟矣，而禮樂豈外是乎？今夫禮，嘉天下之會，而儀文度數特其華耳。以言其實，亦惟於孝弟節文之而已。蓋愛敬之用，情勝則易流也，必損過就中，不使之蕩焉而無節；親長之事，恩勝則易略也，必釋同增美，不使之簡焉而無文。天叙之惇，本乎天秩以爲之則，藹然相愛之中，固有截然而不紊者矣；人紀之脩，本乎人文以爲之質，井然有辨之際，固有燦然而可觀者矣。斯則品節既極其詳，而推行曲當其可，天下之大中在我矣。舉而措之，以嘉天下之會，禮可勝用哉？

樂以平天下之情，而聲容節奏特其文耳。以言其實，在樂乎孝弟而已。夫惟樂也，吾見悅諸心而融諸慮，天性之由衷者，既非勉強以從事，則根於心而生於色，至情之活潑者，自將隨感而即形。由是心和則氣和，而日新月盛，有欲罷不能者，以達其機也；由是氣和則形和，而足蹈手舞，有不言而喻者，以彰其化也。斯則和順積於中，而神應妙
translation_en:
…[nothing?] takes precedence over fully realizing one’s nature. The substance of benevolence, righteousness, and wisdom certainly lies in filial devotion and respect for elder brothers; how could ritual and music lie outside these? Ritual lends beauty to the gatherings of all under Heaven, while ceremonial forms, measures, and numbers are merely its outward flowering. As for its substance, it consists simply in regulating and embellishing filial devotion and fraternal respect. In the exercise of love and reverence, when feeling predominates, it easily becomes unrestrained. One must therefore reduce excess and attain the mean, preventing feeling from running unchecked and without measure. In serving parents and elders, when affection predominates, observance easily becomes perfunctory. One must therefore set aside undifferentiated familiarity and add refinement, preventing simplicity from becoming a lack of proper form. Strengthening Heaven’s ordering of human relationships takes Heaven’s prescribed ranks as its rule: amid warm mutual affection, there are clear distinctions free from disorder. Cultivating the bonds of human society takes cultural forms as its substance: amid orderly distinctions, there is a brilliance worthy of contemplation. Thus, when distinctions and regulations have been worked out in full detail, and their application fits every particular circumstance, the great equilibrium of all under Heaven resides in me. If I put this into practice to lend beauty to the gatherings of all under Heaven, could the uses of ritual ever be exhausted?

Music brings harmony to the feelings of all under Heaven, while sounds, movements, rhythms, and cadences are merely its outward pattern. As for its substance, it consists simply in taking joy in filial devotion and fraternal respect. Precisely because there is joy, I see it delighting the heart and suffusing one’s thoughts. Since what springs sincerely from one’s Heaven-given nature is not pursued through forced effort, it takes root in the heart and manifests itself in the countenance. The vitality of the deepest feelings will naturally become manifest whenever something stirs them. Thus, when the heart is harmonious, the vital energies are harmonious; renewed daily and flourishing monthly, their impulse unfolds so that one cannot stop even if one wishes to. Thus, when the vital energies are harmonious, the body is harmonious; the feet step and the hands dance, and something is understood without words, making their transforming power manifest. In this way, harmony and accord accumulate within, and the spirit’s responsiveness works wondrously…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
於外天下之至和在我矣推而達之以平天下
之情樂可勝用哉是知禮樂之實舉不外於孝
弟人能從事於此則立於禮成於樂而盡性之
能事畢矣亦何必遠有所慕哉斯義也有子嘗
言之矣曰孝弟也者其爲仁之本與曰禮之用
和爲貴蓋達禮樂之致而探其本者矣孟子之
傳得之聖門固不信與然學者何以進之曰禮
可以强而立樂不可强而致有事勿忘而俟
其化斯得之矣故曰惟樂不可以僞爲
===
易
乾元者始而亨者也利貞者性情也乾始
能以美利利天下不言所利大矣哉大
哉乾乎剛健中正純粹精也
趙賢
同考試官教諭劉　批〔理明詞峻得潔靜精微之旨〕
同考試官教諭程　批〔天道類非淺學能言此作指造化如掌說天莫辨於子矣〕
同考試官教諭朱　批〔說乾元之意明透〕
punctuated:
於外，天下之至和在我矣。推而達之，以平天下之情，樂可勝用哉？是知禮樂之實，舉不外於孝弟。人能從事於此，則立於禮，成於樂，而盡性之能事畢矣。亦何必遠有所慕哉？斯義也，有子嘗言之矣，曰：「孝弟也者，其爲仁之本與！」曰：「禮之用，和爲貴。」蓋達禮樂之致而探其本者矣。孟子之傳得之聖門，固不信與？然學者何以進之？曰：「禮可以强而立，樂不可强而致。有事勿忘，而俟其化，斯得之矣。」故曰：「惟樂不可以僞爲。」

易

乾元者，始而亨者也。利貞者，性情也。乾始能以美利利天下，不言所利，大矣哉！大哉乾乎！剛健中正，純粹精也。

趙賢

同考試官教諭劉　批〔理明詞峻，得潔靜精微之旨。〕
同考試官教諭程　批〔天道類非淺學能言，此作指造化如掌，說天莫辨於子矣。〕
同考試官教諭朱　批〔說乾元之意明透。〕
translation_en:
…outwardly, the utmost harmony of all under Heaven resides in me. If I extend it to bring harmony to the feelings of all under Heaven, could the uses of music ever be exhausted? Thus we know that the substance of ritual and music lies entirely within filial devotion and respect for elder brothers. If people devote themselves to these, they will establish themselves through ritual and achieve completion through music, fully accomplishing all that is possible in fulfilling their nature. Why need they seek anything far away to admire? Youzi once expressed this principle, saying: “Are filial devotion and respect for elder brothers not the root of practicing humaneness?” He also said: “In the practice of ritual, harmony is prized.” He thus comprehended the ultimate significance of ritual and music and explored their root. Can it really be doubted that Mencius received his transmission from the school of the Sage? But how should students advance toward this? The answer is: “Through effort one can establish oneself in ritual, but music cannot be attained by forcing it. Keep working at it without forgetting, and await its transforming effect: then one will attain it.” Hence the saying: “Music alone cannot be feigned.”

Book of Changes

“The primal power of Qian is that which initiates and brings to fulfillment. Its beneficence and constancy are its inherent nature and disposition. Through its initiating power, Qian benefits all under Heaven with beautiful benefits, without specifying what it benefits. How great it is! Great indeed is Qian! Firm and vigorous, central and correct, pure and unalloyed: it is the quintessence.”

Zhao Xian

Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: “The principles are clear and the language lofty and forceful. It captures the purport of purity, tranquility, subtlety, and profundity.”

Associate Examiner Cheng, Instructor, comments: “The Way of Heaven is generally [?] beyond the ability of those of shallow learning to discuss. This composition explains the processes of creation and transformation as clearly as if pointing to one’s palm. In explaining Heaven, none is more discerning than you.”

Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: “The explanation of the meaning of Qian’s primal power is clear and penetrating.”

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭胡　批〔精㫖不類衆作〕
考試官學正史　批〔簡潔〕
文言中四德之運必極推而贊之也夫四德運
於一元而統之者乾也乾元之大有如此宜文
言有以贊之也且天地之間本一氣之流行而
有動靜耳自其動而言之有所謂元亨也蓋其
由入而出而物之萌其萌者暢茂之莫過元亨
於是乎見矣自其靜而言之又所謂利貞也蓋
其由出而入而物之歸其根者性情之各足利
===
貞於是乎見矣夫四德之流行如此究之豈外
於一元之運哉蓋乾元之妙其始也運亨嘉之
利而萬象維新其旣也斂神化之功而機緘盡
祕是紀綱造化而爲用而終始萬物以成能蓋
有微元無以爲動靜者矣乾之元不其大乎然
一元之貫通固矣統之又豈外於乾道之大哉
蓋乾之爲道不撓不息純乎剛健之至也而不
雜於陰柔不過不偏粹乎中正之極也而弗流
於邪枉且天載泯聲臭之俱無而帝則妙幾微
punctuated:
考試官教諭胡　批〔精㫖不類衆作〕。
考試官學正史　批〔簡潔〕。

文言中四德之運，必極推而贊之也。夫四德運於一元，而統之者乾也。乾元之大有如此，宜文言有以贊之也。且天地之間，本一氣之流行而有動靜耳。自其動而言之，有所謂元亨也。蓋其由入而出，而物之萌其萌者，暢茂之莫過，元亨於是乎見矣。自其靜而言之，又所謂利貞也。蓋其由出而入，而物之歸其根者，性情之各足，利貞於是乎見矣。夫四德之流行如此，究之豈外於一元之運哉？蓋乾元之妙，其始也，運亨嘉之利而萬象維新；其旣也，斂神化之功而機緘盡祕。是紀綱造化而爲用，而終始萬物以成能，蓋有微元無以爲動靜者矣。乾之元不其大乎？然一元之貫通固矣，統之又豈外於乾道之大哉？蓋乾之爲道，不撓不息，純乎剛健之至也，而不雜於陰柔；不過不偏，粹乎中正之極也，而弗流於邪枉。且天載泯聲臭之俱無，而帝則妙幾微
translation_en:
Examiner Hu, an Instructor, comments: 〔Its subtle purport sets it apart from the other compositions.〕
Examiner Shi, a School Instructor, comments: 〔Concise and clear.〕

In the Commentary on the Words of the Text (Wenyan), the operation of the four virtues must be explored to its utmost and praised. For the four virtues operate within a single originating force, and what unifies them is Qian, the Creative. Such is the greatness of Qian’s origination that the Wenyan rightly offers it praise. Between Heaven and Earth there is fundamentally only the circulation of a single vital force, with its movement and stillness. Viewed in terms of its movement, there are what are called origination and flourishing. As it moves from within to without, things put forth their shoots, and nothing surpasses their luxuriant growth: here origination and flourishing become manifest. Viewed in terms of its stillness, there are also what are called benefit and constancy. As it moves from without to within, things return to their roots, each fully endowed with its own nature and dispositions: here benefit and constancy become manifest.

Such is the circulation of the four virtues. In the final analysis, how could it lie outside the operation of the single originating force? The marvel of Qian’s origination is that, at its beginning, it brings into operation the benefits of flourishing excellence, renewing all phenomena; at its completion, it gathers in the achievements of numinous transformation, concealing all the workings of its inner mechanism. Thus it functions by ordering creation and transformation, and fulfills its capacity by bringing all things to their end and beginning. Indeed, without origination there could be neither movement nor stillness [?]. Is not Qian’s origination great?

Yet, granted that the single originating force pervades everything, how could what unifies it lie outside the greatness of the Way of Qian? As a Way, Qian neither yields nor ceases: it is pure in the utmost degree of firmness and vigor, unmixed with yin softness. It neither exceeds the proper measure nor inclines to either side: it is refined to the highest degree of centrality and correctness, never straying into perversity or crookedness. Moreover, Heaven’s workings are altogether without sound or smell, while the Supreme Lord’s rule is wondrous in its subtlest incipiencies…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
於莫測蓋極天下之至精以爲德者矣乾之大
不其至乎夫語乾道而至於精則所以斡一元
之樞而宰四時之運者固有在矣夫子贊乾其
至哉雖然乾天道也亦君道也天以陽生萬物
以陰成之而一元之氣未嘗不流行於其間聖
人以仁育萬民以義正之而好生之意未嘗不
浹洽於其內茲其乘龍御天而成萬國咸寧之
化矣聖人與天合一吾於此尤信
===
是以君子將有爲也將有行也問焉而以
言其受命也如嚮无有遠近幽深遂知
來物非天下之至精其孰能與於此
許經
同考試官教諭劉　批〔說辭占至精無餘歉矣錄之〕
同考試官教諭程　批〔來物遂知即如嚮中事士〕
多不能發明精瑩之作獨于子見之
同考試官教諭朱　批〔講至精處極有精神〕
考試官教諭胡　批〔明順〕
考試官學正史　批〔精思雅作如子可敬〕
punctuated:
於莫測，蓋極天下之至精以爲德者矣。乾之大，不其至乎？夫語乾道而至於精，則所以斡一元之樞而宰四時之運者，固有在矣。夫子贊乾，其至哉！雖然，乾，天道也，亦君道也。天以陽生萬物，以陰成之，而一元之氣未嘗不流行於其間。聖人以仁育萬民，以義正之，而好生之意未嘗不浹洽於其內。茲其乘龍御天而成萬國咸寧之化矣。聖人與天合一，吾於此尤信。

是以君子將有爲也，將有行也，問焉而以言，其受命也如嚮，无有遠近幽深，遂知來物。非天下之至精，其孰能與於此？
許經

同考試官教諭劉，批〔說辭占至精，無餘歉矣，錄之。〕
同考試官教諭程，批〔來物遂知，即如嚮中事，士〕多不能發明，精瑩之作，獨于子見之。
同考試官教諭朱，批〔講至精處，極有精神。〕
考試官教諭胡，批〔明順。〕
考試官學正史，批〔精思雅作，如子可敬。〕
translation_en:
…in what cannot be fathomed. This indeed takes the utmost subtlety under Heaven as its virtue. Is not the greatness of Qian, the Creative, supreme? When discussion of the Way of Qian reaches its subtlety, the basis for turning the pivot of the primal unity and governing the movement of the four seasons is assuredly established. How consummate is the Master's praise of Qian! Yet Qian is the Way of Heaven and also the Way of the ruler. Heaven generates the myriad things through yang and brings them to completion through yin; the vital energy of the primal unity never ceases to circulate among them. The sage nurtures the myriad people through benevolence and rectifies them through righteousness; his intent to cherish life never ceases to permeate them. Thus he rides the dragons and rules Heaven, bringing about the transformation through which the myriad states all enjoy peace. That the sage is one with Heaven—of this I am especially convinced here.

“Thus, when the gentleman is about to undertake something or put something into practice, he questions it in words. Upon receiving his command, it responds like an echo. Whether distant or near, hidden or profound, he thereupon knows what is to come. Were it not the utmost subtlety under Heaven, what could accomplish this?”
Xu Jing 許經

Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: 〔“The exposition of the utmost subtlety of the hexagram statements and divination leaves nothing wanting. Include it.”〕
Associate Examiner Cheng, Instructor, comments: 〔“Knowing at once what is to come is precisely what is involved in responding like an echo. Scholars〕 generally fail to elucidate this. A work of such refinement and clarity I have seen in you alone.”
Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: 〔“The discussion of utmost subtlety is exceptionally spirited.”〕
Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: 〔“Clear and fluent.”〕
Examiner Shi, School Rector, comments: 〔“Refined thought and elegant composition: someone like you merits respect.”〕

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
大傳即辭占感應之妙而決其理之精焉蓋辭
占之理極其精則體無不備矣以是而應天下
之感尚何有不妙也哉夫子推尚辭尚占之事
而贊之也意謂天下之不可窮者事之變也其
所可周者聖人之易也辭占之可尚何哉彼君
子之於事也或欲措諸躬焉或欲行之天下焉
探吉凶於幾先決言行之定向抱蓍問易夫固
其所不能已也易之所以應命也叩之即應酬
酢啓佑神之機感之遂通易貢極知來之妙機
===
動於此神應於彼蓋有應之如嚮不俟夫擬議
之勞者矣且其所以如嚮者事無遠近而得失
之故咸通理無幽深而機微之情畢見問之無
弗知知之無弗速蓋有兼體不遺不倚于一偏
之累者矣若此者非辭占至精之所爲乎蓋天
下之事盡於理而天下之理盡於辭占純粹不
雜蘊之易者既以極天下之至精故神應而妙
達之人者自以通天下之至感如嚮之應應以
此也來物之知知以此也使非至精則亦物焉
punctuated:
大傳即辭占感應之妙而決其理之精焉。蓋辭占之理極其精，則體無不備矣。以是而應天下之感，尚何有不妙也哉？夫子推尚辭尚占之事而贊之也，意謂天下之不可窮者，事之變也；其所可周者，聖人之易也。辭占之可尚何哉？彼君子之於事也，或欲措諸躬焉，或欲行之天下焉，探吉凶於幾先，決言行之定向，抱蓍問易，夫固其所不能已也。

易之所以應命也，叩之即應，酬酢啓佑，神之機；感之遂通，易貢極知來之妙。機動於此，神應於彼，蓋有應之如嚮，不俟夫擬議之勞者矣。且其所以如嚮者，事無遠近而得失之故咸通，理無幽深而機微之情畢見。問之無弗知，知之無弗速，蓋有兼體不遺，不倚于一偏之累者矣。若此者，非辭占至精之所爲乎？

蓋天下之事盡於理，而天下之理盡於辭占。純粹不雜，蘊之易者，既以極天下之至精；故神應而妙，達之人者，自以通天下之至感。如嚮之應，應以此也；來物之知，知以此也。使非至精，則亦物焉
translation_en:
The Great Commentary considers the wondrous workings of stimulus and response in the Changes’ statements and divinations, and thereby establishes the consummate subtlety of their principles. When the principles of statements and divinations attain their utmost refinement, their substance embraces everything. Responding on this basis to all stimuli under Heaven, how could their workings fail to be wondrous? The Master extols the practice of esteeming the statements and esteeming divination. His meaning is that the transformations of affairs under Heaven are inexhaustible, yet the sages’ Changes can encompass them all. Why should its statements and divinations be esteemed? In dealing with affairs, the gentleman may wish to put something into practice himself or to carry it out throughout the realm. To discern good or ill fortune before events begin to emerge, and to determine a settled course for speech and action, he takes up the milfoil stalks and consults the Changes. This is indeed something he cannot forgo.

As for how the Changes responds to a charge put to it: knock, and it immediately answers; through exchange it enlightens and assists—such is the operation of its spiritual efficacy. Stimulate it, and it immediately penetrates: the Changes brings forth to the utmost [?] the wonder of knowing what is to come. An incipient impulse stirs here, and a spiritually efficacious response arises there. Its answer is like an echo, requiring no labor of deliberation. Moreover, its response is like an echo because, whether affairs are distant or near, it comprehends all the causes of success and failure; however hidden and profound the principles, it reveals every subtle circumstance at their inception. Asked, there is nothing it does not know; in knowing, it is never slow. It embraces all aspects without omission and is free of the encumbrance of leaning to one side. Is this not the accomplishment of the consummate refinement of statements and divinations?

All affairs under Heaven are encompassed by principle, and all principles under Heaven are encompassed by statements and divinations. Pure and unmixed, what is stored within the Changes reaches the utmost refinement under Heaven. Thus, spiritually responsive and wondrous, what it communicates to people naturally penetrates the utmost reaches of stimulus under Heaven. Its echo-like response responds by virtue of this; its knowledge of things to come knows by virtue of this. Were it not supremely refined, it too would be merely a thing…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
而已矣安能隨感隨應而極其速哉吁此辭占
所以為天下之至精也以言以卜筮者其可忽
諸雖然亦聖人之精為之也蓋其心靜乎天地
之鑑萬物之鏡也虛而能照應而不藏以是心
而洩之於易故辭占之至精聖人之至精也不
然是亦推測之知而已矣烏能神故曰聖人之
精畫卦以示聖人之藴因卦以發諒哉
書
天叙有典勑我五典五惇哉天秩有禮自
我五禮有庸哉
===
羅許
同考試官教諭蕭　批〔典禮惇庸意剖析精到録之〕
考試官教諭胡　批〔莊重不浮〕
考試官學正史　批〔醞藉典實讀之親切有味〕
大臣言典禮出於天而有相之道存乎君也夫
天之立君以為民也相天道以立民極謂非君
之事哉臯陶陳安民之謨而廸之舜者如此蓋
曰君道以安民為要安民以敎化為先何則自
punctuated:
而已矣，安能隨感隨應而極其速哉？吁！此辭占所以為天下之至精也。以言以卜筮者，其可忽諸？雖然，亦聖人之精為之也。蓋其心靜乎，天地之鑑、萬物之鏡也，虛而能照，應而不藏。以是心而洩之於易，故辭占之至精，聖人之至精也。不然，是亦推測之知而已矣，烏能神？故曰：「聖人之精，畫卦以示；聖人之藴，因卦以發。」諒哉！

書
天叙有典，勑我五典五惇哉！天秩有禮，自我五禮有庸哉！

羅許
同考試官教諭蕭　批〔典禮惇庸意剖析精到録之〕
考試官教諭胡　批〔莊重不浮〕
考試官學正史　批〔醞藉典實讀之親切有味〕

大臣言典禮出於天，而有相之道存乎君也。夫天之立君，以為民也。相天道以立民極，謂非君之事哉？臯陶陳安民之謨，而廸之舜者如此。蓋曰：君道以安民為要，安民以敎化為先。何則？自
translation_en:
…and nothing more. How could it respond to every stimulus with the utmost speed? Ah! This is why the statements and prognostications are the most refined things under Heaven. Can those who consult them for speech or for divination with tortoise shells and milfoil stalks neglect them? Yet this, too, is accomplished by the sage’s refinement. His mind in its stillness is a mirror of Heaven and Earth, a looking glass for the myriad things: empty yet capable of illuminating, responsive yet retaining nothing. He expresses this mind in the Changes; thus the utmost refinement of its statements and prognostications is the utmost refinement of the sage himself. Otherwise, it would merely be knowledge acquired through conjecture. How could it possess spiritual efficacy? Hence the saying: “The sage’s refinement is displayed by drawing the hexagrams; what the sage holds within is brought forth through the hexagrams.” How true!

Book of Documents
“Heaven has established an order expressed in the constant norms; it charges us with the five norms, that all five may be earnestly observed! Heaven has established distinctions expressed in ritual; through us let the five rites be regularly practiced!”

Luo Xu
Associate Examiner Xiao, Instructor, comments: 〔The meaning of earnestly observing the norms and regularly practicing the rites is analyzed with precision and penetration. Selected for inclusion.〕
Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: 〔Dignified and free of superficiality.〕
Examiner Shi, Instructor, comments: 〔Restrained and rich in implication, grounded in the classics and substantial; it reads with an immediacy and savor.〕

The great minister explains that the constant norms and rites originate in Heaven, while the means of assisting their realization rests with the ruler. Heaven establishes rulers for the sake of the people. To assist the Way of Heaven and establish the ultimate standard for the people—could this be anything other than the ruler’s responsibility? Such was the counsel that Gao Yao presented for bringing peace to the people, thereby guiding Shun. His meaning was this: the essential task of rulership is to bring peace to the people, and in bringing peace to the people, instruction and moral transformation come first. Why is this so? From …

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
夫人有五倫而爲萬世不易之經者謂之典是
典也吾見其井然敘矣孰敘之乎恒性本於降
衷而物則俱畀彝倫定於陰隲而相協惟均天
敘之也然天能敘之豈能使民之必惇哉正其
典而俾益厚蓋有賴於君矣是故因性牖民正
其經以還民生之厚緣物作則綏其猷以篤天
性之良凡父子也君臣也夫婦也昆弟朋友也
以天合者以情屬以人合者以義維務使各率
爾典而後君師之責盡其殆相天之敘乎自夫
===
典有等級而爲上下民志之坊者謂之禮是禮
也吾見其森然秩矣孰秩之乎天地設位而乾
坤之分定卑高以陳而貴賤之體明天秩之也
然天能秩之豈能使民之必庸哉用其禮而俾
有常殆有賴於君矣是故立綱陳紀閑之以等
威之辨考度飭憲約之以品式之詳凡父子也
君臣也夫婦也兄弟朋友也貴而尊者其體隆
賤而卑者其體殺務使各遵其常而後軌物之
道盡其殆相天之秩乎夫典禮自天人道之所
punctuated: 夫人有五倫，而爲萬世不易之經者，謂之典。是典也，吾見其井然敘矣。孰敘之乎？恒性本於降衷，而物則俱畀；彝倫定於陰隲，而相協惟均。天敘之也。然天能敘之，豈能使民之必惇哉？正其典而俾益厚，蓋有賴於君矣。是故因性牖民，正其經以還民生之厚；緣物作則，綏其猷以篤天性之良。凡父子也，君臣也，夫婦也，昆弟朋友也，以天合者以情屬，以人合者以義維，務使各率爾典，而後君師之責盡。其殆相天之敘乎？自夫典有等級，而爲上下民志之坊者，謂之禮。是禮也，吾見其森然秩矣。孰秩之乎？天地設位，而乾坤之分定；卑高以陳，而貴賤之體明。天秩之也。然天能秩之，豈能使民之必庸哉？用其禮而俾有常，殆有賴於君矣。是故立綱陳紀，閑之以等威之辨；考度飭憲，約之以品式之詳。凡父子也，君臣也，夫婦也，兄弟朋友也，貴而尊者其體隆，賤而卑者其體殺，務使各遵其常，而後軌物之道盡。其殆相天之秩乎？夫典禮自天，人道之所
translation_en:
…The five human relationships, as unchanging norms for all generations, are called the constant principles. I see these principles arranged in perfect order. Who arranged them? The enduring human nature originates in the upright disposition bestowed by Heaven, and the standards for all things are bestowed along with it; the constant relationships are established through Heaven’s unseen ordering, and their mutual harmony is perfectly balanced. Heaven has ordered them. Yet although Heaven can order them, can it ensure that the people invariably cultivate them wholeheartedly? To rectify these principles and cause their practice to become ever more substantial surely depends upon the ruler. Thus, following human nature, he enlightens the people, rectifying their norms to restore integrity to human life; taking things as his basis, he establishes standards, setting their proper courses in order to strengthen the goodness of their Heaven-given nature. In the relationships between father and son, ruler and minister, husband and wife, elder and younger brothers, and friends, those joined by Heaven are bound by affection, while those joined through human association are held together by righteousness. He must ensure that all follow these principles; only then does he fully discharge his responsibility as ruler and teacher. Is this not surely to assist Heaven’s ordering?

Where the constant principles have gradations and serve as restraints upon the aspirations of people above and below, they are called rites. I see these rites arrayed in a strict hierarchy. Who established that hierarchy? Heaven and earth take their positions, and the distinction between Qian and Kun is fixed; low and high are set forth, and the forms distinguishing noble and base become clear. Heaven has ranked them. Yet although Heaven can rank them, can it ensure that the people invariably practice them? To put these rites into use and give them constancy surely depends upon the ruler. Thus he establishes guiding principles and sets out regulations, restraining the people through distinctions of rank and dignity; he examines standards and sets ordinances in order, regulating the people through detailed grades and prescribed forms. In the relationships between father and son, ruler and minister, husband and wife, elder and younger brothers, and friends, the ceremonial forms for those of noble and honored station are more elaborate, while those for people of low and humble station are reduced. He must ensure that all observe their enduring rules; only then is the way of regulating human conduct fully realized. Is this not surely to assist Heaven’s ranking? The constant principles and rites come from Heaven and are that through which the human way…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
由立也惇庸由君天道之所由成也安民莫先
於教化如此人君其圖之哉大抵天地設位聖
人成能不以可憂同其無憂者有相之道存焉
相與之際固有相成者在是故以神宰御則格
天有勳以妙參贊則配天有道皐陶斯言不惟
啓萬世性道之源而且求端於天謂非觀其深
識其大乎雖然惇典庸禮德教不可尚已至於
不率教者則又明刑以弼之卒使民協中焉然
則皐陶其亦有功於典禮也夫
道洽政治澤潤生民四夷左衽罔不咸賴
王汝會
同考試官教諭蕭　批〔道洽政治四字作者類皆浮漫無據此篇認理精切脩詞雄健錄之〕
考試官教諭胡　批〔得康王期待畢公本意〕
考試官學正史　批〔說成周化殷功效處有氣象有思致〕
===
賢王期大臣治功之成而因大其效焉夫化被
中國而施及四夷治效可謂大矣然非三后治
punctuated:
由立也，惇庸由君，天道之所由成也。安民莫先於教化，如此，人君其圖之哉！大抵天地設位，聖人成能，不以可憂同其無憂者，有相之道存焉。相與之際，固有相成者在。是故以神宰御，則格天有勳；以妙參贊，則配天有道。皐陶斯言，不惟啓萬世性道之源，而且求端於天，謂非觀其深、識其大乎？雖然，惇典庸禮，德教不可尚已；至於不率教者，則又明刑以弼之，卒使民協中焉。然則皐陶其亦有功於典禮也夫！

道洽政治，澤潤生民，四夷左衽，罔不咸賴。
王汝會
