考試官教諭胡　批〔得康王期待畢公本意。〕
考試官學正史　批〔說成周化殷功效處，有氣象，有思致。〕

賢王期大臣治功之成，而因大其效焉。夫化被中國，而施及四夷，治效可謂大矣。然非三后治
translation_en:
…are the means by which the human order is established. Making these norms substantial and putting these rites into practice depend upon the ruler: through these actions the Way of Heaven is brought to completion. Nothing takes precedence over moral instruction in bringing peace to the people. This being so, should not the ruler give it careful thought? In general, Heaven and Earth establish their positions, and the sage brings their capacities to fulfillment. He does not treat matters that warrant concern as though they were as free from concern as Heaven and Earth, for there remains a way of assisting them. In this relationship of assistance and bestowal, each indeed contributes to the other's fulfillment. Thus, through numinous governance, he achieves the merit of reaching Heaven; through subtle participation and assistance, he possesses the way to match Heaven. These words of Gao Yao not only disclose for all ages the source of human nature and the Way, but also trace their beginnings to Heaven. Can one deny that he perceived their depths and understood their greatness? Nevertheless, in making the norms substantial and putting the rites into practice, nothing can surpass moral instruction. As for those who do not follow that instruction, he further makes punishments clear to reinforce it, ultimately bringing the people into accord with the mean. Thus Gao Yao, too, surely rendered service to the norms and rites!

“The Way pervades, government is well ordered, and beneficence enriches the lives of the people. Even the barbarians of the four quarters, whose robes fasten on the left, all depend upon it.”
Wang Ruhui
Associate Examiner Xiao, Instructor, comments: 〔In treating the four characters ‘the Way pervades, government is well ordered,’ writers are generally vague, diffuse, and without foundation. This essay grasps the principles precisely and incisively, and its composition is vigorous and forceful. Selected for inclusion.〕
Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: 〔It captures King Kang's original intent in expressing his expectations of the Duke of Bi.〕
Examiner Shi, School Director, comments: 〔The passage explaining the achievements of Chengzhou in transforming the people of Yin has grandeur and thoughtful depth.〕

A worthy king anticipates the completion of a great minister's work of governance and accordingly magnifies its effects. When transforming influence covers the central lands and extends to the barbarians of the four quarters, the effects of governance may indeed be called great. Yet without the three sovereigns' work of governance…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
功之成何以致之昔康王命畢公保釐東郊而
預期之若曰天下之治本於道天下之道本於
心三后之相繼心同而道亦同矣要其功效之
成何如自夫心思之運顯而爲經世之猷者謂
之道道固未易洽也玆焉仁義並施而感之者
久剛柔交濟而入之者深凡因時致治以立化
殷之本者罔不融液流通而無有間隔者矣自
其變通之權推而爲宜民之法者謂之政政固
未易治也玆焉樞機周密而大綱之克舉品式
===
咸備而萬目之畢張凡謹始成終以爲化殷之
具者罔不明作敦大而無有叢脞者矣治功不
亦成乎由是近而殷民號稱難治也今則道久
而化以成德施而惠自溥率由訓典沐浴於膏
澤之中會歸皇極涵泳乎泰和之化有淑之可
旌也無慝之可別也蓋有優沃乎江河之潤而
均霑乎雨露之恩者矣尚安有凌德滅義而不
蒙至治之澤者乎遠而四夷左衽固難於遍及
也今則內治脩而遠人自服邦本固而外患不
punctuated: 功之成，何以致之？昔康王命畢公保釐東郊，而預期之若曰：「天下之治本於道，天下之道本於心。三后之相繼，心同而道亦同矣。要其功效之成何如？自夫心思之運，顯而爲經世之猷者謂之道，道固未易洽也。玆焉仁義並施，而感之者久；剛柔交濟，而入之者深。凡因時致治以立化殷之本者，罔不融液流通而無有間隔者矣。自其變通之權，推而爲宜民之法者謂之政，政固未易治也。玆焉樞機周密，而大綱之克舉；品式咸備，而萬目之畢張。凡謹始成終以爲化殷之具者，罔不明作敦大而無有叢脞者矣。治功不亦成乎？由是近而殷民，號稱難治也，今則道久而化以成，德施而惠自溥。率由訓典，沐浴於膏澤之中；會歸皇極，涵泳乎泰和之化。有淑之可旌也，無慝之可別也。蓋有優沃乎江河之潤，而均霑乎雨露之恩者矣。尚安有凌德滅義而不蒙至治之澤者乎？遠而四夷左衽，固難於遍及也，今則內治脩而遠人自服，邦本固而外患不
translation_en:
…the accomplishment of their work of government, how could this have been achieved? Formerly, when King Kang commanded Bi Gong to safeguard and administer the eastern suburbs, he expressed his expectations as though saying: “Order throughout the realm is rooted in the Way, and the Way throughout the realm is rooted in the heart. The three successive sovereigns shared one heart and likewise one Way. What, then, would the full accomplishment of their work be like?

“The workings of thought, manifested as plans for ordering the world, are called the Way. The Way is certainly not easily made all-pervading. Here, benevolence and righteousness are exercised together, exerting their influence over a long period; firmness and gentleness complement each other, penetrating deeply. All measures that establish order in accordance with the times, laying the foundation for transforming the people of Yin, thus flow freely and blend together without obstruction. The discretionary judgment that adapts to changing circumstances, extended into methods suited to the people, is called administration. Administration is certainly not easily brought into good order. Here, the central mechanisms are thorough and precise, allowing the main guiding principles to be upheld; standards and regulations are fully provided, allowing every detail to be put into place. All measures that attend carefully to the beginning and bring the undertaking to completion, serving as instruments for transforming Yin, are thus carried out intelligently, earnestly, and generously, without petty fussiness. Is this not the accomplishment of the work of government?

“Consequently, nearby are the people of Yin, reputed to be difficult to govern. Now, however, the Way has endured and their transformation has been accomplished; virtue has been exercised and its benefits naturally spread widely. Following the canonical instructions, they bathe in abundant beneficence; converging upon the sovereign’s ultimate standard, they are immersed in the transforming influence of supreme harmony. There is goodness to commend, and no wickedness to single out. They are amply nourished as by the moisture of rivers, and share equally in kindness like rain and dew. How could there still be anyone who violates virtue and destroys righteousness, failing to receive the blessings of perfect government?

“In distant regions, the peoples of the four quarters, who fasten their robes on the left, are certainly difficult to reach universally. Now, however, internal government is well ordered and distant peoples submit of their own accord; the foundations of the state are secure, and external troubles do not…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
作引領遐荒仰一王之聲教竝生天地耕中土
之□□□□來享也莫敢不來王也蓋有以
徼懷柔之□□□□之及者矣尚安有干紀
猾夏而自外於覆載之內者乎是則三后治功
之成而化協於遠邇如此然非畢公保釐之政
則亦無以保終吉矣成終之責將安所諉哉抑
於是而知周之至仁享國之所以永也夫以屢
迪不靜之民舒徐容與遲之以三世之久至望
畢公之成終猶以潤澤咸賴爲言有若弗克轉
===
移之者其化之何其漸而望之何其厚乎夫化
之久則入之深入之深則其去之也自難此其
所以衍而爲八百之曆也康王其賢矣哉
詩
蒹葭𦍌兮三英粲兮彼其之子邦之彥兮
陳加命
同考試官教諭吳　批　〔體貼精到文亦粲然此詩　善擬大夫之美子又善擬詩人之言者佳士佳士〕
同考試官教諭何　批　〔講邦彥處不俗不□弟作〕
punctuated:
作。引領遐荒，仰一王之聲教；竝生天地，耕中土之□□□□來享也，莫敢不來王也。蓋有以徼懷柔之□□□□之及者矣，尚安有干紀猾夏而自外於覆載之內者乎？是則三后治功之成，而化協於遠邇如此。然非畢公保釐之政，則亦無以保終吉矣。成終之責，將安所諉哉？抑於是而知周之至仁，享國之所以永也。夫以屢迪不靜之民，舒徐容與，遲之以三世之久，至望畢公之成終，猶以潤澤咸賴爲言，有若弗克轉移之者。其化之何其漸，而望之何其厚乎！夫化之久，則入之深；入之深，則其去之也自難。此其所以衍而爲八百之曆也。康王其賢矣哉！

詩
蒹葭𦍌兮，三英粲兮，彼其之子，邦之彥兮。
陳加命

同考試官教諭吳，批：〔體貼精到，文亦粲然。此詩，善擬大夫之美子，又善擬詩人之言者。佳士！佳士！〕

同考試官教諭何，批：〔講邦彥處不俗，不□弟作〕
translation_en:
…arise. In the distant wilds, people crane their necks, looking up to the civilizing influence of the one king. Living together beneath Heaven and upon Earth, they cultivate the lands of the central realm [four illegible characters] and come to present offerings; none dares fail to acknowledge the king. They have thus received the benefits of his conciliatory rule [four illegible characters; syntax uncertain]. How could any still violate the established order, trouble the Chinese realm, and exclude themselves from all that Heaven covers and Earth sustains? Such were the accomplishments of the three sovereigns in government, and such was the harmony their transforming influence brought to those far and near. Yet without the Duke of Bi’s administration to safeguard and order the realm, there would have been no means of ensuring an auspicious conclusion. To whom, then, could the responsibility for completing this work be shifted?

From this we also understand Zhou’s consummate benevolence and why its possession of the realm endured so long. With a people who had repeatedly behaved restlessly, it proceeded gently and unhurriedly, allowing them as long as three generations. Even when looking to the Duke of Bi to complete the work, the king still spoke of the beneficent influence upon which all depended, as though he might yet be unable to transform them. How gradual was this transformation, and how generous his expectations! When transforming influence operates for a long time, it penetrates deeply; once it has penetrated deeply, people naturally find it difficult to abandon. This is why Zhou’s allotted span extended to eight hundred years. How worthy King Kang was!

The Book of Odes
“The reeds and rushes are [𦍌: unclear; wording doubtful];
The three ornaments shine brightly.
That man there
Is an outstanding man of the state.”
Chen Jiaming

Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor, comments: “The interpretation is sensitive and precise, and the writing, too, is brilliant. In treating this ode, he skillfully captures the excellence of the grand officer [?] and also skillfully captures the poet’s words. A fine scholar! A fine scholar!”

Associate Examiner He, Instructor, comments: “The discussion of ‘an outstanding man of the state’ is far from commonplace; [remaining wording garbled: 不□弟作] …”

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
漫然以爲文者宜錄以式多士
考試官教諭胡　批〔理既精切文亦雅飭其善〕
說詩者
考試官學正史　批〔精緻〕
詩人有取於大夫必即服以表其人之美焉蓋
人之美無所見稱其服者象其人也詩人之於
大夫如此亦善於形容者哉想其意及此若謂
有君子之服者不在承之以君子之名而貴將
之以君子之德我觀大夫取適燕閒而製彼羔
裘安節之貞非過也但見其晏然鮮盛殆于如
===
濡而增美焉備其物采而尚以三英等威之辨
以昭也但見其粲然光明視諸豹飾而益著焉
夫是固足以華君子之躬而彰有位之儀矣然
大夫孰不服此而何之子之可美耶蓋其三德
日宣而章美之內含者不愧於浚明之良一忠
自效而英華之外發者無忝於亮采之佐自夫
順命以居身則成仁取義而光大之行赫然炳
朗以完名由之而羽儀一方庶幾乎虎變以爲
punctuated:
漫然以爲文者，宜錄以式多士。
考試官教諭胡　批〔理既精切，文亦雅飭，其善〕說詩者。
考試官學正史　批〔精緻〕。
詩人有取於大夫，必即服以表其人之美焉。蓋人之美無所見，稱其服者，象其人也。詩人之於大夫如此，亦善於形容者哉！想其意及此，若謂有君子之服者，不在承之以君子之名，而貴將之以君子之德。我觀大夫取適燕閒，而製彼羔裘，安節之貞，非過也。但見其晏然鮮盛，殆于如濡而增美焉。備其物采，而尚以三英，等威之辨以昭也。但見其粲然光明，視諸豹飾而益著焉。夫是固足以華君子之躬，而彰有位之儀矣。然大夫孰不服此，而何之子之可美耶？蓋其三德日宣，而章美之內含者，不愧於浚明之良；一忠自效，而英華之外發者，無忝於亮采之佐。自夫順命以居身，則成仁取義，而光大之行赫然炳朗，以完名由之而羽儀一方，庶幾乎虎變以爲
translation_en:
…one who composes carelessly [?]. This deserves to be recorded as a model for the many candidates.
Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: 〔“The reasoning is precise and pertinent, and the writing elegant and disciplined. He is skilled”〕 at expounding the Odes.
Examiner Shi, School Instructor, comments: 〔“Exquisite.”〕
When the poet finds something to commend in a great officer, he invariably uses the officer’s clothing to express the excellence of the man. Since a person’s excellence has no visible form, praising his clothing represents the man himself. In treating the great officer thus, how skillfully the poet portrays him! Imagining his intention here, it is as though he were saying: possessing a gentleman’s clothing is not a matter of assuming a gentleman’s name; what matters is accompanying it with a gentleman’s virtue. I observe the great officer seeking comfort in his leisure and having that lambskin robe made: this does not exceed the bounds of steadfast adherence to proper measure. We see only its composed and splendid appearance, almost glistening as though moist, which enhances its beauty. Its prescribed materials and ornamentation are complete, and it is further adorned with three embellishments, thereby making distinctions of rank manifest. We see only their brilliant radiance, rendered still more conspicuous beside the leopard-skin trimming.
These things certainly suffice to adorn a gentleman’s person and display the dignity of one who holds office. Yet what great officer does not wear such clothing? Why, then, is this particular man worthy of praise? It is because his three virtues become manifest day by day: the excellence held within him befits a worthy man of profound discernment. His undivided loyalty proves itself in service: the brilliance expressed outwardly brings no dishonor upon an assistant who faithfully discharges his duties. Through conducting himself in obedience to what is commanded, he fulfills humaneness and chooses righteousness; his illustrious conduct shines forth brilliantly. Thereby preserving an untarnished name [?], he becomes an exemplar for an entire region, approaching that transformation whose markings shine like a tiger’s, so as to become…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
□者矣斯人也不將與羔裘而俱長乎自夫國
朝以事上則持公秉正而俊偉之業蔫然朝野
而出色山之而文明一國庶幾乎能光以爲德
者矣斯人也不將與三英而並粲乎即是而知
有服以養德則德爲益著服固不可已也有德
以充服則服爲益美德尤不可已也詩人極美
於鄭之大夫其意不可想見哉抑考鄭在春秋
若子良子太叔之諸國子皮子產之爲政皆能
竭盡忠赤侃侃不回而國祚頼以爲安者詩人
之所詠豈其人乎或者又疑此詩爲緇衣之遺
而謂仍取於桓武也噫允若茲鄭之良不亦修
乎故以若人用以維風宜無不可乃時猶有不
脩德隅如子臧之鷸冠坐取不衷之誚也豈諸
良無所與耶吾於是乎有感
自今以始歲其有君子有穀詒孫子
劉黃裳
同考試官教諭吳 批 是作體裁整齊文詞典雅
而意趣尤爲新奇非得詩人之旨者也尚爲允宜
punctuated:
□者矣。斯人也，不將與羔裘而俱長乎？自夫國朝以事上，則持公秉正，而俊偉之業蔫然朝野，而出色山之，而文明一國，庶幾乎能光以爲德者矣。斯人也，不將與三英而並粲乎？即是而知，有服以養德，則德爲益著，服固不可已也；有德以充服，則服爲益美，德尤不可已也。詩人極美於鄭之大夫，其意不可想見哉？抑考鄭在春秋，若子良、子太叔之諸國，子皮、子產之爲政，皆能竭盡忠赤，侃侃不回，而國祚頼以爲安者，詩人之所詠，豈其人乎？或者又疑此詩爲《緇衣》之遺，而謂仍取於桓、武也。噫！允若茲，鄭之良不亦修乎？故以若人用以維風，宜無不可。乃時猶有不脩德隅，如子臧之鷸冠，坐取不衷之誚也，豈諸良無所與耶？吾於是乎有感。
自今以始，歲其有！君子有穀，詒孫子。
劉黃裳
同考試官教諭吳批：是作體裁整齊，文詞典雅，而意趣尤爲新奇。非得詩人之旨者也，尚爲允宜。
translation_en:
…one who □. Will such a man not endure together with his lambskin robe? In serving his sovereign at the state court, he upholds impartiality and rectitude; his outstanding achievements shine throughout court and country [?], distinguishing him [?] and bringing cultured brilliance to the whole state. He approaches the ideal of one whose virtue gives forth light. Will such a man not shine alongside the three ornaments of his robe? From this we know that, when ceremonial dress nurtures virtue, virtue becomes more manifest: dress certainly cannot be dispensed with. When virtue gives substance to dress, dress becomes more splendid: virtue is still more indispensable. Can we not imagine the intention behind the poet’s unstinting praise of the great officers of Zheng?
Now, examining Zheng during the Spring and Autumn period, we find Ziliang and Zitaishu in their dealings with the states [?], and Zipi and Zichan in their conduct of government. All exhausted their loyal devotion, remaining upright and unbending; upon them depended the security of the state’s fortunes. Could these have been the men whom the poet celebrated? Others suspect that this poem preserves the legacy of “Black Robes” (Zi yi), and maintain that it likewise takes Dukes Huan and Wu as its subjects. Ah! If this is indeed so, how cultivated were Zheng’s worthy men! Employing such men to uphold proper customs should surely have served in every respect. Yet even then there were those who failed to cultivate moral integrity, such as Zizang, whose kingfisher-feather cap brought upon him the reproach of impropriety. Could all those worthy men have had no influence upon him? This gives me cause for reflection.
“From this time onward, may the years yield abundance! May the lord possess goodness and bequeath it to his descendants.”
Liu Huangshang
Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: This composition is orderly in structure and refined in diction, while its conception is especially fresh and original. It does not grasp the poet’s intent, yet remains fitting and appropriate [?].

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭何　批〔詞旨作者多以子孫維持言然非本旨了獨此作曾君身上說出足足川錄之〕
考試官教諭胡　批〔足當時祝頌之意可以式矣〕
考試官學正史　批〔詞婉意足〕
魯人愛君之情在於足國裕後而已矣蓋年豐
則國足善詒則後裕也兼而有之夫非斂福之
極與魯人以是願君而忠愛之情見於辭矣且
君者以安民爲心而又以善後爲悅者也吾人
===
承君之燕何以致望於君哉亦曰國依於民民
依於食年必貴於順成固也我魯慨自歲事告
侵夫固觖望於食矣安得自今伊始天心仁愛
以其庇吾君者推以及吾民雨暘順若而三時
不愆螟螣斂息而百穀用實不獨一歲爲然也
且由稔而登而大熟焉自天降康而樂歲爲之
頻仍由登而成而大有焉將受厥明而豐穰爲
之無已至如不雨而書無麥而書者固無慮也
夫然則粒食之源不竭以充國用以蓄民生相
punctuated:
同考試官教諭何，批〔詞旨，作者多以子孫維持言，然非本旨了。獨此作曾君身上說出，足足川錄之。〕
考試官教諭胡，批〔足當時祝頌之意，可以式矣。〕
考試官學正史，批〔詞婉意足。〕
魯人愛君之情，在於足國裕後而已矣。蓋年豐則國足，善詒則後裕也。兼而有之，夫非斂福之極與？魯人以是願君，而忠愛之情見於辭矣。且君者，以安民爲心，而又以善後爲悅者也。吾人承君之燕，何以致望於君哉？亦曰：國依於民，民依於食，年必貴於順成，固也。我魯慨自歲事告侵，夫固觖望於食矣。安得自今伊始，天心仁愛，以其庇吾君者推以及吾民，雨暘順若而三時不愆，螟螣斂息而百穀用實。不獨一歲爲然也，且由稔而登而大熟焉，自天降康而樂歲爲之頻仍；由登而成而大有焉，將受厥明而豐穰爲之無已。至如不雨而書、無麥而書者，固無慮也。夫然則粒食之源不竭，以充國用，以蓄民生，相
translation_en:
Associate Examiner He, Instructor, comments: 〔As for the meaning of the verse, most writers discuss its preservation by sons and grandsons, but this is not its original purport [?]. This composition alone develops the point with reference to the ruler himself [?]; it fully merits inclusion [?].〕
Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: 〔It fully expresses the intention of the blessings and praises offered at that time and may serve as a model.〕
Examiner Shi, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔The language is graceful and the meaning fully expressed.〕
The affection of the people of Lu for their ruler lay simply in wishing to make the state prosperous and provide abundantly for later generations. For plentiful harvests bring prosperity to the state, and a good legacy brings abundance to posterity. To possess both—is this not the utmost in gathering blessings? The people of Lu wished these things for their ruler, and their loyal affection appeared in their words. Moreover, a ruler takes the people's security to heart and finds pleasure in making good provision for those who come after him. As we receive our ruler's hospitality at his banquet, how should we express our hopes for him? We say: the state depends upon the people, and the people depend upon food. That the year should be valued for its orderly progress toward a successful harvest is surely right. Ever since our Lu suffered a poor harvest, we have lamented it and felt keen anxiety over food. How might we obtain, from this time onward, Heaven's benevolent care, extending its protection of our ruler to our people, so that rain and sunshine come in due season, the three seasons of cultivation suffer no disruption, grain pests subside, and all the grains bear abundantly? Nor should this hold for just one year. May ripening lead to a good harvest and then to a great harvest, with Heaven sending down well-being and years of plenty recurring frequently; may a good harvest lead to full fruition and then to great abundance, so that we receive Heaven's bright blessing and enjoy plentiful crops without end. As for occasions recorded as having no rain or no wheat, there would assuredly be no need to fear them. Then the source of grain for food would never be exhausted, supplying the state's needs and sustaining the people's livelihood, so that they might mutually …

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
依以爲安者不自此其永賴耶吾人所望於君
者固如此不寧維是彼祚保於偂偂保於賢善
必貴於相延固也我魯慨自人往政息道固待
人而行矣安得君子有穀取其承於前者庸以
垂於後或繹思禮教而脩飾以衍其傳或推本
信義而敦崇以復其舊不徒自善其身也由之
而詒厥孫謀凡勸學興禮以順彼長道者期於
自我而作則由之而式穀爾子凡明德慎儀以
昭格烈祖者必使咸正而無缺諸如禮詭於周
===
教詭於魯者罔匪後也大然則敬承之賢可啓
以遵成憲以保侯封克承於先世者不自此其
永托耶吾人所望於君者又如此要而言之年
不徒豐也必有所以兆之之機善不易傳也必
有所以闡之之要魯人頌禱之誠雖殷而意亦
端有在矣何者君所以格天也敬所以聚德也
故豐不豐天也而天不可必善不善人也而敬
宜自勉若能以人合天以敬作所則世守一德
而祈天之本立一機相感而豐年之應隨矣此
punctuated:
依以爲安者，不自此其永賴耶？吾人所望於君者固如此。不寧維是，彼祚保於偂，偂保於賢，善必貴於相延，固也。我魯慨自人往政息，道固待人而行矣。安得君子有穀，取其承於前者，庸以垂於後？或繹思禮教而脩飾，以衍其傳；或推本信義而敦崇，以復其舊。不徒自善其身也，由之而詒厥孫謀，凡勸學興禮以順彼長道者，期於自我而作則；由之而式穀爾子，凡明德慎儀以昭格烈祖者，必使咸正而無缺。諸如禮詭於周、教詭於魯者，罔匪後也。大然則敬承之賢可啓，以遵成憲，以保侯封，克承於先世者，不自此其永托耶？吾人所望於君者又如此。

要而言之，年不徒豐也，必有所以兆之之機；善不易傳也，必有所以闡之之要。魯人頌禱之誠雖殷，而意亦端有在矣。何者？君所以格天也，敬所以聚德也。故豐不豐，天也，而天不可必；善不善，人也，而敬宜自勉。若能以人合天，以敬作所，則世守一德，而祈天之本立；一機相感，而豐年之應隨矣。此
translation_en:
…those who depend upon one another for security: would they not thereby gain an enduring source of support? Such indeed is what we hope for from our ruler. Nor is this all. Blessings are preserved through predecessors, and predecessors are preserved through worthy men [?]; goodness must assuredly be valued for its continuation from generation to generation. We in Lu lament that, when the men departed, their government ceased: the Way indeed depends upon men to put it into practice. How might we obtain a gentleman endowed with goodness, who would take what he inherited from those before him and hand it down to those after him? He might ponder ritual instruction and cultivate and refine it, extending its transmission; or trace things back to trustworthiness and righteousness and earnestly honor them, restoring their former condition. He would not merely perfect his own conduct. Through this he would bequeath plans for his descendants: in all that encourages learning and promotes ritual, following that enduring Way, he would aspire to establish the example himself. Through this he would guide his sons toward goodness: in all that makes virtue illustrious and conduct circumspect, thereby reaching the glorious ancestors, he would ensure that everything was correct and nothing deficient. Such things as ritual departing from Zhou’s standards and instruction departing from Lu’s are all the work of later generations. Then [?] worthy successors who reverently carry on the inheritance could be nurtured, to observe the established statutes and preserve the marquis’s fief. Would not what had been successfully inherited from earlier generations thereby find an enduring trust? This too is what we hope for from our ruler.

To state the essentials: harvests do not become abundant without cause; there must be an incipient force that foreshadows them. Goodness is not easily transmitted; there must be an essential means of bringing it to full expression. Although the people of Lu were fervently sincere in their praise and prayers, their words also had a definite purpose. Why? The ruler is the means of reaching Heaven; reverence is the means of accumulating virtue. Thus, whether harvests are abundant rests with Heaven, and Heaven cannot be counted upon with certainty. Whether conduct is good rests with human beings, and in reverence one should exert oneself. If one can bring human conduct into accord with Heaven and make reverence one’s abiding place, then successive generations will preserve a single virtue, establishing the foundation for praying to Heaven. Through the mutual response of a single moving impulse, abundant harvests will follow as the answering sign. This…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
魯人美不忘規猶足以續卷阿洞酌之音者說
者槩謂其詞誇噫殆亦未之深省與
春秋
秋齊侯宋公江人黄人會于陽穀〔僖公三年〕
王家卿
同考試官教諭吳　批〔齊桓攘楚之謀作者多恢張之其意殊淺此篇辭不費而意足錄之〕
考試官教諭胡　批〔簡明〕
考試官學正史　批〔得聖人予齊桓意〕
===
春秋于伯主之講好而深善其得攘外之謀也
夫制敵莫先於謀也陽穀會而攘楚之謀定矣
獨非春秋之所善乎齊桓主伯志在安攘合諸
侯以謀楚是以爲陽穀之會也春秋善之者何
蓋伯者之匡天下也固在於兵之强而其用兵
也猶在於謀之善使桓舉兵而無謀焉其能得
志于楚乎幸而有見于此以師非厚集不足以
威敵也戒兹八國陳兵以震吾之威焉聚而爲
punctuated:
魯人美不忘規，猶足以續《卷阿》《洞酌》之音者，說者槩謂其詞誇，噫！殆亦未之深省與！

春秋
秋，齊侯、宋公、江人、黄人會于陽穀。〔僖公三年〕
王家卿
同考試官教諭吳　批〔齊桓攘楚之謀，作者多恢張之，其意殊淺。此篇辭不費而意足，錄之。〕
考試官教諭胡　批〔簡明。〕
考試官學正史　批〔得聖人予齊桓意。〕

春秋于伯主之講好，而深善其得攘外之謀也。夫制敵莫先於謀也，陽穀會而攘楚之謀定矣，獨非春秋之所善乎？齊桓主伯，志在安攘，合諸侯以謀楚，是以爲陽穀之會也。春秋善之者何？蓋伯者之匡天下也，固在於兵之强，而其用兵也，猶在於謀之善。使桓舉兵而無謀焉，其能得志于楚乎？幸而有見于此，以師非厚集不足以威敵也，戒兹八國，陳兵以震吾之威焉，聚而爲
translation_en:
…The people of Lu, in praising, did not forget to admonish; their words were thus worthy of continuing the strains of “Winding Slopes” (Juan a) and “Deep Pouring” (Dong zhuo [?], probably “Pouring Water from Afar,” Jiong zhuo). Yet commentators generally call their language exaggerated. Alas! Perhaps they have not reflected deeply upon it!

Spring and Autumn Annals
“In autumn, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, and representatives of Jiang and Huang met at Yanggu.” 〔Third year of Duke Xi.〕
By Wang Jiaqing.
Associate Examiner Wu, an Instructor, comments: 〔Most writers elaborate extravagantly upon Duke Huan of Qi’s plan to repel Chu, but their interpretations are decidedly shallow. This essay expresses its meaning fully without wasting words. Include it.〕
Examiner Hu, an Instructor, comments: 〔Concise and clear.〕
Examiner Shi, a School Instructor, comments: 〔Captures the sage’s intention in approving Duke Huan of Qi.〕

In recording the hegemon’s cultivation of friendly relations, the Spring and Autumn Annals deeply approves his devising a plan to repel external threats. In overcoming an enemy, nothing takes precedence over planning. At the meeting at Yanggu, the plan to repel Chu was settled. Was this not precisely what the Spring and Autumn Annals approved? Duke Huan of Qi assumed leadership as hegemon, intent upon securing peace within and repelling threats from without. He assembled the feudal lords to make plans against Chu; this was the reason for the meeting at Yanggu. Why does the Spring and Autumn Annals approve it? A hegemon’s ordering of the realm certainly depends upon military strength, but his employment of troops depends in turn upon sound planning. Had Duke Huan raised an army without a plan, could he have achieved his purpose against Chu? Fortunately, he understood this. Judging that troops could not overawe the enemy unless assembled in strength, he alerted these eight states and arrayed their troops to display the might of his side. title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
正可以聲楚人之罪也兵無外應非所以濟緩□
也諭彼江黃按兵以爲吾之援焉分而爲奇可□
以擬楚人之後也固不待陘亭之次楚師之震
恐也先事以爲圖桓也籌之素矣勍敵之楚有
出于桓之謀哉固不必召陵之盟屈完之輸款
也慮勝而後會桓也計之久矣萬全之策何有
于楚之兵哉聖人以攘夷安夏伯者事也而況
好謀而成者乎是會也震中夏之威抑外夷之
橫世道之大幸也故諸侯皆在而末言者善是
===
謀也抑桓之茲謀豈一朝之可能哉貫澤之盟
江黃已結楚之黨孤而我之勢盛其所以爲楚
計者不可謂無備而猶事于陽穀之會蓋慮楚
之强而念之勤矣終焉弗怠王道可幾也何楚
人已服而其志遂驕侵陳之兵已非而視黃之
患弗救豈伯主之職哉是故聖人深善攘楚之
謀所以大尊王之義而紀伐黃之師猶欲其敦
不息之誠也
宋師伐陳衛人救陳〔宣公十有二年夏楚〕
punctuated:
正，可以聲楚人之罪也。兵無外應，非所以濟緩□也。諭彼江黃，按兵以爲吾之援焉；分而爲奇，可□以擬楚人之後也。固不待陘亭之次，楚師之震恐也。先事以爲圖，桓也籌之素矣，勍敵之楚有出于桓之謀哉？固不必召陵之盟，屈完之輸款也。慮勝而後會，桓也計之久矣，萬全之策何有于楚之兵哉？聖人以攘夷安夏，伯者事也，而況好謀而成者乎？是會也，震中夏之威，抑外夷之橫，世道之大幸也。故諸侯皆在而末言者，善是謀也。抑桓之茲謀，豈一朝之可能哉？貫澤之盟，江黃已結，楚之黨孤，而我之勢盛。其所以爲楚計者，不可謂無備，而猶事于陽穀之會，蓋慮楚之强而念之勤矣。終焉弗怠，王道可幾也。何楚人已服，而其志遂驕？侵陳之兵已非，而視黃之患弗救，豈伯主之職哉？是故聖人深善攘楚之謀，所以大尊王之義，而紀伐黃之師，猶欲其敦不息之誠也。
宋師伐陳，衛人救陳。〔宣公十有二年夏楚〕
translation_en:
…the regular force, with which to proclaim the offenses of the people of Chu. An army without outside support has no means of meeting contingencies [?]. He instructed Jiang and Huang to hold their troops ready as his reinforcements; deployed separately as an extraordinary force, they could [?] threaten Chu’s rear. Indeed, even before the encampment at Xingting, Chu’s army was already terrified. Duke Huan had laid his plans well in advance: could even so powerful an enemy as Chu escape his calculations? Nor was it necessary to await the covenant at Shaoling for Qu Wan to offer submission. Duke Huan had long considered his strategy, calculating how to secure victory before assembling the meeting. With a plan that ensured complete success, what difficulty could Chu’s troops present? The Sage regarded repelling the barbarians and bringing peace to the Xia as the work of a hegemon; how much more worthy was one who delighted in planning and thereby succeeded! This meeting displayed the might of the central Xia lands and checked the arrogance of the outer barbarians—a great blessing for the world. Thus, although the feudal lords were all present, the wording placed at the end expresses approval of this plan [?].
Yet could Duke Huan have devised this strategy in a single morning? At the covenant of Guanze, ties with Jiang and Huang had already been established; Chu was isolated from its allies, while our strength flourished. His preparations for dealing with Chu could hardly be called inadequate. Nevertheless, he still undertook the meeting at Yanggu, because he feared Chu’s strength and gave the matter diligent thought. Had he remained unflagging to the end, the kingly Way might have been within reach. Why, once the people of Chu had submitted, did he become arrogant? Sending troops to invade Chen was already wrong; to witness Huang’s distress without coming to its rescue—was this the duty of a hegemon? Thus the Sage deeply approved the plan to repel Chu, thereby exalting the principle of honoring the king. Yet in recording the army’s attack on Huang, he still wished Duke Huan to strengthen his sincerity and sustain it without cease.
The army of Song attacked Chen; the men of Wei came to Chen’s rescue. 〔Summer of the twelfth year of Duke Xuan; Chu …〕

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
子伐宋〔宣公十有三年〕
羅名士
同考試官教諭吳　批〔講非義失謀鑿鑿可愛〕
士惟士
考試官教諭胡　批〔得旨〕
考試官學正史　批〔謹嚴〕
春秋于大國虐貳之兵而兩託詞以罪之也于
以見宋之伐陳非義而失謀也春秋致意於書
法也有以哉且宋何爲而伐陳以其從楚也如
是則討貳之兵矣春秋何以責宋夫用兵者非
===
不武之難而無義舉之難當陳之貳于楚也伊
誰之咎哉釋陳罪而遺之楚無乃已德之闕乎
不自省而責人之貳已是先事而加人也兵舉
非義衛是以有救陳之師焉夫衛宋之同盟也
救陳則背盟矣衛何心哉而甘于誓言之食誠
有所忍于陳者經以陳有可救之善衛是以有
能救之名書救而宋之罪著矣不然則失信之
衛春秋且惡之矣而何以書救哉謀國者非叡
punctuated:
子伐宋。〔宣公十有三年〕
羅名士。
同考試官教諭吳，批〔講非義失謀，鑿鑿可愛〕。
士惟士。
考試官教諭胡，批〔得旨〕。
考試官學正史，批〔謹嚴〕。
春秋于大國虐貳之兵，而兩託詞以罪之也，于以見宋之伐陳非義而失謀也。春秋致意於書法也，有以哉！且宋何爲而伐陳？以其從楚也。如是，則討貳之兵矣，春秋何以責宋？夫用兵者，非不武之難，而無義舉之難。當陳之貳于楚也，伊誰之咎哉？釋陳罪而遺之楚，無乃已德之闕乎？不自省而責人之貳已，是先事而加人也。兵舉非義，衛是以有救陳之師焉。夫衛，宋之同盟也，救陳則背盟矣。衛何心哉，而甘于誓言之食？誠有所忍于陳者。經以陳有可救之善，衛是以有能救之名。書救，而宋之罪著矣。不然，則失信之衛，春秋且惡之矣，而何以書救哉？謀國者，非叡
translation_en:
…the Viscount [of Chu] attacked Song. 〔Thirteenth year of Duke Xuan.〕
Luo Mingshi.
Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor, comments: 〔The discussion of unrighteous action and faulty planning is precise and commendable.〕
Shi Weishi [?].
Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: 〔Grasps the purport.〕
Examiner Shi, Instructor, comments: 〔Careful and rigorous.〕
Regarding a great state's campaign to chastise a disloyal state, the Spring and Autumn Annals twice employs wording that condemns it. This shows that Song's attack on Chen was unrighteous and ill-conceived. There is good reason for the Annals' attention to its manner of recording events! Why, then, did Song attack Chen? Because Chen followed Chu. If so, this was a campaign to punish disloyalty. Why does the Annals blame Song? For those who employ troops, the difficulty lies not in a lack of martial prowess but in undertaking a campaign without righteousness. When Chen transferred its allegiance to Chu, whose fault was it? To leave Chen's offense unpunished and surrender it to Chu—was this not a deficiency in one's own virtue? To blame another for disloyalty to oneself without examining oneself is to initiate the quarrel and impose upon another [?]. Since the campaign was unrighteous, Wei therefore sent an army to rescue Chen.
Now Wei was Song's ally; rescuing Chen thus meant violating their covenant. What was Wei's intention, that it willingly broke its sworn word? The text speaks of something it could bear concerning Chen [?]. The Classic regards Chen as possessing goodness that warranted rescue; Wei therefore gains the reputation of having been able to rescue it. By recording a “rescue,” it makes Song's guilt manifest. Otherwise, the Annals would have condemned Wei for breaking faith: why, then, would it have recorded a “rescue”? For those who plan affairs of state, it is not sagacity [?] …

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
強之患而惟無備之患方楚之脅宋也抑何
爲計哉惜民力以固其本寧非禦敵之道乎昧
自治而攻楚之與國是無故而啓釁也爲謀不
臧楚是以有伐宋之師焉夫陳楚之新得也伐
陳是伐楚矣楚何人哉而肯於與國之棄是宜
弗甘于宋者經以宋有可伐之罪楚是以有能
伐之名稱爵而宋之罪見矣不然則猾夏之楚
春秋方懲之矣而何以書爵哉雖然宋之罪大
矣衞之罪可恕耶楚不足責而晉實可尤也清
===
丘之盟恤病討貳乃宋之伐陳衞可以救而宋
之彼兵晉可以弗救耶春秋端本澄源故責宋
爲深而清丘之信誠有不待貶者故曰盟非春
秋之所貴于此益信
禮記
故樂者天地之命中和之紀人情之所不
能免也
許份
同考試官學正袁　批〔命紀皆統聲容此作獨能〕
punctuated:
強之患，而惟無備之患。方楚之脅宋也，抑何爲計哉？惜民力以固其本，寧非禦敵之道乎？昧自治而攻楚之與國，是無故而啓釁也。爲謀不臧，楚是以有伐宋之師焉。夫陳，楚之新得也；伐陳，是伐楚矣。楚何人哉，而肯於與國之棄？是宜弗甘于宋者。經以宋有可伐之罪，楚是以有能伐之名。稱爵而宋之罪見矣。不然，則猾夏之楚，《春秋》方懲之矣，而何以書爵哉？雖然，宋之罪大矣，衞之罪可恕耶？楚不足責，而晉實可尤也。清丘之盟，恤病討貳，乃宋之伐陳，衞可以救，而宋之彼兵，晉可以弗救耶？《春秋》端本澄源，故責宋爲深，而清丘之信，誠有不待貶者。故曰，盟非《春秋》之所貴，于此益信。
禮記
故樂者，天地之命，中和之紀，人情之所不能免也。
許份
同考試官學正袁，批〔命紀皆統聲容，此作獨能〕
translation_en:
…strength that is to be feared, but only a lack of preparedness. When Chu threatened Song, what plans should Song have made? Was conserving the people's strength to secure its foundations not a means of resisting the enemy? To neglect putting its own affairs in order and attack Chu's ally was to provoke hostilities without cause. Its planning was unsound; hence Chu sent an army to attack Song. Chen was an ally Chu had newly acquired: to attack Chen was to attack Chu. What sort of power was Chu, that it would consent to abandoning its ally? It was only to be expected that Chu would not acquiesce in Song's conduct. Because the Classic treats Song as guilty of an offense warranting attack, Chu consequently receives recognition for undertaking that attack. By recording the Chu ruler's rank, it makes Song's guilt apparent. Otherwise, the Spring and Autumn Annals would have been censuring Chu for bringing disorder to the central states; why, then, would it record his rank?
Even so, although Song's guilt was great, could Wei's guilt be excused? Chu hardly merits reproach here; it is Jin that truly deserves blame. The covenant at Qingqiu pledged aid to those in distress and punishment of those of divided allegiance. If Wei could rescue Chen when Song attacked it, could Jin fail to rescue Song when Song itself came under attack [?]? The Spring and Autumn Annals rectifies the root and purifies the source, and therefore reproaches Song severely. As for the good faith pledged at Qingqiu, its failure surely needed no further censure. Thus the saying that covenants are not what the Spring and Autumn Annals values gains further confirmation here.
Book of Rites
“Thus music is the mandate of Heaven and Earth, the ordering principle of centrality and harmony, and something human feelings cannot do without.”
Xu Fen
Associate Examiner Yuan, Instructor, comments: “Both ‘mandate’ and ‘ordering principle’ encompass musical sounds and ceremonial bearing. This composition alone is able to…”

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
體認錄之
考試官教諭胡　批〔深達治情之道者〕
考試官學正史　批〔善發先王立樂本意〕
記者著正樂之用大而於人爲甚切焉夫參造
化而管中和樂之爲用大矣治情之道孰有切
於是乎此記者歷言樂教之感而結之以此若
謂人情必有所樂而先王則惡其亂夫固制爲
雅頌之聲干戚之舞以淑其身心矣是樂也豈
其微哉蓋人受天地之中而塞以成形帥以成
===
性者維天所命也然天固命之而踐形盡性之
不與樂則參贊以通其神明之德輔翊以成其
恭肅之儀是天地之所賦非樂無以成其教矣
樂其天地之命乎心具性情之德而至中無倚
至和無戾者人皆有之也然人固有之而盡善
盡美之難兼樂則裕之於內而志意自融暢之
於外而動容自中是中和之所稟非樂無以統
其全矣樂其中和之紀乎夫天地中和之道無
非人情之寓也樂旣觀其深矣人情其能免乎
punctuated:
體認，錄之。
考試官教諭胡，批〔深達治情之道者〕
考試官學正史，批〔善發先王立樂本意〕
記者著正樂之用大，而於人爲甚切焉。夫參造化而管中和，樂之爲用大矣。治情之道，孰有切於是乎？此記者歷言樂教之感，而結之以此。若謂人情必有所樂，而先王則惡其亂，夫固制爲雅頌之聲、干戚之舞，以淑其身心矣。是樂也，豈其微哉？蓋人受天地之中，而塞以成形、帥以成性者，維天所命也。然天固命之，而踐形盡性之不與，樂則參贊以通其神明之德，輔翊以成其恭肅之儀。是天地之所賦，非樂無以成其教矣。樂其天地之命乎？心具性情之德，而至中無倚、至和無戾者，人皆有之也。然人固有之，而盡善盡美之難兼，樂則裕之於內而志意自融，暢之於外而動容自中。是中和之所稟，非樂無以統其全矣。樂其中和之紀乎？夫天地中和之道，無非人情之寓也。樂旣觀其深矣，人情其能免乎？
translation_en:
…grasps this through personal understanding; I select it for inclusion.

Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: 〔One who profoundly understands the way to regulate the emotions.〕

Examiner Shi, School Director, comments: 〔It ably elucidates the former kings’ original intention in instituting music.〕

The author of the Record makes clear that the function of correct music is great and that it bears especially closely upon human beings. Participating in the creative transformations of Heaven and Earth and governing equilibrium and harmony, music indeed has a great function. Among the ways of regulating the emotions, what could be more pertinent than this? Thus, after explaining in succession the effects of musical instruction, the author of the Record concludes with these words. His meaning is that human feelings must find something in which to delight, but the former kings abhorred their disorder. They therefore established the sounds of the Odes and Hymns and the dances with shields and axes to improve people’s bodies and minds. Could such music be something insignificant?

Human beings receive the equilibrium of Heaven and Earth: that which fills them to constitute their bodily form and guides them to constitute their nature is what Heaven ordains. Yet although Heaven ordains it, fulfilling one’s bodily form and fully realizing one’s nature are not granted thereby [?]. Music assists the creative process, giving free passage to the spiritual intelligence of their virtue, and lends support to bring their reverent and solemn deportment to completion. Thus, with respect to what Heaven and Earth endow, without music there is no means to complete its cultivation. Is music not, then, the ordinance of Heaven and Earth?

The heart possesses the virtues of human nature and feeling. Perfect equilibrium without inclination and perfect harmony without discord are qualities everyone possesses. Yet although people inherently possess them, it is difficult to combine perfect goodness with perfect beauty. Music enriches them within, so that their intentions naturally become harmonious; it gives them free expression outwardly, so that their movements and bearing naturally accord with the proper measure. Thus, with respect to the endowment of equilibrium and harmony, without music there is no means to bring its entirety under unified regulation. Is music not, then, the ordering principle of equilibrium and harmony?

The ways of Heaven and Earth, equilibrium and harmony, are all lodgments of human feeling. Since music has already revealed their depths [?], can human feeling escape it?

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
故樂必發於聲音情之不可以已也則有所防
而不至於流天下孰能舍是以爲之聲樂必形
於舞蹈情之不可以已也則有所制而不至於
蕩天下孰能外是以爲之容避其命焉而道迪
其天性之良以爲持情合危之具非僻之私無
自而入也泰其紀焉而檢束其固有之眞以爲
平心宣化之資和順之心隨感而應也人情其
何以免於樂乎如其可免則天地中和之道或
幾乎息矣樂豈細故而可須臾去哉大抵樂非
===
自先王作也樂之如本於天地而以治人之情
故其成也明備而天地官焉合一之理則然耳
中庸原天命而繼之以致中和終之以天地位
萬物育意類如此然則聖人脩道之教樂固不
居其大端乎此又學者所當察
志之所至詩亦至焉詩之所至禮亦至焉
禮之所至樂亦至焉
許任
同考試官學正袁　批〔立意不外禮樂禮樂實原〕
punctuated:
故樂必發於聲音，情之不可以已也，則有所防而不至於流，天下孰能舍是以爲之聲？樂必形於舞蹈，情之不可以已也，則有所制而不至於蕩，天下孰能外是以爲之容？避其命焉，而道迪其天性之良，以爲持情合危之具，非僻之私無自而入也；泰其紀焉，而檢束其固有之眞，以爲平心宣化之資，和順之心隨感而應也。人情其何以免於樂乎？如其可免，則天地中和之道或幾乎息矣。樂豈細故而可須臾去哉？大抵樂非自先王作也。樂之如本於天地，而以治人之情，故其成也明備，而天地官焉，合一之理則然耳。《中庸》原天命而繼之以致中和，終之以天地位、萬物育，意類如此。然則聖人脩道之教，樂固不居其大端乎？此又學者所當察。

志之所至，詩亦至焉；詩之所至，禮亦至焉；禮之所至，樂亦至焉。
許任
同考試官學正袁　批〔立意不外禮樂，禮樂實原〕
translation_en:
Thus music must find expression in sound. Since feelings cannot be suppressed, they are given restraints so that they do not run to excess. Who under Heaven could dispense with this in producing musical sound? Music must take shape in dance. Since feelings cannot be suppressed, they are given regulation so that they do not become unbridled. Who under Heaven could go beyond this in giving them bodily expression? By avoiding its mandate [?] and guiding the goodness of one's heavenly nature, one makes music an instrument for restraining feelings and reconciling what is precarious [?]; selfish impulses toward wrongdoing and perversity then have no way to enter. By amplifying its ordering principles [?] and keeping one's inherent genuineness under discipline, one makes music a resource for calming the mind and spreading moral transformation; a harmonious and compliant heart then responds whenever it is moved. How could human feelings dispense with music? If they could, the Way of Heaven and Earth, of equilibrium and harmony, would perhaps come close to ceasing. Could music be a trivial matter that one might put aside even for a moment? In general, music did not originate with the former kings. Music is rooted in Heaven and Earth [?] and serves to govern human feelings. Thus, when perfected, it is manifest and complete, and Heaven and Earth perform their offices within it: this simply follows from the principle of their unity. The Doctrine of the Mean begins with Heaven's mandate, proceeds to the attainment of equilibrium and harmony, and ends with Heaven and Earth taking their proper places and the myriad things being nourished. Its meaning is of this kind. Then, within the sages' teaching of cultivating the Way, does music not indeed occupy a principal place? This, too, is something students should examine.

“Where intention reaches, poetry also reaches; where poetry reaches, ritual also reaches; where ritual reaches, music also reaches.”
Xu Ren
Associate Examiner Yuan, School Director, comments: 〔The conception stays within ritual and music; ritual and music are truly rooted in …〕

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
一心是篇歸重於心是有志子民者
考試官教諭胡　批〔說禮樂處最是〕
考試官學正史　批〔說至字精切〕
聖人推治道相因之盛欲賢者達禮樂之本也
蓋心者出治之本也志極其至則詩禮樂一以
貫之矣治道寧復有餘蘊哉夫子因子夏五至
之問而告之也若曰致治之道充之雖極於天
下而歛之則原於一心夫人特患所存之未至
耳誠使子民者以參賛爲極功而念慮之經畫
===
期於兼濟天下而無外以化育爲能事而精神
之運用必欲曲成萬物而無遺如是則志可謂
至矣由是而言焉雖非有期於詩也然詩以言
志者也有諸中者自形諸外歌詠之所發抑揚
足以盡變也聲韻之所宣節奏足以成文也以
觀民風以達國政悉於此乎攸寓矣志至而詩
有不至乎由是而立焉雖非有期於禮也然禮
者履此者也感之深者自立之固威儀之齊壹
而維民之則具焉品節之脩明而維皇之極建
punctuated:
一心。是篇歸重於心，是有志子民者。
考試官教諭胡，批〔說禮樂處最是〕。
考試官學正史，批〔說至字精切〕。
聖人推治道相因之盛，欲賢者達禮樂之本也。蓋心者，出治之本也。志極其至，則詩禮樂一以貫之矣，治道寧復有餘蘊哉？夫子因子夏五至之問而告之也，若曰：致治之道，充之雖極於天下，而歛之則原於一心。夫人特患所存之未至耳。誠使子民者以參賛爲極功，而念慮之經畫期於兼濟天下而無外；以化育爲能事，而精神之運用必欲曲成萬物而無遺，如是則志可謂至矣。由是而言焉，雖非有期於詩也，然詩以言志者也。有諸中者，自形諸外。歌詠之所發，抑揚足以盡變也；聲韻之所宣，節奏足以成文也。以觀民風，以達國政，悉於此乎攸寓矣。志至而詩有不至乎？由是而立焉，雖非有期於禮也，然禮者履此者也。感之深者，自立之固。威儀之齊壹，而維民之則具焉；品節之脩明，而維皇之極建
translation_en:
…a single mind. This essay places its emphasis on the mind; its author is someone intent on caring for the people as his children.
Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: 〔The discussion of ritual and music is particularly sound.〕
Examiner Shi, Instructor, comments: 〔The explanation of the word “utmost” is precise and incisive.〕
The sage expounds the fullness of the successive, interdependent workings of government, wishing worthy men to understand the root of ritual and music. For the mind is the root from which good government proceeds. When intention reaches its utmost, poetry, ritual, and music are all united by a single thread. Could the way of government then have any meaning left unexplored? In response to Zixia’s question about the five things that reach their utmost, the Master instructed him, as though saying: “The way to achieve good government, when extended, reaches throughout all under Heaven; when gathered inward, it originates in a single mind. One need only fear that what one holds within has not reached its utmost. Suppose those who care for the people as their children take assisting Heaven and Earth as their highest accomplishment, and direct their thoughts and plans toward benefiting all under Heaven, excluding none; suppose they take transformation and nurture as their task, and apply their spiritual energies to bringing every being to fulfillment according to its particular nature, omitting none. Then their intention may be said to have reached its utmost.
“When they proceed from this to expression, although they have not deliberately aimed at poetry, poetry is the means of expressing intention. What is within naturally takes form without. In what singing gives forth, rising and falling tones suffice to encompass every variation; in what sounds and rhymes convey, measured rhythms suffice to form an ordered pattern. Observing the customs of the people and making the government of the state understood are both embodied here. Once intention reaches its utmost, could poetry fail to do so?
“When they proceed from this to establishing themselves, although they have not deliberately aimed at ritual, ritual is the means of putting this into practice. Those who are deeply moved naturally establish themselves firmly. Through the uniform order of dignified bearing, the standards that sustain the people are fully provided; through the cultivation and clarification of graded observances, the sovereign’s supreme standard is established…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
焉以辨等威以定民志感於是乎取乘矣詩至
而禮有不至乎然和序一理也有其序必有其
和而樂亦於是乎極矣吾知協氣嘉生泰和充
溢乎宇宙也大化均調歡欣交通於兩間也臣
民和於下一人和於上順氣於玆而成象矣禮
至而樂豈有不至哉夫樂因於禮禮因於詩一
機之相成而不容自已者也然其始基於志焉
禮樂之原不遠於心而得之矣子民者其尚求
其至乎雖然志之所關大矣一念雖微人之聖
===
狂治之隆汙係焉故志苟至矣則詩以風天下
禮以序天下樂以和天下而王道胥此焉出不
然則詩邪禮慝樂淫治斯替矣可不慎乎是故
先王慎所以感之者
第貳塲
論
仁智合一存乎聖
張子奇
同考試官教諭劉　批　題本明正作者類不脫塵
punctuated:
焉。以辨等威，以定民志，感於是乎取乘矣。詩至而禮有不至乎？然和序一理也，有其序必有其和，而樂亦於是乎極矣。吾知協氣嘉生，泰和充溢乎宇宙也；大化均調，歡欣交通於兩間也。臣民和於下，一人和於上，順氣於玆而成象矣。禮至而樂豈有不至哉？夫樂因於禮，禮因於詩，一機之相成而不容自已者也。然其始基於志焉，禮樂之原不遠於心而得之矣。子民者其尚求其至乎！雖然，志之所關大矣。一念雖微，人之聖狂、治之隆汙係焉。故志苟至矣，則詩以風天下，禮以序天下，樂以和天下，而王道胥此焉出。不然，則詩邪、禮慝、樂淫，治斯替矣，可不慎乎？是故先王慎所以感之者。
第貳塲
論
仁智合一存乎聖
張子奇
同考試官教諭劉，批：題本明正，作者類不脫塵
translation_en:
…is established. Through this, distinctions of rank and dignity are clarified and the people's aspirations are settled; the response thus gains momentum [?]. When poetry reaches perfection, could ritual fail to do so? Yet harmony and order share a single principle: where there is order, there must be harmony, and music thereby also reaches its highest perfection. I know that harmonious vital energy and flourishing life will arise, and supreme harmony will fill the universe; the great transforming process will be evenly attuned, and joy will circulate between Heaven and Earth. Ministers and people will be harmonious below, and the sovereign harmonious above; harmonious vital energy will thereby take visible form. When ritual reaches perfection, how could music fail to do so? Music depends upon ritual, and ritual upon poetry: they complete one another through a single impulse that cannot cease of itself. Yet their initial foundation lies in the will. The source of ritual and music is found without looking far beyond the heart. Should not those who treat the people as their children seek its utmost perfection?
Nevertheless, what depends upon the will is momentous. Though a single thought is minute, whether a person becomes a sage or a madman, and whether government flourishes or declines, depend upon it. Thus, if the will attains perfection, poetry transforms the world, ritual orders the world, and music harmonizes the world; the Kingly Way emerges entirely from this. Otherwise, poetry becomes perverse, ritual corrupt, and music licentious, and government declines. Can one fail to exercise care? Hence the former kings were careful about the means by which they moved people's hearts.
Second Session
Discourse
The Unity of Benevolence and Wisdom Resides in the Sage
Zhang Ziqi

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
雜可厭獨此論得張子立言本意而文更俊逸佳士也
同考試官教諭程　批〔詞理精明說聖人仁智合一之妙宛然可誦非深養之士不能也用魁多士〕
同考試官教諭朱　批〔文不俗而理透不可以時論目之〕
考試官教諭胡　批〔冲雅可錄〕
考試官學正史　批〔簡古〕
聖人盡人道之極亦惟全乎所性而已矣夫性
者萬物之一原無人已無內外而一之者也人
惟牿之以一偏之見是以人已分而內外判內
===
外判而體用離以言乎成已也自私而已矣自
私則惡物惡物則非仁以言乎成物也任數而
已矣任數則忘本忘本則非智聖人陰陽合德
而仁智兼備盡人道之極者也豈有待於外哉
亦惟全乎所性而已故曰性之德也合內外之
道也張子豈無稽之言耶雖然聖人亦天道也
吾觀太虛之中冲漠無眹而萬象森羅自其冲
漠謂之體內而非內也自其森羅謂之用外而
punctuated:
雜，可厭。獨此論得張子立言本意，而文更俊逸，佳士也。
同考試官教諭程　批〔詞理精明，說聖人仁智合一之妙，宛然可誦，非深養之士不能也，用魁多士。〕
同考試官教諭朱　批〔文不俗而理透，不可以時論目之。〕
考試官教諭胡　批〔冲雅可錄。〕
考試官學正史　批〔簡古。〕
聖人盡人道之極，亦惟全乎所性而已矣。夫性者，萬物之一原，無人已，無內外，而一之者也。人惟牿之以一偏之見，是以人已分而內外判，內外判而體用離。以言乎成已也，自私而已矣；自私則惡物，惡物則非仁。以言乎成物也，任數而已矣；任數則忘本，忘本則非智。聖人陰陽合德，而仁智兼備，盡人道之極者也，豈有待於外哉？亦惟全乎所性而已。故曰：「性之德也，合內外之道也。」張子豈無稽之言耶？雖然，聖人亦天道也。吾觀太虛之中，冲漠無眹，而萬象森羅。自其冲漠謂之體，內而非內也；自其森羅謂之用，外而
translation_en:
…vulgar clutter, which is tiresome. This discourse alone grasps Master Zhang’s original intent in making this statement; its writing is also outstanding and unfettered. Its author is a fine scholar.
Associate Examiner Cheng, Instructor, comments: 〔The language and reasoning are precise and clear. Its account of the subtle unity of benevolence and wisdom in the sage is vivid and worthy of recitation. Only a scholar of profound self-cultivation could achieve this. On this basis, he is ranked first among the candidates.〕
Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: 〔The writing is free of vulgarity, and its reasoning penetrates deeply. It cannot be regarded as an ordinary discourse of the day.〕
Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: 〔Serene and elegant; worthy of selection.〕
Examiner Shi, School Instructor, comments: 〔Concise and antique in style.〕
The sage reaches the utmost limit of the human Way simply by fully realizing his inherent nature. Nature is the single source of the myriad things: it makes no distinction between others and oneself, or between inner and outer, but unites them. People constrain it with one-sided views; thus others and oneself become divided, and inner and outer are separated. Once inner and outer are separated, substance and function become detached. As for perfecting oneself, this becomes mere selfishness. Selfishness leads to aversion to things, and such aversion is not benevolence. As for perfecting things, this becomes mere reliance on calculation. Reliance on calculation leads to forgetting the root, and forgetting the root is not wisdom. In the sage, yin and yang unite their powers, and benevolence and wisdom are both fully present: he reaches the utmost limit of the human Way. How could he depend on anything external? He simply fully realizes his inherent nature. Thus it is said: “It is the virtue of one’s nature, the Way that unites inner and outer.” Could Master Zhang’s words possibly be without foundation?
Nevertheless, the sage also embodies the Way of Heaven. I observe that within the Great Vacuity there is undifferentiated stillness without a trace, yet the myriad phenomena stand arrayed in abundance. In respect of its undifferentiated stillness, we call it substance: it is inward, yet not merely inward. In respect of its abundant array, we call it function: it is outward, yet…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
非外也是以感遇聚散鼓之爲風霆潤之爲雨
露孚之爲飛走草木含蠢動糟粕煨燼無非
天也無非天則亦無非性也人性諸天者也其
體用猶是也但衆人有之而不知賢人知之而
未盡是故仁者見之謂之仁智者見之謂之智
見仁則偏于內偏內則窒見智則偏于外偏外
則離仁智合一之道其誰知之聖人形天之形
也帥天之帥也其氣之清明質之純粹有若獨
厚於天者而成性存存之地物欲不得而與焉
===
故其靜與天俱也渾焉噩焉而富有之業以根
靜涵乎動也動與天游也弘焉博焉而日新之
德以著動涵乎靜也靜涵乎動則無內動涵乎
靜則無外無外無內則無外則化窮神知化德之
盛也非聖人其孰能之人但見其冲然虛而已
淵然邃而已無將迎無內外而一無不存則曰
聖人之仁也亦智也及其觸之即覺感之即應
變而通之以盡利鼓之舞之以盡神則曰聖人
之智也亦仁也仁存乎內而不可測智運乎外
punctuated: 非外也。是以感遇聚散，鼓之爲風霆，潤之爲雨露，孚之爲飛走草木，含蠢動糟粕煨燼，無非天也。無非天，則亦無非性也。人性諸天者也，其體用猶是也。但衆人有之而不知，賢人知之而未盡。是故仁者見之謂之仁，智者見之謂之智。見仁則偏于內，偏內則窒；見智則偏于外，偏外則離。仁智合一之道，其誰知之？聖人形天之形也，帥天之帥也。其氣之清明、質之純粹，有若獨厚於天者，而成性存存之地，物欲不得而與焉。故其靜與天俱也，渾焉噩焉，而富有之業以根，靜涵乎動也；動與天游也，弘焉博焉，而日新之德以著，動涵乎靜也。靜涵乎動則無內，動涵乎靜則無外。無外無內，則無外則化。窮神知化，德之盛也。非聖人，其孰能之？人但見其冲然虛而已，淵然邃而已，無將迎，無內外，而一無不存，則曰聖人之仁也，亦智也。及其觸之即覺，感之即應，變而通之以盡利，鼓之舞之以盡神，則曰聖人之智也，亦仁也。仁存乎內而不可測，智運乎外
translation_en:
…yet it is not external. Thus, through interaction and encounter, gathering and dispersal, it stirs things into wind and thunder, moistens them as rain and dew, and brings forth birds, beasts, plants, and trees, encompassing [?] wriggling creatures, dregs, and ashes: none of these is other than Heaven. Since none is other than Heaven, none is other than nature. Human beings receive their nature from Heaven; its substance and function are likewise of this kind. Ordinary people possess it without knowing it; worthy people know it but have not fully realized it. Thus, the benevolent see it and call it benevolence; the wise see it and call it wisdom. Seeing benevolence alone inclines one toward the internal, and this inward bias leads to obstruction. Seeing wisdom alone inclines one toward the external, and this outward bias leads to separation. Who understands the Way in which benevolence and wisdom are one?

The sage gives form to Heaven’s form and takes Heaven’s command as his command. His vital energy is clear and luminous, his constitution pure and unalloyed, as though Heaven had endowed him with exceptional generosity. Where he continually preserves his fully realized nature, material desires can gain no foothold. Thus, in stillness he abides with Heaven, whole and uncarved; here his abundantly encompassing work takes root, for his stillness embraces movement. In movement he roams with Heaven, expansive and broad; here his daily renewed virtue becomes manifest, for his movement embraces stillness. When stillness embraces movement, there is no inside; when movement embraces stillness, there is no outside. With neither outside nor inside, there is no outside, and so there is transformation [?]. To fathom the spiritual and understand transformation is the fullness of virtue. Who but the sage could accomplish this?

People see only his tranquil emptiness and his profound depth. He neither escorts what departs nor welcomes what approaches; he has neither inside nor outside, yet the One is everywhere present. They call this the sage’s benevolence, but it is also his wisdom. When he becomes aware as soon as something touches him and responds as soon as something moves him, adapting and opening the way to realize every benefit, stirring and animating things to give full expression to their spiritual efficacy, they call this the sage’s wisdom, but it is also his benevolence. Benevolence abides within and cannot be fathomed; wisdom operates without…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
而不可窮流行於天下磅礴乎萬物而無乎不
至順理而動緣機而起錯綜有倫而無乎不足
又孰非聖人之仁爲之哉何也聖人者秉天地
之精立中和之極內外兩忘體用兼備其所造
膛乎不可及矣由是會人物於一身通古今於
一息以之宰世馭物經紀明時使天下由其理
而不知循其軌而不亂以實天地以序四時以
明日月以行江河以蕃草木以畜鳥獸其功用
有如此是皆聖人智之所運也而亦孰非其仁
===
也哉蓋智而非仁則敦化之原不深仁而非智
則川流之用以息仁敦化則體一用也智川流
則用一體也體用一原顯微無間非天下之至
聖其孰能與於此雖然一至誠而已矣蓋誠者
物之終始不誠無物聖人之所以爲聖亦誠乎
此而已成已成物皆其事也是故成已爲仁誠
之存也成物爲智誠之發也是皆性之德而無
一有待於外也故誠則無事矣未至於此者當
何如亦曰擇善而固執之也惟擇而固則盡人
punctuated: 而不可窮，流行於天下，磅礴乎萬物，而無乎不至；順理而動，緣機而起，錯綜有倫，而無乎不足。又孰非聖人之仁爲之哉？何也？聖人者，秉天地之精，立中和之極，內外兩忘，體用兼備，其所造膛乎不可及矣。由是會人物於一身，通古今於一息，以之宰世馭物，經紀明時，使天下由其理而不知，循其軌而不亂，以實天地，以序四時，以明日月，以行江河，以蕃草木，以畜鳥獸。其功用有如此，是皆聖人智之所運也，而亦孰非其仁也哉？蓋智而非仁，則敦化之原不深；仁而非智，則川流之用以息。仁敦化，則體一用也；智川流，則用一體也。體用一原，顯微無間，非天下之至聖，其孰能與於此？雖然，一至誠而已矣。蓋誠者，物之終始，不誠無物。聖人之所以爲聖，亦誠乎此而已。成已成物，皆其事也。是故成已爲仁，誠之存也；成物爲智，誠之發也。是皆性之德，而無一有待於外也。故誠則無事矣。未至於此者當何如？亦曰擇善而固執之也。惟擇而固，則盡人
translation_en:
…and cannot be exhausted. It flows throughout the world, pervades the myriad things, and reaches everywhere. It moves in accordance with principle and arises in response to circumstances; its intricate workings are orderly, and nowhere is it inadequate. Yet which of these things is not brought about by the sage’s benevolence? Why is this? The sage receives the pure essence of Heaven and Earth and establishes the supreme standard of equilibrium and harmony. He forgets both inner and outer, possessing substance and function in their completeness; his attainment is far beyond reach [?]. Thus he gathers people and things into his own person and comprehends past and present in a single breath. With this he governs the world and directs its affairs, ordering an enlightened age. He enables all under Heaven to follow his principle without knowing it and to keep to his course without disorder. Thereby he brings Heaven and Earth to fullness, orders the four seasons, makes the sun and moon shine, causes the rivers to flow, makes plants flourish, and nurtures birds and beasts. Such are his achievements and effects. All these are the workings of the sage’s wisdom; yet which of them is not also his benevolence?
For if there is wisdom without benevolence, the source of profound transformation is not deep; if there is benevolence without wisdom, the operation that flows like a river ceases. Benevolence brings profound transformation: substance unifies function. Wisdom flows like a river: function unifies substance. Substance and function share one source; the manifest and the subtle admit no separation. Who but the utmost sage in the world could participate in this? Nevertheless, it is simply perfect sincerity. Sincerity is the beginning and end of things; without sincerity there are no things. What makes the sage a sage is likewise simply being sincere in this. Perfecting himself and perfecting things are both his tasks. Thus perfecting himself constitutes benevolence: sincerity abiding within. Perfecting things constitutes wisdom: sincerity issuing forth. These are all virtues of his nature, and none depends upon anything external. Hence, with sincerity, nothing further needs to be done. What should those who have not reached this point do? The answer is simply to choose the good and hold firmly to it. Only by choosing it and holding firmly to it can one fully realize the human…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
而天而至誠可幾矣又何仁智之不可及哉故
曰及其成功則一也是爲論
同前
陳加命
同考試官教諭吳　批〔仁智本誠論中且檃括義命動靜陰陽性道意最是至引西銘形聖人仁智尤〕
親切有味足徵子自得之學矣
同考試官教諭何　批〔文與理俱遂宜録爲式〕
考試官教諭胡　批〔有見識有論議非苟作者〕
考試官學正史　批〔論之佳者〕
===
聖人所以貫天下之道者誠焉而已矣夫誠者
天之道也人心之所自來也聖人純於天道而
全體不息焉以立人極是故由其體也而誠斯
立焉由其用也而誠斯通焉存之而爲仁發之
而爲智仁智一而聖人之事備唯誠以貫之也
是故以撰義命而理達以效動靜而神存以體
陰陽而道行以窮性與天道而妙合大哉誠乎
斯其至矣非聖人其孰能與於斯今夫天以太
punctuated:
而天，而至誠可幾矣，又何仁智之不可及哉？故曰：「及其成功，則一也。」是爲論。

同前。
陳加命。
同考試官教諭吳，批〔仁智本誠，論中且檃括義命、動靜、陰陽、性道，意最是。至引西銘形聖人仁智，尤〕親切有味，足徵子自得之學矣。
同考試官教諭何，批〔文與理俱遂，宜録爲式。〕
考試官教諭胡，批〔有見識，有論議，非苟作者。〕
考試官學正史，批〔論之佳者。〕

聖人所以貫天下之道者，誠焉而已矣。夫誠者，天之道也，人心之所自來也。聖人純於天道，而全體不息焉，以立人極。是故由其體也，而誠斯立焉；由其用也，而誠斯通焉。存之而爲仁，發之而爲智。仁智一，而聖人之事備，唯誠以貫之也。是故以撰義命而理達，以效動靜而神存，以體陰陽而道行，以窮性與天道而妙合。大哉，誠乎！斯其至矣！非聖人，其孰能與於斯？今夫天以太
translation_en:
…and accord with Heaven, so that utmost sincerity may be attained. How, then, could benevolence and wisdom be beyond reach? Thus it is said: “When they achieve success, the result is one and the same.” This concludes the discourse.

Same topic as above.
By Chen Jiaming.
Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor, comments: “Benevolence and wisdom are rooted in sincerity. The discourse also draws together rightness and destiny, activity and stillness, yin and yang, and human nature and the Way; its meaning is most apt. Its citation of the Western Inscription to portray the sage’s benevolence and wisdom is especially pertinent and rich in meaning, amply demonstrating the learning you have made your own.”
Associate Examiner He, Instructor, comments: “Both the writing and the reasoning are fully accomplished. It should be recorded as a model.”
Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: “It has insight and reasoned argument; this is no carelessly composed work.”
Examiner Shi, Instructor, comments: “An excellent discourse.”

That by which the sage unifies the Way throughout the world is sincerity alone. Sincerity is the Way of Heaven and the source from which the human heart derives. The sage is pure in his accord with the Way of Heaven and embodies it completely and without ceasing, thereby establishing the ultimate standard for humanity. Thus, considered in terms of substance, sincerity is established; considered in terms of function, sincerity operates everywhere. Preserved within, it constitutes benevolence; expressed outwardly, it constitutes wisdom. Benevolence and wisdom are one, and the work of the sage is complete: sincerity alone runs through them both. Thus, through comprehending rightness and destiny, principle becomes clear; through manifesting activity and stillness, spiritual efficacy is preserved; through embodying yin and yang, the Way operates; and through fathoming human nature and the Way of Heaven, a wondrous union is achieved. Great indeed is sincerity! Here it reaches its utmost. Who but a sage could attain this? Now Heaven, through the Supreme …

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
極之理運行於兩間莫之不道施之不悖而
不有而其所以顯諸仁藏諸用合一而不測一
誠爲之也蓋天之所以爲天也天惟誠故貞實
之理流行賦予物與無妄參和不偏合仁與智
德性之所固有也聖人與人同耳乃庶民去之
而體用之理淆君子存之而內外之迹判於是
有是內非外者於是有徇生執有者是內非智
而亦不得爲仁執有非仁而又不得爲智聖人
之道遠矣故曰仁者見之謂之仁智者見之謂
===
之智百姓日用而不知嗚呼非聖人其孰與於
斯聖人者承天之道而立人之極者也所謂陰
陽之會動靜之交義命之準而性與天道之極
致也而與非一誠爲之也故仁智者聖人之道
而誠者聖人之本也仁智合一非誠其孰爲之
聖人之仁智原於性統於心流行於事物充塞
乎天地無不備也無不體也是故以盡其性而
察之由之無不盡也是誠之成己也以盡人物
之性而知之處之無不當也是誠之成物也成
punctuated: 極之理運行於兩間，莫之不道，施之不悖，而不有。而其所以顯諸仁、藏諸用，合一而不測，一誠爲之也，蓋天之所以爲天也。天惟誠，故貞實之理流行賦予，物與無妄，參和不偏。合仁與智，德性之所固有也，聖人與人同耳。乃庶民去之，而體用之理淆；君子存之，而內外之迹判。於是有是內非外者，於是有徇生執有者。是內非智，而亦不得爲仁；執有非仁，而又不得爲智。聖人之道遠矣。故曰：「仁者見之謂之仁，智者見之謂之智，百姓日用而不知。」嗚呼！非聖人，其孰與於斯？聖人者，承天之道而立人之極者也。所謂陰陽之會、動靜之交、義命之準，而性與天道之極致也。而與非一誠爲之也？故仁智者，聖人之道，而誠者，聖人之本也。仁智合一，非誠其孰爲之？聖人之仁智，原於性，統於心，流行於事物，充塞乎天地，無不備也，無不體也。是故以盡其性，而察之由之，無不盡也，是誠之成己也；以盡人物之性，而知之處之，無不當也，是誠之成物也。成
translation_en:
…the principle of the Supreme Ultimate operates between Heaven and Earth. Nothing fails to follow it; its bestowal is without error, yet it claims no possession. That it manifests itself in benevolence and is concealed in its functioning, united as one yet unfathomable, is brought about by sincerity alone. This, indeed, is what makes Heaven Heaven. Because Heaven is sincere, its steadfast and genuine principle flows forth and is bestowed upon things; things partake of freedom from falsity, harmonizing without partiality [?]. The union of benevolence and wisdom is inherent in moral nature. In this, the sage is simply the same as other people. Yet ordinary people abandon it, and the principles of substance and function become confused; gentlemen preserve it, yet distinctions between the inner and outer remain. Thus there are those who affirm the inner and reject the outer, and those who follow life and cling to existence [?]. Affirming only the inner is not wisdom, nor can it count as benevolence; clinging to existence is not benevolence, nor can it count as wisdom. How distant the Way of the sage has become! Hence it is said: “The benevolent see it and call it benevolence; the wise see it and call it wisdom. The common people use it daily without knowing it.” Alas! Who but the sage can participate in this?

The sage receives the Way of Heaven and establishes the ultimate standard for humanity. He is what is called the meeting of yin and yang, the intersection of activity and stillness, the standard of righteousness and destiny, and the highest realization of human nature and the Way of Heaven. Is this not brought about by sincerity alone [?]? Thus benevolence and wisdom constitute the sage’s Way, while sincerity is the sage’s foundation. What but sincerity could unite benevolence and wisdom? The sage’s benevolence and wisdom originate in his nature, are unified in his mind, flow through affairs and things, and fill Heaven and Earth. There is nothing they do not encompass, nothing they do not embody. Thus, in fully realizing his own nature, he examines and follows it, leaving nothing unrealized: this is sincerity’s completion of oneself. In fully realizing the natures of people and things, he understands and deals with them with unfailing appropriateness: this is sincerity’s completion of things. Completing…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
已爲仁成物爲智性德之合乎內外者如是也
聖人時措之而非有所加也是故以其仁而神
天之德化天之道聖人之所以爲體也而莫非
智也以其智而成人之能賛天之化聖人之所
以爲用也而莫非仁也由是而存心養性知化
窮神是聖人之仁也達之而爲繼述之善匪懈
之恭矣由是而育英錫類底豫顧養是聖人之
智也存之而爲時保之翼踐形之肖矣又由是
而屋漏之敬歸全之純所以合天地之德而體
===
仁也而孰非智之所以存乎又由是而高年之
尊孤弱之慈天下之疲癃殘疾惸獨鰥寡皆有
所養所以體天地之化以盡智也而孰非仁之
所以發乎故敦厚而不化有體而無用者也非
而自失焉徇物而喪己者也性性爲能存神物
物爲能過化存神過化忘物累而順性命仁智
之極也非聖人孰與於斯惟聖人之克全於是
也而後無我得正己之盡可以觀仁存神妙應
物之感可以察智以之範圍天地則陰陽之化
punctuated: 已爲仁，成物爲智，性德之合乎內外者如是也。聖人時措之，而非有所加也。是故，以其仁而神天之德、化天之道，聖人之所以爲體也，而莫非智也；以其智而成人之能、賛天之化，聖人之所以爲用也，而莫非仁也。由是而存心養性，知化窮神，是聖人之仁也；達之而爲繼述之善、匪懈之恭矣。由是而育英錫類，底豫顧養，是聖人之智也；存之而爲時保之翼、踐形之肖矣。又由是而屋漏之敬、歸全之純，所以合天地之德而體仁也，而孰非智之所以存乎？又由是而高年之尊、孤弱之慈，天下之疲癃殘疾、惸獨鰥寡皆有所養，所以體天地之化以盡智也，而孰非仁之所以發乎？故敦厚而不化，有體而無用者也；非而自失焉，徇物而喪己者也。性性爲能存神，物物爲能過化；存神過化，忘物累而順性命，仁智之極也。非聖人孰與於斯？惟聖人之克全於是也，而後無我得正己之盡，可以觀仁；存神妙應物之感，可以察智。以之範圍天地，則陰陽之化
translation_en:
…completing oneself constitutes benevolence; completing other beings constitutes wisdom. Such is the way the virtue of one's nature unites the inner and the outer. The sage puts it into practice as circumstances require, adding nothing to it. Thus, through benevolence, he gives spiritual efficacy to Heaven's virtue and transformative expression to Heaven's Way: this constitutes the sage's substance, yet none of it is other than wisdom. Through wisdom, he fulfills human capacities and assists Heaven's transforming work: this constitutes the sage's functioning, yet none of it is other than benevolence.

From this come preserving the mind and nurturing one's nature, understanding transformation and fathoming the spiritual: these are the sage's benevolence. Extended into practice, they become excellence in carrying forward one's forebears' intentions and undertakings, and unremitting reverence. From this also come nurturing the talented and extending goodness to others of one's kind, bringing one's parents joy and caring for them: these are the sage's wisdom. Preserved within, they become the vigilance with which one constantly safeguards oneself and the likeness to one's parents achieved by fully realizing the endowment embodied in one's person.

From this also come reverence even in the privacy of one's chamber and the purity of returning one's person intact at death. These are the means of joining in the virtue of Heaven and Earth and embodying benevolence; yet which of them is not also a means by which wisdom is preserved? From this also come respect for the aged and kindness toward the orphaned and weak, so that throughout the world the infirm, disabled, solitary, widowed, and bereft all receive support. These are the means of embodying the transforming work of Heaven and Earth and fully realizing wisdom; yet which of them is not also a means by which benevolence finds expression?

Thus, being earnest and generous without transforming is to possess substance without functioning. To be wrong and lose oneself [?] is to follow external things and forfeit oneself. Only by fully realizing one's nature can one preserve spiritual efficacy; only by treating things according to their proper character can one transform wherever one passes. Preserving spiritual efficacy and transforming wherever one passes, forgetting the encumbrances of external things and following one's nature and Heaven's decree: this is the utmost of benevolence and wisdom. Who but the sage could attain this?

Only when the sage can fully realize these things does selflessness bring the rectification of oneself to completion, allowing benevolence to be discerned; preserving spiritual efficacy, he responds wondrously to the stimuli of things, allowing wisdom to be discerned. Through this he encompasses and regulates Heaven and Earth, so that the transformations of yin and yang…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
溥焉而氣之昏明不足以蔽之矣以之成其變
化則動靜之機裕焉而滯於有偏於無者不足
以惑之矣以之默成德行則義命之歸順焉而
遇之吉凶不足以戕之矣以之通乎晝夜之道
而知則性與天道昭焉而窮理盡性以至於命
矣苟誠之不足則天人異其知也內外異致也物
我異觀也不能以自成而何有於道之行於物
耶此聖人之道所以遠也斯道也信非聖人莫
能與矣是故欽明克讓濬哲溫恭堯舜其極也
===
祇台德先建中錫知禹湯其隆也懿恭緝熙敬
義灼俊文武其盛也上律下襲不厭不倦孔子
其全也而莫非一誠焉以貫之矣嗚呼斯大君
宗子所以繼天立極以肇開創之仁以大制作
之智而孔子之繼往開來以盡夫家相之責也
學焉者無私以體仁變通以盡智而惟誠之爲
貴焉則聖人之道其庶幾乎
表
擬宋以杜衍同平章事兼樞密使謝表〔慶〕
punctuated:
溥焉，而氣之昏明不足以蔽之矣；以之成其變化，則動靜之機裕焉，而滯於有、偏於無者不足以惑之矣；以之默成德行，則義命之歸順焉，而遇之吉凶不足以戕之矣；以之通乎晝夜之道而知，則性與天道昭焉，而窮理盡性以至於命矣。苟誠之不足，則天人異其知也，內外異致也，物我異觀也，不能以自成，而何有於道之行於物耶？此聖人之道所以遠也。斯道也，信非聖人莫能與矣。是故欽明克讓、濬哲溫恭，堯舜其極也；祇台德先、建中錫知，禹湯其隆也；懿恭緝熙、敬義灼俊，文武其盛也；上律下襲、不厭不倦，孔子其全也。而莫非一誠焉以貫之矣。嗚呼！斯大君宗子所以繼天立極，以肇開創之仁，以大制作之智，而孔子之繼往開來，以盡夫家相之責也。學焉者，無私以體仁，變通以盡智，而惟誠之爲貴焉，則聖人之道其庶幾乎！

表
擬宋以杜衍同平章事兼樞密使謝表〔慶〕
translation_en:
…spread far and wide, and the obscurity or clarity of material force cannot veil it. By this, one brings transformations to completion: the workings of activity and stillness have ample scope, and attachment to being or partiality toward nonbeing cannot cause confusion. By this, one silently perfects virtuous conduct: righteousness and destiny find their proper accord, and good or ill fortune cannot inflict harm. By this, one comprehends the Way of day and night and attains understanding: human nature and the Way of Heaven become clear, and one investigates principle fully and fulfills one’s nature, thereby reaching an understanding of destiny.

If sincerity is insufficient, however, Heaven and humanity differ in their knowing, the inner and outer have different ends, and things and the self are viewed differently. If one cannot perfect oneself, how could one put the Way into practice in relation to things? This is why the Way of the sages remains distant. Truly, none but sages can participate in this Way.

Thus, in reverence, illumination, and the capacity to yield, and in profound wisdom, warmth, and respect, Yao and Shun attained the utmost. In “reverently placing my virtue first” and “establishing the mean and bestowing knowledge” [?], Yu and Tang reached great heights. In admirable reverence and sustained illumination, and in “reverence, righteousness, and illuminating the outstanding” [?], Kings Wen and Wu attained greatness. In taking what is above as the standard and following what is below, and in being neither sated with learning nor weary of teaching, Confucius achieved completeness. A single sincerity ran through all of these.

Ah! This is how the great sovereign, as heir to the ancestral line, succeeds Heaven and establishes the supreme standard, initiating the benevolence of founding a dynasty and magnifying the wisdom of creating its institutions. It is also how Confucius carried forward the past and opened the way for the future, fully discharging the responsibility of a minister to the ruling house [?]. If those who study this are without selfishness in embodying benevolence, adapt to changing circumstances in fully exercising wisdom, and prize sincerity above all, might they not come close to the Way of the sages?

Memorial
A simulated memorial of thanks on the Song appointment of Du Yan as Joint Manager of Affairs and concurrently Military Affairs Commissioner. 〔Qing…〕

曆四年。

translation_en:
… the fourth year [of Qingli].

Luo Xu.

Associate Examiner Xiao, Instructor, comments: 〔In the language of this memorial one clearly sees〕〔the atmosphere of an enlightened ruler and a worthy minister finding fulfillment in one another. Its merit is more than the beauty of its parallel prose alone. It deserves inclusion.〕

Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: 〔Refined, polished, elegant, and beautiful; read aloud, it has a ringing cadence that delights.〕

Examiner Shi, Instructor, comments: 〔Classical and exemplary.〕

On a certain day of the ninth month of the fourth year of Qingli, I, your servant Yan, humbly received your sacred favor appointing me Grand Councilor and concurrently Military Affairs Commissioner. My rank places me among those within the guarded palace; like the golden handles of the state’s great cauldron, I occupy an office corresponding to the stars of the Three Terraces and the Dipper. Holding the levers of the great pivot of military affairs, I bear the jade insignia and am entrusted with military strategy. In standing, these offices rise above the Three Departments; in responsibility, they carry particular weight beyond the Six Ministers. Such high offices should surely draw upon a great minister’s support. Thus Your Majesty’s attention has been directed especially toward me, graciously entrusting me with both capacities. Yet how can my feeble strength bear them, as still more honors are bestowed upon me? I, your servant Yan, in deepest fear and trepidation, bow my head to the ground and repeatedly kowtow.

I humbly reflect that displaying martial might must aim at cultivating civil virtue, and that repelling external threats is the means of securing peace within. When Shun undertook the direction of the hundred offices, all nine virtues were made manifest; when Yu brought the Sanmiao into submission, the peoples of the four quarters all obeyed. Aheng [Yi Yin] answered the summons to service and thereby accomplished the founding at Bo. A worthy assistant [Fu Yue] was sought far and wide, and splendidly established achievements that took Heaven as their model. For ordering the state and discussing the Way, the Three Dukes and Three Solitary Dignitaries must be chosen with care; in eliminating violence and pacifying the people, the Minister of War’s responsibilities are truly difficult. Zhongshan [Zhong Shanfu] mended the sovereign’s ceremonial robe—that is, remedied his shortcomings—and the work of dynastic restoration grew ever more splendid; Fang Shu’s mighty …

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
猷大原之功丕著巡覩往跡累重殊階自
三臺易於前朝惟二府合於
昭代

北闕之文昌星轉
宸垣帷幄總中台之武庫折衝樽俎秉政鈞衡
自非經文緯武之才曷稱出將入相之任

===

進士之科徒讀父書恪守先臣之業甘心
苦節絕意干名筮仕理刑旋領祕丘之佐

良吏乾州
賜宴遥承
天語之温淮使問名特荷
中朝之眷承
内降之旨爰自封還阻攻守之師不圖僥倖
punctuated: 猷，大原之功丕著。巡覩往跡，累重殊階。自三臺易於前朝，惟二府合於昭代。天廻斗柄，閣門鄰北闕之文昌；星轉宸垣，帷幄總中台之武庫。折衝樽俎，秉政鈞衡，自非經文緯武之才，曷稱出將入相之任？是以魏仁浦之當國，偉績猶存；陳堯叟之秉司，芳聲尚著。豈圖妙選，誤畀庸流？伏念臣衍，粗有朴忠，本無學術。濫登仕版，榮叨進士之科；徒讀父書，恪守先臣之業。甘心苦節，絕意干名。筮仕理刑，旋領祕丘之佐；再爲令尹，尋陞別駕之官。屢列薦書，忝稱良吏。乾州賜宴，遥承天語之温；淮使問名，特荷中朝之眷。承内降之旨，爰自封還；阻攻守之師，不圖僥倖。
translation_en:
…plans, and his achievement at Taiyuan was splendidly manifest. Reviewing the precedents of the past, one finds exceptional ranks repeatedly invested with weighty responsibilities. Since the Three Terraces were altered under the preceding dynasty, the Two Administrations alone have been united in this illustrious age. Heaven turns the handle of the Dipper: the cabinet gates adjoin Wenchang at the northern palace portals. The stars revolve within the imperial enclosure: the command tent directs the military arsenal of the Central Terrace. To overcome opponents at ceremonial banquets and hold the balance of government—unless one possesses the talent to order civil affairs and marshal military power, how could one be equal to serving as a general in the field and a chief minister at court? Thus, the great achievements of Wei Renpu when he directed the state endure, and the fine reputation of Chen Yaosou when he held office remains renowned. Who could have imagined that so discerning a selection would mistakenly confer appointment upon a mediocrity?
I humbly reflect that I, your servant Yan, possess only a little plain loyalty and have no learning or skill. Undeservedly entered upon the rolls of office, I was honored beyond my merits with success in the metropolitan graduate (jinshi) examination. I merely read my father’s books and conscientiously preserved the calling of my late father, your servant. Willingly embracing hardship and strict integrity, I abandoned all thought of seeking fame. I began my official career administering criminal justice and soon held an assistant post at Miqiu [?]. I twice served as magistrate and shortly afterward was promoted to administrative assistant. Repeatedly named in letters of recommendation, I was undeservedly acclaimed a good official. At an imperially bestowed banquet in Qianzhou, I received from afar the warmth of Your Majesty’s words; when an envoy in the Huai region asked my name [?], I was especially favored with the central court’s regard. Upon receiving an instruction issued from within the palace, I returned it under seal on my own initiative. I obstructed the forces assigned to attack and defense [?], without seeking any chance advantage.

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
辭右樞而補外但知清整自將犹內選以
簪官敢任吏胥滋弊獨以晋愚觸憲常包
答〔〕
覆載之仁不能死合隨時重倚賴乎
生成之德祥非鳳集詎希黃閣奇勳勇謝鷹揚
豈有白旄遠略省躬知懼愈深覆餗之懷
撫巳增慙莫遂循牆之請茲蓋伏遇
===
睿質天成
徽猷神授守
祖宗之家法文治聿臻
握海宇之輿圖武功時戢遇水旱而
心存民瘼
密禱禁廷憂西北而
念軫邊防
躬親騎射
威宣靈武羽干效順於虞階
禮御辟雍奎壁纏輝於孔廟
punctuated: 辭右樞而補外，但知清整自將；犹內選以簪官，敢任吏胥滋弊？獨以晋愚觸憲，常包答〔〕覆載之仁，不能死合隨時，重倚賴乎生成之德。祥非鳳集，詎希黃閣奇勳；勇謝鷹揚，豈有白旄遠略？省躬知懼，愈深覆餗之懷；撫巳增慙，莫遂循牆之請。茲蓋伏遇睿質天成，徽猷神授，守祖宗之家法，文治聿臻；握海宇之輿圖，武功時戢。遇水旱而心存民瘼，密禱禁廷；憂西北而念軫邊防，躬親騎射。威宣靈武，羽干效順於虞階；禮御辟雍，奎壁纏輝於孔廟。
translation_en:
…Declining the right-hand post in the military administration [?] and taking an appointment outside the capital, I knew only to conduct myself with integrity and discipline. Yet, selected for an appointment within the capital [?], how could I dare allow clerks to multiply abuses? Through my own rash stupidity [?] alone I transgressed the statutes. Ever embraced by a benevolence that shelters and sustains like Heaven and Earth [?], unable to repay it even in death [?], I rely still more heavily upon the virtue that gives life and brings all things to maturity. My auspicious qualities are no gathering of phoenixes: how could I hope for extraordinary achievements in the Yellow Hall of the grand councillors? My courage falls short of the soaring hawk: how could I possess far-reaching military strategies beneath the white command banner? Examining myself, I know fear, and feel ever more deeply the dread of overturning the sacrificial food through my inadequacy. Reflecting upon myself, I grow more ashamed, yet my plea to withdraw modestly along the wall has not been granted.
This is because I have humbly encountered Your Majesty, whose sagely qualities are perfected by Heaven and whose splendid counsels are divinely bestowed. Preserving the ancestral house laws, you have brought civil governance to fruition; holding the map of all the realm, you keep military force in restraint as circumstances permit. When floods and droughts occur, your heart dwells on the people’s suffering, and you pray privately within the palace. Concerned about the northwest, you give anxious thought to frontier defense and personally practice riding and archery. Your awe-inspiring might manifests itself in divinely potent martial power; those bearing feather plumes and shields display submission before the steps of Shun. With ritual propriety you preside at the Imperial Academy; the celestial lodges Kui and Bi shed their intertwined radiance upon the Temple of Confucius…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
堯歌擊壤祌化難名
舜治垂衣穆清有象
德巳聖而不自聖世巳安而若未安寤寐興懷
思集夔龍于沼上搜佇增歎欲收頗牧于
禁中惟此在
廷之賢悉出〔臣〕愚之右〔臣〕獨蒙
聖眷深激愚衷敢不仰酬
天地之恩俯效涓埃之報期調商鼎勉樹周楨
陰陽和而風雨時賛
===
一人之斡旋元化萬國賓而四夷服脩五伐以
控制遐方伏願
任賢勿貳
保治無虞
審蓄威昭德之機
操居重馭輕之柄
慮周天下敦恭儉以先民
明照日中撫豐亨而御世
惟精惟一
punctuated:
堯歌擊壤，祌化難名；舜治垂衣，穆清有象。德巳聖而不自聖，世巳安而若未安，寤寐興懷，思集夔龍于沼上；搜佇增歎，欲收頗牧于禁中。惟此在廷之賢，悉出〔臣〕愚之右。〔臣〕獨蒙聖眷，深激愚衷，敢不仰酬天地之恩，俯效涓埃之報？期調商鼎，勉樹周楨，陰陽和而風雨時，賛一人之斡旋元化；萬國賓而四夷服，脩五伐以控制遐方。
伏願任賢勿貳，保治無虞，審蓄威昭德之機，操居重馭輕之柄，慮周天下，敦恭儉以先民；明照日中，撫豐亨而御世，惟精惟一。
translation_en:
…As under Yao, songs accompany the game of striking the earth; your wondrous transforming influence [?] defies description. As under Shun, you govern with robes hanging loosely, giving visible form to serene and pure rule. Though your virtue is already sagely, you do not regard yourself as a sage; though the realm is already secure, you act as if it were not yet secure. Waking and sleeping, you ponder affairs, wishing to gather men like Kui and Long beside the palace pool. Searching and waiting, with mounting sighs [?], you wish to bring men like Lian Po and Li Mu into the palace. All these worthy men at court surpass your foolish servant. Yet your servant alone has received your sagely favor, which deeply stirs his humble heart. How could I fail to repay, looking upward, your grace as vast as Heaven and Earth, and offer, from below, a recompense as slight as a drop of water or a speck of dust? I hope to blend the flavors in the Shang cauldron and strive to establish pillars of support like those of Zhou. May yin and yang be harmonious, and wind and rain arrive in season, as I assist the One Man—the sovereign—in directing the primal processes of creation. May the myriad states render homage and the peoples of the four quarters submit, as the five punitive expeditions are duly undertaken to bring distant regions under control.
I humbly wish that you would employ worthy men without wavering and preserve good order free from peril; discern the proper occasions for husbanding your might and displaying your virtue; and hold fast to the authority by which the weighty center directs the outlying parts. Let your concern encompass all under Heaven, and cultivate reverence and frugality to lead the people. Let your insight shine like the sun at noon, and preside over abundance and prosperity in governing the world. Be ever discerning and single-minded…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
天命𠖥勑於時幾
允武允文
道化覃敷於中外䜟
皇圖於有永綿
聖壽於無疆臣無任瞻
天仰
聖感激屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
===
第叁場
策五道
第一問
趙賢
同考試官教諭劉　批〔大學帝王心學所載洪惟我〕
聖祖
皇上獨得道統眞傳遠邁堯舜是以
留神衍義先後一揆乎能鋪張而揚厲之其忝泳
punctuated:
天命𠖥勑於時幾，允武允文，道化覃敷於中外，䜟皇圖於有永，綿聖壽於無疆。臣無任瞻天仰聖、感激屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。

第叁場，策五道。

第一問。
趙賢。

同考試官教諭劉　批〔大學，帝王心學所載。洪惟我〕聖祖、皇上獨得道統眞傳，遠邁堯舜，是以留神衍義，先後一揆乎！能鋪張而揚厲之，其忝泳
translation_en:
…Heaven’s mandate graciously admonishes concerning the subtle beginnings of events [?]. Truly martial and truly cultured, your transforming Way spreads far and wide, within and beyond the realm, foretelling [?] the everlasting endurance of the imperial dominion and extending Your Majesty’s sacred longevity without limit. Your servant, gazing toward Heaven and looking up to Your Majesty, cannot contain his profound gratitude and trembling reverence. I respectfully submit this memorial to express my thanks for Your Majesty’s hearing.

Third Session: Five Policy Questions.

First Question.
Zhao Xian.

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: 〔The Great Learning records the learning of the mind practiced by emperors and kings. Magnificent indeed are our〕 sagely imperial progenitor and our reigning emperor, who alone have received the true transmission of the succession of the Way, far surpassing Yao and Shun. Thus, in devoting their attention to the Expanded Meaning (Yanyi), predecessor and successor follow the same standard! You can expound and extol this at length; perhaps you have steeped yourself [?] in …

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
聖化而有得者乎
同考試官教諭程　批
聖學淵微未易窺測名言子能以一日述須明備難矣中州傑士非子而誰
同考試官教諭朱　批〔此策揄揚我〕
聖祖心學之妙
皇上道統之傳明粹可式敬爲子録之
考試官教諭胡　批〔文俯思深對揚策肯無踰子〕
考試官學正史　批〔忠敬之意溢然宜録〕
道之大原其出於天而統於
===
聖乎惟涵之於心者極其至精斯渙之於文者
極其至粹夫惟至精也則
聖德緝熙而統會於宥密
大業由此而日隆夫惟至粹也則
皇極敷言而垂憲於宇宙
盛德由此而日顯以淵懿端純之則而肇駿龐
高朗之休以開拓積累之勤而衍昌明弘
遠之緒是心也其契帝王道統之傳者乎
是文也其盡古今授受之妙者乎以此法
punctuated:
聖化而有得者乎？
同考試官教諭程，批：聖學淵微，未易窺測。名言，子能以一日述須明備，難矣！中州傑士，非子而誰？
同考試官教諭朱，批〔此策揄揚我〕聖祖心學之妙、皇上道統之傳，明粹可式，敬爲子録之。
考試官教諭胡，批〔文俯思深，對揚策肯，無踰子〕
考試官學正史，批〔忠敬之意溢然，宜録〕
道之大原，其出於天而統於聖乎？惟涵之於心者極其至精，斯渙之於文者極其至粹。夫惟至精也，則聖德緝熙而統會於宥密，大業由此而日隆；夫惟至粹也，則皇極敷言而垂憲於宇宙，盛德由此而日顯。以淵懿端純之則，而肇駿龐高朗之休；以開拓積累之勤，而衍昌明弘遠之緒。是心也，其契帝王道統之傳者乎？是文也，其盡古今授受之妙者乎？以此法
translation_en:
…one who has gained something from the sagely transforming influence?

Associate Examiner Cheng, Instructor, comments: “Sagely learning is profound and subtle, and not easily fathomed. These are fine words; that you could, in a single day, produce an exposition so clear and complete [?] is difficult indeed! Who but you is an outstanding scholar of Zhongzhou?”

Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: 〔“This policy essay extols〕 the wondrous learning of the mind of our Sagely Progenitor and His Majesty’s transmission of the succession of the Way. Clear and refined, it can serve as a model. I respectfully record it for you.”

Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: 〔“The writing is [?] and the thought profound. In responding to and extolling the substance of the policy question [?], none surpasses you.”〕

Examiner Shi, School Instructor, comments: 〔“Loyalty and reverence overflow throughout; it merits selection.”〕

Does not the great source of the Way issue from Heaven and find its unity in the sage? Only when what is nurtured within the mind reaches the utmost spiritual refinement can what pours forth in writing attain the utmost purity. Through this utmost refinement, sagely virtue grows ever more luminous and comes together in profound stillness; the great undertaking thereby grows more exalted each day.
