Through this utmost purity, the august standard is expounded in words and establishes enduring models throughout the cosmos; abundant virtue thereby becomes more manifest each day. Through principles profound, admirable, upright, and pure, magnificent and lofty blessings are inaugurated; through the diligent work of opening new ground and building upon accumulated achievements, a flourishing, enlightened, expansive, and enduring legacy is extended. Does not this mind accord with the transmission of the succession of the Way among emperors and kings? Does not this writing fully express the subtlety of its transmission and reception, past and present? With this to emulate …

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
天則垂世
立極而啓佑乎後人作者之謂聖也以此法
祖則
世德作求而對揚乎
前烈述之者之謂明也
作述一道後先一揆知此則我
聖祖心學之妙
皇上道統之傳可得而颺言矣請徵陳之書曰
天降下民作之君作之師凡有天下者不
皆有君師之責者乎吾見大道在斯世三
===
極賴之而立心學在聖人道統賴之而承
自古聖帝明王以謨以訓以箴以戒無非
本諸此而已求諸五帝之世黄帝嘗有輿
几之箴矣一傳而執中再傳而精一其統
同其道同也求諸三王之世大禹嘗有夏
氏之箴矣商繼而建中周繼而建極其統
同其道同也至吾孔子統集羣聖而删述
六經作爲大學一書首之明德新民而極
punctuated: 天，則垂世立極，而啓佑乎後人，作者之謂聖也。以此法祖，則世德作求，而對揚乎前烈，述之者之謂明也。作述一道，後先一揆。知此，則我聖祖心學之妙、皇上道統之傳，可得而颺言矣。請徵陳之。《書》曰：「天降下民，作之君，作之師。」凡有天下者，不皆有君師之責者乎？吾見大道在斯世，三極賴之而立；心學在聖人，道統賴之而承。自古聖帝明王，以謨以訓，以箴以戒，無非本諸此而已。求諸五帝之世，黄帝嘗有輿几之箴矣。一傳而執中，再傳而精一，其統同，其道同也。求諸三王之世，大禹嘗有夏氏之箴矣。商繼而建中，周繼而建極，其統同，其道同也。至吾孔子，統集羣聖而删述六經，作爲《大學》一書，首之明德新民，而極
translation_en: …Heaven, thereby establishing the supreme standard for generations to come and enlightening and aiding posterity: one who originates is called a sage. By taking the ancestors as models through this, one carries forward their virtue from generation to generation and extols their glorious achievements: one who transmits is called enlightened. Origination and transmission follow one Way; those who come before and those who follow conform to a single standard. Understanding this, we may openly proclaim the subtlety of our Sagely Ancestor’s learning of the mind and His Majesty’s transmission of the succession of the Way. Allow me to adduce evidence and set it forth. The Book of Documents says: “Heaven brought forth the common people and established rulers and teachers for them.” Do not all who possess All-under-Heaven bear the responsibilities of ruler and teacher? I see that the Great Way exists in this world, and the Three Ultimates—Heaven, Earth, and humanity—depend upon it for their establishment; the learning of the mind resides in the sages, and the succession of the Way depends upon it for its transmission. Since antiquity, the counsels, instructions, admonitions, and warnings of sage emperors and enlightened kings have all been rooted in this alone. Looking to the age of the Five Emperors, Huangdi once had admonitions inscribed on his carriage and armrest. With one transmission came holding fast to the mean; with a second came refinement and single-mindedness. Their succession was the same, and their Way was the same. Looking to the age of the Three Kings, Yu the Great once had the admonitions of the Xia house. The Shang succeeded and established the mean; the Zhou succeeded and established the supreme standard. Their succession was the same, and their Way was the same. When it came to our Confucius, he gathered together the heritage of all the sages, edited and transmitted the Six Classics, and composed the book Great Learning, beginning with making bright virtue manifest and renewing the people, and culminating in…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
於止至善始於格致誠正而終之脩齊治
平規模廣大節目詳明帝之所以帝者此
也王之所以王者此也夫何去古既遠聖
學就湮大道之要無聞而至治之澤不被
雖韓愈之原道李翺之復性要皆遺而未
畵駁而不精道之不明不行也不有自哉
宋儒真德秀氏作爲衍義羽翼聖經觀其
綱則有二焉其目則有四焉先之以典謨
訓誥與思齊之詩家人之卦子思孟子荀
===
况董仲舒楊雄周敦頤之說言帝王爲治
之序也次之以堯舜禹湯文武商宗周成
漢唐以下數君之賢言帝王爲學之綱也
至於聖功始於窮理而曰明道術辨人材
焉窮理可以盡性而曰審治體察民情焉
誠意正心不可不務也而崇敬畏戒逸欲
者其要矣脩身齊家不可不急也而謹言
行正威儀重配匹嚴內治定國本教戚屬
者其切矣是言出於性命道德者必鉤其
punctuated:
於止至善，始於格致誠正，而終之脩齊治平。規模廣大，節目詳明。帝之所以帝者，此也；王之所以王者，此也。夫何去古既遠，聖學就湮，大道之要無聞，而至治之澤不被？雖韓愈之《原道》、李翺之《復性》，要皆遺而未畵，駁而不精。道之不明不行也，不有自哉？
宋儒真德秀氏作爲《衍義》，羽翼聖經。觀其綱則有二焉，其目則有四焉。先之以典謨訓誥與《思齊》之詩、《家人》之卦、子思、孟子、荀况、董仲舒、楊雄、周敦頤之說，言帝王爲治之序也；次之以堯舜禹湯文武、商宗周成、漢唐以下數君之賢，言帝王爲學之綱也。至於聖功始於窮理，而曰明道術、辨人材焉；窮理可以盡性，而曰審治體、察民情焉。誠意正心不可不務也，而崇敬畏、戒逸欲者其要矣。脩身齊家不可不急也，而謹言行、正威儀、重配匹、嚴內治、定國本、教戚屬者其切矣。是言出於性命道德者，必鉤其
translation_en:
…in resting in the highest good, beginning with the investigation of things, extension of knowledge, sincerity of intention, and rectification of the mind, and ending with cultivation of the person, regulation of the family, governance of the state, and bringing peace to the world. Its scope is vast, and its particular provisions are detailed and clear. This is what makes a sage emperor an emperor and a true king a king. Why, then, as antiquity grew distant, did the learning of the sages fall into obscurity, so that the essentials of the Great Way went unheard and the blessings of perfect government failed to reach the people? Even Han Yu’s Inquiry into the Way and Li Ao’s Returning to One’s Nature were, in the end, incomplete and insufficiently delineated [?], mixed in doctrine and lacking refinement. Surely there are reasons why the Way has neither been understood nor put into practice!
The Song Confucian Zhen Dexiu composed the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning to support the sages’ classic. Examining its structure, we find two guiding divisions and four principal headings. It begins with the canons, counsels, instructions, and announcements of the Book of Documents, together with the poem “Si Qi” (“Emulating the Exemplary”), the hexagram “Jiaren” (“The Family”), and the teachings of Zisi, Mengzi, Xun Kuang, Dong Zhongshu, Yang Xiong, and Zhou Dunyi, explaining the sequence by which emperors and kings establish good government. It then treats the worthiness of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu, the revered Shang rulers and King Cheng of Zhou, and several rulers of the Han, Tang, and later periods, explaining the guiding principles of imperial and royal learning. As for the work of becoming a sage, it begins with investigating principles; hence the headings “Clarifying the Way and Its Arts” and “Discerning Human Talent.” Investigating principles enables one to realize one’s nature fully; hence “Examining the Structure of Government” and “Observing the People’s Circumstances.” Making one’s intentions sincere and rectifying one’s mind are indispensable tasks, whose essentials are fostering reverence and awe and guarding against ease and desire. Cultivating oneself and regulating one’s family are urgent tasks, whose pressing concerns are exercising care in speech and conduct, maintaining proper dignity and deportment, giving due weight to the choice of a spouse, strictly regulating the palace household, securing the foundation of the state through the succession, and educating imperial relatives. Thus, whenever statements concern human nature, Heaven’s mandate, the Way, and virtue, he invariably probes their …

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
玄事關乎治亂安危者必提其要表君子
小人之情狀如以鑑而別衆形裒周程張
朱之講明猶揭囊而收百物非擴前聖所
未發而爲後聖之法程者耶夫何一陳於
理宗端平之朝祗悅而不繹再見於吳澄
進講之日亦善而不行是致治之要道雖
不售於當時而心源之相契其將有待於
昭代者乎恭惟我
太祖高皇帝
===
睿智遠邁於百王
精義妙契乎千古
兢業恒存
幽獨之地凛天監之在茲
寅長中切
燕閒之時惕朽索之是戒投戈講藝殫精
帝學因宋濂之請
命左右大書衍義揭之廡壁更
令濂條析衍義中司馬遷之論濂進曰人主能
punctuated:
玄；事關乎治亂安危者，必提其要。表君子小人之情狀，如以鑑而別衆形；裒周程張朱之講明，猶揭囊而收百物。非擴前聖所未發，而爲後聖之法程者耶？夫何一陳於理宗端平之朝，祗悅而不繹；再見於吳澄進講之日，亦善而不行？是致治之要道，雖不售於當時，而心源之相契，其將有待於昭代者乎？

恭惟我太祖高皇帝，睿智遠邁於百王，精義妙契乎千古。兢業恒存，幽獨之地，凛天監之在茲；寅長中切，燕閒之時，惕朽索之是戒。投戈講藝，殫精帝學。因宋濂之請，命左右大書衍義，揭之廡壁；更令濂條析衍義中司馬遷之論。濂進曰：「人主能
translation_en:
…their profundities; in matters concerning order and disorder, security and danger, it invariably brings out the essentials. It displays the dispositions and conduct of gentlemen and petty men as though using a mirror to distinguish their many forms. It gathers the elucidations of Zhou, Cheng, Zhang, and Zhu as though opening a bag to collect a hundred things. Does it not expand upon what the earlier sages had left unexpressed and provide a model for later sages? Why, then, when it was first presented at the court of Emperor Lizong during the Duanping reign period, did he merely delight in it without exploring its implications? And when it appeared again in Wu Cheng’s court lectures, why was it likewise approved but not put into practice? Although this essential way of achieving good government found no acceptance in its own time, might its meeting with a kindred mind have awaited our illustrious dynasty?

We reverently consider our Emperor Taizu Gao, whose sagely wisdom far surpassed that of the hundred kings, and whose subtle grasp of essential principles accorded wondrously with the wisdom of all ages. Ever vigilant and conscientious, even in private solitude he stood in awe of Heaven’s watchfulness over him. Reverence pressed deeply within him [?]; even in moments of leisure he remained alert to the warning conveyed by a rotten rope. Setting aside his spear, he expounded the learned arts and devoted all his energies to the learning of emperors. At Song Lian’s request, he ordered his attendants to write out the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning (Yanyi) in large characters and display it on the corridor walls. He further ordered Lian to analyze, point by point, the discussion of Sima Qian in the Extended Meaning. Lian submitted: “If the ruler can…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
以義理養性則非僻不能侵興學校教民
則外侮無從作
聖祖因謂濂曰朕之爲君上畏
天地下畏兆民兢兢業業不敢自逸又嘗覩衍
義蠱錯之語德秀解之曰人君不窮兵黷
武則能生之而不傷
聖祖顧謂侍臣曰蠱錯之言其所該甚廣眞氏
之言其所見甚切朕嘗思爲君恤民所重者
兵與刑爾濫刑者陷人於無辜黷武者置人
於危地有國者所宜深戒也由前則心正身
===
脩而敬畏尤
愼獨審幾之本也其誠意之實功乎由後則
物格知至而兵刑尤畏
天畏民之要也其治平之絜矩乎是至精之涵
於心者
聖學淵源有取於盤銘之日新至粹之渙於文
者
天葩炳燿深合乎丑傷之敬勝固駕湯武而竝
punctuated:
以義理養性，則非僻不能侵；興學校教民，則外侮無從作。聖祖因謂濂曰：「朕之爲君，上畏天地，下畏兆民，兢兢業業，不敢自逸。」又嘗覩《衍義》蠱錯之語，德秀解之曰：「人君不窮兵黷武，則能生之而不傷。」聖祖顧謂侍臣曰：「蠱錯之言，其所該甚廣；眞氏之言，其所見甚切。朕嘗思爲君恤民，所重者兵與刑爾。濫刑者陷人於無辜，黷武者置人於危地，有國者所宜深戒也。」
由前則心正身脩，而敬畏尤愼獨審幾之本也，其誠意之實功乎？由後則物格知至，而兵刑尤畏天畏民之要也，其治平之絜矩乎？是至精之涵於心者，聖學淵源有取於盤銘之日新；至粹之渙於文者，天葩炳燿，深合乎丑傷之敬勝，固駕湯武而竝
translation_en:
…by nourishing his nature with moral principle, he prevents perversity and wrongdoing from intruding; by establishing schools to educate the people, he leaves foreign aggression no opening to arise. The Sagely Progenitor thereupon told Lian: “As ruler, above I stand in awe of Heaven and Earth, and below I stand in awe of the myriad people. Ever watchful and diligent, I dare not indulge in ease.” He also once read the words of Gu Cuo [?; apparently Chao Cuo] in the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning, which Dexiu explained as follows: “If the ruler does not exhaust his forces and recklessly wage war, he can sustain the people’s lives without harming them.” The Sagely Progenitor turned to his attendant officials and said: “Gu Cuo’s [?] words embrace a very broad range; Master Zhen’s insight is very penetrating. I have often reflected that, in a ruler’s care for the people, the weightiest matters are warfare and punishment. Those who punish indiscriminately ensnare innocent people; those who wage war recklessly place people in peril. Those who govern a state must guard most earnestly against these things.”
From the former, the mind is rectified and the person cultivated; reverent awe is above all the foundation for vigilance in solitude and discernment of the first stirrings of action. Is this not the concrete achievement of making one’s intentions sincere? From the latter, things are investigated and knowledge brought to completion; warfare and punishment are especially crucial matters in standing in awe of Heaven and the people. Is this not the principle of the measuring square through which the state is governed and the realm brought to peace? Thus, in the utmost refinement nurtured within his heart, the sources of his sagely learning drew upon the daily renewal enjoined by the inscription on the bathing basin. In the utmost purity displayed in his writings, his celestial blossoms shone brilliantly, deeply according with the notion that reverence prevails in “chou shang” [?]. Indeed, he surpassed Tang and Wu and stood alongside …

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
堯舜矣則
聖祖所以得道統之傳者不於是而可見哉至
我
皇上憲
天以凝命法
祖而臨民惜大禹之寸陰與高宗之舊學凡大
而極於典謨之奧細而苞夫史册之繁罔
不
洞覽雖
===
睿哲
天授固不待於師資而
虛心樂善乃留心於衍義觀
諭輔臣曰是書綱舉目張治亂興亡罔不該括
朕勉循是言爲脩已治人之則豈不大有裨
益又曰匪徒知之實欲行之尚賴卿等竭誠
協恭輔導朕躬則衍義之功不在眞氏而在
卿等矣因侍臣進講之餘
默契化源乃賦詩一章曰帝王所圖治務學當
punctuated: 堯舜矣，則聖祖所以得道統之傳者，不於是而可見哉？至我皇上憲天以凝命，法祖而臨民，惜大禹之寸陰，與高宗之舊學。凡大而極於典謨之奧，細而苞夫史册之繁，罔不洞覽。雖睿哲天授，固不待於師資，而虛心樂善，乃留心於衍義。觀諭輔臣曰：「是書綱舉目張，治亂興亡罔不該括。朕勉循是言，爲脩已治人之則，豈不大有裨益？」又曰：「匪徒知之，實欲行之。尚賴卿等竭誠協恭，輔導朕躬，則衍義之功不在眞氏，而在卿等矣。」因侍臣進講之餘，默契化源，乃賦詩一章曰：「帝王所圖治，務學當
translation_en:
…Yao and Shun. Is it not evident from this how the sagely ancestor received the transmission of the Way? As for our present Emperor, he models himself on Heaven to secure the Mandate and follows his ancestors in governing the people. He cherishes every moment, as did the Great Yu, and values former learning, as did Gaozong. From the profound subtleties of the Canons and Counsels to the manifold details of the historical records, there is nothing he has not thoroughly examined. Although his sagacity is Heaven-bestowed and assuredly does not depend on teachers, he remains receptive and delights in goodness, giving particular attention to the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning (Daxue yanyi).
Consider his instruction to his assisting ministers: “This book sets forth its main principles and unfolds their particulars, encompassing everything concerning order and disorder, rise and decline. If I earnestly follow these words as the standard for cultivating myself and governing others, will this not be of great benefit?” He also said: “I wish not merely to understand them, but truly to put them into practice. I must still rely on you, my ministers, to devote your utmost sincerity and cooperate reverently in assisting and guiding me. Then the merit of the Extended Meaning will lie not with Master Zhen, but with you.” After the attendant ministers’ lectures, he inwardly apprehended the source of transforming influence and composed a poem, saying: “Emperors and kings aspire to good government; diligent learning should…”

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
爲先下作民之主上乃承乎
天致治貴有本本端化自平人君所學者其序
有後前正心誠其意志定必不遷吾志旣能
定理道從復顚身脩本心正家國治同然國
治乃昭明萬邦斯協焉於變帝堯典思齊文
王篇萬化脩身始朕念方拳拳於是親灑
宸翰
賜二三輔臣
令賡和之彙爲一帙而名曰
===
翊學詩自今觀之首言務學者卽顧諟之謂
也繼言定志者卽知止之謂也曰誠曰正
曰脩者雖異矣而明德之功未始不同曰
家曰國曰萬邦名雖殊矣而新民之理未
嘗不一言天則嚴其心之所自出言民則
謹其心之所由施治期於於變非祖述帝
堯之峻德者耶詩詠乎思齊非儀刑文王
之敬止者耶
本源澄徹而探之極其至精
punctuated:
爲先。下作民之主，上乃承乎天。致治貴有本，本端化自平。人君所學者，其序有後前。正心誠其意，志定必不遷。吾志旣能定，理道從復顚。身脩本心正，家國治同然。國治乃昭明，萬邦斯協焉。於變帝堯典，思齊文王篇。萬化脩身始，朕念方拳拳。」於是親灑宸翰，賜二三輔臣，令賡和之，彙爲一帙，而名曰《翊學詩》。
自今觀之，首言務學者，卽顧諟之謂也。繼言定志者，卽知止之謂也。曰誠、曰正、曰脩者，雖異矣，而明德之功未始不同；曰家、曰國、曰萬邦，名雖殊矣，而新民之理未嘗不一。言天，則嚴其心之所自出；言民，則謹其心之所由施。治期於於變，非祖述帝堯之峻德者耶？詩詠乎思齊，非儀刑文王之敬止者耶？
本源澄徹，而探之極其至精。
translation_en:
…take precedence.
Below, one serves as lord of the people;
Above, one receives Heaven’s charge.
Bringing about good government requires a foundation;
When the foundation is upright, transforming influence naturally brings peace.
What the ruler of men must learn
Has its proper sequence, earlier and later.
Rectify the mind and make the intention sincere;
Once resolve is fixed, it surely will not shift.
Once my resolve can be fixed,
The way of principle follows, restoring what was overturned [?].
Cultivating the person rests on rectifying the mind;
Ordering the family and state follows the same principle.
When the state is ordered, all becomes manifestly bright,
And the myriad states are brought into harmony.
“Oh, the transformation!”—the Canon of Emperor Yao;
“Thinking of the worthy”—the ode to King Wen.
All transforming influence begins with cultivating the person;
My thoughts now dwell earnestly upon this.”

He then personally committed the poem to his imperial calligraphy and bestowed it upon his chief ministers, ordering them to compose matching poems. These were gathered into one volume entitled Poems to Aid Learning (Yixue shi).

Viewed from the present, its opening injunction to devote oneself to learning means keeping bright virtue constantly in view. Its subsequent injunction to fix one’s resolve means knowing where to rest. Although “making sincere,” “rectifying,” and “cultivating” differ in expression, the work of making bright virtue manifest has never differed. Although “family,” “state,” and “myriad states” bear different names, the principle of renewing the people has always been one. Speaking of Heaven expresses reverence for the source from which this mind issues; speaking of the people expresses care over the application of this mind. In aspiring to the transformation celebrated in “Oh, the transformation!”, does he not follow and transmit Emperor Yao’s lofty virtue? In singing of “Thinking of the Worthy,” does he not take as his model King Wen’s abiding reverence?

The fundamental source is clear and limpid, and his exploration of it reaches its utmost subtlety…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
眞機動盪而發之極其至粹帝王之所授受
聖祖之所述作固會其全而無遺闡其妙而殆
盡矣則
皇上所以得道統之傳者又不於是而可見哉
由是
大典微言昭如日星
鴻恩濊澤同乎
天地遵道者丕變覩
聖者奕新親賢樂利之化著孝弟仁讓之風行
以是而言法
===
天則
天心合而裁成輔相範圍彌綸贊化育之不及
以是而言法
祖則
祖德孚而長養培植開廣流衍增創造於維新
玄化
鴻庥淳曜充溢其始也法
天旣則克配乎
punctuated:
眞機動盪，而發之極其至粹。帝王之所授受，聖祖之所述作，固會其全而無遺，闡其妙而殆盡矣。則皇上所以得道統之傳者，又不於是而可見哉？
由是，大典微言昭如日星，鴻恩濊澤同乎天地。遵道者丕變，覩聖者奕新。親賢樂利之化著，孝弟仁讓之風行。以是而言法天，則天心合，而裁成輔相、範圍彌綸，贊化育之不及；以是而言法祖，則祖德孚，而長養培植、開廣流衍，增創造於維新。玄化鴻庥，淳曜充溢。其始也法天，旣則克配乎
translation_en:
…the true animating impulse stirs, and its expression attains the utmost purity. What the sage emperors and kings transmitted and received, and what the Sagely Ancestor expounded and composed, assuredly encompass the whole without omission and elucidate its subtleties almost exhaustively. Is this not also where we can see how His Majesty has received the transmission of the Way?
Thus the subtle teachings of the great canon shine as clearly as the sun and stars, and His Majesty’s immense grace and abundant beneficence equal Heaven and Earth. Those who follow the Way undergo a great transformation; those who behold the sage are splendidly renewed. The transforming influence that leads people to cherish the worthy, delight in happiness, and enjoy its benefits becomes manifest, and the practices of filial devotion, fraternal respect, benevolence, and deference prevail. If we speak of this as modeling oneself on Heaven, then his heart accords with Heaven’s heart: he shapes and assists its processes, encompasses and comprehensively orders them, and supplements what remains unfulfilled in its transforming and nourishing activity. If we speak of this as modeling oneself on the ancestor, then the ancestor’s virtue finds its fulfillment: he nurtures and cultivates, broadens and perpetuates, adding to the founding achievement through renewal. Mysterious transformation and vast blessings, pure radiance, fill all things. At the outset he modeled himself on Heaven; thereafter he could match …

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
天矣其始也法
祖既則有光乎
祖矣可見
聖祖之學舉其大而
皇上之學會其精信乎作述一道後先一揆者
歟雖然周公頌文王之德而作清廟於頌
首孔子贊周監於二代郁郁乎文而願從
之臣子逢時之幸固如是也愚也生際
昌時涵泳
===
聖化鋪張揚厲之心雖激於中然聞簫韶者知
舜德之難名覩河洛者知禹功之莫及果
何以塞明問也惟執事進而敎之
第二問
王家卿
同考試官敎諭吳　批〔華以明時豫以作樂乃古人制作之精意察乎天地者也子能槩以理氣數而不臭不蠡殆覩其深者耶〕
考試官敎諭胡　批〔此策塲中類襲浮套應問〕
punctuated:
天矣。其始也法祖，既則有光乎祖矣。可見聖祖之學舉其大，而皇上之學會其精，信乎作述一道、後先一揆者歟！雖然，周公頌文王之德而作《清廟》於頌首，孔子贊周監於二代、郁郁乎文而願從之，臣子逢時之幸固如是也。愚也生際昌時，涵泳聖化，鋪張揚厲之心雖激於中，然聞簫韶者知舜德之難名，覩河洛者知禹功之莫及，果何以塞明問也？惟執事進而敎之。
第二問
王家卿
同考試官敎諭吳批〔華以明時，豫以作樂，乃古人制作之精意，察乎天地者也。子能槩以理氣數，而不臭不蠡，殆覩其深者耶？〕
考試官敎諭胡批〔此策塲中類襲浮套應問〕
translation_en:
…Heaven. At the outset he modeled himself on his ancestors; thereafter he brought glory to them. Thus we can see that the learning of the Sagely Ancestor embraced its grand essentials, while the learning of His Majesty brings together its finest subtleties. Truly, creating and transmitting follow a single Way, and predecessors and successors apply the same standard!
Nevertheless, the Duke of Zhou praised King Wen’s virtue and composed “The Pure Temple,” placing it first among the Hymns. Confucius praised Zhou for looking to the two preceding dynasties and for its richly flourishing culture, and wished to follow it. Such indeed is the good fortune of a subject who encounters a propitious age. I, in my ignorance, was born in a flourishing age and am steeped in the sage’s transforming influence. Though the desire to expound and exalt it stirs within me, those who hear the Shao music know how difficult it is to describe Shun’s virtue, and those who behold the He and Luo rivers know that Yu’s achievements cannot be equaled. How, then, can I adequately answer your discerning question? I can only hope that you, sir, will bring me forward and instruct me.
Second Question
Wang Jiaqing
Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: 〔“‘Hua’ serves to clarify the seasons [?], and ‘Yu’ to make music: these express the subtle intent behind the institutions of the ancients, who discerned Heaven and Earth. You can encompass this through principle, vital energy, and number, without ‘smelling’ or ‘measuring with a gourd’ [?]. Perhaps you have perceived its depths?”〕
Comment by Examiner Hu, Instructor: 〔“In this policy-essay examination, candidates generally copy empty conventional formulas to answer the questions…”〕

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
殊無心得之論知曆樂本原而文更藻潤者僅見此
作是用錄之
曆合一之理塲中知者絕少子能合而一之歸于自
然可與語制作矣
考試官學正史　批〔以律起曆以曆驗律此律〕
明於天地自然之數與氣而後可以窺制
作之原察於天地自然之理而後可以達
制作之妙盈天地間氣與數而已而理實
主宰之得其數與氣而不得其理則所謂
===
數者不過推測占步之遺術而已爾所謂
氣者不過聲響節奏之繁音而已爾其何
以欽若乾象協和神人弼成雍熙泰和之
治哉知此則知治曆明時者固當知曆數
之運而曆之理尤所當明作樂崇德者固
當求聲氣之元而樂之理尤所當察矣執
事發策下詢承學之意或在于此且曆果
何始乎神農以前尚已黃帝考定星曆建
立五行起消息正閏餘于時撓成擅其術
punctuated:
殊無心得之論，知曆樂本原而文更藻潤者，僅見此作，是用錄之。
曆合一之理，塲中知者絕少。子能合而一之，歸于自然，可與語制作矣。
考試官學正史　批〔以律起曆，以曆驗律，此律〕
明於天地自然之數與氣，而後可以窺制作之原；察於天地自然之理，而後可以達制作之妙。盈天地間，氣與數而已，而理實主宰之。得其數與氣而不得其理，則所謂數者，不過推測占步之遺術而已爾；所謂氣者，不過聲響節奏之繁音而已爾。其何以欽若乾象，協和神人，弼成雍熙泰和之治哉？知此，則知治曆明時者，固當知曆數之運，而曆之理尤所當明；作樂崇德者，固當求聲氣之元，而樂之理尤所當察矣。執事發策下詢承學之意，或在于此。且曆果何始乎？神農以前尚已。黃帝考定星曆，建立五行，起消息，正閏餘。于時撓成擅其術，
translation_en:
…arguments utterly lacking in personal insight. This is the only composition I have seen that understands the foundations of calendrical science and music and also possesses an elegant, polished style; hence its inclusion here.
Very few in the examination hall understand the principle of unifying calendrical science [with pitch standards?]. You can bring them together as one and trace them back to what is naturally so; with you one may discuss the establishment of institutions.
Examiner Shi, School Instructor, comments: 〔“Derive the calendar from pitch standards, and verify pitch standards through the calendar: these pitch standards…”〕
Only after understanding the natural numbers and vital energies of Heaven and Earth can one glimpse the origins of institutional creation; only after discerning the natural principles of Heaven and Earth can one comprehend its subtleties. What fills the space between Heaven and Earth is simply vital energy and number, yet principle truly governs them. If one grasps number and vital energy without grasping their principle, then what one calls number amounts merely to inherited techniques of conjecture and astronomical calculation, and what one calls vital energy amounts merely to a profusion of sounds, rhythms, and measures. How could these enable one reverently to follow celestial phenomena, harmonize spirits and humans, and help bring about flourishing government in supreme concord?
Understanding this, one knows that those who regulate the calendar and clarify the seasons must indeed understand the workings of calendrical numbers, but must above all elucidate the principles of the calendar. Those who create music to exalt virtue must indeed seek the source of sound and vital energy, but must above all discern the principles of music. Perhaps this is your intention, honored examiners, in issuing policy questions and condescending to inquire of us students.
Where, then, did calendrical science actually begin? Let us leave aside the period before Shennong. The Yellow Emperor investigated and established stellar and calendrical calculations, instituted the Five Phases, determined the cycles of waxing and waning, and corrected intercalation and residual fractions. At that time, Nao and Cheng [?] excelled in these arts…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
羲和專其業神降嘉穀民物阜康天地之
數正也嗣是而後舜受堯禪首察璣衡是
即堯欽若昊天敬授民時意也唐虞之際
其慎重星曆也如此降自夏商率皆是重
至周則有馮相氏掌日月星辰之次辨其
叙事以會天位保章氏掌志五物之變動
以詔救政訪序事焉其所以步時序之常
占象緯之異本五行以敬五事而休徵咎
徵寓焉職任之重何如也秦不師古慢天
===
虐民而星曆之官遂廢乃緣鄒衍五德之
運而自爲水德以亥爲正以十爲紀意棄
三正何其悖也漢興脩復古制改更正朔
曆凡五變張蒼用顓帝劉歆作三統李梵
造四分劉洪有乾象而唐都洛下閎鄧平
輩分部運筭術各不同惟司馬遷之太初
最稱精密志所謂日月如合璧五星如連
珠蓋有得于曆元也獨恨夫古未遠而保
章馮相之職竟莫之復此馬遷所以有史
punctuated: 羲和專其業，神降嘉穀，民物阜康，天地之數正也。嗣是而後，舜受堯禪，首察璣衡，是即堯欽若昊天、敬授民時意也。唐虞之際，其慎重星曆也如此。降自夏商，率皆是重。至周，則有馮相氏掌日月星辰之次，辨其叙事，以會天位；保章氏掌志五物之變動，以詔救政、訪序事焉。其所以步時序之常，占象緯之異，本五行以敬五事，而休徵咎徵寓焉。職任之重何如也！秦不師古，慢天虐民，而星曆之官遂廢，乃緣鄒衍五德之運，而自爲水德，以亥爲正，以十爲紀，意棄三正，何其悖也！漢興，脩復古制，改更正朔，曆凡五變。張蒼用顓帝，劉歆作三統，李梵造四分，劉洪有乾象，而唐都、洛下閎、鄧平輩分部運筭，術各不同。惟司馬遷之太初最稱精密，志所謂「日月如合璧，五星如連珠」，蓋有得于曆元也。獨恨夫古未遠，而保章、馮相之職竟莫之復，此馬遷所以有史
translation_en:
…Xi and He devoted themselves to this work; the spirits sent down fine grain, and the people and all living things flourished in peace, because the numerical order of Heaven and Earth was correctly established. Thereafter, when Shun received the throne through Yao’s abdication, he first examined the jade astronomical instrument and its sighting tube. This embodied Yao’s intention of reverently following August Heaven and respectfully communicating the seasons to the people. Such was the care accorded astronomy and calendrical calculation in the age of Yao and Shun. Under the Xia and Shang, these matters generally continued to receive such attention. By the Zhou, the Astronomer (Fengxiang shi) oversaw the successive positions of the sun, moon, and stars, distinguishing their orderly courses to correlate the celestial positions. The Astrologer (Baozhang shi) recorded changes in the five kinds of celestial phenomena, thereby advising on remedial measures in government and investigating the proper ordering of affairs. In calculating the regular succession of seasons and divining anomalies in celestial configurations, they took the Five Phases as their basis for attending reverently to the Five Duties; auspicious and ominous signs were embodied therein. How weighty were their responsibilities!

Qin did not take antiquity as its model: it slighted Heaven and oppressed the people, and the offices responsible for astronomy and the calendar consequently fell into disuse. Following Zou Yan’s cycle of the Five Powers, it declared itself to possess the Power of Water, made the month corresponding to hai the first month, and used ten as its numerical standard. It deliberately rejected the Three Correct Beginnings of the year [?]. How perverse this was!

When the Han arose, it restored ancient institutions and altered the beginning of the calendrical year; its calendar underwent five changes in all. Zhang Cang used the calendar of Emperor Zhuanxu; Liu Xin devised the Three Concordances calendar; Li Fan [?] created the Quarter-Remainder calendar; and Liu Hong produced the Celestial Configurations calendar. Tang Du, Luoxia Hong, Deng Ping, and others divided the work of calculation among themselves, each using different methods. Only Sima Qian’s Grand Inception calendar was especially acclaimed for its precision. As the treatise puts it, “The sun and moon were like paired jade discs, and the five planets like strung pearls.” Evidently, it had correctly grasped the calendrical epoch. The sole regret is that, although antiquity was not yet distant, no one ever restored the offices of Astrologer and Astronomer. This was why Sima Qian lamented that the historiographers…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
官喪紀疇人子弟分散之憾也唐之曆凡
六變而說者以僧一行之太衍爲最一行
之論氣朔推步也有七一曰步中朔術二
曰發斂術三曰步日躔術四曰步月離術
五曰步軌漏術六曰步交會術七曰步五
星術其議曆數十有二曰曆本曰中氣曰
合朔曰沒滅曰卦候曰卦氣曰日度曰日
躔盈縮曰九道曰晷漏中星曰日蝕曰五
星雖論議多端要之本乎天地之二中始
===
于冬至之中氣以晦朔定日月之會以日
度正周天之度以卦氣正七十二候以中
星正二十四氣合二始以正剛柔推一終
以紀閏餘至于制作之精微又莫詳于測
景其言曰古人所以步圭影之意將以節
宣和氣輔相物宜不在乎辰次之周徑所
以重曆數之意將以恭授人時欽若乾象
而不在渾蓋之是非似有得於天地之數
之外者此太衍所以爲妙而獨冠乎諸家
punctuated: 官喪紀、疇人子弟分散之憾也。唐之曆凡六變，而說者以僧一行之太衍爲最。一行之論氣朔推步也有七：一曰步中朔術，二曰發斂術，三曰步日躔術，四曰步月離術，五曰步軌漏術，六曰步交會術，七曰步五星術。其議曆數十有二：曰曆本，曰中氣，曰合朔，曰沒滅，曰卦候，曰卦氣，曰日度，曰日躔盈縮，曰九道，曰晷漏中星，曰日蝕，曰五星。雖論議多端，要之本乎天地之二中，始于冬至之中氣，以晦朔定日月之會，以日度正周天之度，以卦氣正七十二候，以中星正二十四氣，合二始以正剛柔，推一終以紀閏餘。至于制作之精微，又莫詳于測景。其言曰：「古人所以步圭影之意，將以節宣和氣，輔相物宜，不在乎辰次之周徑；所以重曆數之意，將以恭授人時，欽若乾象，而不在渾蓋之是非。」似有得於天地之數之外者。此太衍所以爲妙而獨冠乎諸家
translation_en: …the regret that the astronomical officials had lost their guiding traditions and that the descendants of hereditary specialists had scattered. Under the Tang, the calendar underwent six changes, and commentators regard the monk Yixing’s Taiyan calendar [?] as the best. Yixing’s treatment of the calculation of solar terms and new moons comprised seven procedures: first, calculating principal solar terms and new moons; second, calculating the unfolding and gathering of seasonal influences; third, calculating the sun’s course; fourth, calculating the moon’s positions; fifth, calculating celestial tracks and water-clock timings; sixth, calculating conjunctions and eclipses; and seventh, calculating the motions of the five planets. His discussion of calendrical reckoning had twelve sections: the foundations of the calendar; principal solar terms; conjunctions at the new moon; “submergence and extinction”; the hexagrams and seasonal periods; the hexagrams and solar terms; solar degrees; acceleration and retardation in the sun’s course; the nine lunar paths; sundial shadows, water clocks, and culminating stars; solar eclipses; and the five planets. Although his discussions ranged widely, their essentials rested on the two central points of Heaven and Earth, beginning with the principal solar term of the winter solstice. He used the last and first days of the lunar month to determine the conjunction of sun and moon; solar degrees to establish the degrees of the celestial circuit; the solar influences associated with the hexagrams to regulate the seventy-two seasonal periods; and culminating stars to regulate the twenty-four solar terms. He combined the two beginnings to set the firm and yielding in proper order, and calculated a complete cycle to record the remainder requiring intercalation. As for the subtle precision of his methods, nowhere was his treatment more detailed than in measuring shadows. He said: “The ancients’ purpose in calculating shadows on the sundial was to regulate and disseminate harmonious influences and assist all things in attaining their appropriate conditions; it did not lie in the circumference and diameter of the celestial divisions. Their purpose in valuing calendrical reckoning was reverently to provide the people with the proper times for their activities and respectfully to follow the celestial patterns; it did not lie in deciding between the spherical-heaven and canopy-heaven theories.” He seems to have grasped something beyond the numerical workings of Heaven and Earth. This is why the Taiyan was so subtle and uniquely surpassed all the other systems…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
也歷宋而元有郭守敬者出焉雖其智巧
絕人而其意一主于推筭其說曰上能合
乎數百載之前則下可以行之永久如推
春秋獻公以來二千一百六十餘年中間
四十九事以校諸厯惟授時曆爲密是其
精微所在殆與一行意同此丘濬所以有
度越前人太衍莫過之許也樂果何肪乎
太昊以前邈矣黃帝截竹製筩以命伶倫
聽鳳鳴箬雄雌六爲陽律六爲陰呂吹之
===
聲和候之氣應天地之氣合也自時厥後
舜初即位首命后夔書所載直寬剛簡詩
歌聲律是也明良之會其愼重樂律也如
此至周則有大司樂掌教國子而大合樂
以和邦國所謂陰竹之管龍門琴瑟由一
變而九變而神祇人鬼格焉功用之盛何
如也秦不師古燔書燬籍而古樂之亡漸
盡乃廢廟祀六代之樂而獨存韶武改大
武爲五行名房中爲壽人導慾增悲何其
punctuated:
也。歷宋而元，有郭守敬者出焉。雖其智巧絕人，而其意一主于推筭。其說曰：「上能合乎數百載之前，則下可以行之永久。」如推春秋獻公以來二千一百六十餘年，中間四十九事，以校諸厯，惟授時曆爲密。是其精微所在，殆與一行意同。此丘濬所以有度越前人、太衍莫過之許也。
樂果何肪乎？太昊以前邈矣。黃帝截竹製筩，以命伶倫聽鳳鳴，箬雄雌，六爲陽律，六爲陰呂。吹之聲和，候之氣應，天地之氣合也。自時厥後，舜初即位，首命后夔，《書》所載直寬剛簡、詩歌聲律是也。明良之會，其愼重樂律也如此。至周，則有大司樂掌教國子，而大合樂以和邦國。所謂陰竹之管、龍門琴瑟，由一變而九變，而神祇人鬼格焉。功用之盛何如也！秦不師古，燔書燬籍，而古樂之亡漸盡。乃廢廟祀六代之樂，而獨存韶武，改大武爲五行，名房中爲壽人。導慾增悲，何其
translation_en:
…Thus it was. After the Song and into the Yuan, there emerged a man named Guo Shoujing. Although his ingenuity surpassed that of others, his approach centered entirely on calculation. He said: “If it can agree with events several hundred years in the past, it can be used indefinitely into the future.” For example, forty-nine events over the more than 2,160 years since Duke Xian in the Spring and Autumn period were calculated and used to compare the various calendars; only the Season-Granting Calendar (Shoushi li) proved precise. In this precision, his intent was probably the same as Yixing’s. This is why Qiu Jun praised him as surpassing his predecessors and as being unsurpassed even by the Great Expansion Calendar (Dayan li).
As for music, what indeed … [?] The time before Taihao is remote. The Yellow Emperor cut bamboo to make tubes and commanded Ling Lun to listen to phoenix calls, distinguishing [?] male and female: six became the yang pitch standards (lü 律), and six the yin pitch standards (lü 呂). Blown, they produced harmonious sounds; used to observe the seasonal qi, they responded accordingly: the qi of Heaven and Earth united. Thereafter, when Shun first ascended the throne, he immediately issued commands to Kui. These are what the Book of Documents records concerning being straightforward, generous, firm, and unassuming, and concerning poetry, song, musical tones, and pitch standards. Such was the care devoted to musical pitch at a meeting of an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers. Under the Zhou, the Grand Director of Music was responsible for teaching the sons of the state and brought music together in grand performances to harmonize the states. With what were called pipes of bamboo from shaded slopes and zithers from Longmen, the music proceeded from one movement to nine, and the spirits of Heaven and Earth and the ghosts of men arrived. How magnificent its efficacy was! Qin did not take antiquity as its model: it burned books and destroyed records, and ancient music gradually disappeared almost entirely. It abolished the music of the Six Dynasties used in ancestral-temple sacrifices, preserving only the Shao and Wu. It renamed the Great Martial Dance (Da Wu) the Five Phases (Wu Xing), and called the Music of the Inner Chambers (Fangzhong) the Long-Lived Person (Shou Ren) [?]. Inciting desire and deepening sorrow—how very …

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
靡也漢興雅用世官聲器未遠奈何高祖
安馬上之習御氏纔鏗鏘之末賈生前席
而未遑河間好古而徒議至于叔孫通夏
侯寬司馬相如輩因陋就簡雙俳雜隷至
于哀成之際鄭聲盈耳非趙代秦楚之謳
則鼓吹鐃歌之曲詎可薦之郊廟哉獨怪
夫雅音不振而琴瑟管絃之間流湎已甚
此宋暈所以有脩起舊文放鄭近雅之請
也唐之樂雜乎夷而論者有取于宋儒蔡
===
元定律呂新書元定論律呂諸辨有十一
造律二長短徑圍之數三黃鍾之實四損
益相生五和聲六大小七變宮變徵八六
十調九候氣十度量權衡其議本源十有
三曰黃鍾曰黃鍾之實曰黃鍾生十二律
曰十二律之實曰變律曰律生五聲圖曰
變聲曰八十四聲圖曰九十四調圖曰候
氣曰審度曰嘉量曰謹權衡雖考究詳盡
其言多出于近世之未講而明白縝密實
punctuated: 靡也！漢興，雅用世官，聲器未遠，奈何高祖安馬上之習，御氏纔鏗鏘之末，賈生前席而未遑，河間好古而徒議。至于叔孫通、夏侯寬、司馬相如輩，因陋就簡，雙俳雜隷。至于哀成之際，鄭聲盈耳，非趙代秦楚之謳，則鼓吹鐃歌之曲，詎可薦之郊廟哉？獨怪夫雅音不振，而琴瑟管絃之間流湎已甚，此宋暈所以有脩起舊文、放鄭近雅之請也。唐之樂雜乎夷，而論者有取于宋儒蔡元定《律呂新書》。元定論律呂諸辨有十：一，造律；二，長短徑圍之數；三，黃鍾之實；四，損益相生；五，和聲；六，大小；七，變宮變徵；八，六十調；九，候氣；十，度量權衡。其議本源十有三：曰黃鍾，曰黃鍾之實，曰黃鍾生十二律，曰十二律之實，曰變律，曰律生五聲圖，曰變聲，曰八十四聲圖，曰九十四調圖，曰候氣，曰審度，曰嘉量，曰謹權衡。雖考究詳盡，其言多出于近世之未講，而明白縝密，實
translation_en:
…how decadent it was! When the Han arose, hereditary officials were regularly employed, and the old sounds and instruments were not yet far removed. Yet Gaozu remained content with the habits of horseback life; Yu [?] attained only the superficial clanging of instruments. Master Jia was received with the emperor drawing his seat closer, but there was no opportunity to pursue the matter; the Prince of Hejian loved antiquity, but his efforts amounted only to discussion. Men such as Shusun Tong, Xiahou Kuan, and Sima Xiangru made do with crude conditions and simplified practices, mingling paired entertainers and menials [?]. By the time of Emperors Ai and Cheng, the sounds of Zheng filled the ears: if not songs from Zhao, Dai, Qin, and Chu, they were pieces for drums and wind instruments or military songs accompanied by bells. How could these be offered at the suburban sacrifices and in the ancestral temples? Particularly troubling was that orthodox music languished while indulgence in the music of zithers, pipes, and strings had already become excessive. This was why Song Yun [?] petitioned to restore the old musical forms, banish the sounds of Zheng, and approach orthodox music.

The music of the Tang was mixed with that of foreign peoples, whereas commentators have found merit in the New Treatise on Pitch Standards (Lülü xinshu) by the Song Confucian scholar Cai Yuanding. Yuanding’s discussions distinguishing matters of pitch comprise ten topics: first, constructing pitch pipes; second, numerical measures of length, diameter, and circumference; third, the capacity of the Huangzhong pipe; fourth, generating pitches from one another through subtraction and addition; fifth, harmonizing sounds; sixth, greater and lesser pitch standards; seventh, the altered gong and altered zhi notes; eighth, the sixty modes; ninth, observing the seasonal qi; and tenth, lengths, capacities, and weights.

His discussion of fundamental principles has thirteen topics: Huangzhong; the capacity of the Huangzhong pipe; Huangzhong generating the twelve pitch standards; the capacities of the twelve pitch pipes; altered pitch standards; a diagram of the pitch standards generating the five notes; altered notes; a diagram of the eighty-four notes; a diagram of the ninety-four modes [?]; observing the seasonal qi; examining measures of length; establishing correct measures of capacity; and carefully regulating weights and balances. Although his investigations are detailed and exhaustive, much of what he says concerns matters left undiscussed in recent times; his exposition is clear and meticulous, and indeed…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
無一字不本諸古人已試之法如黃鍾徑
圍之數則漢斛之積分可考寸以九分爲
法則淮南太史小司馬之說可推五聲二
變之數半律半聲之例則杜氏通典具焉
變宮變徵之不得爲調則孔氏之禮疏可
見至于制作之精微又在于求聲氣之元
其言曰黃鍾者陽氣之動陽聲之始分寸
之數具于聲氣之元不可得而見及斷竹
爲管吹之而聲和候之而氣應而數始形
===
焉是爲律本十一律由之而損益似有得
于天地之氣之外者此新書所以爲至而
朱子有取之也何近世儒者乃有倡爲含
少之說詆訾漢儒以爲誤用蕤賓之管其
言曰黃鍾非九寸之管而引通鑑外紀呂
氏春秋所載含少之說以爲證不知黃鍾
以八十一分之積吹三十九分以爲聲故
謂之含少而非指三十九分爲黃鍾之律
也若執含少以爲清管則十一律何所稟
punctuated: 無一字不本諸古人已試之法。如黃鍾徑圍之數，則漢斛之積分可考；寸以九分爲法，則淮南、太史、小司馬之說可推；五聲二變之數、半律半聲之例，則杜氏《通典》具焉；變宮變徵之不得爲調，則孔氏之《禮疏》可見。至于制作之精微，又在于求聲氣之元。其言曰：「黃鍾者，陽氣之動，陽聲之始。分寸之數，具于聲氣之元，不可得而見。及斷竹爲管，吹之而聲和，候之而氣應，而數始形焉。是爲律本，十一律由之而損益。」似有得于天地之氣之外者，此《新書》所以爲至，而朱子有取之也。何近世儒者乃有倡爲含少之說，詆訾漢儒，以爲誤用蕤賓之管？其言曰：「黃鍾非九寸之管。」而引《通鑑外紀》《呂氏春秋》所載含少之說以爲證。不知黃鍾以八十一分之積，吹三十九分以爲聲，故謂之含少，而非指三十九分爲黃鍾之律也。若執含少以爲清管，則十一律何所稟
translation_en: …not a single word fails to rest on methods already tested by the ancients. For the diameter and circumference of the Huangzhong pitch pipe, the cubic measure of the Han hu vessel can be examined. For the rule that one cun comprises nine fen, the explanations of the Master of Huainan, the Grand Astrologer, and the Lesser Sima can be worked out. The numerical relations of the five notes and the two altered notes, and the rules for half-length pitch pipes and half pitches, are fully set out in Du’s Comprehensive Institutions. That the altered gong and altered zhi cannot serve as the basis of modes can be seen in Kong’s Commentary on the Rites. As for the subtleties of construction, these further depend on seeking the origin of sound and qi. The work states: “Huangzhong is the stirring of yang qi and the beginning of yang sound. The numerical measures in fen and cun are inherent in the origin of sound and qi, but cannot be perceived. Only when bamboo is cut into a pipe, blowing it produces a harmonious sound, and observing it reveals a response to qi, do the numerical measures first take form. This constitutes the foundation of the pitch standards; the other eleven are derived from it through subtraction and addition.” This seems to apprehend something beyond the qi of Heaven and Earth. This is why the New Book represents the utmost achievement, and why Master Zhu approved of it. Why, then, have some recent Confucian scholars advocated the theory of hanshao, “containing the lesser,” and disparaged Han scholars for supposedly misusing the Ruibin pipe? They say, “Huangzhong is not a pipe nine cun long,” and cite the accounts of hanshao in the Outer Annals of the Comprehensive Mirror and Master Lü’s Spring and Autumn Annals as evidence. They do not understand that Huangzhong has an accumulated measure of eighty-one fen and is blown at thirty-nine fen to produce its sound [?]; hence it is called “containing the lesser.” This does not mean that thirty-nine fen constitutes the Huangzhong pitch standard. If one insists that “containing the lesser” means a high-register pipe, then from what would the eleven other pitch standards derive…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
正是其好爲立異而未詳律呂本原徒資
談說而不可施之實用也抑曆者測候之
書其重存乎數律者作樂之具其重存乎
聲初若不相關涉者然究極其理則元氣
必發爲元聲而元數必本乎元運是以史
遷作記言律必兼曆而後世宗之朱子亦
謂治曆家用律呂候氣蓋此氣都由地中
透出如十一月冬至緹室布管距地飛葭
若非元氣之至其何以得元聲之數哉此
===
理也數也氣也三者渾融無間而制曆者
必先于協律作樂者必先于推曆二者交
相爲用者也我
國家
大統曆承用勝國之舊即許衡郭守敬所訂定
而
大祀樂章皆
皇祖所親製宴饗九奏贊以陶凱
皇祖謂其有和平廣大之意一切流俗諠澆淫
punctuated:
正？是其好爲立異，而未詳律呂本原，徒資談說，而不可施之實用也。抑曆者，測候之書，其重存乎數；律者，作樂之具，其重存乎聲。初若不相關涉者，然究極其理，則元氣必發爲元聲，而元數必本乎元運。是以史遷作記，言律必兼曆，而後世宗之。朱子亦謂治曆家用律呂候氣，蓋此氣都由地中透出。如十一月冬至，緹室布管，距地飛葭，若非元氣之至，其何以得元聲之數哉？此理也、數也、氣也，三者渾融無間，而制曆者必先于協律，作樂者必先于推曆，二者交相爲用者也。
我國家《大統曆》承用勝國之舊，即許衡、郭守敬所訂定。而大祀樂章，皆皇祖所親製；宴饗九奏，贊以陶凱。皇祖謂其有和平廣大之意，一切流俗諠澆淫
translation_en:
…derive their correct standard? This shows their fondness for advancing divergent views without thoroughly understanding the origins of the pitch standards. Their claims merely furnish material for discussion and cannot be put to practical use. Now, calendrical treatises are writings for measuring and observing celestial phenomena; their emphasis lies in numbers. Pitch standards are instruments for making music; their emphasis lies in sound. At first these seem unrelated, yet when their principles are investigated to the utmost, primordial qi must issue as primordial sound, and primordial numbers must be grounded in primordial cycles. Thus, when Sima Qian composed the Records of the Historian, his treatment of pitch standards necessarily included calendrical matters, and later generations followed his example. Master Zhu likewise said that calendrical specialists use pitch pipes to observe qi, for this qi emerges entirely from within the earth. For example, at the winter solstice in the eleventh month, pipes are arranged in a chamber hung with red silk, and reed ashes fly up at a distance from the ground [?]. If primordial qi had not arrived, how could the numerical values of primordial sound be obtained? Principle, number, and qi: these three blend seamlessly together. Those who construct calendars must first harmonize the pitch standards, while those who make music must first calculate the calendar. The two serve one another in their application.
Our dynasty’s Grand Concordance Calendar (Datong li) continues the system of the preceding dynasty, namely that established by Xu Heng and Guo Shoujing. The musical texts for the great sacrifices were all personally composed by the imperial ancestor, while Tao Kai assisted with the nine musical performances for court banquets. The imperial ancestor said that these conveyed a spirit of peace, harmony, breadth, and grandeur. All vulgar, clamorous, debased, licentious …

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
蘇之樂悉屏去之二百年來遵行已久而
海宇乂安民物和同
列聖相承丕歷泰運肆我
皇上中和
建極
敬一承天三辰順序而不忒六樂和同而盡善
和氣致祥而天不愛道順氣感人而物無
札厲
欽天有監而星官專其業
===
神樂有觀而春卿掌其事制度一定播諸仰成
以繇
宗社之福以享
享嘉之會執事謂欲聞局求人毋乃過慮乎
愚生管窺蠡測之見獻芹炙背之忱惟願
聖天子和德于上賢公卿和職于朝萬物咸和
于野則聲和氣和形和而
天地之泰和應億萬載無疆之休實在于此矣
愚也何幸躬逢其盛
punctuated:
蘇之樂，悉屏去之。二百年來，遵行已久，而海宇乂安，民物和同。列聖相承，丕歷泰運。肆我皇上中和建極，敬一承天，三辰順序而不忒，六樂和同而盡善。和氣致祥，而天不愛道；順氣感人，而物無札厲。欽天有監，而星官專其業；神樂有觀，而春卿掌其事。制度一定，播諸仰成，以繇宗社之福，以享享嘉之會。執事謂欲聞局求人，毋乃過慮乎？

愚生管窺蠡測之見，獻芹炙背之忱，惟願聖天子和德于上，賢公卿和職于朝，萬物咸和于野，則聲和、氣和、形和，而天地之泰和應。億萬載無疆之休，實在于此矣。愚也何幸，躬逢其盛！
translation_en:
…such decadent music [?] was entirely banished. These practices have long been observed, for two hundred years; all within the seas is peaceful and well governed, and the people and all creatures live in harmony. Successive sage sovereigns have inherited the throne, continuing a great age of peace. Thus our present Emperor establishes the supreme standard through equilibrium and harmony, and serves Heaven through reverent singleness of purpose. The sun, moon, and stars follow their proper courses without deviation; the Six Musical Traditions are harmonious and wholly excellent. Harmonious vital energies bring auspicious signs, and Heaven does not withhold its Way [?]; favorable vital energies move human beings, and living things suffer no pestilence.

There is a Directorate of Astronomy, whose astronomical officials specialize in their work; there is an Abbey of Divine Music, whose affairs the Minister of Rites oversees. Once the institutions and regulations are established, they are promulgated among those who look to their superiors for accomplishment [?], thereby securing the blessings of the ancestral temples and altars of soil and grain, and enjoying an auspicious gathering [?]. You, sir, speak of wishing to hear about offices and the recruitment of suitable men [?]: is this not excessive concern?

The views of this humble student are like looking through a tube or measuring the sea with a ladle; my sincerity is that of one who offers humble celery or recommends the warmth of the sun upon his back. I wish only that the sage Son of Heaven harmonize virtue above, that worthy dukes and ministers harmonize their duties at court, and that all things live in harmony throughout the countryside. Then sounds, vital energies, and forms will be harmonious, and the great harmony of Heaven and Earth will respond. The boundless blessings of hundreds of millions of years truly depend upon this. How fortunate I, ignorant as I am, am to witness this flourishing age in person!

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
許份
同考試官學正裴　批〔策士以人物一槩考古之學一䝉評生能中錄爾〕〔且漫然博采而策雖之也子能考核評盡品藻明當非尚友有素者能之乎〕
考試官教諭胡　批〔敘斷鄉先哲抑揚有體錄之〕
考試官學正史　批〔評斷精當人物策無踰此作〕
君子之所以自立而流聲實于無窮者有
本焉有末焉明于本末之義者可與論世
矣夫天下之道出于一原君子之學初無
二致本立而末隨之則其被天下傳後世
者莫非養盛自致而君子無心焉外此而
性資之暗合智力之□成非不足以表見
于時而與君子之一貫者異矣是故道德
者士之上也合本與末而爲言者也德之
不足而功業焉次也文章焉又其次也觀
此則百代之士與一方之才胥以辨矣孰
事以中土人才下詢承學愚也敢方人乎
punctuated:
許份

同考試官學正裴　批〔策士以人物一槩，考古之學一䝉評，生能中錄爾。〕〔且漫然博采，而策雖之也。子能考核評盡，品藻明當，非尚友有素者能之乎？〕
考試官教諭胡　批〔敘斷鄉先哲，抑揚有體，錄之。〕
考試官學正史　批〔評斷精當，人物策無踰此作。〕

君子之所以自立而流聲實于無窮者，有本焉，有末焉。明于本末之義者，可與論世矣。夫天下之道出于一原，君子之學初無二致。本立而末隨之，則其被天下、傳後世者，莫非養盛自致，而君子無心焉。外此而性資之暗合、智力之□成，非不足以表見于時，而與君子之一貫者異矣。是故道德者，士之上也，合本與末而爲言者也。德之不足而功業焉，次也；文章焉，又其次也。觀此，則百代之士與一方之才胥以辨矣。孰事以中土人才下詢承學，愚也敢方人乎
translation_en:
Xu Fen 許份

Comment by Associate Examiner Pei, School Instructor: 〔In testing candidates through a policy question on historical figures, a single standard is applied; learning concerning antiquity receives an assessment [?]. This candidate merits selection [?].〕〔Moreover, indiscriminately gathering material widely—the policy essay nevertheless … [?]. You can investigate and assess thoroughly, and your appraisals are clear and fitting. Could anyone accomplish this without long practice in taking the ancients as friends?〕
Comment by Examiner Hu, Instructor: 〔In recounting and judging the earlier worthies of his native region, he handles praise and criticism appropriately. Select it.〕
Comment by Examiner Shi, School Instructor: 〔The assessments are precise and fitting. No policy essay on historical figures surpasses this work.〕

There are roots and branches to the means by which a gentleman establishes himself and transmits his reputation and substantive achievements without end. With someone who understands the significance of roots and branches, one may discuss the men of past ages. The Way of all under Heaven issues from a single source, and the gentleman’s learning has never had two divergent aims. Once the roots are established, the branches follow. Thus, whatever spreads throughout the world and is transmitted to later generations comes naturally from the fullness of his cultivation; the gentleman has no deliberate intention of achieving such effects. Outside this, an unconscious accord arising from one’s natural endowment, or an accomplishment [?] achieved through intelligence and effort, may indeed suffice to bring a person to prominence in his time. Yet these differ from the single principle that runs through the gentleman’s learning.

Thus, moral virtue is the highest attainment of a scholar: it embraces both roots and branches. Where virtue falls short, meritorious deeds rank next, and literary accomplishment next again. Viewed in this light, the scholars of a hundred generations and the talented men of a particular region can all be distinguished and assessed. You, honored examiners [?], have graciously questioned us students about the talented men of the Central Lands. Would I, ignorant as I am, dare to judge others …

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
哉雖然居是鄉而不能道其鄉先正恥也
吾河南昔爲梁豫境嵩行盤峙河洛滙流
孕秀鍾賢不爲無自而況虞夏甫還敎隆
經正士咸自立而奮起者乎是故伊尹之
在商啓格帝之功于奕葉申甫之在周翊
中興之業于重光功業則盛矣而以功業
盡之可乎卜商告往知來大啓二乇之派
子貢多學能識竟聞一貫之傳文章則著
矣而以文章槩之可乎是皆聖賢之學豫
===
養者深愚之所謂本立而末隨之者也漢
而降人才未易縷數姑舉其著者言之張
良爲韓報讎而赤松之遊有得保身之哲
黃霸寬明有體而潁川之治允服士民之
心丰采凝峻聞者解綬李膺所以係登龍
之望也脩德淸淨遺絹化盜陳寔所以有
文範之謚也謝安之舉謝玄不避親矣捷
傳淝水其鎭靜之效乎張方平之器三蘇
能知人矣不屈安石其凝定之操乎要說
punctuated:
哉！雖然，居是鄉而不能道其鄉先正，恥也。吾河南昔爲梁豫境，嵩行盤峙，河洛滙流，孕秀鍾賢，不爲無自。而況虞夏甫還，敎隆經正，士咸自立而奮起者乎？是故伊尹之在商，啓格帝之功于奕葉；申甫之在周，翊中興之業于重光。功業則盛矣，而以功業盡之可乎？卜商告往知來，大啓二乇之派；子貢多學能識，竟聞一貫之傳。文章則著矣，而以文章槩之可乎？是皆聖賢之學，豫養者深，愚之所謂本立而末隨之者也。

漢而降，人才未易縷數，姑舉其著者言之。張良爲韓報讎，而赤松之遊，有得保身之哲；黃霸寬明有體，而潁川之治，允服士民之心。丰采凝峻，聞者解綬，李膺所以係登龍之望也；脩德淸淨，遺絹化盜，陳寔所以有文範之謚也。謝安之舉謝玄，不避親矣，捷傳淝水，其鎭靜之效乎？張方平之器三蘇，能知人矣，不屈安石，其凝定之操乎？要說
translation_en:
…! Even so, to live in this province yet be unable to speak of its worthy predecessors is a disgrace. Our Henan formerly lay within the territories of Liang and Yu. Mount Song and the Taihang Mountains stand massed and lofty; the Yellow and Luo Rivers converge. That this land nurtures outstanding talent and brings forth worthies is not without cause. How much more so when the age of Yu and Xia had just returned [?], teaching flourished, and the classics were rightly understood, and scholars all established themselves and rose to action! Thus Yi Yin, serving the Shang, initiated achievements that reached Heaven and endured through successive generations; Shen and Fu, serving the Zhou, assisted the work of dynastic restoration as its glory shone anew. Their achievements were indeed magnificent, but can achievements alone encompass them? Bu Shang, when told of what had gone before, understood what would follow, and greatly opened the way for the lineage of “二乇” [?]. Zigong learned much and retained it, and ultimately heard the teaching of the single thread running through all. Their literary learning was indeed distinguished, but can literary learning alone sum them up? These men had all deeply nurtured themselves beforehand through the learning of the sages and worthies. They exemplify what I, in my humble view, have called establishing the root so that the branches follow.

From the Han onward, talented men are not easily enumerated one by one; let me discuss just the most distinguished. Zhang Liang avenged the state of Han, yet in his proposed wanderings with the immortal Chi Song he grasped the wisdom of preserving himself. Huang Ba was generous and discerning, and observed proper forms; his administration of Yingchuan truly won the hearts of scholars and commoners. His bearing solemn and stern, those who heard of him relinquished their official seal-ribbons: this was why Li Ying became the focus of hopes for “ascending the dragon gate” through his recognition. He cultivated virtue in purity and tranquility, and reformed a thief by giving him silk: this was why Chen Shi received the posthumous title Wenfan, “Model of Cultivation.” In recommending Xie Xuan, Xie An did not avoid appointing a relative; when news of victory came from the Fei River, was this not the fruit of his calm composure? Zhang Fangping recognized the abilities of the three Sus and thus showed that he could judge men; in refusing to yield to Wang Anshi, did he not display steadfast integrity? In setting forth the essentials …

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
十事而應變不窮則姚元之之抹時有賴
身經百戰而東京幾復則岳武穆之報國
略酬錢若水善決疑獄四十致仕殆二疏
之儔乎韓魏公擁英立神聲色不動真社
稷之臣乎富弼再使彊虜和議以成人以
富文並稱當矣鄧禹杖策軍門大計遂定
卒爲東京元功宜矣忠義如巡遠則雖以
雎陽之小克保江淮德量如叔度則雖以
林宗之賢推爲顏子茲數子者功業雖有
===
顯晦均之有裨于當時者也賈山陳言于
文帝借秦爲喻有憂時致主之忠丁寬受
學丁田何載易而東啓施孟梁丘之學治
安一書試無不驗賈誼所以爲通國體也
隸書六經人爭傳習蔡邕所以爲時儒宗
也漢政方移曹氏而荀悅作申鑒奏之寓
憫時之意焉張說許諡元忠而吳兢于唐
史書之有董狐之筆焉陳摶隱臥于華山
乃有指玄之作得于沉潛者久矣韓愈抒
punctuated: 十事而應變不窮，則姚元之之抹時有賴；身經百戰而東京幾復，則岳武穆之報國略酬。錢若水善決疑獄，四十致仕，殆二疏之儔乎？韓魏公擁英立神，聲色不動，真社稷之臣乎？富弼再使彊虜，和議以成，人以富文並稱，當矣。鄧禹杖策軍門，大計遂定，卒爲東京元功，宜矣。忠義如巡遠，則雖以雎陽之小，克保江淮；德量如叔度，則雖以林宗之賢，推爲顏子。茲數子者，功業雖有顯晦，均之有裨于當時者也。賈山陳言于文帝，借秦爲喻，有憂時致主之忠；丁寬受學丁田何，載易而東，啓施孟梁丘之學。治安一書，試無不驗，賈誼所以爲通國體也；隸書六經，人爭傳習，蔡邕所以爲時儒宗也。漢政方移曹氏，而荀悅作申鑒奏之，寓憫時之意焉；張說許諡元忠，而吳兢于唐史書之，有董狐之筆焉。陳摶隱臥于華山，乃有指玄之作，得于沉潛者久矣；韓愈抒
translation_en:
…ten matters, responding inexhaustibly to changing circumstances: thus the age could rely on Yao Yuanzhi’s assistance [?]. Having fought a hundred battles and nearly recovered the Eastern Capital, Yue Wumu’s aspiration to repay his country was in some measure fulfilled. Qian Ruoshui excelled at resolving doubtful legal cases and retired at forty: was he not perhaps a peer of the two Shu? Duke Han of Wei supported Emperor Yingzong and enthroned Emperor Shenzong, without any change in his voice or expression: was he not truly a minister who upheld the state? Fu Bi twice went as envoy to the powerful northern enemy and successfully concluded peace negotiations; people were right to speak of Fu Bi and Wen Yanbo together. Deng Yu came, staff in hand, to the army’s gates, and the grand strategy was thereupon settled; it was fitting that he ultimately became a foremost founding contributor to the Eastern Han. With loyalty and righteousness such as those of Zhang Xun and Xu Yuan, even a place as small as Suiyang could protect the Jiang and Huai regions. With virtue and magnanimity such as Huang Shudu’s, even someone as worthy as Guo Linzong acclaimed him as another Master Yan. Although the achievements of these men varied in prominence, all benefited their times.

Jia Shan presented his views to Emperor Wen, using Qin as an admonitory example, with the loyalty of one concerned for his age and intent on guiding his ruler to good government. Ding Kuan studied under Tian He [?], carried the Book of Changes eastward, and opened the way for the teachings of Shi, Meng, and Liangqiu. Whenever the proposals in his essay On Order and Security were put to the test, they proved sound: this is why Jia Yi was regarded as understanding the essentials of government. He wrote the Six Classics in clerical script, and people competed to copy and study them: this is why Cai Yong became a leading Confucian scholar of his age. Just as Han political power was passing to the Cao family, Xun Yue composed A Mirror of Admonitions (Shenjian) and submitted it to the throne, embedding in it his concern for the times. When Zhang Yue agreed to slander Yuanzhong [?], Wu Jing recorded the matter in his History of Tang, displaying the uncompromising historical pen of Dong Hu. Chen Tuan lived secluded on Mount Hua and produced Pointing to the Mysterious (Zhixuan); long had he cultivated his understanding through deep contemplation. Han Yu gave expression to…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
文于三變遂起八代之衰功于聖經者多
矣韋應物之詩一藝之工也而高潔之趣
故近風雅之餘音張衡之賦十年之思也
而曆筭之精似得璣衡之遺意宋庠之兄
弟聯舉榮矣而追白著述均之不愧科名
應劭之著風俗通末矣而物類名號亦足
以資多識玆數子者文章雖有高下均之
有功于道藝者也夫惟數子者徒以其性
資之合乎道才力之偶于時而于聖賢之
===
學未之聞也故智如子房而渝鴻溝之約
正如太丘而從宦者之喪濮議之非魏公
猶兄遠于君實仲約之議鄭公猶重忤于
希文四子且然餘可知矣此其功業果皆
般周之功業乎賈大傳之志乃發憤于長
沙蔡中郎之賢至失身于董卓學遺格致
昌黎原道之疎也請誅仲淹雍丘謀國之
陋也四子且然餘可知矣此其文章果皆
聖門之文章乎道德之儒合本末而一之
punctuated:
文于三變，遂起八代之衰，功于聖經者多矣。韋應物之詩，一藝之工也，而高潔之趣，故近風雅之餘音。張衡之賦，十年之思也，而曆筭之精，似得璣衡之遺意。宋庠之兄弟聯舉，榮矣，而追白著述，均之不愧科名。應劭之著《風俗通》，末矣，而物類名號，亦足以資多識。玆數子者，文章雖有高下，均之有功于道藝者也。
夫惟數子者，徒以其性資之合乎道，才力之偶于時，而于聖賢之學未之聞也。故智如子房，而渝鴻溝之約；正如太丘，而從宦者之喪。濮議之非，魏公猶兄遠于君實；仲約之議，鄭公猶重忤于希文。四子且然，餘可知矣。此其功業，果皆般周之功業乎？賈大傳之志，乃發憤于長沙；蔡中郎之賢，至失身于董卓。學遺格致，昌黎《原道》之疎也；請誅仲淹，雍丘謀國之陋也。四子且然，餘可知矣。此其文章，果皆聖門之文章乎？道德之儒，合本末而一之
translation_en:
…his writing through three transformations, thereby reviving literature after eight dynasties of decline; his contributions to the sages’ classics were considerable. Wei Yingwu’s poetry displayed mastery of a single art, yet its lofty and pure spirit approached the lingering strains of the Airs and Elegantiae of the Book of Poetry. Zhang Heng’s rhapsodies embodied ten years of thought, while his precision in calendrical calculation seemed to preserve the intent behind the ancient astronomical instruments. The successive examination successes of Song Xiang and his brother were glorious; their writings, too [the wording 追白 is doubtful], were equally worthy of their examination distinction. Ying Shao’s Comprehensive Account of Customs (Fengsu tong) concerned lesser matters, yet its names and classifications of things could also broaden knowledge. Although these men’s literary accomplishments differed in quality, all contributed to the Way and the arts.
These men, however, merely possessed natural endowments that accorded with the Way and abilities that happened to suit their times; they had not learned the teachings of the sages and worthies. Thus even one as wise as Zifang violated the Honggou treaty, and one as upright as the Magistrate of Taiqiu attended a eunuch’s funeral. Over the errors of the Pu succession controversy, the Duke of Wei nevertheless became estranged from Junshi [?]; over the deliberations concerning Zhongyue, the Duke of Zheng again sharply opposed Xiwen. If even these four men were like this, the rest may readily be judged. Were their achievements truly all achievements like those of Ban and Zhou [般周, possibly a corruption of “Yin and Zhou”]? Grand Mentor Jia, for all his ambition, vented his indignation in Changsha; Court Gentleman Cai, for all his worthiness, went so far as to compromise himself by serving Dong Zhuo. Omitting the investigation of things and the extension of knowledge from learning was the shortcoming of Changli’s Inquiry into the Way (Yuan dao); requesting Zhongyan’s execution was the narrowness of Yongqiu’s counsel on affairs of state. If even these four men were like this, the rest may readily be judged. Were their writings truly all writings of the sages’ school? Confucian scholars of moral virtue unite root and branch into one…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
者宜執事之有取于二程子也自今觀之
充養有道和氣粹然伯醇之道德何如也
學極精微行全純粹正叔之道德何如也
今其見于二程遺書者無非闡孔孟不傳
之緒辨異端似是之非眞足以正人心維
世道至於誠意以動人主講學以隆師道
平氣之論則安石愧心求薦之言則韓公
服義時有能聽而用之者君心其無欲乎
士爭其有行乎人才其可正而風俗其可
===
厚乎豈止于漢唐以下之功業已哉由是
而觀本焉旣立自可以卜其末之必昌末
焉足崇末足以信其本之必盛蓋三代而
上文行出於一故士多全德三代而下文
行出于二故士率偏才以世而論則上之
爲德行次之爲功業次之爲文章者其品
異也以理而言則存之爲道德發之爲功
業著之爲文章者其本一也有志者將爲
百代之上乎將爲一方之才乎學二程子
punctuated: 者，宜執事之有取于二程子也。自今觀之，充養有道，和氣粹然，伯醇之道德何如也？學極精微，行全純粹，正叔之道德何如也？今其見于二程遺書者，無非闡孔孟不傳之緒，辨異端似是之非，眞足以正人心、維世道。至於誠意以動人主，講學以隆師道，平氣之論則安石愧心，求薦之言則韓公服義。時有能聽而用之者，君心其無欲乎？士爭其有行乎？人才其可正而風俗其可厚乎？豈止于漢唐以下之功業已哉？由是而觀，本焉旣立，自可以卜其末之必昌；末焉足崇，末足以信其本之必盛。蓋三代而上，文行出於一，故士多全德；三代而下，文行出于二，故士率偏才。以世而論，則上之爲德行，次之爲功業，次之爲文章者，其品異也；以理而言，則存之爲道德，發之爲功業，著之爲文章者，其本一也。有志者將爲百代之上乎？將爲一方之才乎？學二程子
translation_en:
…it is fitting that you should esteem the two Masters Cheng. Viewed from the present, how great was the moral virtue of Bochun [伯醇, apparently Cheng Hao’s courtesy name, usually written 伯淳; ?], who cultivated himself by the proper Way and whose harmonious disposition was utterly pure! How great was the moral virtue of Zhengshu [Cheng Yi], whose learning reached the most subtle depths and whose conduct was wholly pure! What appears in the Surviving Writings of the Two Chengs invariably elucidates the threads of Confucius’s and Mencius’s teaching whose transmission had been broken, and distinguishes the specious errors of heterodox teachings. It truly suffices to rectify people’s minds and uphold the moral order of the world. As for moving the ruler through sincerity and enhancing the authority of teachers through the exposition of learning, their discussion of a calm disposition made Anshi [Wang Anshi] feel ashamed, while their words about seeking recommendations made Lord Han acknowledge their righteousness. Had there been someone in their time able to heed and employ them, might the ruler’s mind have been free of selfish desires? Could contention among scholars still have prevailed [?]? Might men of talent have been set right and customs made generous? Would their achievements have amounted merely to those of the Han, Tang, and later ages?

Viewed in this light, once the root is established, one may predict that its branches will flourish; when the branches are worthy of esteem, the branches suffice to confirm that the root must be vigorous [?]. From the Three Dynasties back into antiquity, literary accomplishment and conduct issued from a single source, and thus scholars often possessed complete virtue. After the Three Dynasties, literary accomplishment and conduct issued from separate sources, and thus scholars generally possessed only partial talents. Judged in worldly terms, moral conduct ranks highest, practical achievement next, and literary composition next after that: their grades differ. Judged in terms of principle, however, what is preserved within constitutes moral virtue, what is put into action constitutes practical achievement, and what is expressed in writing constitutes literary composition: their root is one. Will those with ambition seek to stand above a hundred generations, or merely to possess talent in one sphere? Learn what the two Masters Cheng…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
之所學焉思過半矣愚也非真能尚友者
也願與執事就正焉
第四問
孫坤
同考試官教諭蕭　批〔書生談兵乃能知機達變〕
〔咸中肯綮不出樽俎而折衝千里予非其人與〕
考試官教諭胡　批〔有斷制有經畧〕
考試官學正史　批〔條對無遺末歸重於治氣〕
養心尤爲探本之論
===
善敵敵者在辨其勢而後天下之制得善
用兵者在握其機而後天下之功成勢在
敵而所以因之必當其機則較於利害其
敵不可爲也機在我而所以應之必當其
勢則決於權陷其兵不可禦也故曰善戰
者動於九天之上而敵不知其所守善計
者藏於九地之下而敵不知其所攻然辨
其勢而不脉非智莫覩也握其機而不失
非勇莫斷也由之而討彊平亂夷險救危
punctuated:
之所學焉，思過半矣。愚也，非真能尚友者也，願與執事就正焉。
第四問
孫坤
同考試官教諭蕭批〔書生談兵，乃能知機達變，〕〔咸中肯綮，不出樽俎而折衝千里，予非其人與？〕
考試官教諭胡批〔有斷制，有經畧。〕
考試官學正史批〔條對無遺，末歸重於治氣，〕養心尤爲探本之論。
善敵敵者，在辨其勢，而後天下之制得；善用兵者，在握其機，而後天下之功成。勢在敵，而所以因之必當其機，則較於利害，其敵不可爲也；機在我，而所以應之必當其勢，則決於權陷，其兵不可禦也。故曰：「善戰者動於九天之上，而敵不知其所守；善計者藏於九地之下，而敵不知其所攻。」然辨其勢而不脉，非智莫覩也；握其機而不失，非勇莫斷也。由之而討彊平亂，夷險救危，
translation_en:
…what they studied, and more than half the matter will have been understood. In my humble ignorance, I cannot truly claim to be capable of taking the ancients as my friends. I hope to seek correction from you, honored sir.
Fourth Question
Sun Kun
Associate Examiner Xiao, Instructor, comments: 〔A scholar discussing warfare, yet he understands opportunities and adapts to changing circumstances.〕〔Every point strikes home. Without leaving the ceremonial wine vessels and sacrificial stands, he can repel an enemy a thousand li away. Am I not such a person? [?]〕
Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: 〔He has decisiveness and strategic understanding.〕
Examiner Shi, Instructor, comments: 〔His point-by-point response omits nothing; at the end, he places the chief emphasis on regulating one's vital energy.〕His discussion of cultivating the mind especially probes the root of the matter.
Skill in confronting an enemy lies in discerning his strategic configuration; only then can mastery of the realm be secured. Skill in employing troops lies in grasping the critical opportunity; only then can achievements throughout the realm be accomplished. The strategic configuration belongs to the enemy, but one's means of exploiting it must accord with the critical opportunity. Then, weighing advantages and disadvantages, the enemy can do nothing. The opportunity lies with us, but our response must accord with the strategic configuration. Then, deciding through tactical expedients and traps [?], our troops cannot be resisted. Thus it is said: “Those skilled in warfare move above the nine heavens, and the enemy does not know what to defend; those skilled in planning conceal themselves beneath the nine depths of the earth, and the enemy does not know what to attack.” Yet discerning the strategic configuration without ‘mai’ [?] requires wisdom to perceive it; grasping the opportunity without losing it requires courage to make the decision. By these means one campaigns against the powerful, quells disorder, levels dangers, and relieves peril…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
而抗敵圖功者之所必由也嗚呼天下之
事未有不辨於勢而能行不擬其機而能
達者况兵爲國之大事乎執事以古人已
事下詢承學始乃謂有文事者必有武備
而考古鏡今亦學者格致之一端乎敢不
悉心以對漢趙充國曰兵者所以明德除
害也故舉得於外禍生於內此言勢之不
可不審也然非得其機焉則禍福之際憯
於大較敗乃事矣太史公曰誅伐不可廢
===
於天下用之有巧拙行之有順逆耳此言
機之不可不得也然非審於勢焉則巧拙
順逆之間失於應制隳乃功矣稽之班氏
藝文志稱兵家者流蓋古司馬之職王官
之武備也今之司馬法故其遺事所言仁
救義戰不專權謀有古昔盛時之遺焉春
秋以降出奇設伏變詐之兵並作迨於漢
興張良韓信序次古兵法凡百八十二家
孝成之際任宏論次兵書爲權謀形勢陰
punctuated:
而抗敵圖功者之所必由也。嗚呼！天下之事，未有不辨於勢而能行、不擬其機而能達者，况兵爲國之大事乎？執事以古人已事下詢承學，始乃謂有文事者必有武備，而考古鏡今亦學者格致之一端乎？敢不悉心以對！漢趙充國曰：「兵者，所以明德除害也。故舉得於外，禍生於內。」此言勢之不可不審也。然非得其機焉，則禍福之際，憯於大較，敗乃事矣。太史公曰：「誅伐不可廢於天下，用之有巧拙，行之有順逆耳。」此言機之不可不得也。然非審於勢焉，則巧拙順逆之間，失於應制，隳乃功矣。
稽之班氏《藝文志》，稱兵家者流，蓋古司馬之職，王官之武備也。今之《司馬法》，故其遺事，所言仁救義戰，不專權謀，有古昔盛時之遺焉。春秋以降，出奇設伏、變詐之兵並作。迨於漢興，張良、韓信序次古兵法，凡百八十二家。孝成之際，任宏論次兵書爲權謀、形勢、陰
translation_en:
…and this is the path that those who resist the enemy and seek achievement must follow. Alas! In the affairs of the world, none can act successfully without discerning the configuration of circumstances, or attain their ends without assessing the critical opportunity. How much more is this true of warfare, a great affair of state! You, honored examiners, have deigned to question a student about the deeds of the ancients. Only now do I grasp the saying that those engaged in civil affairs must also possess military preparedness. Is examining antiquity as a mirror for the present not also one aspect of a scholar’s investigation of things and extension of knowledge? How could I dare not answer with all my heart?
Zhao Chongguo of the Han said: “Arms are the means to manifest virtue and eliminate harm. Thus, an undertaking may gain success abroad while calamity arises within.” This speaks to the necessity of carefully assessing circumstances. Yet unless one seizes the critical opportunity, at the juncture between calamity and good fortune one may suffer grievously in the larger reckoning [?], thereby ruining one’s undertaking. The Grand Historian said: “Punitive campaigns cannot be abolished from the world. There is merely skill or clumsiness in their use, and accordance or contrariety in their execution.” This speaks to the necessity of grasping the critical opportunity. Yet unless one carefully assesses circumstances, amid these distinctions of skill and clumsiness, accordance and contrariety, one may fail to respond and exercise control, thereby destroying one’s achievement.
Examining Ban’s Treatise on Literature, we find its statement that the military school derived from the duties of the ancient Minister of War and constituted the military preparedness of the royal administration. The present Methods of the Minister of War (Sima fa) thus preserves those earlier practices. Its teachings on benevolent rescue and righteous warfare do not concern strategic calculation alone; they retain something of antiquity’s flourishing age. From the Spring and Autumn period onward, warfare employing surprise maneuvers, ambushes, shifting tactics, and deception arose in profusion. When the Han arose, Zhang Liang and Han Xin arranged the ancient military writings in sequence, comprising 182 schools in all. During the reign of Emperor Xiaocheng, Ren Hong examined and classified military books under strategic calculation, dispositions and configurations, yin…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
陽技巧四種後世皆不傳存宋元豐中以
孫子吳子司馬法李衛公問對尉繚子三
略六韜號稱七書至今襲用焉由觀其義
類多真贗相半而得失因之去非存是以
取其長固武之善經也然古之善用兵以
制敵者率不外於是矣以今考之三晉之
兵以齊號爲怯也孫臏因勢利導日減竈
以示弱焉卒之火舉弩發遂斃魏將此審
於料敵者也若虞詡之羌遮崤谷增竈兼
行以疑虜追逼不得不示强矣詡固善法
===
臏也孫子曰勇怯勢也强弱形也其以是
夫濰水之陣以信爲易與也韓信囊沙壅
流還走以誘之焉因之決壅半渡急擊殺
且此巧於覆人者也若檀道濟之轉戰濟
上唱籌量沙以降者告竭非是故不免矣
道濟固善自全也吳子曰涉水半渡可擊
善戰者以形其以是夫百里而趨利者蹶
上將此軍志也龐涓固以輿輕銳倍進而
punctuated: 陽、技巧四種，後世皆不傳存。宋元豐中，以《孫子》《吳子》《司馬法》《李衛公問對》《尉繚子》《三略》《六韜》，號稱七書，至今襲用焉。由觀其義類，多真贗相半，而得失因之。去非存是，以取其長，固武之善經也。然古之善用兵以制敵者，率不外於是矣。以今考之，三晉之兵以齊號爲怯也，孫臏因勢利導，日減竈以示弱焉。卒之火舉弩發，遂斃魏將，此審於料敵者也。若虞詡之羌遮崤谷，增竈兼行以疑虜，追逼不得不示强矣，詡固善法臏也。《孫子》曰：「勇怯，勢也；强弱，形也。」其以是夫！濰水之陣，以信爲易與也，韓信囊沙壅流，還走以誘之焉。因之決壅，半渡急擊，殺且，此巧於覆人者也。若檀道濟之轉戰濟上，唱籌量沙，以降者告竭，非是故不免矣，道濟固善自全也。《吳子》曰：「涉水半渡可擊。」善戰者以形，其以是夫！百里而趨利者蹶上將，此《軍志》也。龐涓固以輿輕銳倍進而
translation_en:
…yang, and technical skills, making four categories; these writings were all lost to later generations. During the Yuanfeng reign period of the Song, the Sunzi, Wuzi, Methods of the Minister of War (Sima fa), Questions and Replies of Duke Li of Wei, Weiliaozi, Three Strategies, and Six Secret Teachings were designated the Seven Books. They continue to be used to this day. Examining their meanings and categories [?], one finds that authentic and spurious material often occur in equal measure, with success and failure following accordingly. To discard what is wrong, retain what is right, and draw on their strengths is certainly a sound guiding principle for warfare. Indeed, those in antiquity who excelled at employing troops to overcome an enemy generally did not go beyond this.

Examining these cases now, the troops of the Three Jin states regarded those of Qi as notoriously cowardly. Sun Bin took advantage of this disposition, reducing his cooking fires each day to display weakness. In the end, when the fire was raised and the crossbows discharged, he killed the Wei commander. This shows discernment in assessing an enemy. In the case of Yu Xu, when the Qiang blocked Xiaogu [?], he increased his cooking fires and marched double stages to bewilder the enemy. Pressed by pursuit, he had no choice but to display strength. Xu was indeed adept at taking Bin as his model. The Sunzi says: “Courage and cowardice depend on strategic circumstances; strength and weakness depend on dispositions.” Surely this is what it means!

At the battle of the Wei River, the enemy considered Han Xin easy to contend with. Han Xin dammed the river with sacks of sand, then turned and fled to lure the enemy forward. He then breached the dam and attacked fiercely when the enemy had crossed halfway, killing [Long] Ju. This shows skill in overthrowing an opponent. In the case of Tan Daoji, who fought successive engagements in the region of the Ji River, he counted out measures aloud while measuring sand, because a deserter had reported that his supplies were exhausted. Without this stratagem he would not have escaped. Daoji was indeed adept at preserving his own forces. The Wuzi says: “When troops ford a river, they may be attacked halfway across.” Those skilled in warfare make use of dispositions: surely this is what it means!

“Those who rush a hundred li to seize an advantage will lose their chief commander”: this is a saying from the Military Records. Pang Juan indeed advanced at twice the usual pace with his light, picked troops [?], and…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
不免於馬陵矣唐之太宗所以累勝之威西
向長安所謂兵貴神速圖天下之大幾也
取若振槁其巳計之明乎包原隰而軍者
爲敵禽此兵忌也先主國以七百里連營
而困於秭歸矣魏之鄧艾乘劒門之守深
入險平所謂衝其腹心伐國之祕謀也攻
其無備其巳籌之素乎諸葛孔明以三代
遺法列八陣於魚腹敵不敢屈此黃帝遺
謀昔戰者所必稽也而岳武穆乃謂運用
===
之妙存乎一心則兵識將意將識士情必
武形而後可也不然則無制之兵不可以
得志矣程不識爲邊將太守每將軍屯必
正部伍此師出以律善將者所必由也而
李廣乃令人人自便不擊刁斗則士卒佚
樂咸爲之死必嚴而後可也不然則虜卒
犯之無以禁矣狄武襄之破儂智高也上
元變宴夜半奪關謁出其不意之義也稱
疾如內數使勞客得算而開暇耳說者謂
punctuated: 不免於馬陵矣。唐之太宗所以累勝之威，西向長安，所謂兵貴神速，圖天下之大幾也。取若振槁，其巳計之明乎？包原隰而軍者，爲敵禽，此兵忌也。先主國以七百里連營，而困於秭歸矣。魏之鄧艾乘劒門之守，深入險平，所謂衝其腹心，伐國之祕謀也。攻其無備，其巳籌之素乎？諸葛孔明以三代遺法，列八陣於魚腹，敵不敢屈，此黃帝遺謀，昔戰者所必稽也。而岳武穆乃謂：「運用之妙，存乎一心。」則兵識將意，將識士情，必武形而後可也。不然，則無制之兵，不可以得志矣。程不識爲邊將太守，每將軍屯，必正部伍，此師出以律，善將者所必由也。而李廣乃令人人自便，不擊刁斗，則士卒佚樂，咸爲之死，必嚴而後可也。不然，則虜卒犯之，無以禁矣。狄武襄之破儂智高也，上元變宴，夜半奪關，謁出其不意之義也。稱疾如內，數使勞客，得算而開暇耳。說者謂
translation_en:
…he could not escape defeat at Maling. Emperor Taizong of the Tang, drawing upon the might of successive victories, advanced west toward Chang’an. This exemplifies the saying that extraordinary speed is prized in warfare: he was planning at the crucial juncture for gaining all under Heaven. His conquests were as easy as shaking down withered leaves; surely his calculations had already been clear!

Those who encamp with their forces spread across uplands and lowlands become their enemy’s captives: this is a military taboo. The First Sovereign of Shu established linked camps extending seven hundred li [?] and came to grief at Zigui. Deng Ai of Wei took advantage of the defense of Jianmen to penetrate deep into difficult and level terrain [?]. This exemplifies striking at an enemy’s heart, a secret stratagem for conquering a state. He attacked where the enemy was unprepared; surely his plans had long been laid!

Zhuge Kongming, following methods handed down from the Three Dynasties, arranged the Eight Formations at Yufu, and the enemy dared not overpower him. These were plans inherited from the Yellow Emperor, which warriors of old necessarily consulted. Yet Yue Wumu said: “The subtlety of their employment lies in the mind alone.” Thus the soldiers must understand their commander’s intentions, and the commander must understand his men’s feelings; only then can military dispositions be effective [?]. Otherwise, an army without regulation cannot achieve its aims.

When Cheng Bushi served as a frontier commander and governor, whenever he led troops into camp he invariably put their units in proper order. This exemplifies the principle that an army takes the field under discipline, which every skilled commander must follow. Yet Li Guang allowed everyone to act as he pleased and did not strike the watch cauldrons. His soldiers consequently enjoyed ease and comfort, and all were willing to die for him. Nevertheless, strictness was indispensable. Otherwise, if enemy troops suddenly attacked, there would be no means of stopping them.

When Di Wuxiang defeated Nong Zhigao, he altered the banquet on the Lantern Festival and seized the pass at midnight, exemplifying [?] the principle of taking the enemy by surprise. Claiming illness, he went inside [?] and repeatedly sent people to attend to his guests: he had secured a winning plan and merely appeared at leisure [?]. Commentators say…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
只一易字其獨觀其深耶韓淮陰之言於
高帝也自謂將兵多多益辨蓋識衆寡之
用也乘勝遠鬬鋒不可當國士之無雙者
也說者謂只一簡字其善發其蘊耶軍志
有之曰計險厄遠近上將之道也馬援之
聚米指畫明於滅囂之形矣乃充國之於
羌有謂兵難遥度則因敵變化而取勝信
非老臣不可也視之伏波其用異宜耳傳
有之曰一日縱敵數世之患張良勸帝襲
===
羽於於與漢之幾矣乃充國之於羌有謂
窮寇勿迫則緩之走不顧信乎以全取勝
也擬之留侯其敵異勢耳赤壁之戰曹操
驅中國之士遠涉江湖所謂强弩之末不
穿魯縞者也其敗宜矣謝玄以七萬衆大
潰苻堅則亂而取之周瑜之遺智也李靖
曰淝水之役非玄之善堅之不善也其有
以辨此乎泜水之捷韓信以背水爲陣人
殊死戰所謂投之亡地然後存者也其勝
punctuated: 只一易字，其獨觀其深耶？韓淮陰之言於高帝也，自謂將兵多多益辨，蓋識衆寡之用也。乘勝遠鬬，鋒不可當，國士之無雙者也。說者謂只一簡字，其善發其蘊耶？軍志有之曰：「計險厄遠近，上將之道也。」馬援之聚米指畫，明於滅囂之形矣。乃充國之於羌，有謂兵難遥度，則因敵變化而取勝，信非老臣不可也。視之伏波，其用異宜耳。傳有之曰：「一日縱敵，數世之患。」張良勸帝襲羽，於於與漢之幾矣。乃充國之於羌，有謂窮寇勿迫，則緩之走不顧，信乎以全取勝也。擬之留侯，其敵異勢耳。赤壁之戰，曹操驅中國之士遠涉江湖，所謂强弩之末不穿魯縞者也，其敗宜矣。謝玄以七萬衆大潰苻堅，則亂而取之，周瑜之遺智也。李靖曰：「淝水之役，非玄之善，堅之不善也。」其有以辨此乎？泜水之捷，韓信以背水爲陣，人殊死戰，所謂投之亡地然後存者也，其勝
translation_en:
…merely the single word “ease”: did this interpreter alone perceive its deeper significance? When Han Xin, Marquis of Huaiyin, spoke to Emperor Gao, he said of his own command of troops that the more he had, the better he could manage them. He understood how to employ forces both large and small. Riding the momentum of victory to fight far afield, his advance was irresistible: he was an unparalleled talent of the realm. An interpreter says that it comes down to the single word “simplicity.” Does this aptly disclose the underlying meaning?

The Records of Warfare states: “To assess difficult terrain and distances is the way of a superior commander.” By piling up rice and pointing out the terrain, Ma Yuan demonstrated his understanding of the strategic configuration needed to destroy Xiao. Yet Chongguo, dealing with the Qiang, said that military affairs were difficult to assess from afar. Victory must therefore be won by adapting to changes in the enemy: truly, this required a seasoned minister. Compared with the General Who Calms the Waves, his methods simply suited different circumstances.

The tradition states: “To let an enemy escape for one day brings trouble for several generations.” Zhang Liang urged the emperor to attack Yu—at a critical juncture for the Han [?]. Yet Chongguo, dealing with the Qiang, said that a desperate enemy should not be pressed. By easing the pressure, he let them flee without looking back: this was indeed winning victory while preserving one’s forces intact. Compared with the Marquis of Liu, he simply faced an enemy in a different strategic situation.

At the Battle of Chibi, Cao Cao drove men from the Central Lands far across rivers and lakes. This was what is meant by saying that a bolt from a powerful crossbow, at the end of its flight, cannot penetrate even fine silk from Lu. His defeat was to be expected. Xie Xuan, with seventy thousand men, utterly routed Fu Jian: he took advantage of disorder to overcome him, applying the strategic wisdom handed down by Zhou Yu. Li Jing said: “The outcome at the Battle of the Fei River was due not to Xuan’s skill but to Jian’s lack of skill.” Is there a way to distinguish between these interpretations?

In the victory at the Zhi River, Han Xin drew up his formation with its back to the water, and every man fought to the death. This was what is meant by placing men on deadly ground so that they may then survive. His victory…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
宜矣王霸以往視河水詭言氷合則欲前
阻水亦信之遺謀也光武曰王霸權以濟
事殆天瑞也其有以識此乎是皆審於得
失之勢而當其機是謂因敵而制勝決於
勝敗之機而當其勢是謂因時而制宜古
之善用兵者由是其選也不然則龐涓與
臏共學兵法爲魏大將權非輕也龍且提
二十萬衆以信易與勇非微也曹操兼荆
州之新附符堅率三秦以投鞭勢非寡也
===
昭烈以全蜀之衆銳於報怨力非弱也乃
其計之不得威盡勢極爲天下笑咎生於
恃强鬬力其機之不察而其勢之不早辨
也孰事曰犄角之勢覆人之逵計也奇正
之變馭敵之祕機也無乃亦以是乎雖然
知犄人而不知自犄勝不可必也知奇正
而不知奇中之正正中之奇勝不可必也
無窮如天地不竭如江河非通陰陽之機
達萬物之變者其孰能知哉然必何如而
punctuated: 宜矣。王霸以往視河水，詭言氷合，則欲前阻水，亦信之遺謀也。光武曰：「王霸權以濟事，殆天瑞也。」其有以識此乎？是皆審於得失之勢而當其機，是謂因敵而制勝；決於勝敗之機而當其勢，是謂因時而制宜。古之善用兵者，由是其選也。不然，則龐涓與臏共學兵法，爲魏大將，權非輕也；龍且提二十萬衆，以信易與，勇非微也；曹操兼荆州之新附，符堅率三秦以投鞭，勢非寡也；昭烈以全蜀之衆，銳於報怨，力非弱也。乃其計之不得，威盡勢極，爲天下笑，咎生於恃强鬬力，其機之不察，而其勢之不早辨也。孰事曰：「犄角之勢，覆人之逵計也；奇正之變，馭敵之祕機也。」無乃亦以是乎？雖然，知犄人而不知自犄，勝不可必也；知奇正而不知奇中之正、正中之奇，勝不可必也。無窮如天地，不竭如江河，非通陰陽之機、達萬物之變者，其孰能知哉？然必何如而
translation_en:
…was only to be expected. Wang Ba went to inspect the river and falsely reported that the ice had closed over it. With the advance blocked by water, this too followed a stratagem handed down by Han Xin. Emperor Guangwu said: “Wang Ba used an expedient to bring the affair to a successful conclusion; this was surely an auspicious sign from Heaven.” How are we to understand this? All these men scrutinized the circumstances governing gain and loss and acted at the opportune moment: this is called securing victory by adapting to the enemy. They judged the critical moment governing victory and defeat and acted as the circumstances required: this is called adopting appropriate measures according to the time. Those of antiquity who excelled in warfare distinguished themselves through this.

Otherwise, consider Pang Juan: he studied military methods together with Sun Bin and became a great general of Wei; his authority was hardly slight. Long Ju led two hundred thousand troops and thought Han Xin easy to contend with; his courage was hardly small. Cao Cao absorbed the newly submitted forces of Jingzhou, and Fu Jian led the forces of the Three Qin regions, boasting that their thrown whips could block a river; their forces were hardly few. Emperor Zhaolie, with the troops of all Shu, was intent on avenging his grievance; his strength was hardly feeble. Yet their plans failed, their might was exhausted, and their power reached its limit, making them laughingstocks throughout the realm. The fault arose from relying on strength and competing in force: they failed to perceive the critical moment and to discern the circumstances early enough.

An unclear attribution [?] introduces the saying: “A mutually supporting deployment is a far-reaching plan [?] for overthrowing others; transformations between the unorthodox and orthodox are the hidden key to controlling the enemy.” Is this not also the reason? Even so, if one knows how to outflank others but does not know how to protect one’s own flanks, victory cannot be assured. If one knows the unorthodox and orthodox but does not know the orthodox within the unorthodox and the unorthodox within the orthodox, victory cannot be assured. Boundless as Heaven and Earth, inexhaustible as the Yangzi and Yellow Rivers—who can understand these transformations unless he comprehends the workings of yin and yang and grasps the changes of all things? Yet what must one be like before…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
後可曰泰山覆於前而色不變麋鹿興於
左而目不瞬然後可以制利害可以持敵
不然敵未交而心已怵矣雖有利害其孰
知之然則欲成天下之將材者亦於治心
養氣中求之乎此非老生之常談也
廟堂之上宜留神焉
第五問
陳加命
同考試官教諭吳　批〔條列弭盜之方援古酌今〕
===
曲盡籌畫蓋抱經世之蘊者與
同考試官教諭何　批〔採本銷萌其說良是非識〕
時務者不能道此
考試官教諭胡　批〔詳明切當鑿鑿可行〕
考試官學正史　批〔文古而慮周策之佳者〕
治盜之法必探其本而後可與慮始必銷
其萌而後可與圖成夫盜之所由生也有
本焉昧者爲之則標末是務譬之揚湯以
止沸夫是之謂悖盜之所由盛也有萌焉
punctuated:
後可？曰：「泰山覆於前而色不變，麋鹿興於左而目不瞬，然後可以制利害，可以持敵。不然，敵未交而心已怵矣。雖有利害，其孰知之？然則欲成天下之將材者，亦於治心養氣中求之乎？此非老生之常談也。廟堂之上宜留神焉。」

第五問
陳加命
同考試官教諭吳，批〔條列弭盜之方，援古酌今〕曲盡籌畫，蓋抱經世之蘊者與！
同考試官教諭何，批〔採本銷萌，其說良是，非識〕時務者不能道此。
考試官教諭胡，批〔詳明切當，鑿鑿可行。〕
考試官學正史，批〔文古而慮周，策之佳者。〕

治盜之法，必探其本而後可與慮始，必銷其萌而後可與圖成。夫盜之所由生也，有本焉。昧者爲之，則標末是務，譬之揚湯以止沸，夫是之謂悖。盜之所由盛也，有萌焉。
translation_en:
…before this can be achieved? The answer is: “Only when Mount Tai topples before him without his expression changing, and deer spring up at his left without his eyes blinking, can he control advantage and harm and hold his own against the enemy. Otherwise, before the enemy has even been engaged, his heart is already fearful. Though advantages and dangers exist, how could he discern them? Thus, should those who seek to develop talent for generalship throughout the realm also seek it in disciplining the mind and nurturing vital energy? This is no commonplace of old scholars.
