Those in the highest councils of government should give it careful attention.”

Fifth Policy Question
Chen Jiaming

Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: “He sets out in order the methods for suppressing banditry, drawing on antiquity and weighing present circumstances. His planning encompasses every detail. Surely he possesses a store of learning for ordering the world!”

Comment by Associate Examiner He, Instructor: “Addressing the root and extinguishing the first stirrings—his argument is sound indeed. No one unfamiliar with the affairs of the day could say this.”

Comment by Examiner Hu, Instructor: “Detailed, clear, pertinent, and appropriate; each proposal is demonstrably practicable.”

Comment by Examiner Shi, School Instructor: “Antique in style and comprehensive in deliberation: an excellent policy essay.”

In dealing with banditry, one must investigate its roots before one can take part in deliberations on initial measures; one must extinguish its first stirrings before one can take part in planning for success. There are roots from which banditry arises. When the uncomprehending deal with it, they concern themselves only with superficial manifestations. This is like ladling up hot water to stop it boiling: this is what is called acting perversely. There are incipient causes from which banditry grows rampant.…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
玩者爲之則姑息是安譬之養莠以藝苗
夫是之謂弛弛者不能治悖者不知所以
治而盜賊之日熾不息職此矣執事惻心
民隱計安中土惓惓以弭盜下問然往歲
宋郊逋孽假擾鄢潁間賴羣策壯猷旋即
掃蕩已事得失大可見矣語曰前事之不
忘後事之師鑒也今幸比歲收入四境稱
治然無賴子弟猶業椎剽倏爲聚散長民
者誠不可忽必思其故而規制之今前所
===
陳不由矣稽之周禮太宰以九職任萬民
則民有常業不見異物而遷焉猶懼其富
而莫之教也而司徒訓之以五典施之十
有二教於是有鄉大夫以考德行察道藝
有州長屬州民而讀法以勸戒之有黨正
掌黨之政令教治有族師掌族之戒令政
事司諫以糾民德司救以誅讓其邪惡其
所以道民於善者至悉也雖有驁悍之徒
庚行莫或逞矣大司馬以九伐正邦國則
punctuated:
玩者爲之，則姑息是安，譬之養莠以藝苗，夫是之謂弛。弛者不能治，悖者不知所以治，而盜賊之日熾不息，職此矣。執事惻心民隱，計安中土，惓惓以弭盜下問。然往歲宋郊逋孽假擾鄢潁間，賴羣策壯猷，旋即掃蕩，已事得失大可見矣。語曰：「前事之不忘，後事之師鑒也。」今幸比歲收入，四境稱治，然無賴子弟猶業椎剽，倏爲聚散。長民者誠不可忽，必思其故而規制之。今前所陳不由矣。
稽之《周禮》，太宰以九職任萬民，則民有常業，不見異物而遷焉。猶懼其富而莫之教也，而司徒訓之以五典，施之十有二教。於是有鄉大夫以考德行、察道藝，有州長屬州民而讀法以勸戒之，有黨正掌黨之政令教治，有族師掌族之戒令政事，司諫以糾民德，司救以誅讓其邪惡。其所以道民於善者至悉也，雖有驁悍之徒，庚行莫或逞矣。大司馬以九伐正邦國，則
translation_en:
…Those who treat the matter carelessly rest content with indulgence, like nurturing weeds in order to cultivate grain: this is called laxity. The lax cannot bring order, while the misguided do not know how to do so. This is precisely why banditry grows daily more rampant without abating. You, sir, feel compassion for the people's hidden sufferings and devise ways to secure the Central Lands; in your earnest concern, you have condescended to ask how banditry may be quelled. In past years, fugitive rebels from the environs of Song caused disturbances [?] between Yan and Ying. Through collective planning and vigorous strategy, they were swiftly swept away. The successes and failures of those past events are plain to see. As the saying goes, “Past events, if not forgotten, serve as lessons and a mirror for what follows.” Fortunately, recent years have brought harvests [?], and the territory is said to be well governed. Yet dissolute young men still make a trade of violent robbery, suddenly gathering and dispersing. Those who govern the people must certainly not neglect this: they must consider its causes and devise measures to control it. Now, what was set forth above is not followed [?].
Examining the Rites of Zhou, we find that the Grand Steward assigned the myriad people to the nine occupations. Thus the people had settled livelihoods and would not change them upon seeing unfamiliar goods. Yet there remained concern that they might become prosperous without receiving instruction, so the Minister of Education instructed them in the five norms and applied the twelve teachings. There were therefore Township Grand Masters to assess virtue and conduct and examine mastery of the Way and the arts; District Chiefs to assemble their district's people and read the laws to encourage and admonish them; Neighborhood Heads to administer their neighborhoods' ordinances, instruction, and governance; and Clan Masters to administer their groups' admonitions, ordinances, and governmental affairs. The Admonishers corrected the people's moral conduct, while the Correctors censured their depravity and wrongdoing. The means of guiding the people toward goodness were most comprehensive. Even if there were unruly and violent men, none could give free rein to their conduct [?]. The Grand Minister of War used the nine punitive expeditions to rectify the states, and thus…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
國不興政民得少過焉猶懼其流而莫之
防也而士師掌士之八成聯民之什伍以
比追胥之事於是有司厲氏以辨盜物有
野廬氏以聚㰕賓客達道路有司寤氏以
詔夜禁有脩閭氏以禁徑踰馳騁國中者
其所以防民之慝者至備也雖有凶獷之
衆苟計亦銷沮矣況其時中原之地田以
井授疆理其畝而川涂溝澮止水浚坊民
之經往循途旅進莫有鶩心後世阡陌旣
===
廢民失常業兼幷恣睢征斂無藝庠教化
陵夷風俗頽敗而所在四鄙無爲限隔旣
損德心又長跋扈即水旱歲仍盜賊繁興
矣此大較也今欲令盜不興發莫若脩其
本周人之教固難幾企也而九職任民可
容失所乎欲令盜不延蔓莫若折其萌周
人之政迹亦今事也而備舉不隳豈不在
人乎是故其未形也探其本而制之則理
道豫得民莫與爲姦也其始形也銷其萌
punctuated:
國不興政，民得少過焉。猶懼其流而莫之防也，而士師掌士之八成，聯民之什伍，以比追胥之事。於是有司厲氏以辨盜物，有野廬氏以聚㰕賓客、達道路，有司寤氏以詔夜禁，有脩閭氏以禁徑踰、馳騁國中者。其所以防民之慝者至備也，雖有凶獷之衆，苟計亦銷沮矣。況其時中原之地，田以井授，疆理其畝，而川涂溝澮，止水浚坊，民之經往循途旅進，莫有鶩心。後世阡陌旣廢，民失常業，兼幷恣睢，征斂無藝，庠教化陵夷，風俗頽敗，而所在四鄙無爲限隔，旣損德心，又長跋扈，即水旱歲仍，盜賊繁興矣。此大較也。
今欲令盜不興發，莫若脩其本。周人之教固難幾企也，而九職任民，可容失所乎？欲令盜不延蔓，莫若折其萌。周人之政迹亦今事也，而備舉不隳，豈不在人乎？是故其未形也，探其本而制之，則理道豫得，民莫與爲姦也；其始形也，銷其萌
translation_en:
…the states did not undertake governance [?], and the people were able to commit fewer transgressions. Yet there was still concern that their wayward tendencies might go unchecked. The Chief Judge therefore administered the eight established judicial procedures and organized the people into groups of ten and five to coordinate pursuit and apprehension. There were then officials responsible for penal laborers who identified stolen property; officials responsible for lodgings in the countryside who assembled guests [?] and kept roads open; officials responsible for night watches who proclaimed nighttime prohibitions; and officials responsible for neighborhood lanes who prohibited taking shortcuts, climbing over barriers, and galloping within the capital. The provisions for preventing wrongdoing among the people were utterly comprehensive. Even among fierce and unruly groups, illicit schemes would be dispelled and frustrated. Moreover, in those days, land in the Central Plain was allotted under the well-field system, with the fields demarcated and laid out. Waterways, roads, ditches, and channels, together with water barriers and dredged embankments [?], regulated the people's movements: they followed established routes and advanced in company, with no thought of straying. In later ages, once the field boundaries had been abolished, the people lost their settled livelihoods. Those who engrossed land acted without restraint, and taxation knew no bounds. Education in the schools declined [?], customs deteriorated, and throughout the outlying districts there were no barriers to restrict movement. This both weakened moral inclinations and encouraged defiance. When floods and droughts then recurred year after year, banditry proliferated. Such is the general outline.
If we now wish to prevent banditry from arising, nothing is better than putting its foundations in order. The instruction practiced by the people of Zhou is admittedly difficult to approach, but if the people are assigned work in the nine occupations, can we allow them to be left without a livelihood? If we wish to prevent banditry from spreading, nothing is better than cutting off its first shoots. The governmental practices of Zhou are also matters for the present day. Does not their comprehensive implementation, without neglect, depend upon those responsible? Thus, before banditry takes shape, if we investigate its roots and bring it under control, the way of good government will have been secured in advance, and none of the people will join in wrongdoing. When it first takes shape, extinguish its first shoots…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
以遏之則先人奪人民莫能爲姦也自漢
而下人殊其制無非息患之訏謨也乃所
以底厥成效可考鏡而行焉渤海歲饑盜
賊並起至難勝也龔遂之治計於安之遂
至使民賣刀買犢郡中稱大治焉則移教
罷捕民安其業勸農發廩選用良吏遂已
端其本矣京兆尹抱鼓數起至無道也
召廣張敞起刺冀州遂能至部令盜屏息
不敢復忩焉則威名素著吏民祗令豪猾
===
聞風氣遂餒解敞誠折其萌矣朝歌之賊
州郡莫禁虞詡爲之則設三科以募壯士
誘賊劫掠因伏殺之由是駭散詡之所以
稱明其計得也廣陵之盜寇亂余揚張綱
爲之則單車之職以書譬諭咸謂釜中遊
魚得更生焉由是降息綱之所爲推誠其
仁沃也賈琮之刺交趾也觸倨誅帥簡選
良吏民稱賈父由清平焉朱儁之攻黃巾
也不聽納降恐開逆意凜然大義眞良計
punctuated: 以遏之，則先人奪人，民莫能爲姦也。自漢而下，人殊其制，無非息患之訏謨也。乃所以底厥成效，可考鏡而行焉。渤海歲饑，盜賊並起，至難勝也。龔遂之治，計於安之，遂至使民賣刀買犢，郡中稱大治焉。則移教罷捕，民安其業，勸農發廩，選用良吏，遂已端其本矣。京兆尹抱鼓數起，至無道也。召廣張敞起刺冀州，遂能至部令盜屏息，不敢復忩焉。則威名素著，吏民祗令，豪猾聞風，氣遂餒解，敞誠折其萌矣。朝歌之賊，州郡莫禁。虞詡爲之，則設三科以募壯士，誘賊劫掠，因伏殺之，由是駭散。詡之所以稱明，其計得也。廣陵之盜，寇亂余揚。張綱爲之，則單車之職，以書譬諭，咸謂釜中遊魚得更生焉，由是降息。綱之所爲推誠，其仁沃也。賈琮之刺交趾也，觸倨誅帥，簡選良吏，民稱賈父，由清平焉。朱儁之攻黃巾也，不聽納降，恐開逆意，凜然大義，眞良計
translation_en:
…to check them, one anticipates and overawes them, so that the people cannot perpetrate wrongdoing. From the Han onward, men adopted different measures, all of them grand plans for ending disorder. The means by which they achieved results can be examined as precedents and put into practice. In Bohai, famine brought bandits rising everywhere, until they became exceedingly difficult to subdue. Gong Sui’s administration aimed to pacify them, ultimately inducing the people to sell their swords and buy calves; the commandery was acclaimed as thoroughly well governed. By issuing instructions to halt arrests, allowing the people to pursue their livelihoods in peace, encouraging agriculture, opening the granaries, and appointing good officials, Sui had already set the root of the problem right. Under the Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao, incidents of “embracing drums” repeatedly arose [?], and lawlessness became extreme. Zhang Chang was summoned—“guang” [?]—and appointed Regional Inspector of Jizhou. Upon reaching his jurisdiction, he made the bandits hold their breath in fear, not daring to cause further disturbance. His imposing reputation was already established; officials and commoners obeyed his orders respectfully, while powerful malefactors, hearing of him, lost heart and their resolve dissolved. Chang truly checked the trouble at its inception.

The bandits of Chaoge could not be restrained by the regional or commandery authorities. When Yu Xu took charge, he established three categories for recruiting stalwart men, lured the bandits into plundering, and then killed them in ambush. Thus terrified, they scattered. Xu was acclaimed as discerning because his strategy was sound. The bandits of Guangling pillaged and disrupted Yu and Yang [?]. When Zhang Gang took charge, he traveled to his post in a single carriage and reasoned with them by letter. They all said that, like fish swimming in a cauldron, they had gained a new lease on life; they consequently surrendered and ceased their depredations. Gang’s dealings with them displayed sincerity, and his benevolence was abundant. When Jia Cong served as Regional Inspector of Jiaozhi, he confronted the arrogant [?], executed the ringleaders, and carefully selected good officials. The people called him Father Jia, and peace and order followed. When Zhu Jun attacked the Yellow Turbans, he would not consent to accepting their surrender, fearing that this would encourage rebellious intentions. His solemn commitment to the greater moral duty was truly a sound strategy…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
焉善乎楊賜之言曰宜敕州縣簡別流民
以孤其黨然後誅其渠帥可不勞而定此
達權之通計其明於遏盜之機矣自宋以
來人異其議無非弭盜之遠猷也乃所以
當厥機宜可更僕而數焉富弼之言曰兇
險之徒自負圖大結煽民間亦能始禍要
在得而縻之使其謀不成則鼠輩為羣不
足慮矣此唐人失之於黃巢者也蘇軾之
言曰德不足而才有餘者困於無門無所
===
不至願召豪猾而籠用之使歆利進身則
縱有嘯聚亦自無徒矣亦弼之慮於慶曆
者也至於歐陽修所謂四事則州郡置兵
為備也選捕盜之官也明賞罰之法也用
良吏以撫疲民也而用良吏之一言尤為
首務其諸龔買之已事乎秦觀所謂二弊
則以患莫大於招降禍莫深於窮治招降
則誘民為盜窮治則驅民為盜而傷惠損
威之論尤為明備其諸殲渠之深意乎善
punctuated: 焉。善乎，楊賜之言曰：「宜敕州縣簡別流民，以孤其黨，然後誅其渠帥，可不勞而定。」此達權之通計，其明於遏盜之機矣。自宋以來，人異其議，無非弭盜之遠猷也。乃所以當厥機宜，可更僕而數焉。富弼之言曰：「兇險之徒，自負圖大，結煽民間，亦能始禍。要在得而縻之，使其謀不成，則鼠輩為羣，不足慮矣。」此唐人失之於黃巢者也。蘇軾之言曰：「德不足而才有餘者，困於無門，無所不至。願召豪猾而籠用之，使歆利進身，則縱有嘯聚，亦自無徒矣。」亦弼之慮於慶曆者也。至於歐陽修所謂四事，則州郡置兵為備也，選捕盜之官也，明賞罰之法也，用良吏以撫疲民也。而用良吏之一言，尤為首務，其諸龔買之已事乎？秦觀所謂二弊，則以患莫大於招降，禍莫深於窮治。招降則誘民為盜，窮治則驅民為盜。而傷惠損威之論，尤為明備，其諸殲渠之深意乎？善
translation_en:
…indeed. How excellent were Yang Ci’s words: “The prefectures and counties should be ordered to distinguish and separate out the displaced people, thereby isolating the bandits’ following. Then execute their ringleaders, and the trouble can be settled without toil.” This was a comprehensive strategy showing mastery of expedient action and a clear understanding of the crucial means of checking banditry. Since the Song, men have differed in their proposals, yet all were farsighted plans for suppressing banditry. As for the ways these suited particular circumstances, one could go on enumerating them through successive changes of attendants.

Fu Bi said: “Violent and devious men, confident in themselves and harboring grand designs, form connections and stir up the populace; they too can initiate disorder. The essential thing is to secure and keep them under control, preventing their schemes from succeeding. Then, even if those rats gather in bands, they are no cause for concern.” This is what the men of the Tang failed to do in the case of Huang Chao. Su Shi said: “Those whose virtue is deficient but whose talents are abundant will stop at nothing when frustrated by the lack of an avenue for advancement. I ask that powerful and cunning men be summoned, brought within our control, and employed. Let them be enticed by the benefits of advancement; then, even if someone calls for a band to gather, he will find no followers.” This, too, was Fu Bi’s concern during the Qingli reign period.

As for Ouyang Xiu’s so-called four measures, they were: station troops in prefectures and commanderies as a precaution; select officials to apprehend bandits; make the rules for rewards and punishments clear; and employ good officials to soothe the exhausted people. Of these, employing good officials is especially the foremost task. Was this perhaps what Gong Mai [?] had already accomplished? Qin Guan’s so-called two abuses rested on the view that no trouble is greater than soliciting surrender, and no calamity deeper than pursuing investigations to the utmost. Soliciting surrender entices people to become bandits; exhaustive investigation drives people to become bandits. His discussion of impairing benevolence and diminishing authority was particularly clear and comprehensive. Was this perhaps the deeper intent behind annihilating the ringleaders? How excellent…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
乎觀又有言曰盜之羣起也必速戢以折
其氣勿迫以携其心初緩則勢縱後急則
變生此權筭之達論其審於弭盜之術矣
是故稽古人之成效而因地制宜則其理
得緣古人之讜議而因時致用則其制盡
選用良吏民樂資業探本者所必由也準
而行之不有以窒盜之源乎孤弱黨與籠
取豪猾此鋤萌者所必務也擇而施之不
有以遏盜之漸乎不然則窮治之不已是
===
亂繩之絞急不可圖也禦之於已熾是續
膏而滅燄不可得也揚雄有言曰御得其
道天下狙詐咸作使御失其道天下狙詐
咸作敵長民者可以觀矣雖然猶有出於
是焉本所當敦矣而今之所尤急者風教
之不端也風教端而民習正庶乎無蕩心
萌不可長矣而今之所當先者積窩之不
絶也積窩絶而民黨除庶乎無隱慝夫民
習之靡也誘於賭博溺於酒食遲投於控
punctuated:
乎！觀又有言曰：「盜之羣起也，必速戢以折其氣，勿迫以携其心。初緩則勢縱，後急則變生。」此權筭之達論，其審於弭盜之術矣。是故稽古人之成效而因地制宜，則其理得；緣古人之讜議而因時致用，則其制盡。選用良吏，民樂資業，探本者所必由也。準而行之，不有以窒盜之源乎？孤弱黨與，籠取豪猾，此鋤萌者所必務也。擇而施之，不有以遏盜之漸乎？不然，則窮治之不已，是亂繩之絞急，不可圖也；禦之於已熾，是續膏而滅燄，不可得也。揚雄有言曰：「御得其道，天下狙詐咸作使；御失其道，天下狙詐咸作敵。」長民者可以觀矣。
雖然，猶有出於是焉。本所當敦矣，而今之所尤急者，風教之不端也。風教端而民習正，庶乎無蕩心。萌不可長矣，而今之所當先者，積窩之不絶也。積窩絶而民黨除，庶乎無隱慝。夫民習之靡也，誘於賭博，溺於酒食，遲投於控
translation_en:
…well said! Qin Guan further said: “When bandits rise in groups, they must be swiftly restrained to break their spirit, but not pressed so hard that their hearts are driven away. If action is lax at the outset, their power grows unchecked; if pressure is severe afterward, upheaval results.” This is a penetrating discussion of practical strategy, showing a thorough understanding of the methods for suppressing banditry. Thus, if we examine the effective achievements of the ancients and adapt measures to local conditions, we grasp the underlying principles; if we follow their sound counsels and apply them to present circumstances, we fully realize the efficacy of their measures. Selecting and employing good officials so that the people take pleasure in their livelihoods is the necessary course for those who address the root. If we act according to this standard, will we not thereby stop up the source of banditry? Isolating and weakening their adherents, and entrapping powerful villains, are essential tasks for those who would root out its first shoots. If we select and implement these measures, will we not check the growth of banditry? Otherwise, pursuing investigations relentlessly is like tightening a tangled cord: the knot becomes impossible to resolve. Resisting banditry only after it has blazed up is like adding oil while trying to extinguish a flame: success is impossible. Yang Xiong said: “When governance follows the proper way, all the cunning and deceitful under Heaven become its servants; when governance loses the proper way, all the cunning and deceitful under Heaven become its enemies.” Those who govern the people may take heed of this.
Nevertheless, there is something beyond these considerations. The root must indeed be strengthened, but what is especially urgent today is the failure to set moral influence and instruction aright. Once these are set aright and the people’s habits are corrected, we may hope that their hearts will cease to stray. The first shoots must not be allowed to grow, but what should take precedence today is the failure to eliminate longstanding bandit hideouts. Once these hideouts are eliminated and the people’s bandit affiliations removed, we may hope that no concealed wickedness will remain. As for the corruption of the people’s habits, they are enticed by gambling, submerged in wine and food, and drawn into [?] …

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
縱恍心於紛華資財之不竭不已也何也
其心蕩也竭且不繼則取非其有羣趨而
爲之甘心於狝髦就戮而莫之恤矣愚甞
曰豫土之多盜末游之未剏也夫困於饑
寒而敢於剽刼亦人情也乃樂歲而不息
焉此其故可槪識矣由是而飭之以擯姦
萌可不嚴其禁耶夫積窩之固結也坐享
其利人畏其勢無爲盜之形擅爲盜之實
爲之愈久而愈無忌也何也其利厚也心
===
且無忌則深根蟠結里閈效尤甘心於爲
之黨而莫之恤矣愚甞曰豫土之治盜刻
窩其急務也夫剽吏而奪之金猶懼其逐
捕而莫之掩匿固賊情也乃養寇以自資
而深爲逋藪焉此其姦益甚矣由是而詧
之以除惡本可不重其法耶由是而小行
剽刼則嚴爲緝捕以抉摘其姦而安業之
民可無虞也由是而大或嘯聚則速爲□
發以挫折其氣而窺伺之衆可無附□□
punctuated:
縱恍心於紛華，資財之不竭不已也。何也？其心蕩也。竭且不繼，則取非其有，羣趨而爲之，甘心於狝髦就戮而莫之恤矣。愚甞曰：「豫土之多盜，末游之未剏也。」夫困於饑寒而敢於剽刼，亦人情也；乃樂歲而不息焉，此其故可槪識矣。由是而飭之以擯姦萌，可不嚴其禁耶？

夫積窩之固結也，坐享其利，人畏其勢，無爲盜之形，擅爲盜之實，爲之愈久而愈無忌也。何也？其利厚也。心且無忌，則深根蟠結，里閈效尤，甘心於爲之黨而莫之恤矣。愚甞曰：「豫土之治盜，刻窩其急務也。」夫剽吏而奪之金，猶懼其逐捕而莫之掩匿，固賊情也；乃養寇以自資，而深爲逋藪焉，此其姦益甚矣。由是而詧之以除惡本，可不重其法耶？由是而小行剽刼，則嚴爲緝捕，以抉摘其姦，而安業之民可無虞也。由是而大或嘯聚，則速爲□發，以挫折其氣，而窺伺之衆可無附□□
translation_en:
…letting their minds wander amid dazzling luxuries [?], they will not stop until their resources are exhausted. Why? Because their minds are unrestrained. Once their resources are exhausted and cannot be replenished, they take what does not belong to them, flocking together to do so, willingly facing slaughter and execution [?] without concern. I have often said: “The prevalence of bandits in Henan results from the failure to eliminate idle pursuits and secondary occupations [?].” That people driven by hunger and cold should dare to plunder is understandable human behavior. Yet when such acts persist even in years of plenty, their cause can be broadly discerned. If we are therefore to impose discipline and suppress the beginnings of wrongdoing, can we fail to enforce strict prohibitions?

Long-established harborers of bandits form entrenched networks. They sit back and enjoy the profits, while others fear their power. Without appearing to act as bandits, they exercise the substance of banditry; the longer they continue, the fewer their scruples. Why? Because their profits are substantial. Once their minds are without restraint, their roots grow deep and intertwine, and their neighbors follow their bad example, willingly becoming their accomplices without concern. I have often said: “In suppressing banditry in Henan, the urgent task is to deal sternly with those who harbor bandits [?].” Those who rob officials and seize their money still fear pursuit and arrest, and fear that no one will shelter or conceal them: such is certainly the disposition of criminals. Yet these harborers maintain bandits for their own enrichment and make themselves secure refuges for fugitives. Their wickedness is all the greater. If we are therefore to investigate them and eradicate the roots of evil, can we fail to impose severe penalties? Then, when plundering occurs on a small scale, pursue and arrest the offenders rigorously, exposing their wrongdoing, so that people peacefully pursuing their livelihoods may be free from anxiety. When bandits gather in large numbers, swiftly undertake [an illegible character] mobilization [?] to break their spirit, so that those watching for an opportunity may have none to join [two illegible characters]…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
由是而隣州縣之交地苟有事焉必同心
捕獲無論彼此盜固無所容也又由是而
嚴差捕之詐欺苟有犯焉必重罰以懲無
及平民盜固無由縱也若夫嚴保甲之什
伍謹覘諜之期會申告賞之明規舉連坐
之重罰皆亟行之故事惟良有司作之以
精明持之於悠久耳易曰神而明之存乎
其人君子可以觀矣
punctuated: 由是而隣州縣之交地，苟有事焉，必同心捕獲，無論彼此，盜固無所容也。又由是而嚴差捕之詐欺，苟有犯焉，必重罰以懲，無及平民，盜固無由縱也。若夫嚴保甲之什伍，謹覘諜之期會，申告賞之明規，舉連坐之重罰，皆亟行之故事，惟良有司作之以精明，持之於悠久耳。《易》曰：「神而明之，存乎其人。」君子可以觀矣。
translation_en: Furthermore, if an incident occurs along the boundaries of neighboring prefectures and counties, their officials must cooperate in apprehending the offenders, without distinguishing between their respective jurisdictions. Bandits will then have nowhere to find refuge. Furthermore, fraud and deception by officers assigned to apprehend criminals must be strictly checked. Any offenders must receive severe punishment as a deterrent, without implicating ordinary people; bandits will then have no means of escaping apprehension. As for rigorously organizing the baojia household security system into groups of ten and five, carefully observing appointed times for intelligence gathering, reiterating clear regulations on rewards for reporting crimes, and enforcing severe penalties for collective liability, these are all established measures to be implemented urgently. It only remains for capable officials to carry them out with discernment and sustain them over the long term. The Book of Changes says: “To bring out their wondrous efficacy and make them clear rests with the person.” Here is something for the gentleman to consider.

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
嘉靖乙卯河南鄉試事竣直
以執事當告成於末簡乃作
而颺言曰人材之興裨乎治
道而其生也關乎氣運之盛
道化之隆蓋自昔然矣豫當
寰宇中央陰陽冲會固天地
===
之奧區也粵自洪濛始判天
乃出圖書於河洛肇洩靈祕
授之聖神性道之玄機經世
之鴻猷於此乎開緘啓鑰邈
焉爲萬世宗仰玆非天所特
厚而眞元之氣所獨鍾者乎
故奕代發祥伊傅接軫周道
punctuated: 嘉靖乙卯河南鄉試事竣，直以執事當告成於末簡，乃作而颺言曰：「人材之興裨乎治道，而其生也關乎氣運之盛、道化之隆，蓋自昔然矣。豫當寰宇中央，陰陽冲會，固天地之奧區也。粵自洪濛始判，天乃出圖書於河洛，肇洩靈祕，授之聖神。性道之玄機、經世之鴻猷，於此乎開緘啓鑰，邈焉爲萬世宗仰。玆非天所特厚，而眞元之氣所獨鍾者乎？故奕代發祥，伊傅接軫，周道
translation_en: When the Henan Provincial Examination of the yimao year of Jiajing [1555] had concluded, I, Zhi, having served in its administration, was obliged to record its completion on the final pages. I therefore rose and proclaimed: “The emergence of talented men benefits the Way of government, while their birth depends upon the flourishing of cosmic forces and the fullness of moral transformation through the Way. This has been so since antiquity. Yu [Henan] occupies the center of the world, where yin and yang blend and converge; it is indeed an inner sanctuary of Heaven and Earth. When primordial chaos first divided, Heaven brought forth the Chart and the Writing from the He and Luo rivers, first revealing its numinous secrets and bestowing them upon the divine sages. Here the mysterious workings of human nature and the Way, and the grand plans for ordering the world, were unsealed and unlocked, to be revered as exemplary for all generations to come. Is this not a place especially favored by Heaven, where the true primordial vital force is uniquely concentrated? Thus, successive ages brought forth auspicious men, with Yi Yin and Fu Yue following one another in succession. The Way of Zhou…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
中興申甫降嶽至宋伊洛眞
儒倡明道學斯文賴以不墜
往牒昭然休哉遐矣
國朝奄有四海
祖宗
列聖統一聖眞
湛恩汪濊
===
聲教旁孚茲惟近藩漸被獨先
焉至我
皇上道契先天
德侔祇台
臨宇以來
建極錫福龥俊右文
皇極敷言之訓布列黌宮昭回雲
punctuated:
中興，申甫降嶽。至宋，伊洛眞儒倡明道學，斯文賴以不墜。往牒昭然，休哉，遐矣！
國朝奄有四海，祖宗列聖統一聖眞，湛恩汪濊，聲教旁孚。茲惟近藩，漸被獨先焉。至我皇上，道契先天，德侔祇台，臨宇以來，建極錫福，龥俊右文。皇極敷言之訓布列黌宮，昭回雲
translation_en:
…was restored to flourishing, and Shen and Fu descended from the sacred mountain. By the Song dynasty, the true Confucians of the Yi and Luo rivers expounded and clarified the Learning of the Way; through them this cultural tradition was preserved from decline. The records of the past bear clear witness. How glorious, and how far-reaching!
Our dynasty possesses all within the Four Seas. Its founding ancestors and successive sage sovereigns unified the sagely truth [?]. Their profound benevolence spread abundantly, and their civilizing influence reached everywhere. This nearby province was especially early to receive that influence. As for our present Emperor, his Way accords with what precedes Heaven, and his virtue equals that of the earth spirits [?]. Since assuming rule over the realm, he has established the supreme standard and bestowed blessings, summoned outstanding talent [?], and honored literary learning. His instructions expounding the imperial standard are displayed throughout the schools, their radiance shining amid the clouds…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
漢即遐方萬里之外罔不風
動影從雲蒸豹變㲊兹髦士
密邇
神化涵濡漸摩獨深且久者乎固
宜濟濟彬彬若是乎盛也〔直〕
竊自幸兹得縱觀多士之文
見其據經協度茂實振華闡
===
明道術則悟旨於義畫勲陳
化理則取裁於箕範渾乎大
河之涵泓而巍乎嵩行之具
瞻允矣其爲豫之良矣世際
休明川嶽效祉理不可誣而久
道化成人文宣朗信非坤靈
所獨擅者爾若是而曰多士
punctuated: 漢，即遐方萬里之外，罔不風動影從，雲蒸豹變，㲊兹髦士密邇神化，涵濡漸摩獨深且久者乎？固宜濟濟彬彬，若是乎盛也。〔直〕竊自幸兹得縱觀多士之文，見其據經協度，茂實振華，闡明道術，則悟旨於義畫；勲陳化理，則取裁於箕範。渾乎大河之涵泓，而巍乎嵩行之具瞻，允矣其爲豫之良矣！世際休明，川嶽效祉，理不可誣；而久道化成，人文宣朗，信非坤靈所獨擅者爾。若是而曰多士
translation_en:
…the Milky Way. Even in distant regions ten thousand li away, none fail to stir as before the wind and follow like shadows, rising like clouds and undergoing the transformation of the leopard’s patterned coat. How much more, then [?], these eminent scholars, so close to the sovereign’s wondrous transforming influence, who have been steeped in it and gradually cultivated with exceptional depth and duration! It is surely fitting that they should be so numerous, so accomplished, and so flourishing.
I, 〔Zhi〕, count myself fortunate now to have been able to survey the writings of these many scholars. I see that they ground themselves in the Classics and conform to proper standards, richly endowed with substance and displaying literary brilliance. In elucidating the Way and its methods, they grasp its purport through the diagrams of Fu Xi [?]; in setting forth the principles of transformative governance [?], they take their standard from the Great Plan of Jizi. Their writings are profound and capacious like the Yellow River’s deep waters, and lofty like Mount Song and the Taihang Mountains, toward which all look up. Truly, these are the outstanding men of Yu!
In an age of auspicious and enlightened rule, rivers and mountains bestow blessings: this principle cannot be denied. Yet the enduring practice of the Way brings transformation to fruition, and human culture shines forth in clarity; surely these are not achievements attributable solely to the spiritual powers of the earth. Such being the case, to say that among these many scholars…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
之中果無伊傅申甫諸賢其
人焉豈理也哉爾多士進矣
不可必者遇也不可負者時
也士生斯時孰無
帝臣之願而皓首窮經不沾一命
者何限也多士拔茅彙征登
名玆選既遇而獲時矣盍思
所以報稱者哉以用世則思
爲四輔以明道則思爲二賢
功業未必同而同其志道德
未必同而同其學則本諸身
而達諸政矣其心以圖報於
國者當無愧於爾鄉之先闈人
雖山川且藉以增重賓興大
punctuated: 之中果無伊傅申甫諸賢其人焉，豈理也哉？爾多士進矣！不可必者，遇也；不可負者，時也。士生斯時，孰無帝臣之願？而皓首窮經，不沾一命者何限也！多士拔茅彙征，登名玆選，既遇而獲時矣，盍思所以報稱者哉？以用世，則思爲四輔；以明道，則思爲二賢。功業未必同，而同其志；道德未必同，而同其學，則本諸身而達諸政矣。其心以圖報於國者，當無愧於爾鄉之先闈人，雖山川且藉以增重。賓興大
translation_en: …among these many scholars there should truly be none like the worthies Yi Yin, Fu Yue, Shen Bo, and Zhong Shanfu—how could that be reasonable? You scholars have now advanced! What cannot be assured is opportunity; what must not be failed is the age in which one lives. What scholar born in this age does not aspire to serve as the Emperor’s minister? Yet how countless are those who grow white-haired exhausting the Classics without receiving even a single appointment! You scholars have advanced together, like clumps of thatch uprooted with their intertwined roots, and have had your names entered among those selected. You have encountered opportunity and found your time. Should you not consider how to render a fitting return? In serving the world, aspire to be like the four counsellors; in illuminating the Way, aspire to be like the two worthies. Your achievements need not be identical to theirs, but share their aspirations; your moral attainment need not be identical, but follow their learning. Then what is rooted in your own persons will extend into government. In your resolve to repay the state, you should have nothing to be ashamed of before the earlier distinguished men of your native region [?]. Even its mountains and rivers will thereby gain added dignity. The great ceremony of honoring and recommending worthy scholars…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
典不亦休有烈光耶是舉也
巡按御史李〔初元〕殫精瘁力
務獲眞材以對揚
明命而〔直〕謬叨斯役敢攄御史之
意用申茲告多士其懋敬之
哉
應天府句容縣儒學教諭胡
〔直〕謹序
punctuated:
典，不亦休有烈光耶？是舉也，巡按御史李〔初元〕殫精瘁力，務獲眞材，以對揚明命。而〔直〕謬叨斯役，敢攄御史之意，用申茲告，多士其懋敬之哉！
應天府句容縣儒學教諭胡〔直〕謹序。
translation_en:
…ceremony—would it not also be splendid and brilliantly glorious? For this examination, Regional Inspector Li Chuyuan 李初元 exhausted his energies and strength, striving to obtain men of true talent and thereby fulfill and proclaim the illustrious imperial command. I, Zhi, undeservedly entrusted with this duty, venture to express the Censor’s intent and thus set forth this admonition. May you scholars diligently and reverently heed it!
Respectfully prefaced by Hu Zhi 胡直, Instructor of the Confucian School of Jurong County, Yingtian Prefecture.

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
河南鄉試錄序
嘉靖乙卯歲在寅興乃河南
當天下文明之中際
聖主萬年之運被服儒術之士以
鴻漸之翼戢于草野延頸而
瞻倂肩而奮盱衡而趨彬彬
蒸蒸何其盛也先是巡按監
===
察御史蔡〔汴〕展采錯事旣脩
旣戒會
請告
上特命御史李〔初元〕來代之〔初元〕
旣受
命唯謹趨程而進至則厲士風揚
德意靡夙靡夜風采振肅經畫精
punctuated:
河南鄉試錄序

嘉靖乙卯歲，在寅興，乃河南當天下文明之中，際聖主萬年之運，被服儒術之士，以鴻漸之翼戢于草野，延頸而瞻，倂肩而奮，盱衡而趨，彬彬蒸蒸，何其盛也！

先是，巡按監察御史蔡〔汴〕展采錯事，旣脩旣戒，會請告，上特命御史李〔初元〕來代之。〔初元〕旣受命，唯謹趨程而進，至則厲士風，揚德意，靡夙靡夜，風采振肅，經畫精
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Henan Provincial Examination

In the yimao year of the Jiajing reign (1555), as activity commenced in reverence [?], Henan stood at the center of the realm’s cultural brilliance and enjoyed the sage sovereign’s reign of ten thousand years. Scholars steeped in Confucian learning, their wings poised for gradual ascent like wild geese but still folded away in the countryside, stretched their necks to gaze expectantly, strove shoulder to shoulder, and pressed forward with lifted brows. So cultivated and so flourishing—what a splendid gathering!

Previously, the Regional Inspector, Investigating Censor Cai Bian 蔡汴, had carried out his duties and arranged affairs, completing preparations and issuing instructions. He then happened to request leave, and His Majesty specially commanded Censor Li Chuyuan 李初元 to come and replace him. Having received the command, Chuyuan proceeded on his journey with the utmost diligence. Upon arriving, he encouraged scholarly standards and proclaimed the sovereign’s benevolent intentions, working early and late. His bearing inspired respect and discipline, and his planning was meticulous…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
執事以從而諸校官胥以聘
至乃以學正袁〔隨〕教諭何〔子〕
顯蕭〔謙〕朱〔褒〕程〔汝昌〕劉〔澤〕吳
朝周吳〔守蒙〕分經而校而屬
齊欽與教諭胡〔直〕使總其事
曰學以徵業也文以徵志也
眞才是庸罔敢弗虔以左布
===
政使鄭〔紳〕右叅政裴〔紳〕司提
調按察使張〔渙〕副使雷〔賀〕司
監試分職而按而屬右布政
使岑〔萬〕左叅政周〔大禮〕左叅
議曹〔忭〕孟〔養性〕副使焦〔璉〕僉
永通寇〔陽〕僉事李〔燧〕許〔彥忠〕
楊〔延相〕朱〔舜民〕與署都指揮
punctuated:
執事以從，而諸校官胥以聘至。乃以學正袁〔隨〕、教諭何〔子〕顯、蕭〔謙〕、朱〔褒〕、程〔汝昌〕、劉〔澤〕、吳朝周、吳〔守蒙〕分經而校，而屬齊欽與教諭胡〔直〕使總其事，曰：「學以徵業也，文以徵志也。眞才是庸，罔敢弗虔。」
以左布政使鄭〔紳〕、右叅政裴〔紳〕司提調，按察使張〔渙〕、副使雷〔賀〕司監試，分職而按，而屬右布政使岑〔萬〕、左叅政周〔大禮〕、左叅議曹〔忭〕、孟〔養性〕、副使焦〔璉〕、僉永通寇〔陽〕、僉事李〔燧〕、許〔彥忠〕、楊〔延相〕、朱〔舜民〕與署都指揮
translation_en:
…the functionaries accompanied them, and the school officials all arrived upon invitation. Yuan Sui, a Prefectural School Instructor, and the County School Instructors He Zixian, Xiao Qian, Zhu Bao, Cheng Ruchang, Liu Ze, Wu Chaozhou, and Wu Shoumeng were then assigned to examine the papers by Classic. Qi Qin and County School Instructor Hu Zhi were charged with overall responsibility. They were instructed: “Learning provides evidence of scholarly attainment; writing provides evidence of aspiration. Employ only genuine talent, and let none dare be less than reverent in this duty.”
Zheng Shen, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner, and Pei Shen, Right Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner, were placed in charge of proctoring; Zhang Huan, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner, and Lei He, Surveillance Vice Commissioner, were placed in charge of examination supervision. Their duties were divided for inspection. Responsibility was also assigned to Cen Wan, Right Provincial Administration Commissioner; Zhou Dali, Left Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner; Cao Bian and Meng Yangxing, Left Provincial Administration Assistant Commissioners; Jiao Lian, Surveillance Vice Commissioner; Yong Tong and Kou Yang, whose titles or names are garbled here [?]; Li Sui, Xu Yanzhong, Yang Yanxiang, and Zhu Shunmin, Surveillance Assistant Commissioners; together with the acting Regional Military…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
僉事陳〔惟喬宣〕程〔繼隆〕呂各
嚴其防範曰簾以內毋出也
簾以外毋入也祇奉
憲章罔敢不愼比鎖院乃又申誓
之合提學副使徐〔霈〕所取士
約二千有奇三試而拔尤異
者得士八十人并刻其文以
===
獻〔賚敎〕謹稽首序曰〔賚敎〕聞之
昔者周之盛代也明良康乂
泰和流於宇宙然始未甞不
以賓賢斂才爲先務故其時
歌之曰藹藹王多吉士惟君
子使媚于天子又曰藹藹王
多吉人惟君子使媚于庶人
punctuated:
僉事陳〔惟喬宣〕、程〔繼隆〕、呂，各嚴其防範，曰：「簾以內毋出也，簾以外毋入也。」祇奉憲章，罔敢不愼。比鎖院，乃又申誓之。合提學副使徐〔霈〕所取士，約二千有奇，三試而拔尤異者，得士八十人，并刻其文以獻。
〔賚敎〕謹稽首序曰：〔賚敎〕聞之，昔者周之盛代也，明良康乂，泰和流於宇宙，然始未甞不以賓賢斂才爲先務。故其時歌之曰：「藹藹王多吉士，惟君子使，媚于天子。」又曰：「藹藹王多吉人，惟君子使，媚于庶人。」
translation_en:
…Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Chen〔Weiqiao Xuan [?]〕, Cheng〔Jilong〕, and Lü [name incomplete?] each tightened their precautions, declaring: “Those inside the curtain must not go out; those outside the curtain must not enter.” They reverently upheld the regulations, none daring to be negligent. When the examination compound was locked, they solemnly reiterated these injunctions. The candidates selected by Education Intendant Xu Pei numbered altogether somewhat over two thousand. Through three examination sessions, the most outstanding were selected, yielding eighty successful candidates; their essays were also printed for presentation.
Lai Jiao respectfully bows his head to the ground and writes this preface: I, Lai Jiao, have heard that in the flourishing age of the Zhou, an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers brought peace and good government, and supreme harmony pervaded the universe. Yet from the outset they invariably made honoring the worthy as guests and gathering talent their foremost task. Thus the songs of that age said: “In abundant throngs, the king has many excellent officers; it is gentlemen whom he employs, pleasing to the Son of Heaven.” They also said: “In abundant throngs, the king has many excellent men; it is gentlemen whom he employs, pleasing to the common people.”

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
周之稱爲上爲德爲下爲民
樹勳名而耀龍光者宜蔑以
逾於此矣光嶽氣完賢哲竝
毓聖作物覩實維其期是以
修思皇之譽崇蒸髦之美故
其歌曰周王壽考遐不作人
龍興而雲虎嘯而風豈其機
===
則然乎我
國家之興也變夷而華撥亂而
治功超萬古比於開闢之一
初視周則過之我
聖祖創垂鴻烈
列祖綏和茂勳至于我
皇上以
punctuated:
周之稱爲上爲德、爲下爲民，樹勳名而耀龍光者，宜蔑以逾於此矣。光嶽氣完，賢哲竝毓，聖作物覩，實維其期。是以修思皇之譽，崇蒸髦之美。故其歌曰：「周王壽考，遐不作人。」龍興而雲，虎嘯而風，豈其機則然乎？
我國家之興也，變夷而華，撥亂而治，功超萬古，比於開闢之一初，視周則過之。我聖祖創垂鴻烈，列祖綏和茂勳，至于我皇上以
translation_en:
As for Zhou’s reputation for serving virtue above and the people below, establishing illustrious achievements and displaying imperial favor, surely nothing could surpass this. The vital energies of heaven’s light and earth’s great mountains were whole; worthy and wise men were nurtured together. A sage arose, and all beheld him: this was indeed the appointed time. Thus they cultivated the reputation for “a splendid multitude of officers” and enhanced the glory of abundant outstanding talent. Hence their song said: “May the king of Zhou enjoy long life! How could he fail to nurture men of worth?” When the dragon rises, clouds gather; when the tiger roars, winds arise. Could it be that the underlying impulse naturally works thus?
When our dynasty arose, it transformed barbarian ways into Chinese civilization and brought order out of chaos. Its achievements surpassed those of all antiquity, matching the very beginning when heaven and earth were first opened; compared with Zhou, it surpassed it. Our sagely founding ancestor established great achievements and handed them down; the successive ancestors achieved magnificent feats in securing peace and harmony. Now, under our Emperor, through…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
大聖人之德體仁履義經文緯武
涵漸而化成之功實並於
天地泰和之氣燁燁乎眞與盛周
比隆矣夫山以嶽爲尊嵩宅
中而鎭水以瀆爲長河繞地
而抱降神儲精環四履而疆
也於玆土獨先焉爾多士之
===
生也豈其徒哉矧我
皇上右文弘化彝倫式敘
至道汾穆
湛恩洪鬯
德至于
天而慶雲見甘露降
德至于地而靈芝生嘉禾秀乃玆
punctuated: 大聖人之德，體仁履義，經文緯武，涵漸而化成之功，實並於天地。泰和之氣，燁燁乎眞與盛周比隆矣！夫山以嶽爲尊，嵩宅中而鎭；水以瀆爲長，河繞地而抱。降神儲精，環四履而疆也，於玆土獨先焉。爾多士之生也，豈其徒哉？矧我皇上右文弘化，彝倫式敘，至道汾穆，湛恩洪鬯。德至于天，而慶雲見、甘露降；德至于地，而靈芝生、嘉禾秀。乃玆
translation_en: …with the virtue of a great sage, embodies benevolence and practices righteousness, weaving together civil and military accomplishments. His achievement in gradually nurturing and transforming the people truly equals that of Heaven and Earth. The radiance of this supreme harmony indeed rivals the flourishing Zhou! Among mountains, the sacred peaks are most honored: Mount Song occupies the center and stands guard. Among waters, the great rivers take precedence: the Yellow River encircles and embraces the land. In sending down divine influences and gathering vital essence throughout the bounded realm, this land holds a place of particular precedence. Could the birth of you many scholars here be without purpose? Moreover, our Emperor honors letters and extends his transforming influence, bringing the enduring human relationships into proper order. The supreme Way is harmonious [?], and his profound bounty flows abundantly and freely. His virtue reaches Heaven, and auspicious clouds appear and sweet dew descends; his virtue reaches Earth, and numinous fungi grow and auspicious grain flourishes. Now here…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
而事弗秉遵條而節弗立恐
諛而職弗脩技害而心弗廓
有一於此其流將何所不至
哉士之蠹也斯所謂實弗中
聲虛名而寡效者
國家亦何賴於此乎〔賁 敎〕又緣
是而夙夜以憂也將亦不免
===
是懼亦曰惟爾多士於乎爾
多士敬之哉語不云乎唐虞
之際於斯爲盛士蓋無負於
周矣孰謂爾多士也顧不比
於鳶飛魚躍獨有負於
大聖人之世者耶研慮攄力勉卒
景行〔賁 敎〕第觀之是役也右
punctuated:
而事弗秉，遵條而節弗立，恐諛而職弗脩，技害而心弗廓。有一於此，其流將何所不至哉？士之蠹也，斯所謂實弗中聲、虛名而寡效者。國家亦何賴於此乎？〔賁 敎〕又緣是而夙夜以憂也，將亦不免是懼。亦曰：惟爾多士，於乎！爾多士敬之哉！語不云乎：「唐虞之際，於斯爲盛。」士蓋無負於周矣。孰謂爾多士也，顧不比於鳶飛魚躍，獨有負於大聖人之世者耶？研慮攄力，勉卒景行。〔賁 敎〕第觀之是役也。

右
translation_en:
…yet affairs are not managed; regulations are followed, yet integrity is not established; fear and flattery leave duties unfulfilled [?]; jealousy and malice leave the mind narrow [?]. If even one of these faults is present, to what lengths might its consequences not extend? These are the corruptions of scholars: what is called substance failing to match reputation, an empty name with little accomplishment. What use can such men be to the state? [Ben Jiao 賁敎 [?]] On this account, too, I worry day and night, unable to escape this apprehension. I can only say: you many scholars—ah! You many scholars, take heed! Does not the Analects say, “In the age of Tang and Yu, and in this age, talent flourished most”? The scholars surely did not fail the Zhou. Who could say that you many scholars, unlike the kites soaring and the fish leaping, would alone fail the age of the great sage? Think deeply, exert your strength, and strive to carry your noble conduct through to the end. [Ben Jiao 賁敎 [?]] I shall simply observe your performance in this examination.

The Right …

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
叅議李〔豸〕僉事王〔之誥〕以入
賀行右叅政董〔德明〕僉事陳〔夢
鶴〕以兵賦出始事鈞勞所不
可泯保定侯梁〔繼璠〕安鄉伯
張〔鐸〕兵科給事中曹〔禾〕户部
主事沈〔應乾〕劉〔效祖〕中書舍
人謝〔朝錫〕行人司行人祝〔堯〕
〔煥〕金〔應奎〕蕭〔九成〕以奉使至
雅意崇尚又咸喜中土人文
之盛而樂觀厥成云
陝西西安府同州儒學學正
史〔貢教〕謹序
punctuated:
叅議李〔豸〕、僉事王〔之誥〕以入賀行，右叅政董〔德明〕、僉事陳〔夢鶴〕以兵賦出，始事鈞勞，所不可泯。保定侯梁〔繼璠〕、安鄉伯張〔鐸〕、兵科給事中曹〔禾〕、户部主事沈〔應乾〕、劉〔效祖〕、中書舍人謝〔朝錫〕、行人司行人祝〔堯〕〔煥〕、金〔應奎〕、蕭〔九成〕以奉使至，雅意崇尚，又咸喜中土人文之盛，而樂觀厥成云。
陝西西安府同州儒學學正史〔貢教〕謹序。
translation_en:
… Assistant Administration Commissioner Li Zhi and Surveillance Assistant Commissioner Wang Zhigao departed to offer congratulations at court; Administration Vice Commissioner of the Right Dong Deming and Surveillance Assistant Commissioner Chen Menghe went away on military and fiscal duties. All shared equally in the labors of initiating this undertaking, and their contributions must not go unrecorded. Liang Jifan, Marquis of Baoding; Zhang Duo, Earl of Anxiang; Cao He, Supervising Secretary in the Office of Scrutiny for War; Shen Yingqian and Liu Xiaozu, Secretaries in the Ministry of Revenue; Xie Chaoxi, Central Drafting Office Secretary; and Zhu Yaohuan, Jin Yingkui, and Xiao Jiucheng, Messengers in the Messenger Office, arrived on official missions. They held this undertaking in high esteem, and all rejoiced in the flourishing literary culture of the Central Lands and were pleased to witness its successful completion.
Preface respectfully written by Shi Gongjiao, School Director of the Confucian School of Tongzhou, Xi’an Prefecture, Shaanxi.

嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
翊學詩心學淵源與
聖祖先後一轍猗與盛哉傳播海內諸士子誦
而習之蓋有年矣請明著於篇以觀對
揚之懿
問治曆明時作樂崇德大有關于治道在
儒者所必講也以帝舜之聖而首察璣
衡以后夔之賢而專職音樂則其事亦
有未易言者漢而下論曆律者代有其
人據其說果足以被之琴瑟管絃而克
===
舉乎保章馮相之職與唐一行論氣朔
推步者凡七議曆數者十有二其詳可
得聞與元郭守敬曆法或者謂太衍莫
過焉果何所取衷與宋蔡元定律呂證
辨者凡十論本原者十有三其說可悉
數與黃鍾分寸或者執含少之說以疑
之抑自有見與夫曆莫重于曆元而其
要在候氣律莫首于黃鍾而其要在定
管制作之方諸家必有可憑者即欲開
punctuated:
《翊學詩》，心學淵源，與聖祖先後一轍，猗與盛哉！傳播海內，諸士子誦而習之，蓋有年矣。請明著於篇，以觀對揚之懿。

問：治曆明時，作樂崇德，大有關于治道，在儒者所必講也。以帝舜之聖而首察璣衡，以后夔之賢而專職音樂，則其事亦有未易言者。漢而下，論曆律者代有其人，據其說，果足以被之琴瑟管絃，而克舉乎保章、馮相之職與？唐一行論氣朔推步者凡七，議曆數者十有二，其詳可得聞與？元郭守敬曆法，或者謂太衍莫過焉，果何所取衷與？宋蔡元定律呂，證辨者凡十，論本原者十有三，其說可悉數與？黃鍾分寸，或者執含少之說以疑之，抑自有見與？夫曆莫重于曆元，而其要在候氣；律莫首于黃鍾，而其要在定管。制作之方，諸家必有可憑者，即欲開
translation_en:
…the “Poem in Support of Learning” (Yixue shi) [?]. The sources of its learning of the mind follow precisely the same course as those of the Sagely Progenitor, earlier and later alike. Ah, how splendid! It has circulated throughout the realm, and scholars have recited and studied it for years. Please set this forth clearly in your essay, so that we may see the excellence of your response in extolling the imperial teaching.

Question: Regulating the calendar to clarify the seasons and creating music to exalt virtue bear greatly upon the way of governance; scholars of the Confucian tradition must study them. Even with Emperor Shun’s sageliness, his first concern was to examine the astronomical instruments; even with Hou Kui’s worthiness, he was assigned specifically to music. These matters are therefore not easily discussed. From the Han onward, every age has had men who discussed calendrical computation and musical pitch. If their theories were followed, would they truly suffice for application to zithers, pipes, and strings, and enable the duties of the Baozhang, the Astrologer, and the Fengxiang, the Astronomical Observer, to be fulfilled?

Yixing of the Tang produced seven discussions of calculating solar terms and new moons, and twelve discussions of calendrical numbers. May we hear their details? Concerning Guo Shoujing’s calendrical methods under the Yuan, some say that the Taiyan [?] calendar could not surpass them. What, in fact, did he take as his standard? In his treatment of musical pitches, Cai Yuanding of the Song provided ten evidential analyses and thirteen discussions of fundamental principles. Can you enumerate his explanations in full? Regarding the dimensions of the Huangzhong, or Yellow Bell, pitch pipe in cun and fen, some invoke the theory of “containing the lesser” [?] to cast doubt upon them. Might they have insights of their own?

For calendrical calculation, nothing is more important than the calendrical epoch, and the key lies in observing the seasonal qi. For musical pitch, nothing takes precedence over Huangzhong, and the key lies in fixing the dimensions of the pitch pipe. Among the various authorities there must be dependable methods for their construction. If we now wished to establish…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
局求人以專斯業爾多士豈無義燹之
選乎願有以先告我也
問昔之君子所以垂世而不朽者曰道德
曰功業曰文章是三者非判然不相須
也惟兹中土雅號多賢若格天奕業降
嶽楨時詩啓二毛學傳一貫于斯三者
亦兼之矣自是以降代不乏人雖才器
不同而顯微可述有智爲帝師功成高
蹈者有外寛內明士民歸心者有攬轡
===
澄清願爲容接者有平心化盜私謚文
範者有舉親却敵閒捷不動者有望高
一時器異三蘇者有忠義報國矢志恢
復者有十事要說抹時自慶者有決獄
有聲急流勇退者有唱名奏瑞竟安社
稷者有大節難奪彥博竝稱者有杖策
一言遂定大計者有孤城抗賊保全江
淮者有德量難測人稱顏子者其于古
人之功業有相彷彿否與有陳至言而
punctuated:
局求人以專斯業，爾多士豈無義燹之選乎？願有以先告我也。

問：昔之君子所以垂世而不朽者，曰道德，曰功業，曰文章。是三者非判然不相須也。惟兹中土，雅號多賢，若格天奕業、降嶽楨時、詩啓二毛、學傳一貫，于斯三者亦兼之矣。自是以降，代不乏人，雖才器不同，而顯微可述。有智爲帝師、功成高蹈者，有外寛內明、士民歸心者，有攬轡澄清、願爲容接者，有平心化盜、私謚文範者，有舉親却敵、閒捷不動者，有望高一時、器異三蘇者，有忠義報國、矢志恢復者，有十事要說、抹時自慶者，有決獄有聲、急流勇退者，有唱名奏瑞、竟安社稷者，有大節難奪、彥博竝稱者，有杖策一言、遂定大計者，有孤城抗賊、保全江淮者，有德量難測、人稱顏子者。其于古人之功業，有相彷彿否與？有陳至言而
translation_en:
…establish a bureau and seek men to devote themselves to this work. Among you many scholars, are there no suitable candidates of outstanding expertise [?]? I hope you will first give me your views.

Question: What enabled gentlemen of antiquity to leave an enduring legacy was morality, achievement, and literary composition. These three are not sharply separated and independent of one another. This central region has long been renowned for its many worthy men: those whose magnificent achievements moved Heaven; those born through the numinous influence of the mountains to serve as pillars of their age; those who opened the way for the two Mao masters in the study of the Book of Odes; and those who transmitted learning through a single unifying principle. They combined these three attainments.

From that time onward, no age has lacked such men. Although their talents and capacities differed, their deeds, both conspicuous and obscure, can be recounted. There were those whose wisdom made them teachers of emperors and who withdrew to lofty seclusion once their work was accomplished; those who were outwardly generous and inwardly discerning, winning the allegiance of scholars and common people; those who took up the reins determined to cleanse the realm and wished to be granted an audience; those who transformed robbers through their impartiality and received the private posthumous title Wenfan, “Model of Cultivation”; those who recommended their kinsmen and repelled enemies, remaining composed and unperturbed [?]; those whose reputation towered over their age and whose exceptional capacity was recognized by the three Su; those who served the state with loyalty and righteousness and vowed to accomplish its restoration; those who presented essential proposals in ten points and congratulated themselves on their encounter with the times [?]; those renowned for deciding legal cases who courageously retired amid the swift current of official life; those whose names were proclaimed and auspicious signs reported, and who ultimately secured the altars of soil and grain; those whose integrity could not be shaken and who were ranked alongside Yanbo; those who came staff in hand and settled a great plan with a single utterance; those who resisted rebels in an isolated city and preserved the Jiang–Huai region; and those whose virtue and magnanimity were unfathomable and whom people called Master Yan. Did their achievements resemble those of the ancients?

There were those who presented words of the utmost truth and…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
動主者有受易學而東歸者有進策治
安號通國體者有較正六經立碑大學
者有作申鑒以匡時政者有脩直史人
稱董狐者有寖處百日指玄著論者有
佐佑六經斗山著望者有高潔工詩冲
澹可法者有賦二京兼精曆筭者有不
愧科名兄弟並美者有博覽洽聞類物
辨俗者其于古人之文章有相彷彿否
與其所謂功業文章果皆不詭于道與
===
道學初明眞儒挺出若其參造化關盛
衰今古賴之似又不可以一鄉論也諸
士子高山景行將誰與歸願詳述之以
觀尚友之學
問兵者所以明德除害也故舉得於外福
生於內三代而下談說經武要略無慮
數十百家今所存七書而已乃其攻討
克備貴謀多筭行之有順逆用之有巧
拙昭然可覩識矣遡觀古昔若減竈增
punctuated:
動主者，有受易學而東歸者，有進策治安、號通國體者，有較正六經、立碑大學者，有作《申鑒》以匡時政者，有脩直史、人稱董狐者，有寖處百日、指玄著論者，有佐佑六經、斗山著望者，有高潔工詩、冲澹可法者，有賦二京、兼精曆筭者，有不愧科名、兄弟並美者，有博覽洽聞、類物辨俗者。其于古人之文章有相彷彿否與？其所謂功業文章，果皆不詭于道與？道學初明，眞儒挺出，若其參造化、關盛衰，今古賴之，似又不可以一鄉論也。諸士子高山景行，將誰與歸？願詳述之，以觀尚友之學。
問：兵者，所以明德除害也。故舉得於外，福生於內。三代而下，談說經武要略，無慮數十百家，今所存七書而已。乃其攻討克備，貴謀多筭，行之有順逆，用之有巧拙，昭然可覩識矣。遡觀古昔，若減竈增
translation_en:
…moved their ruler; some received instruction in the learning of the Changes and returned east; some submitted proposals for good government and peace and were acclaimed as understanding the essentials of statecraft; some collated and corrected the Six Classics and erected stone inscriptions at the Imperial University; some composed the Mirror of Admonition (Shen jian) to rectify the government of their time; some compiled forthright histories and were called Dong Hu; some dwelt in seclusion for a hundred days [?], expounding mysteries and composing treatises; some upheld the Six Classics and gained the prestige of the Northern Dipper and Mount Tai; some were lofty and pure in character and skilled in poetry, their unaffected serenity worthy of emulation; some composed rhapsodies on the two capitals and also excelled in calendrical calculation; some lived up to their examination distinction, brothers alike renowned for excellence; and some were widely read and extensively informed, classifying things and distinguishing customs. Did their literary achievements resemble those of the ancients? And did all their so-called accomplishments in public service and letters truly accord with the Way? When the Learning of the Way first became clear, true Confucians emerged outstandingly. Insofar as they participated in the transforming and nurturing work of Heaven and Earth and influenced flourishing and decline, people past and present have depended upon them: it seems that they cannot be judged merely within the bounds of one region. You examination candidates look up to lofty mountains and follow the great road: whom will you choose to follow? Please explain in detail, so that we may see your learning in taking the worthy of antiquity as friends.
Question: Military force is the means by which virtue is made manifest and harm removed. Thus, when action abroad is properly undertaken, blessings arise at home. Since the Three Dynasties, writers discussing the essentials of military administration have numbered in the dozens and hundreds; today, only the Seven Military Classics survive. Their teachings on attack, punitive expeditions, victory, and preparedness [?], and their emphasis on planning and ample calculation, make it plainly possible to discern how their implementation may accord with or run counter to circumstances, and how their application may be skillful or clumsy. Looking back to antiquity, consider such cases as reducing cooking fires and increasing…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
竈之殊其形囊沙量沙之異其用百里
趨利則馬陵之斃軍志所戒也或曰兵
貴神速何與包原隰而陣則秭歸之役
宜爲人所乗也乃又褁氊深入何與魚
腹列陣誠三代才也而或謂運用之妙
存乎一心嚴飭部伍眞漢名將也而有
不擊刁斗者將才無出其右其故可得
聞與夜半奪關不踰易字多多益辨以
簡得之其義何所指與至於聚米指畫
===
虜在目中矣何以曰兵難遥度養虎遺
患敵固不可縱矣何以曰窮寇勿追背
水之陣與氷堅可渡者其指安在淮淝
之捷與赤壁之戰者其計安得夫掎角
之勢覆人之逹計也奇正之變馭敵之
祕機也呼吸存亡於茲攸繫昔人所稱
微乎微矣孔子曰我戰則克其必有所
以矣諸士握機抱筭而來豈以是爲危
事而諱言之耶
punctuated: 竈之殊其形，囊沙、量沙之異其用。百里趨利，則馬陵之斃，軍志所戒也；或曰：「兵貴神速。」何與？包原隰而陣，則秭歸之役宜爲人所乗也；乃又褁氊深入，何與？魚腹列陣，誠三代才也，而或謂：「運用之妙，存乎一心。」嚴飭部伍，眞漢名將也，而有不擊刁斗者，將才無出其右，其故可得聞與？夜半奪關，不踰易字；多多益辨，以簡得之：其義何所指與？至於聚米指畫，虜在目中矣，何以曰：「兵難遥度」？養虎遺患，敵固不可縱矣，何以曰：「窮寇勿追」？背水之陣與氷堅可渡者，其指安在？淮淝之捷與赤壁之戰者，其計安得？夫掎角之勢，覆人之逹計也；奇正之變，馭敵之祕機也。呼吸存亡，於茲攸繫。昔人所稱：「微乎微矣！」孔子曰：「我戰則克。」其必有所以矣。諸士握機抱筭而來，豈以是爲危事而諱言之耶？
translation_en: …stoves differed in their outward form, while filling sacks with sand and measuring out sand differed in their application. Rushing a hundred li to gain an advantage led to destruction at Maling—precisely what military writings warn against. Yet some say, “In warfare, divine speed is prized.” How is this to be reconciled? When an army encamped across both high ground and low, as in the campaign at Zigui, it deserved to be exploited by the enemy. Yet there was also the feat of wrapping oneself in felt and penetrating deep into enemy territory. How is this to be explained? To deploy formations at Yufu indeed showed talent worthy of the Three Dynasties; yet some say, “Subtlety in their application rests entirely in the mind.” Strictly ordering the ranks marked a true celebrated general of the Han; yet there was one who did not strike the watch cauldrons, and whose talent as a commander none surpassed. May we hear the reason? Seizing a pass at midnight required no more than changing a written character [?]; the capacity to handle ever greater numbers of troops was attained through simplicity. What principles do these examples illustrate? As for piling up rice to indicate terrain and explain a plan, the enemy was as though before one’s eyes. Why, then, is it said, “Military affairs are difficult to assess from afar”? Raising a tiger leaves trouble for the future: an enemy certainly must not be allowed to escape. Why, then, is it said, “Do not pursue a desperate enemy”? What was the underlying intent in the formation with its back to the water and in the case where ice was firm enough to cross? How were the plans for the victory at Huai–Fei and the battle of Chibi devised? A disposition like that of seizing an animal’s hind leg and its horn is an effective plan for overthrowing an opponent; transformations between unconventional and conventional forces are the hidden key to controlling the enemy. Survival or destruction within a single breath depends upon these things. As men of old exclaimed, “Subtle—how subtle!” Confucius said, “If I fought, I would prevail.” Surely he had grounds for saying so. You scholars have come with a grasp of strategic opportunities and plans in mind. Would you regard this as a perilous subject and therefore shrink from discussing it?

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
問古者制民之産田以井受民安其生然
井田之中溝涂川澮疆理限隔設險之
義存焉故其時人樂爲善至比屋可封
後世阡陌久廢貧富不均易與爲姦乃
今河南所在平曠盜賊四起小行剽劫
大且嘯聚豈無能爲生耶抑地險不足
人懷恣睢也說者謂古昔能止盜者莫
善於漢言治盜者莫詳於宋今觀渤海
弄兵安之而治冀州起刺到部屛息有
===
三科募士而稱明朝歌有單車之職而
更生魚釜至於賈父清平歌與交趾朱
君良計戒於納降又人人殊矣而當時
所稱有謂簡別流民弱黨殲渠不勞而
定者豈確論與宋之名臣或謂縻用兇
險以消始禍或謂籠取豪猾使自歆利
其意同與至於歐陽四事太虛二弊固
禦盜之律令也而所謂折氣攜心尤爲
至計可得悉言其義與夫比追胥施刑
punctuated: 問：古者制民之産，田以井受，民安其生。然井田之中，溝涂川澮，疆理限隔，設險之義存焉。故其時人樂爲善，至比屋可封。後世阡陌久廢，貧富不均，易與爲姦。乃今河南所在平曠，盜賊四起，小行剽劫，大且嘯聚，豈無能爲生耶？抑地險不足，人懷恣睢也？說者謂古昔能止盜者莫善於漢，言治盜者莫詳於宋。今觀渤海弄兵，安之而治；冀州起刺，到部屛息；有三科募士而稱明朝歌；有單車之職而更生魚釜。至於賈父清平歌與交趾朱君良計，戒於納降，又人人殊矣。而當時所稱，有謂簡別流民，弱黨殲渠，不勞而定者，豈確論與？宋之名臣，或謂縻用兇險以消始禍，或謂籠取豪猾使自歆利，其意同與？至於歐陽四事、太虛二弊，固禦盜之律令也。而所謂折氣攜心，尤爲至計，可得悉言其義與？夫比追胥、施刑
translation_en:
Question: In antiquity, the people’s livelihoods were regulated, and fields were allotted according to the well-field system, so that the people could live securely. Within the well-fields, however, ditches and roads, streams and drainage channels, boundaries and divisions also embodied the principle of creating defensive obstacles. Thus people in those days delighted in doing good, to the point that every household was worthy of receiving an enfeoffment. In later ages, the field boundaries long fell into disuse, wealth and poverty became unequal, and people were readily drawn into wrongdoing. Now Henan is flat and open throughout, and bandits arise on every side. In small groups they plunder and rob; in larger groups they gather in armed bands. Is this because they have no means of making a living? Or is it because the terrain offers insufficient obstacles, allowing people to indulge their lawlessness?

Commentators say that, among ancient dynasties, none surpassed the Han in stopping banditry, and none discussed its suppression more fully than the Song. Consider those who took up arms in Bohai: they were pacified and order was restored. In Jizhou, an official rose to become Regional Inspector [?], and upon his arrival in the region, the troublemakers fell silent. One recruited men in three categories and won praise for his discernment at Chaoge; another went to his post in a single carriage and restored to life those who were like fish in a cooking pot. As for the song praising Father Jia’s pure and peaceful rule, and Master Zhu’s excellent plans in Jiaozhi and his caution about accepting surrender, their methods likewise differed from person to person. Among the measures praised at the time were distinguishing among displaced people, weakening the followers, and annihilating the ringleaders, thereby restoring order without great exertion. Is this a sound judgment?

Among the celebrated ministers of the Song, some advocated keeping violent and dangerous men in service to extinguish trouble at its inception; others advocated drawing powerful and crafty men into their orbit so that they themselves would be eager for the benefits. Were their intentions the same? As for Ouyang’s four measures and Taixu’s two abuses, these surely constitute authoritative rules for resisting banditry. Yet what is called breaking their spirit and dividing their loyalties is an especially effective strategy. Can you explain its meaning in full? As for enforcing deadlines for pursuing and apprehending bandits, and administering punishments…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
慶建樓置鼓義營賞告之法有司之已
事也能不廢格足矣採本銷萌達權握
筭必有出於是者何以告我而擇行之
punctuated: 慶、建樓、置鼓、義營、賞告之法，有司之已事也，能不廢格足矣。採本銷萌，達權握筭，必有出於是者，何以告我而擇行之？
translation_en: …and rewards, building watchtowers, installing drums, organizing militia encampments [?], and rewarding informants: these are established practices of the responsible officials. It suffices to ensure that they are not neglected or obstructed. Yet probing the roots and eliminating trouble as it sprouts, understanding expedient measures and commanding effective strategies—surely there are approaches that go beyond these. What can you tell me so that I may select and implement them?
