title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
感審至正以端向往之趨而克念以從事者不
淆於似是之非夫固以天下之定理爲吾心之
定見而所入之途正矣夫道而曰志猶未得也
至於得之而爲德焉不有以守之可乎必也隨
吾踐履之所有益敦夫固執之功卽吾力行之
所至恒懋夫秉持之力蓋有始終如一而日新
又新者矣夫德而曰據猶與我二也至於熟之
而爲仁焉不有以存之可乎必也奉帝則以周
旋而全體之不息順天理以游衍而成性之恒
===
存蓋有常變一致而終食不違者矣夫然則大
本巳立而學亦至矣至若藝者又至理所寓而
日用所須也不有以游之亦非所以多識而畜
德矣是必朝與游焉旁通之以極義理之趣夕
與游焉博觀之以盡事物之情則應務有餘而
此心不放中之所養者益熟矣夫本與末而兼
該內與外而交養輕重不失先後有序謂非聖
脩之極乎雖然志也者聖學之所以成始而成
終者也是故始乎此志終乎此志一志立則道
punctuated: 感審至正，以端向往之趨，而克念以從事者，不淆於似是之非。夫固以天下之定理爲吾心之定見，而所入之途正矣。夫道而曰志，猶未得也。至於得之而爲德焉，不有以守之可乎？必也隨吾踐履之所有，益敦夫固執之功；卽吾力行之所至，恒懋夫秉持之力。蓋有始終如一，而日新又新者矣。夫德而曰據，猶與我二也。至於熟之而爲仁焉，不有以存之可乎？必也奉帝則以周旋，而全體之不息；順天理以游衍，而成性之恒存。蓋有常變一致，而終食不違者矣。夫然則大本巳立，而學亦至矣。至若藝者，又至理所寓，而日用所須也。不有以游之，亦非所以多識而畜德矣。是必朝與游焉，旁通之以極義理之趣；夕與游焉，博觀之以盡事物之情。則應務有餘，而此心不放，中之所養者益熟矣。夫本與末而兼該，內與外而交養，輕重不失，先後有序，謂非聖脩之極乎？雖然，志也者，聖學之所以成始而成終者也。是故始乎此志，終乎此志，一志立則道
translation_en:
…Those who apprehend and examine what is supremely correct [?], thereby setting right the direction of their aspirations, and who undertake their work with sustained mindfulness, are not confused by errors that resemble truth. They assuredly take the settled principles of all under Heaven as the settled convictions of their own minds, and thus the path they enter is correct. When, in speaking of the Way, one says that one sets one's resolve upon it, one has not yet attained it. Once one has attained it and it becomes virtue, can one dispense with the means to hold fast to it? Whatever one achieves in practice, one must further strengthen the effort to adhere firmly to it; wherever one's strenuous conduct reaches, one must continually exert oneself to maintain it. Thus one remains consistent from beginning to end while renewing oneself daily, again and again. When, in speaking of virtue, one says that one holds to it, it is still something distinct from oneself. Once it has become fully familiar and becomes humaneness, can one dispense with the means to preserve it? One must conduct oneself in accordance with the Supreme Lord's standards, embodying them wholly without cessation; one must move freely in accordance with Heaven's principles, so that one's perfected nature remains constantly present. Thus one is consistent amid both ordinary circumstances and change, never departing from humaneness even for the duration of a meal.

When this is so, the great foundation has been established, and learning has also reached its culmination. As for the arts, they too are where ultimate principle resides, and they are needed in daily life. Without the means to roam among them, one cannot broaden one's knowledge and nurture virtue. One must therefore roam among them in the morning, making connections in every direction to fathom the purport of moral principles; one must roam among them in the evening, surveying them broadly to comprehend fully the realities of things and affairs. Then one will have more than sufficient capacity to respond to affairs, while the mind will not stray, and what is nurtured within will become increasingly mature. Encompassing both root and branch, nurturing both the inward and the outward, preserving their proper relative importance and their orderly sequence—could this be called anything other than the utmost in sagely cultivation?

Nevertheless, resolve is what enables sagely learning to accomplish both its beginning and its completion. Thus one begins with this resolve and ends with this resolve. Once a single resolve is established, the Way…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
窮誠貫天下之道而廣大莫禦聖人之德固有
所謂溥博矣仰而觀之其如天矣乎蓋其冲漠
無联積元氣以上浮渾闢無窮普貞觀以下濟
言天下之廣大者至天焉極矣而聖人之德如
之則是大心體物無一理之不備者卽天之無
不覆幬也全體大極無一善之不該者卽天之
無不包含也天也聖也固有異象而同體者矣
聖同天不其大乎至若寂然不動靜以涵萬化
之原湛然無欲虛以妙萬物之感聖人之德固
===
有所謂淵泉矣俯而察之其如淵矣乎蓋其山
下出泉而源之所發者深地中有水而流之所
達者遠言天下之靜深者至淵焉極矣而聖人
之德如之則是洗心以藏密而探之莫究其極
者卽淵之渾淪而無涘也資深以逢原而取之
莫盡其量者卽淵之涵蓄而不竭也淵也聖也
固有異形而同理者矣聖同淵不其深乎夫聖
德所積至於極盛如此由是而發見有不當其
可哉大抵有盛德必有大業如天如淵言聖德
punctuated:
窮誠貫天下之道，而廣大莫禦，聖人之德固有所謂溥博矣。仰而觀之，其如天矣乎？蓋其冲漠無联，積元氣以上浮，渾闢無窮，普貞觀以下濟。言天下之廣大者，至天焉極矣，而聖人之德如之，則是大心體物，無一理之不備者，卽天之無不覆幬也；全體大極，無一善之不該者，卽天之無不包含也。天也，聖也，固有異象而同體者矣。聖同天，不其大乎？
至若寂然不動，靜以涵萬化之原；湛然無欲，虛以妙萬物之感，聖人之德固有所謂淵泉矣。俯而察之，其如淵矣乎？蓋其山下出泉，而源之所發者深；地中有水，而流之所達者遠。言天下之靜深者，至淵焉極矣，而聖人之德如之，則是洗心以藏密，而探之莫究其極者，卽淵之渾淪而無涘也；資深以逢原，而取之莫盡其量者，卽淵之涵蓄而不竭也。淵也，聖也，固有異形而同理者矣。聖同淵，不其深乎？
夫聖德所積，至於極盛如此，由是而發見，有不當其可哉？大抵有盛德，必有大業。如天如淵，言聖德
translation_en:
…Through sincerity carried to its utmost, he penetrates the Way throughout the world, and his vastness admits no bounds: the sage’s virtue assuredly possesses what is called all-embracing breadth. Looking upward to contemplate it, is it not like Heaven? Empty and still, without connection [?], it gathers primordial vital energy to float above; its undivided openness is inexhaustible [?], and its universal, constant manifestation extends beneficence below [?]. Among all things called vast in the world, Heaven is the utmost. The sage’s virtue resembles it: enlarging his mind to embody all things, he lacks no principle, just as Heaven leaves nothing uncovered; embodying the Supreme Ultimate in its entirety, he encompasses every good, just as Heaven leaves nothing unembraced. Heaven and the sage differ in appearance yet share the same substance. Since the sage is like Heaven, is he not great?
As for being silent and unmoving, in stillness embracing the source of all transformations; being limpid and free of desire, through emptiness responding wondrously to all things—the sage’s virtue assuredly possesses what is called the depth of a pool and its springs. Looking downward to examine it, is it not like a deep pool? Springs emerge beneath mountains, and the sources from which they issue lie deep; water lies within the earth, and its streams reach far. Among all things called still and deep in the world, a deep pool is the utmost. The sage’s virtue resembles it: cleansing his mind to store away the hidden mysteries, so that no inquiry can fathom its limits, he is like a pool, vast and undivided, without a shore; drawing deeply upon what he has acquired and encountering the source at every turn, so that no drawing upon it can exhaust its measure, he is like a pool whose accumulated waters never run dry. The pool and the sage differ in form yet share the same principle. Since the sage is like a deep pool, is he not profound?
Now, when the sage’s accumulated virtue reaches such supreme fullness, could its ensuing manifestations ever fail to be fitting? In general, abundant virtue necessarily brings forth great achievements. To say “like Heaven” and “like a deep pool” describes the sage’s virtue…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
莫先於盡性仁義智之實固在於孝弟矣而禮
樂豈外是乎今夫禮嘉天下之會而儀文度數
特其華耳以言其實亦惟於孝弟節文之而已
蓋愛敬之用情勝則易流也必損過就中不使
之蕩焉而無節親長之事恩勝則易略也必釋
同增美不使之簡焉而無文天叙之惇本乎天
秩以爲之則藹然相愛之中固有截然而不紊
者矣人紀之脩本乎人文以爲之貢井然有辨
之際固有燦然而可觀者矣斯則品節旣極其
===
詳而推行曲當其可天下之大中在我矣舉而
措之以嘉天下之會禮可勝用哉樂以平天下
之情而聲容節奏特其文耳以言其實在樂乎
孝弟而已夫惟樂也吾見悅諸心而融諸慮天
性之由衷者旣非勉強以從事則根於心而生
於色至情之活潑者自將隨感而卽形由是心
和則氣和而日新月盛有欲罷不能者以達其
機也由是氣和則形和而足蹈手舞有不言而
喻者以彰其化也斯則和順積於中而神應妙
punctuated: 莫先於盡性。仁義智之實，固在於孝弟矣，而禮樂豈外是乎？今夫禮，嘉天下之會，而儀文度數特其華耳。以言其實，亦惟於孝弟節文之而已。蓋愛敬之用，情勝則易流也，必損過就中，不使之蕩焉而無節；親長之事，恩勝則易略也，必釋同增美，不使之簡焉而無文。天叙之惇，本乎天秩以爲之則，藹然相愛之中，固有截然而不紊者矣；人紀之脩，本乎人文以爲之貢，井然有辨之際，固有燦然而可觀者矣。斯則品節旣極其詳，而推行曲當其可，天下之大中在我矣。舉而措之，以嘉天下之會，禮可勝用哉？樂以平天下之情，而聲容節奏特其文耳。以言其實，在樂乎孝弟而已。夫惟樂也，吾見悅諸心而融諸慮。天性之由衷者，旣非勉強以從事，則根於心而生於色，至情之活潑者，自將隨感而卽形。由是心和則氣和，而日新月盛，有欲罷不能者，以達其機也；由是氣和則形和，而足蹈手舞，有不言而喻者，以彰其化也。斯則和順積於中，而神應妙
translation_en:
…nothing takes precedence over fully realizing one’s nature. The substance of benevolence, righteousness, and wisdom surely lies in filial devotion and respect for elder brothers; how could ritual and music lie outside these? Now ritual lends beauty to the gatherings of all under Heaven, while ceremonial forms and prescribed measures are merely its outward flowering. As for its substance, it consists simply in giving filial devotion and brotherly respect due measure and patterned expression. In expressing love and reverence, when feeling predominates, it easily runs to excess: one must reduce excess and attain the mean, preventing unrestrained indulgence. In serving parents and elders, when affection predominates, observances easily become cursory: one must dispel undifferentiated familiarity and add refinement [?], preventing simplicity from becoming a lack of patterned expression. Strengthening Heaven’s appointed relationships takes Heaven’s ordained ranks as its rule; thus, amid warm mutual affection, there are clear distinctions without disorder. Cultivating the bonds of human society takes human cultural forms as its contribution [?]; thus, amid orderly distinctions, there is a brilliance worthy of contemplation. When these gradations and regulations have been worked out in the fullest detail, and their application fits every particular circumstance, the great mean of all under Heaven resides in oneself. Put this into practice to lend beauty to the gatherings of all under Heaven: could the uses of ritual ever be exhausted?

Music brings equilibrium to the feelings of all under Heaven, while sounds, movements, and rhythms are merely its patterned expression. As for its substance, it lies simply in taking joy in filial devotion and brotherly respect. It is precisely this joy that, as I see it, delights the heart and brings harmony to one’s thoughts. Since what issues sincerely from one’s inborn nature is not something undertaken through forced effort, it takes root in the heart and appears in one’s countenance; the vitality of the truest feelings will naturally become manifest whenever something stirs them. Thus, when the heart is harmonious, the vital energies become harmonious; renewed daily and flourishing monthly, this development becomes something one could not stop even if one wished, allowing its inner impulse full expression. Thus, when the vital energies are harmonious, the body becomes harmonious; the feet tread and the hands dance, and something is understood without words, making its transforming power manifest. In this way, harmony and accord accumulate within, while the spirit’s response works wondrously…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
於外天下之至和在我矣推而達之以平天下
之情樂可勝用哉是知禮樂之實舉不外於孝
弟人能從事於此則立於禮成於樂而盡性之
能事畢矣亦何必遠有所慕哉斯義也有子嘗
言之矣曰孝弟也者其爲仁之本與曰禮之用
和爲貴蓋達禮樂之致而探其本者矣孟子之
傳得之聖門固不信與然學者何以進之曰禮
可以强而立而樂不可强而致有事勿忘而俟
其化斯得之矣故曰惟樂不可以僞爲
===
易
乾元者始而亨者也利貞者性情也乾始
能以美利利天下不言所利大矣哉大
哉乾乎剛健中正純粹精也
趙賢
同考試官教諭劉 批〔理明詞峻得潔靜精微之旨〕
同考試官教諭程 批〔天道類非淺學能言此作指造化如掌說天莫辨於子矣〕
同考試官教諭朱 批〔說乾元之意明透〕
punctuated:
於外，天下之至和在我矣。推而達之，以平天下之情，樂可勝用哉？是知禮樂之實，舉不外於孝弟。人能從事於此，則立於禮，成於樂，而盡性之能事畢矣。亦何必遠有所慕哉？斯義也，有子嘗言之矣，曰：「孝弟也者，其爲仁之本與！」曰：「禮之用，和爲貴。」蓋達禮樂之致而探其本者矣。孟子之傳得之聖門，固不信與？然學者何以進之？曰：「禮可以强而立，而樂不可强而致。有事勿忘，而俟其化，斯得之矣。」故曰：「惟樂不可以僞爲。」

易
乾元者，始而亨者也；利貞者，性情也。乾始能以美利利天下，不言所利，大矣哉！大哉乾乎！剛健中正，純粹精也。

趙賢

同考試官教諭劉，批〔理明詞峻，得潔靜精微之旨。〕
同考試官教諭程，批〔天道類非淺學能言，此作指造化如掌，說天莫辨於子矣。〕
同考試官教諭朱，批〔說乾元之意明透。〕
translation_en:
…outwardly, and the utmost harmony under Heaven resides within me. Extend it and bring it everywhere to harmonize the feelings of all under Heaven: could the uses of music ever be exhausted? Thus we know that the substance of ritual and music lies entirely within filial devotion and brotherly respect. If people can devote themselves to these, they will establish themselves through ritual and attain completion through music, fully accomplishing the work of realizing their nature. Why must they seek something distant to admire? Master You once expressed this principle, saying, “Filial devotion and brotherly respect—are these not the root of practicing benevolence?” He also said, “In the practice of ritual, harmony is prized.” He thus understood the ultimate purport of ritual and music and explored their root. Can it truly be doubted that what Mencius transmitted came from the school of the Sage? Yet how can students advance toward this? The answer is: “One may establish oneself in ritual through deliberate effort, but the attainment of music cannot be forced. Keep working at it without forgetting, and await its transforming effect: thus one will attain it.” Hence the saying: “Music alone cannot be counterfeited.”

Book of Changes

“The primal power of Qian is that which initiates and brings things to fulfillment; its beneficence and constancy are its nature and disposition. Qian initiates and can benefit all under Heaven with its excellent benefits, without specifying what it benefits. How great it is! Great indeed is Qian! Firm and vigorous, central and correct, pure and unmixed: it is the utmost refinement.”

Zhao Xian

Comment by Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor: 〔The principles are clear and the language forceful; it captures the purport of purity, stillness, refinement, and subtlety.〕

Comment by Associate Examiner Cheng, Instructor: 〔Matters concerning the Way of Heaven [?] cannot be discussed by those of shallow learning. This composition points out the workings of creation as clearly as something in the palm of one’s hand. In explaining Heaven, none is more discerning than you.〕

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor: 〔The meaning of Qian’s primal power is explained clearly and penetratingly.〕

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
於莫測蓋極天下之至精以爲德者矣乾之大
不其至乎夫語乾道而至於精則所以斡一元
之樞而宰四時之運者固有在矣夫子贊乾其
至哉雖然乾天道也亦君道也天以陽生萬物
以陰成之而一元之氣未嘗不流行於其間聖
人以仁育萬民以義正之而好生之意未嘗不
浹洽於其內茲其乘龍御天而成萬國咸寧之
化矣聖人與天合一吾於此尤信
是以君子將有爲也將有行也問焉而以
言其受命也如嚮无有遠近幽深遂知
來物非天下之至精其孰能與於此
===
許經
同考試官教諭劉　批〔說辭占至精無餘歉矣錄之〕
同考試官教諭程　批〔來物遂知即如嚮中專士〕
多不能發明精瑩之作獨于子見之
同考試官教諭朱　批〔講至精處極有精神〕
考試官教諭胡　批〔明順〕
考試官學正史　批〔精思雅作如子可敬〕
punctuated:
於莫測，蓋極天下之至精以爲德者矣。乾之大，不其至乎？夫語乾道而至於精，則所以斡一元之樞而宰四時之運者，固有在矣。夫子贊乾，其至哉！雖然，乾，天道也，亦君道也。天以陽生萬物，以陰成之，而一元之氣未嘗不流行於其間。聖人以仁育萬民，以義正之，而好生之意未嘗不浹洽於其內。茲其乘龍御天而成萬國咸寧之化矣。聖人與天合一，吾於此尤信。

是以君子將有爲也，將有行也，問焉而以言，其受命也如嚮，无有遠近幽深，遂知來物。非天下之至精，其孰能與於此？

許經

同考試官教諭劉，批〔說辭占至精，無餘歉矣，錄之。〕
同考試官教諭程，批〔來物遂知，即如嚮中，專士〕多不能發明，精瑩之作，獨于子見之。
同考試官教諭朱，批〔講至精處，極有精神。〕
考試官教諭胡，批〔明順。〕
考試官學正史，批〔精思雅作，如子可敬。〕
translation_en:
…in the unfathomable. Its virtue indeed embodies the utmost refinement under Heaven. Is not the greatness of Qian—the Creative—supreme? When discussion of the Way of Qian reaches its refinement, there is surely a foundation for its turning the pivot of the primal unity and governing the movement of the four seasons. How consummate is the Master's praise of Qian! Yet Qian is the Way of Heaven and also the Way of the ruler. Heaven generates the myriad things through yang and brings them to completion through yin, while the vital energy of the primal unity never ceases to circulate among them. The sage nurtures the myriad people through benevolence and sets them right through righteousness, while his concern for fostering life never ceases to permeate them. Thus he rides the dragons and governs Heaven, bringing about the transformation through which all states enjoy peace. Here I am especially convinced that the sage and Heaven form a unity.

“Thus, when the gentleman is about to undertake something or take action, he questions it [the Changes] in words. It receives his command like an echo; whether distant or near, hidden or deep, he thereupon knows what is to come. Were it not the utmost refinement under Heaven, what could participate in this?”

Xu Jing

Associate Examiner Liu, Instructor, comments: 〔The explanation of the utmost refinement of the statements and divination leaves nothing wanting. Accept it.〕
Associate Examiner Cheng, Instructor, comments: 〔Immediately knowing what is to come is already contained in ‘like an echo.’ Specialists [?]〕 often cannot elucidate this. Only in you do I find a composition of such refinement and clarity.
Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor, comments: 〔The discussion of utmost refinement is exceptionally spirited.〕
Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: 〔Clear and fluent.〕
Examiner Shi, School Instructor, comments: 〔Subtle thought and an elegant composition: someone like you deserves respect.〕

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
而已矣安能隨感隨應而極其速哉吁此辭占
所以爲天下之至精也以言以卜筮者其可忽
諸雖然亦聖人之精爲之也蓋其心靜乎天地
之鑑萬物之鏡也虛而能照應而不藏以是心
而洩之於易故辭占之至精聖人之至精也不
然是亦推測之知而已矣烏能神故曰聖人之
精畫卦以示聖人之藴因卦以發諒哉
書
天敘有典勅我五典五惇哉天秩有禮自
我五禮有庸哉
===
羅許
同考試官教諭蕭　批〔典禮惇庸意剖析精到錄之〕
考試官教諭胡　批〔莊重不浮〕
考試官學正史　批〔醞藉典實議之親切有味〕
大臣言典禮出於天而有相之道存乎君也夫
天之立君以爲民也相天道以立民極謂非君
之事哉皐陶陳安民之謨而廸之舜者如此蓋
曰君道以安民爲要安民以敎化爲先何則自
punctuated:
而已矣，安能隨感隨應而極其速哉？吁！此辭占所以爲天下之至精也。以言以卜筮者，其可忽諸？雖然，亦聖人之精爲之也。蓋其心靜乎，天地之鑑，萬物之鏡也，虛而能照，應而不藏。以是心而洩之於易，故辭占之至精，聖人之至精也。不然，是亦推測之知而已矣，烏能神？故曰：「聖人之精，畫卦以示；聖人之藴，因卦以發。」諒哉！

書
天敘有典，勅我五典五惇哉！天秩有禮，自我五禮有庸哉！

羅許
同考試官教諭蕭　批〔典禮惇庸意剖析精到錄之〕
考試官教諭胡　批〔莊重不浮〕
考試官學正史　批〔醞藉典實議之親切有味〕

大臣言典禮出於天，而有相之道存乎君也。夫天之立君，以爲民也。相天道以立民極，謂非君之事哉？皐陶陳安民之謨，而廸之舜者如此。蓋曰：君道以安民爲要，安民以敎化爲先。何則？自
translation_en:
…and nothing more. How could it respond to each stimulus with the utmost speed? Ah! This is why the statements and prognostications constitute the most subtle refinement under Heaven. Can those who consult them for words or for divination with tortoise shells and milfoil neglect them? Yet this, too, is the work of the sage’s subtle refinement. His mind is still: a mirror of Heaven and Earth, a mirror of the myriad things. Empty, it can illuminate; it responds without retaining. With this mind he gives expression to the Changes. Thus the utmost subtlety of its statements and prognostications is the utmost subtlety of the sage himself. Otherwise, this would be merely knowledge obtained through conjecture. How could it possess spiritual efficacy? Hence the saying: “The sage’s subtle essence is displayed by drawing the hexagrams; the sage’s accumulated wisdom is brought forth through the hexagrams.” How true!

Book of Documents
“Heaven has set forth the constant norms of human relations: let us put our five teachings in order, that all five may be made substantial! Heaven has ranked the rites: let our five rites be put into constant practice!”

Luo Xu
Associate Examiner Xiao, Instructor, comments: 〔The meaning of making the norms substantial and putting the rites into constant practice is analyzed with precision and insight. Selected for inclusion.〕
Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: 〔Dignified and free of superficiality.〕
Examiner Shi, School Instructor, comments: 〔Restrained and rich in implication, grounded in the classics and substantial in content; its discussion is apt and full of savor.〕

The great minister says that the constant norms and rites originate in Heaven, while the way to assist Heaven rests with the ruler. Heaven establishes rulers for the sake of the people. Could assisting the Way of Heaven to establish the supreme standard for the people be anything other than the ruler’s duty? Such was Gao Yao’s presentation of his plans for bringing peace to the people and his guidance to Shun. His meaning was this: the essential task of rulership is to bring peace to the people, and in bringing peace to the people, moral instruction and transformation come first. Why is this? From…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
由立也惇庸由君天道之所由成也安民莫先
於教化如此人君其圖之哉大抵天地設位聖
人成能不以可憂同其無憂者有相之道存焉
相與之際固有相成者在是故以神宰御則格
天有勳以妙參贊則配天有道臯陶斯言不惟
啓萬世性道之源而且求端於天謂非覩其深
識其大乎雖然惇典庸禮德教不可尚已至於
不率教者則又明刑以弼之卒使民協中焉然
則臯陶其亦有功於典禮也夫
===
道洽政治澤潤生民四夷左衽罔不咸賴
王汝魯
同考試官教諭蕭 批〔道洽政治四字作者類皆浮漫無據此篇認理精切詞雄健錄之〕
考試官教諭胡 批〔得康王期待畢公本意〕
考試官學正史 批〔說成周化啟功效處有氣象有思致〕
賢王期大臣治功之成而因大其效焉夫化被
中國而施及四夷治效可謂大矣然非三后治
punctuated:
由立也，惇庸由君，天道之所由成也。安民莫先於教化，如此，人君其圖之哉！大抵天地設位，聖人成能，不以可憂同其無憂者，有相之道存焉。相與之際，固有相成者在。是故以神宰御，則格天有勳；以妙參贊，則配天有道。臯陶斯言，不惟啓萬世性道之源，而且求端於天，謂非覩其深、識其大乎？雖然，惇典庸禮，德教不可尚已。至於不率教者，則又明刑以弼之，卒使民協中焉。然則臯陶其亦有功於典禮也夫！

道洽政治，澤潤生民，四夷左衽，罔不咸賴。
王汝魯
同考試官教諭蕭批〔道洽政治四字，作者類皆浮漫無據，此篇認理精切，詞雄健，錄之。〕
考試官教諭胡批〔得康王期待畢公本意。〕
考試官學正史批〔說成周化啟功效處，有氣象，有思致。〕
賢王期大臣治功之成，而因大其效焉。夫化被中國而施及四夷，治效可謂大矣。然非三后治
translation_en:
…is thereby established. Strengthening and employing these norms rests with the ruler; through this the Way of Heaven is brought to fulfillment. Nothing takes precedence over moral instruction in bringing peace to the people. Such being the case, should not the ruler give thought to it? Broadly speaking, Heaven and Earth take their appointed places, and the sage fulfills their capacities. That he does not treat what warrants concern as though it were free of concern [?] is because a way of assisting them exists. In their mutual interaction, they assuredly bring one another to fulfillment. Thus, through numinous governance, there is achievement that reaches Heaven; through subtle participation and assistance, there is a way to match Heaven. These words of Gao Yao not only disclose the source of human nature and the Way for all generations, but also seek their origins in Heaven. Can one say that he did not perceive their depth and comprehend their greatness? Nevertheless, in strengthening the constant norms and putting ritual into practice, nothing surpasses instruction through virtue. As for those who do not follow that instruction, clearly established punishments must further support it, ultimately bringing the people into accord with the mean. Thus Gao Yao, too, surely contributed to the constant norms and ritual!

“Your Way has spread everywhere and your governance is well ordered; your beneficence nourishes the people. The peoples of the four quarters, who fasten their robes on the left, all alike depend upon it.”
Wang Rulu
Associate Examiner Xiao, Instructor, comments: 〔In treating the four characters meaning ‘the Way has spread everywhere and governance is well ordered,’ writers are generally superficial, diffuse, and without foundation. This essay grasps the principles precisely and incisively, and its language is vigorous. Selected for inclusion.〕
Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: 〔Captures King Kang’s original intent in expressing his expectations of the Duke of Bi.〕
Examiner Shi, School Instructor, comments: 〔The passage discussing the achievements of the transforming influence initiated at Chengzhou [?] has grandeur and thoughtful subtlety.〕

The worthy king expected his great minister to bring the achievements of governance to completion, and accordingly extolled the magnitude of their effects. Indeed, when transforming influence encompasses the central states and extends to the peoples of the four quarters, the effects of governance may truly be called great. Yet, were it not for the governance of the three sovereigns…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
文者矣斯人也不將與羔裘而並晏乎自夫司
直以事上則特公秉正而俊偉之業褎然朝野
而出色由之而文明一國庶幾乎龍光以爲德
者矣斯人也不將與三英而並粲乎即是而知
有服以表德則德爲益著服固不可已也有德
以充服則服爲益美德尤不可已也詩人極美
於鄭之大夫其意不可想見哉抑考鄭在春秋
若子良子太叔之謀國子皮子產之爲政皆能
竭盡忠赤佩佩不回而國社賴以爲安者詩人
===
之所詠豈其人乎或者又疑此詩爲緇衣之遺
而謂仍取於桓武也噫允若茲鄭之良不亦侈
乎故以若人用以維風宜無不可乃時猶有不
脩德隅如子臧之鷸冠坐取不衷之誚也豈諸
良無所與耶吾於是乎有感
自今以始歲其有君子有穀詒孫子
劉黃裳
同考試官教諭吳　批　是作體裁整齊文詞典雅
而意獨申盡殆冲夷許子之撰也而薦允宜□
punctuated:
文者矣。斯人也，不將與羔裘而並晏乎？自夫司直以事上，則特公秉正，而俊偉之業褎然朝野而出色，由之而文明一國，庶幾乎龍光以爲德者矣。斯人也，不將與三英而並粲乎？即是而知，有服以表德，則德爲益著，服固不可已也；有德以充服，則服爲益美，德尤不可已也。詩人極美於鄭之大夫，其意不可想見哉？抑考鄭在春秋，若子良、子太叔之謀國，子皮、子產之爲政，皆能竭盡忠赤，佩佩不回，而國社賴以爲安者。詩人之所詠，豈其人乎？或者又疑此詩爲《緇衣》之遺，而謂仍取於桓、武也。噫！允若茲，鄭之良不亦侈乎？故以若人用以維風，宜無不可，乃時猶有不脩德隅，如子臧之鷸冠，坐取不衷之誚也。豈諸良無所與耶？吾於是乎有感。
自今以始，歲其有。君子有穀，詒孫子。
劉黃裳
同考試官教諭吳　批：是作體裁整齊，文詞典雅，而意獨申盡，殆冲夷許子之撰也，而薦允宜□。
translation_en:
…one possessed of refinement. Would such a man not share the serene dignity of his lambskin robe? When he serves his superiors by maintaining rectitude, he upholds impartiality [?] and adheres to what is right. His outstanding achievements distinguish him at court and beyond, bringing cultural brilliance to the whole state. He comes close to making glorious distinction itself a virtue. Would such a man not shine alongside the robe’s three ornaments?
From this we know that when clothing expresses virtue, virtue becomes more conspicuous: clothing certainly cannot be dispensed with. When virtue gives substance to clothing, clothing becomes more beautiful: virtue is still less dispensable. Can we not readily imagine the poet’s intention in praising the great officers of Zheng so highly? Looking back at Zheng during the Spring and Autumn period, men such as Ziliang and Zitaishu in their deliberations for the state, and Zipi and Zichan in their administration, devoted themselves with utter loyalty, steadfast and unswerving [?], and the state’s altars depended upon them for security. Might these have been the men whom the poet celebrated? Others suspect that this poem preserves the legacy of “The Black Robes” and hold that it likewise concerns Dukes Huan and Wu. Ah! If this is indeed so, how abundant were Zheng’s worthy men!
With such men employed to sustain its moral customs, all should have been well. Yet there were still those who failed to cultivate moral integrity, such as Zizang, whose kingfisher-feather cap brought upon him the reproach of impropriety. Could it be that these worthy men had no influence upon them? This moves me to reflection.
“From this time onward, may the years bring abundance. May the lord possess goodness and bequeath it to his descendants.”
Liu Huangshang
Comment by Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor: This composition is orderly in form and elegant in diction, while its meaning is developed with exceptional completeness. It is probably the work of Master Xu of Chongyi [?]; recommending it is entirely fitting [illegible].

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭何　批〔詞字作者多以子孫繼述言殊非本旨子獨就魯君身上說甚是是用錄之〕
考試官教諭胡　批〔是當時祝頌之意可以式矣〕
考試官學正史　批〔詞婉意足〕
魯人愛君之情在於足國裕後而已矣蓋年豐
則國足善詒則後裕也兼而有之夫非斂福之
極與魯人以是願君而忠愛之情見於辭矣且
君者以安民爲心而又以善後爲悅者也吾人
===
承君之燕何以致望於君哉亦曰國依於民民
依於食年必貴於順成固也我魯慨自歲事告
侵夫固觖望於食矣安得自今伊始天心仁愛
以其庇吾君者推以及吾民兩暘順若而三時
不愆螟螣斂息而百穀用實不獨一歲爲然也
且由稔而登而大熟焉自天降康而樂歲爲之
頻仍由登而成而大有焉將受厥明而豐穰爲
之無已至如不雨而書無麥而書者固無慮也
夫然則粒食之源不竭以充國用以蕃民生相
punctuated:
同考試官教諭何　批〔詞字作者多以子孫繼述言，殊非本旨。子獨就魯君身上說，甚是，是用錄之。〕
考試官教諭胡　批〔是當時祝頌之意，可以式矣。〕
考試官學正史　批〔詞婉意足。〕
魯人愛君之情，在於足國裕後而已矣。蓋年豐則國足，善詒則後裕也。兼而有之，夫非斂福之極與？魯人以是願君，而忠愛之情見於辭矣。且君者，以安民爲心，而又以善後爲悅者也。吾人承君之燕，何以致望於君哉？亦曰：國依於民，民依於食，年必貴於順成，固也。我魯慨自歲事告侵，夫固觖望於食矣。安得自今伊始，天心仁愛，以其庇吾君者推以及吾民，兩暘順若而三時不愆，螟螣斂息而百穀用實。不獨一歲爲然也，且由稔而登而大熟焉，自天降康，而樂歲爲之頻仍；由登而成而大有焉，將受厥明，而豐穰爲之無已。至如不雨而書、無麥而書者，固無慮也。夫然則粒食之源不竭，以充國用，以蕃民生，相
translation_en:
Associate Examiner He, Instructor, comments: 〔In treating these words [?], most writers speak of descendants carrying on their forebears’ work, which entirely misses the original meaning. You alone explain them with reference to the ruler of Lu himself. This is quite right, and for this reason I have selected the essay.〕
Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: 〔This captures the intention of the blessings and praises offered at the time. It may serve as a model.〕
Examiner Shi, Instructor, comments: 〔The language is graceful and the meaning fully expressed.〕
The people of Lu expressed their love for their ruler simply by wishing abundance for the state and ample provision for posterity. For when the harvest is plentiful, the state has enough; when a good legacy is bequeathed, posterity is amply provided for. To possess both—is this not the utmost accumulation of blessings? The people of Lu wished these things for their ruler, and their loyal affection appeared in their words. Moreover, a ruler sets his heart on bringing peace to his people and takes pleasure in making good provision for those to come. Receiving our ruler’s hospitality at his feast, how should we express our hopes for him? We can only say: the state depends upon the people, and the people depend upon food. It is therefore fitting to prize a year in which the crops ripen in due season. Alas, since our Lu suffered a failed harvest, we have indeed longed for food. If only, from this time onward, Heaven in its benevolence would extend the protection it gives our ruler to our people, so that rain [?] and sunshine follow their proper courses and the three farming seasons suffer no disruption, grain pests subside, and all the crops bear their grain. Nor should this be so for just one year. May ripening lead to a full harvest and then to a great abundance; may Heaven send down well-being, so that years of plenty recur continually. May harvests reach fulfillment and then yield still greater plenty; may we receive Heaven’s radiant blessing [?], so that abundance never ends. As for occasions recorded as ‘no rain’ or ‘no wheat,’ there would assuredly be no need to fear them. Then the supply of grain for food would never be exhausted, furnishing the state’s needs, enriching the people’s livelihood, and assisting …

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
魯人美不忘規猶足以續卷阿洞酌之音者說
者槩謂其詞誇噫殆亦未之深省與
春秋
秋齊侯宋公江人黃人會于陽穀〔僖公三年〕
王家卿
同考試官教諭吳　批〔齊桓攘楚之謀作者多恢張之其意殊淺此篇辭不費而意足錄之〕
考試官教諭胡　批〔簡明〕
考試官學正史　批〔得聖人予齊桓意〕
===
春秋于伯主之講好而深善其得攘外之謀也
夫制敵莫先於謀也陽穀會而攘楚之謀定矣
獨非春秋之所善乎齊桓主伯志在安攘合諸
侯以謀楚是以爲陽穀之會也春秋善之者何
蓋伯者之匡天下也固在於兵之强而其用兵
也猶在於謀之善使桓舉兵而無謀焉其能得
志于楚乎幸而有見于此以師非厚集不足以
威敵也戒玆八國陳兵以震吾之威焉聚而爲
punctuated:
魯人美不忘規，猶足以續卷阿洞酌之音者，說者槩謂其詞誇，噫！殆亦未之深省與！

春秋
秋，齊侯、宋公、江人、黃人會于陽穀。〔僖公三年〕
王家卿
同考試官教諭吳　批〔齊桓攘楚之謀，作者多恢張之，其意殊淺。此篇辭不費而意足，錄之。〕
考試官教諭胡　批〔簡明。〕
考試官學正史　批〔得聖人予齊桓意。〕

春秋于伯主之講好，而深善其得攘外之謀也。夫制敵莫先於謀也，陽穀會而攘楚之謀定矣，獨非春秋之所善乎？齊桓主伯，志在安攘，合諸侯以謀楚，是以爲陽穀之會也。春秋善之者何？蓋伯者之匡天下也，固在於兵之强，而其用兵也，猶在於謀之善。使桓舉兵而無謀焉，其能得志于楚乎？幸而有見于此，以師非厚集不足以威敵也，戒玆八國，陳兵以震吾之威焉，聚而爲
translation_en:
…the people of Lu, in their praise, did not forget admonition, and their verses were still worthy of carrying on the strains of “The Winding Mound” (Juan A) and “Drawing Water” (Dong Zhuo [?]). Yet commentators generally call their language exaggerated. Alas! Perhaps they have not reflected deeply upon it!

Spring and Autumn Annals
“In autumn, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, and men of Jiang and Huang met at Yanggu.” 〔Third year of Duke Xi.〕
By Wang Jiaqing.
Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor, comments: 〔Writers mostly embellish Duke Huan of Qi’s plans to repel Chu, but their interpretations are exceedingly shallow. This essay conveys its meaning fully without wasting words. Selected for inclusion.〕
Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: 〔Concise and clear.〕
Examiner Shi, School Instructor, comments: 〔Captures the Sage’s intention in commending Duke Huan of Qi.〕
In recording the hegemon’s cultivation of friendly relations, the Spring and Autumn Annals deeply approves his securing a strategy for repelling external threats. In overcoming an enemy, nothing takes precedence over planning. With the meeting at Yanggu, the plan to repel Chu was settled. Was this not precisely what the Spring and Autumn Annals approved? Duke Huan of Qi assumed leadership as hegemon, intent on securing peace within and repelling threats from without. He assembled the feudal lords to devise a plan against Chu: this was the purpose of the meeting at Yanggu. Why does the Spring and Autumn Annals approve it? For a hegemon to set the world right certainly depends upon the strength of his troops; yet his employment of those troops depends in turn upon the excellence of his plans. Had Duke Huan raised troops without a plan, could he have achieved his aims against Chu? Fortunately, he understood this. Considering that troops could not overawe the enemy unless assembled in great numbers, he alerted these eight states and arrayed their forces to make his might felt, gathering them to form …

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
正可以聲楚人之罪也兵無外應非所以濟變
也諭彼江黄按兵以為吾之援焉夘而為奇可
以擬楚人之後也固不待陘亭之次楚師之震
恐也先事以為圖桓也籌之素矣兢敵之楚有
出乎桓之謀哉固不必召陵之盟屈完之輸欵
也慮勝而後會桓也討之久矣萬全之策何有
于楚之兵哉聖人以攘夷安夏伯者事也而况
好謀而成者乎是會也震中夏之威抑外夷之
横世道之大幸也故諸侯皆在而末言者善是
===
謀也抑桓之兹謀豈一朝之可能哉貫澤之盟
江黄巳結楚之黨孤而我之勢盛其所以為楚
計者不可謂無備而猶事于陽穀之會蓋慮楚
之强而念之勤矣終焉弗怠王道可幾也何楚
人巳服而其志遂驕侵陳之兵巳非而視黄之
患弗救豈伯主之職哉是故聖人深善攘楚之
謀所以大尊王之義而紀伐黄之師猶欲其敦
不息之誠也
宋師伐陳衛人救陳〔宣公十有二年〕夏楚
punctuated:
正，可以聲楚人之罪也。兵無外應，非所以濟變也。諭彼江、黄，按兵以為吾之援焉；夘而為奇，可以擬楚人之後也。固不待陘亭之次、楚師之震恐也，先事以為圖，桓也籌之素矣。兢敵之楚，有出乎桓之謀哉？固不必召陵之盟、屈完之輸欵也，慮勝而後會，桓也討之久矣。萬全之策，何有于楚之兵哉？聖人以攘夷安夏，伯者事也，而况好謀而成者乎？是會也，震中夏之威，抑外夷之横，世道之大幸也。故諸侯皆在而末言者，善是謀也。
抑桓之兹謀，豈一朝之可能哉？貫澤之盟，江、黄巳結，楚之黨孤，而我之勢盛。其所以為楚計者，不可謂無備，而猶事于陽穀之會，蓋慮楚之强而念之勤矣。終焉弗怠，王道可幾也。何楚人巳服，而其志遂驕？侵陳之兵巳非，而視黄之患弗救，豈伯主之職哉？是故聖人深善攘楚之謀，所以大尊王之義；而紀伐黄之師，猶欲其敦不息之誠也。
宋師伐陳，衛人救陳。〔宣公十有二年〕夏，楚
translation_en:
…as the main force, they could publicly proclaim the offenses of Chu. Troops without outside support cannot cope with unforeseen developments. He instructed Jiang and Huang to hold their troops ready to support him; deployed separately as an auxiliary force [?], they could threaten Chu’s rear. Indeed, even before the encampment at Xingting and the terror of Chu’s army, Duke Huan had long been laying his plans in advance. Could Chu, his rival, do anything beyond his calculations? Indeed, even without waiting for the covenant at Shaoling and Qu Wan’s submission, Duke Huan had long deliberated on the matter, calculating how to secure victory before convening the meeting. With a strategy that ensured complete success, what difficulty could Chu’s troops present? The Sage regarded repelling the foreign peoples and securing the Chinese states as the work of a hegemon. How much more would he approve one who delighted in planning and brought his plans to fruition? This meeting displayed the might of the central Chinese states and checked the aggression of the peoples beyond them: a great blessing for the order of the world. Thus, although the feudal lords were all present, the wording placed at the end [?] expresses approval of this plan.
Yet could Duke Huan’s plan have been devised in a single day? At the covenant of Guanze, alliances with Jiang and Huang had already been secured; Chu was isolated from its supporters, while our strength flourished. His preparations for dealing with Chu could hardly be called inadequate. Nevertheless, he still undertook the meeting at Yanggu, because he was concerned about Chu’s strength and gave the matter diligent thought. Had he remained tireless to the end, he might have approached the Way of the True King. Why, once the people of Chu had submitted, did his intentions turn to arrogance? His military invasion of Chen was already wrong; to look on at Huang’s plight without coming to its rescue—was this fulfilling a hegemon’s duty? Thus the Sage deeply approved the plan to repel Chu, thereby greatly exalting the principle of honoring the king. Yet in recording the army’s attack on Huang, he still wished Duke Huan to strengthen his unceasing sincerity.
The army of Song attacked Chen; the men of Wei came to Chen’s rescue. 〔The twelfth year of Duke Xuan〕 In summer, Chu …

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
強之患而惟無備之患方楚之脅夫宋也抑何
爲計哉惜民力以固其本寧非禦敵之道乎昧
自治而攻楚之與國是無故而啓釁也爲謀不
臧楚是以有伐宋之師焉夫陳楚之新得也伐
陳是伐楚矣楚何人哉而肯於與國之棄是宜
弗甘于宋者經以宋有可伐之罪楚是以有能
伐之名稱爵而宋之罪見矣不然則猾夏之楚
春秋方懲之矣而何以書爵哉雖然宋之罪大
矣衛之罪可恕耶楚不足責而晉實可尤也清
===
丘之盟恤病討貳乃宋之伐陳衛可以救而宋
之被兵晉可以弗救耶春秋端本澄源故責宋
爲深而清丘之信誠有不待貶者故曰盟非春
秋之所貴于此益信
禮記
故樂者天地之命中和之紀人情之所不
能免也
許份
同考試官學正袁　批　〔命紀皆統聲容此作獨能〕
punctuated:
強之患，而惟無備之患。方楚之脅夫宋也，抑何爲計哉？惜民力以固其本，寧非禦敵之道乎？昧自治而攻楚之與國，是無故而啓釁也。爲謀不臧，楚是以有伐宋之師焉。夫陳，楚之新得也；伐陳，是伐楚矣。楚何人哉，而肯於與國之棄？是宜弗甘于宋者。經以宋有可伐之罪，楚是以有能伐之名。稱爵而宋之罪見矣。不然，則猾夏之楚，《春秋》方懲之矣，而何以書爵哉？雖然，宋之罪大矣，衛之罪可恕耶？楚不足責，而晉實可尤也。清丘之盟，恤病討貳，乃宋之伐陳，衛可以救，而宋之被兵，晉可以弗救耶？《春秋》端本澄源，故責宋爲深，而清丘之信，誠有不待貶者。故曰：盟非《春秋》之所貴，于此益信。

禮記
故樂者，天地之命，中和之紀，人情之所不能免也。

許份

同考試官學正袁　批　〔命紀皆統聲容，此作獨能〕
translation_en:
…the danger of [an enemy’s] strength, but only the danger of being unprepared. When Chu threatened Song, what course should Song have adopted? Would conserving the people’s strength to secure its foundations not have been a way to resist the enemy? To neglect putting its own affairs in order and instead attack Chu’s ally was to provoke hostilities without cause. Its planning was unsound; hence Chu dispatched an army against Song. Chen had newly come over to Chu: to attack Chen was to attack Chu. What sort of power was Chu, that it would consent to abandon an ally? It was natural that Chu would not let Song’s action pass. Since the Classic regarded Song as guilty of an offense warranting attack, Chu consequently had grounds for undertaking that attack. By naming Chu’s ruler by his noble rank, it made Song’s guilt apparent. Otherwise, the Spring and Autumn Annals would have been condemning Chu for bringing disorder to the Chinese states: why, then, would it record his noble rank?

Even so, although Song’s guilt was great, could Wei’s guilt be excused? Chu scarcely merits reproach, while Jin truly deserves blame. The covenant at Qingqiu pledged aid to those in distress and punishment of those who were disloyal. When Song attacked Chen, Wei could come to Chen’s rescue; but when Song itself came under attack, could Jin withhold assistance? The Spring and Autumn Annals rectifies matters at their root and clears them at their source; hence it reproaches Song particularly severely. As for the good faith pledged at Qingqiu, its failure truly needed no explicit censure. Thus the saying that covenants are not what the Spring and Autumn Annals prizes is further confirmed here.

Record of Rites
“Thus music is the mandate of Heaven and Earth, the ordering principle of equilibrium and harmony, and something human feelings cannot do without.”

Xu Fen
