title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
非外也是以感遇聚散鼓之為風霆潤之為雨
露孚之為飛走草木含靈蠢動穉粕煨燼無非
天也無非天則亦無非性也人性諸天者也其
體用猶是也但衆人有之而不知賢人知之而
未盡是故仁者見之謂之仁智者見之謂之智
見仁則偏于內偏內則窒見智則偏于外偏外
則離仁智合一之道其誰知之聖人形天之形
也帥天之帥也其氣之清明質之純粹有若獨
厚於天者而成性存存之地物欲不得而與焉
===
故其靜與天俱也渾焉噩焉而富有之業以根
靜涵乎動也動與天游也弘焉博焉而日新之
德以著動涵乎靜也靜涵乎動則無內動涵乎
靜則無外無內則神無外則化窮神知化德之
盛也非聖人其孰能之人但見其冲然虛而已
淵然邃而已無將迎無內外而一疵不有則曰
聖人之仁也亦智也及其觸之即覺感之即應
變而通之以盡利鼓之舞之以盡神則曰聖人
之智也亦仁也仁存乎內而不可測智運乎外
punctuated:
非外也。是以感遇聚散，鼓之為風霆，潤之為雨露，孚之為飛走草木，含靈蠢動，穉粕煨燼，無非天也。無非天，則亦無非性也。人性諸天者也，其體用猶是也。但衆人有之而不知，賢人知之而未盡。是故仁者見之謂之仁，智者見之謂之智。見仁則偏于內，偏內則窒；見智則偏于外，偏外則離。仁智合一之道，其誰知之？聖人形天之形也，帥天之帥也。其氣之清明，質之純粹，有若獨厚於天者，而成性存存之地，物欲不得而與焉。
故其靜與天俱也，渾焉噩焉，而富有之業以根，靜涵乎動也；動與天游也，弘焉博焉，而日新之德以著，動涵乎靜也。靜涵乎動則無內，動涵乎靜則無外。無內則神，無外則化。窮神知化，德之盛也。非聖人，其孰能之？人但見其冲然虛而已，淵然邃而已，無將迎，無內外，而一疵不有，則曰：「聖人之仁也，亦智也。」及其觸之即覺，感之即應，變而通之以盡利，鼓之舞之以盡神，則曰：「聖人之智也，亦仁也。」仁存乎內而不可測，智運乎外
translation_en:
…is not external. Thus, through mutual stimulation and encounter, gathering and dispersal, it is stirred into wind and thunder, moistens as rain and dew, and brings forth flying creatures, running beasts, grasses, and trees. Beings endowed with spirit and creatures that stir, immature growth and dregs [?], embers and ashes—all are Heaven. Since all are Heaven, all are also nature. Human beings derive their nature from Heaven; its substance and functioning are likewise such. Yet ordinary people possess it without knowing it, while the worthy know it without fully comprehending it. Therefore, the benevolent see it and call it benevolence; the wise see it and call it wisdom. To see benevolence alone is to incline toward the internal; such an inclination leads to obstruction. To see wisdom alone is to incline toward the external; such an inclination leads to separation. Who understands the Way in which benevolence and wisdom are one? The sage embodies the form of Heaven and follows what Heaven directs. His vital energy is clear and luminous, his constitution pure and unalloyed, as though Heaven had shown him exceptional favor. Where his perfected nature is continuously preserved, material desires can have no part.
Thus, in stillness he abides together with Heaven, undifferentiated and pristine, and the work of abundant possession takes root: stillness embraces movement. In movement he roams with Heaven, expansive and vast, and the virtue of daily renewal becomes manifest: movement embraces stillness. When stillness embraces movement, there is no inside; when movement embraces stillness, there is no outside. With no inside, there is spiritual efficacy; with no outside, there is transformation. To fathom spiritual efficacy and understand transformation is the fullness of virtue. Who but the sage could accomplish this? People see only his tranquil emptiness and profound depth, his neither sending off what passes nor welcoming what comes, his freedom from distinctions between inside and outside, and his absence of even a single flaw. They then say: “This is the sage’s benevolence, and it is also his wisdom.” When, however, he perceives immediately upon contact and responds immediately upon stimulation, adapting and opening ways through change to realize every benefit, stirring and animating things to give full expression to spiritual efficacy, they say: “This is the sage’s wisdom, and it is also his benevolence.” Benevolence abides within and cannot be fathomed; wisdom operates without…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
極之理運行於兩間舉之不遺施之不匱揣而
不有而其所以顯諸仁藏諸用合一而不測一
誠爲之也蓋天之所以爲天也天惟誠故眞實
之理流行賦予物與無妄參和不偏合仁與智
德性之所固有也聖人與人同耳乃庶民去之
而體用之理淆君子存之而內外之迹判於是
有是內非外者於是有徇生執有者是內非智
而亦不得爲仁執有非仁而又不得爲智聖人
之道遠矣故曰仁者見之謂之仁智者見之謂
===
之智百姓日用而不知嗚呼非聖人其孰與於
斯聖人者承天之道而立人之極者也所謂陰
陽之會動靜之交義命之準而性與天道之極
致也而莫非一誠爲之也故仁智者聖人之道
而誠者聖人之本也仁智合一非誠其孰爲之
聖人之仁智原於性統於心流行於事物充塞
乎天地無不備也無不體也是故以盡其性而
察之由之無不盡也是誠之成己也以盡人物
之性而知之處之無不當也是誠之成物也成
punctuated: 極之理，運行於兩間，舉之不遺，施之不匱，揣而不有，而其所以顯諸仁、藏諸用，合一而不測，一誠爲之也。蓋天之所以爲天也。天惟誠，故眞實之理流行賦予，物與無妄，參和不偏，合仁與智，德性之所固有也。聖人與人同耳，乃庶民去之，而體用之理淆；君子存之，而內外之迹判。於是有是內非外者，於是有徇生執有者。是內非智，而亦不得爲仁；執有非仁，而又不得爲智。聖人之道遠矣。故曰：「仁者見之謂之仁，智者見之謂之智，百姓日用而不知。」嗚呼！非聖人，其孰與於斯？聖人者，承天之道而立人之極者也。所謂陰陽之會、動靜之交、義命之準，而性與天道之極致也，而莫非一誠爲之也。故仁智者，聖人之道，而誠者，聖人之本也。仁智合一，非誠其孰爲之？聖人之仁智，原於性，統於心，流行於事物，充塞乎天地，無不備也，無不體也。是故以盡其性而察之、由之，無不盡也，是誠之成己也；以盡人物之性而知之、處之，無不當也，是誠之成物也。成
translation_en: …the principle of the Ultimate operates between Heaven and Earth. In encompassing things it leaves nothing out; in application it is inexhaustible; it measures yet does not possess [?]. That it manifests itself in benevolence and conceals itself in functioning, united as one yet unfathomable, is accomplished solely by sincerity. This is what makes Heaven Heaven. Because Heaven is sincere, its genuine principle flows forth and bestows endowments: things are endowed with freedom from falsity [?], harmoniously blended without partiality, uniting benevolence and wisdom. These are inherent in moral nature. The sage is simply the same as other people. Yet ordinary people abandon this, and the principles of substance and function become confused; the gentleman preserves it, yet the manifestations of inner and outer become divided. Thus there are those who affirm the inner and reject the outer, and those who pursue life and cling to existence [?]. Affirming the inner is not wisdom, nor can it qualify as benevolence; clinging to existence is not benevolence, nor can it qualify as wisdom. Far indeed is this from the Way of the sage! Thus it is said: “The benevolent see it and call it benevolence; the wise see it and call it wisdom; the common people use it daily without knowing it.” Alas! Who but a sage could participate in this? A sage is one who receives the Way of Heaven and establishes the ultimate standard for humanity. This is what is called the meeting of yin and yang, the intersection of activity and stillness, the standard of righteousness and destiny, and the highest realization of human nature and the Way of Heaven. All of this is accomplished solely by sincerity. Thus benevolence and wisdom constitute the sage’s Way, while sincerity is the sage’s foundation. What but sincerity could unite benevolence and wisdom as one? The sage’s benevolence and wisdom originate in his nature, are unified in his mind, flow through affairs and things, and fill Heaven and Earth. There is nothing they do not encompass, nothing they do not embody. Thus, in fully realizing his own nature, he examines and follows it, leaving nothing unrealized: this is sincerity’s completion of oneself. In fully realizing the natures of people and things, he understands and deals with them, with nothing inappropriate: this is sincerity’s completion of things. Completing…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
曆四年
羅許
同考試官教諭蕭　批〔陳詢中宛然見明良相得〕
〔氣象非直駢麗之佳美耳宜錄〕
考試官教諭胡　批〔精練雅麗讀之有鏗鏘聲可愛〕
考試官學正史　批〔典則〕
慶曆四年九月某日伏蒙
聖恩以臣衍同平章事兼樞密使者班聯
虎禁金鉉當台斗之司機握
===
鴻樞玉節掌韜鈐之寄地望獨高于三省職
司特重乎六卿似此元寮宜資碩輔肆
皇情之獨注寵假兼資顧綿力以何堪榮將拜
授臣衍誠惶誠恐稽首頓首竊惟耀武必
期於脩文攘外乃所以安內舜納百揆九
德咸宣禹比三苗四夷率服阿衡應聘遂
成造亳之功良弼旁求茂建憲天之烈經
邦論道公孤必慎其人除暴安民司馬實
難厥任仲山補袞中興之業彌隆方叔壯
banxin: 鄉試錄文　　　　　　　　卷二十五
punctuated:
曆四年。
羅許。
同考試官教諭蕭批〔陳詢中宛然見明良相得氣象，非直駢麗之佳美耳，宜錄。〕
考試官教諭胡批〔精練雅麗，讀之有鏗鏘聲，可愛。〕
考試官學正史批〔典則。〕
慶曆四年九月某日，伏蒙聖恩，以臣衍同平章事兼樞密使者。班聯虎禁，金鉉當台斗之司；機握鴻樞，玉節掌韜鈐之寄。地望獨高于三省，職司特重乎六卿。似此元寮，宜資碩輔。肆皇情之獨注，寵假兼資；顧綿力以何堪，榮將拜授。臣衍誠惶誠恐，稽首頓首。竊惟耀武必期於脩文，攘外乃所以安內。舜納百揆，九德咸宣；禹比三苗，四夷率服。阿衡應聘，遂成造亳之功；良弼旁求，茂建憲天之烈。經邦論道，公孤必慎其人；除暴安民，司馬實難厥任。仲山補袞，中興之業彌隆；方叔壯
translation_en:
…the fourth year of [Qing]li.
Luo Xu.
Associate Examiner Xiao, Instructor, comments: “In the presentation and consultation [?], one distinctly sees an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers working in harmony. Its excellence goes beyond beautiful parallel prose. It deserves inclusion.”
Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: “Refined, polished, elegant, and beautiful; read aloud, it has a ringing resonance. Delightful.”
Examiner Shi, Instructor, comments: “Classically correct.”
On a certain day of the ninth month of the fourth year of Qingli, I humbly received Your Majesty’s gracious appointment of me, your servant Yan, as Grand Councilor concurrently serving as Military Affairs Commissioner. My rank places me among those in the palace’s guarded precincts; as the golden carrying-bar of the cauldron, I assume the office symbolized by the exalted stars of state. Holding the great pivot of affairs, and bearing the jade tally, I am entrusted with military strategy. This standing rises above the Three Departments; these duties bear exceptional weight among the Six Ministers. Such a chief office ought to draw upon an eminent counselor. Your Majesty has therefore bestowed special attention upon me, graciously granting me both appointments. Yet how can my feeble abilities bear them? I am about to bow and accept this honor. Your servant Yan, in utmost awe and trepidation, bows his head to the ground and knocks his forehead upon it.
I humbly consider that displaying military might must aim at cultivating civil government, and that repelling external threats is the means of securing peace within. When Shun assumed charge of the hundred offices, all nine virtues were made manifest; when Yu brought the Sanmiao into submission, the peoples of the four quarters obediently submitted. When Aheng accepted the summons to serve, he accomplished the founding at Bo; when a worthy counselor was sought far and wide, he gloriously established achievements patterned on Heaven. To order the realm and discourse upon the Way, the men appointed as the Three Dukes and Three Solitaries must be chosen carefully; to eliminate violence and bring peace to the people, the Minister of War’s charge is indeed difficult. Zhongshan mended the ruler’s ceremonial robe, and the achievement of dynastic restoration grew ever more splendid; Fang Shu, mighty…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
獻大原之功不著遡觀往跡累重殊階自
三臺易於前朝惟二府合於
昭代
天廻斗柄閣門鄰
北闕之文昌星轉
宸垣帷幄總中台之武庫折衝樽俎秉政鈞衡
匈非經文緯武之才曷稱出將入相之任
是以魏仁浦之當國偉績猶存陳堯叟之
兼司芳聲尚著豈圖妙選誤畀庸流伏念
===
臣衍粗有朴忠本無學術濫登仕版榮叨
進士之科徒讀父書恪守先臣之業甘心
苦節絕意干名筮仕理刑旋領祕丘之佐
再爲令尹尋陞別駕之官屢列薦書忝稱
良吏乾州
賜宴遥承
天語之溫淮使問名特荷
中朝之眷承
內降之旨奭自封還阻攻守之師不圖僥倖
punctuated: 獻大原之功不著。遡觀往跡，累重殊階。自三臺易於前朝，惟二府合於昭代。天廻斗柄，閣門鄰北闕之文昌；星轉宸垣，帷幄總中台之武庫。折衝樽俎，秉政鈞衡。匈非經文緯武之才，曷稱出將入相之任？是以魏仁浦之當國，偉績猶存；陳堯叟之兼司，芳聲尚著。豈圖妙選，誤畀庸流？伏念臣衍，粗有朴忠，本無學術。濫登仕版，榮叨進士之科。徒讀父書，恪守先臣之業。甘心苦節，絕意干名。筮仕理刑，旋領祕丘之佐；再爲令尹，尋陞別駕之官。屢列薦書，忝稱良吏。乾州賜宴，遥承天語之溫；淮使問名，特荷中朝之眷。承內降之旨，奭自封還；阻攻守之師，不圖僥倖。
translation_en:
…presented achievements at Dayuan that were not manifest [?]. Looking back over past precedents, these exceptional ranks carried weighty responsibilities. Since the Three Terraces were altered under the preceding dynasty, only in this illustrious age have the Two Administrations been united. Heaven turns the handle of the Dipper: the cabinet gates adjoin Wenchang, the celestial seat of civil administration, at the northern palace. The stars revolve around the imperial enclosure: within the command tent, one directs the military arsenal of the Central Terrace. One repels adversaries over ceremonial wine vessels and controls the balance of government. Without the talent to order civil affairs and coordinate military affairs [?], how could one be equal to serving as a general in the field and a chief minister at court? Thus the great achievements of Wei Renpu when he governed the state endure, and the illustrious reputation of Chen Yaosou, who held concurrent responsibilities, remains renowned. Who could have imagined that this discerning selection would mistakenly confer office upon someone so ordinary?

I humbly reflect that I, your servant Yan, possess some simple loyalty but have neither learning nor expertise. Unworthily entered on the official rolls, I undeservedly enjoyed the distinction of becoming a metropolitan graduate (jinshi). I merely read my father's books and scrupulously maintained the vocation of my late father, your servant. I willingly embraced austere integrity and abandoned all thought of seeking fame. On first entering office, I administered criminal justice; soon afterward, I held an assistant's post at Miqiu [?]. I served again as a magistrate and was shortly promoted to administrative aide (biejia). Repeatedly included in letters of recommendation, I was undeservedly called a good official. At the banquet bestowed at Qianzhou, I received from afar the warmth of Your Majesty's words. When the envoy to the Huai region asked my name, I was especially favored by the central court's regard. Upon receiving an order issued from within the palace, I returned it under seal [?]; I opposed the deployment of troops for attack and defense, seeking no success through mere good fortune…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
堯歌擊壤神化難名
舜治垂衣穆清有象
德已聖而不自聖世已安而若未安縉紳興懷
思集夔龍于沼上耕氓增歎欲收頗牧于
禁中惟此在
廷之賢悉出臣愚之右臣獨蒙
聖眷深激愚衷敢不仰酬
天地之恩俯效涓埃之報期調商鼎勉樹周楨
陰陽和而風雨時贊
===
一人之斡旋元化萬國賓而四夷服脩五伐以
控制遐方伏願
任賢勿貳
保治無虞
審蓄威昭德之機
操居重馭輕之柄
慮周天下敦恭儉以先民
明照日中撫豐亨而御世
惟精惟一
punctuated:
堯歌擊壤，神化難名；舜治垂衣，穆清有象。德已聖而不自聖，世已安而若未安。縉紳興懷，思集夔龍于沼上；耕氓增歎，欲收頗牧于禁中。惟此在廷之賢，悉出臣愚之右。臣獨蒙聖眷，深激愚衷，敢不仰酬天地之恩，俯效涓埃之報？期調商鼎，勉樹周楨。陰陽和而風雨時，贊一人之斡旋元化；萬國賓而四夷服，脩五伐以控制遐方。
伏願任賢勿貳，保治無虞，審蓄威昭德之機，操居重馭輕之柄，慮周天下，敦恭儉以先民；明照日中，撫豐亨而御世。惟精惟一。
translation_en:
…Under Yao, the song of striking the earth celebrated a transforming influence so wondrous that it could scarcely be named; under Shun, who governed with his robes hanging loosely, serene purity found visible expression. Though your virtue is already sagely, you do not deem yourself a sage; though the realm is already at peace, you act as though peace were not yet secured. The gentlemen of office cherish the hope of gathering men like Kui and Long beside the imperial pool; the farming commoners sigh with longing to see men like Lian Po and Li Mu brought into the palace. These worthy men at court all surpass your foolish servant. Yet I alone have received your sagely favor, which deeply stirs my humble heart. How could I fail to repay, looking upward, your kindness as vast as Heaven and Earth, and offer, from below, a recompense as slight as a drop of water or a speck of dust? I aspire to blend the flavors in the cauldron of Shang and strive to establish pillars like those of Zhou. With yin and yang in harmony and wind and rain arriving in season, I would assist the One Man, the emperor, in directing the primal work of transformation. With the myriad states paying homage and the peoples of the four quarters submitting, I would put in order the five forms of punitive expedition to control distant lands.
I humbly pray that you employ the worthy without wavering and preserve orderly government free from peril; discern the occasions for husbanding your might and displaying your virtue; and hold the authority by which the weighty center governs the lesser periphery. Let your concern encompass all under Heaven, and cultivate reverence and frugality to set an example for the people. Let your discernment shine like the noonday sun, and preside over abundance and prosperity as you govern the world. Remain discerning and single-minded…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
聖化而有得者乎
同考試官教諭程　批
聖學淵微未易窺測名言子能以一日述須明備難矣中州傑士非子而誰
同考試官教諭朱　批〔此策揄揚我〕
聖祖心學之妙
皇上道統之傳明粹可式敬爲子錄之
考試官教諭胡　批〔文偉思深對揚策嘗無踰子〕
考試官學正史　批〔忠敬之意溢然宜錄〕
道之大原其出於天而統於
===
聖乎惟涵之於心者極其至精斯渙之於文者
極其至粹夫惟至精也則
聖德緝熙而統會於宥密
大業由此而日隆夫惟至粹也則
皇極敷言而垂憲於宇宙
盛德由此而日顯以淵懿端純之則而肇駿厖
高朗之休以開拓積累之勤而衍昌明弘
遠之緒是心也其契帝王道統之傳者乎
是文也其盡古今授受之妙者乎以此法
punctuated:
聖化而有得者乎？

同考試官教諭程批：聖學淵微，未易窺測。名言子能以一日述須明備，難矣！中州傑士，非子而誰？

同考試官教諭朱批〔此策揄揚我聖祖心學之妙、皇上道統之傳，明粹可式，敬爲子錄之。〕

考試官教諭胡批〔文偉思深，對揚策嘗無踰子。〕

考試官學正史批〔忠敬之意溢然，宜錄。〕

道之大原，其出於天而統於聖乎？惟涵之於心者極其至精，斯渙之於文者極其至粹。夫惟至精也，則聖德緝熙而統會於宥密，大業由此而日隆；夫惟至粹也，則皇極敷言而垂憲於宇宙，盛德由此而日顯。以淵懿端純之則，而肇駿厖高朗之休；以開拓積累之勤，而衍昌明弘遠之緒。是心也，其契帝王道統之傳者乎？是文也，其盡古今授受之妙者乎？以此法
translation_en:
…to have gained something through sagely transformation?

Comment by Associate Examiner Cheng, Instructor: Sagely learning is profound and subtle; its depths are not easily fathomed. Your fine words, composed in a single day, present it clearly and fully [?]—a difficult accomplishment indeed! Who but you could be an outstanding scholar of Zhongzhou?

Comment by Associate Examiner Zhu, Instructor: 〔This policy essay extols the subtlety of our Sagely Ancestor’s learning of the mind and His Majesty’s transmission of the succession of the Way. Clear and refined, it can serve as a model. I respectfully select it for you.〕

Comment by Examiner Hu, Instructor: 〔The writing is magnificent and the thought profound. In responding to and acclaiming the policy question [?], none surpasses you.〕

Comment by Examiner Shi, Instructor: 〔Loyalty and reverence overflow from it. It deserves selection.〕

Does not the great source of the Way issue from Heaven and find its unifying succession in the sage? Only when what is nurtured in the mind attains the utmost refinement can what flows forth in writing attain the utmost purity. Through this utmost refinement, sagely virtue grows ever more luminous and converges in profound stillness; the great undertaking thereby flourishes daily. Through this utmost purity, the Sovereign Standard is set forth in words, bequeathing a model to the universe; abundant virtue thereby becomes more manifest each day. Through a standard of profound excellence, uprightness, and purity, vast, lofty, and luminous blessings are inaugurated; through diligent expansion and accumulation, a flourishing, enlightened, far-reaching legacy is extended. Does not this mind accord with the transmission of the succession of the Way among emperors and kings? Does not this writing fully express the subtlety of its handing down and reception, past and present? Taking this as a model…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
玄事關乎治亂安危者必提其要表君子
小人之情狀如以鑑而别衆形𡚁周程張
朱之講明猶揭囊而收百物非擴前聖所
未發而爲後聖之法程者耶夫何一陳於
理宗端平之朝祗悅而不繹再見於吳澄
進講之日亦善而不行是致治之要道雖
不售於當時而心源之相契其將有待於
昭代者乎恭惟我
太祖高皇帝
===
睿智遠邁於百王
精義妙契乎千古
兢業恒存
幽獨之地凜天監之在玆
寅畏中切
燕閒之時惕朽索之是戒投戈講藝殫精
帝學因宋濂之請
命左右大書衍義揭之廡壁㪅
令濂條析衍義中司馬遷之論濂進曰人主能
punctuated:
玄，事關乎治亂安危者，必提其要，表君子小人之情狀，如以鑑而别衆形𡚁。周程張朱之講明，猶揭囊而收百物，非擴前聖所未發，而爲後聖之法程者耶？夫何一陳於理宗端平之朝，祗悅而不繹；再見於吳澄進講之日，亦善而不行？是致治之要道，雖不售於當時，而心源之相契，其將有待於昭代者乎？
恭惟我太祖高皇帝，睿智遠邁於百王，精義妙契乎千古。兢業恒存，幽獨之地，凜天監之在玆；寅畏中切，燕閒之時，惕朽索之是戒。投戈講藝，殫精帝學。因宋濂之請，命左右大書《衍義》，揭之廡壁；㪅令濂條析《衍義》中司馬遷之論。濂進曰：「人主能
translation_en:
…the profound [?]. In matters bearing upon order and disorder, security and peril, it invariably brings out the essentials and reveals the dispositions and conduct of noble men and petty men, like a mirror distinguishing the many forms before it [?]. It gathers the elucidations of Zhou, Cheng, Zhang, and Zhu as though opening a sack to collect a hundred things. Does it not expand upon what earlier sages had left unexpressed and provide a standard for later sages? Why, then, when it was first presented at Emperor Lizong’s court during the Duanping era, did he merely delight in it without exploring its meaning; and when it appeared again in Wu Cheng’s court lectures, was it likewise approved but not put into practice? Although this essential Way of achieving good government found no acceptance in its own time, might its accord with the very source of the mind have awaited our illustrious dynasty?
We reverently reflect that our Emperor Taizu Gao possessed sagacious wisdom far surpassing the hundred kings, and a wondrous understanding of the finest moral principles across the ages. Ever vigilant and conscientious, even in secluded places where he was alone, he stood in awe of Heaven’s watchful presence. Reverent fear pressed deeply within him; even in moments of leisure, he remained alert to the warning conveyed by a rotten rope. Laying aside his spear, he discoursed on the arts of learning, devoting his utmost attention to the learning proper to an emperor. At Song Lian’s request, he ordered his attendants to write out the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning (Daxue yanyi) in large characters and display it on the walls of the side galleries. He further ordered Lian to analyze, point by point, the discussion of Sima Qian in that work. Lian submitted: “If the ruler can…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
以義理養性則非僻不能侵興學校教民
則外侮無從作
聖祖因謂濂曰朕之爲君上畏
天地下畏兆民兢兢業業不敢自逸又嘗觀衍
義鼂錯之語德秀解之曰人君不窮兵黷
武則能生之而不傷
聖祖顧謂侍臣曰鼂錯之言其所該甚廣眞氏
之言其所見甚切朕嘗思爲君恤民所重者
兵與刑爾濫刑者陷人於無辜黷武者置人
於危地有國者所宜深戒也由前則心正身
===
脩而敬畏尤
愼獨審幾之本也其誠意之實功乎由後則
物格知至而兵刑尤畏
天畏民之要也其治平之絜矩乎是至精之涵
於心者
聖學淵源有取於盤銘之日新至粹之渙於文
者
天葩炳燿深合乎豆觴之敬勝罔駕湯武而並
punctuated: 以義理養性，則非僻不能侵；興學校教民，則外侮無從作。」聖祖因謂濂曰：「朕之爲君，上畏天地，下畏兆民，兢兢業業，不敢自逸。」又嘗觀衍義鼂錯之語，德秀解之曰：「人君不窮兵黷武，則能生之而不傷。」聖祖顧謂侍臣曰：「鼂錯之言，其所該甚廣；眞氏之言，其所見甚切。朕嘗思爲君恤民，所重者兵與刑爾。濫刑者陷人於無辜，黷武者置人於危地，有國者所宜深戒也。」由前則心正身脩，而敬畏尤愼獨審幾之本也，其誠意之實功乎！由後則物格知至，而兵刑尤畏天畏民之要也，其治平之絜矩乎！是至精之涵於心者，聖學淵源有取於盤銘之日新；至粹之渙於文者，天葩炳燿，深合乎豆觴之敬勝。罔駕湯武而並
translation_en:
…if one nurtures one’s nature through moral principles, perversity and depravity cannot intrude; if one establishes schools to educate the people, foreign aggression has no opening to arise.” The Sagely Ancestor then said to Song Lian: “As ruler, above I stand in awe of Heaven and Earth; below I stand in awe of the countless people. Ever vigilant and conscientious, I dare not indulge in ease.” He also once read Chao Cuo’s words in the Extended Meaning of the Great Learning (Daxue yanyi), which Zhen Dexiu explained thus: “If a ruler does not exhaust his forces and recklessly wage war, he can sustain the people’s lives without harming them.” The Sagely Ancestor turned to his attendant officials and said: “Chao Cuo’s words are very broad in their scope; Master Zhen’s words are especially incisive in their insight. I have often reflected that, for a ruler who cares for the people, the crucial matters are warfare and punishment. Those who abuse punishments ensnare the innocent; those who recklessly wage war place people in peril. Those who rule a state should take this deeply to heart as a warning.”

From the former, the mind is rectified and the person cultivated; reverence and awe are especially the foundation for vigilance when alone and discernment of the first stirrings of action. Is this not the practical achievement of making one’s intentions sincere? From the latter, things are investigated and knowledge reaches its fullest extent; warfare and punishment are especially crucial to standing in awe of Heaven and the people. Is this not the principle of the measuring square applied to governing the state and bringing peace to the realm? Thus, in the utmost refinement held within his heart, the sources of his sagely learning drew upon the daily renewal enjoined by the basin inscription; in the utmost purity flowing forth in his writings, his heavenly blossoms shone brilliantly, profoundly according with the triumph of reverence expressed in the inscriptions on the ritual food vessel and drinking cup. [The wording concerning surpassing Tang and Wu is unclear: 罔駕, ?] and stand alongside …

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
爲先下作民之主上乃承乎
天致治貴有本本端化自平人君所學者其序
有後前正心誠其意志定必不遷吾志既能
定理道豈復頗身脩本心正家國治同然國
治乃昭明萬邦斯協焉於變帝堯典思齊文
王篇萬化脩身始朕念方拳拳於是親灑
宸翰
賜二三輔臣
今廣和之彙爲一帙而名曰
===
翊學詩自今觀之首言務學者卽顧諟之謂
也繼言定志者卽知止之謂也曰誠曰正
曰脩旨雖異矣而明德之功未始不同曰
家曰國曰萬邦名雖殊矣而新民之理未
嘗不一言天則嚴其心之所自出言民則
謹其心之所由施治期於於變非祖述帝
堯之峻德者耶詩誦乎思齊非儀刑文王
之敬止者耶
本源澄徹而探之極其至精
punctuated:
爲先，下作民之主，上乃承乎天。致治貴有本，本端化自平。人君所學者，其序有後前。正心誠其意，志定必不遷。吾志既能定，理道豈復頗？身脩本心正，家國治同然。國治乃昭明，萬邦斯協焉。於變帝堯典，思齊文王篇。萬化脩身始，朕念方拳拳。於是親灑宸翰，賜二三輔臣。今廣和之，彙爲一帙，而名曰《翊學詩》。
自今觀之，首言務學者，卽顧諟之謂也；繼言定志者，卽知止之謂也。曰誠，曰正，曰脩，旨雖異矣，而明德之功未始不同；曰家，曰國，曰萬邦，名雖殊矣，而新民之理未嘗不一。言天，則嚴其心之所自出；言民，則謹其心之所由施。治期於於變，非祖述帝堯之峻德者耶？詩誦乎思齊，非儀刑文王之敬止者耶？本源澄徹，而探之極其至精，
translation_en:
…comes first. Below, one acts as lord of the people; above, one receives Heaven’s charge. Bringing about good government requires a foundation; when the foundation is correct, transformation naturally brings peace. What a ruler learns has its proper sequence, earlier and later. Rectify the mind and make its intentions sincere: once resolve is settled, it will surely not shift. Once my resolve is settled, how could the way of governance again go astray? Cultivating oneself rests on rectifying the mind; ordering the family and governing the state follow the same principle. When the state is governed, illustrious virtue shines forth, and the myriad states are brought into harmony. ‘Ah, the transformation!’ appears in the Canon of Emperor Yao; ‘Si qi’ is the ode concerning King Wen. All transformation begins with cultivating oneself; my thoughts dwell earnestly upon this.
Thereupon His Majesty personally wielded the imperial brush and bestowed his calligraphy upon his senior ministers. Now poems written in response have been gathered more widely and assembled into one volume, entitled Poems to Aid Learning (Yixue shi).
Viewed now, its opening discussion of diligent learning means precisely keeping this luminous virtue constantly in view; its subsequent discussion of settling one’s resolve means precisely knowing where to rest. Sincerity, rectification, and cultivation differ in their particular purport, yet the work of manifesting luminous virtue is throughout the same. Family, state, and the myriad states differ in name, yet the principle of renewing the people is invariably one. Speaking of Heaven entails reverence for the source from which the mind proceeds; speaking of the people entails care in how the mind’s influence is exercised. In aspiring to the transformation celebrated in ‘Ah, the transformation!’, does he not follow and carry forward Emperor Yao’s lofty virtue? In reciting ‘Si qi’, does he not take as his model King Wen’s abiding reverence? The fundamental source is clear and limpid, and his exploration of it reaches its utmost subtlety …

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
真機動盪而發之極其至粹帝王之所授受
聖祖之所述作固會其全而無遺闡其妙而殆
盡矣則
皇上所以得道統之傳者又不於是而可見哉
由是
大典微言昭如日星
鴻恩滋澤同乎
天地遵道者丕變覩
聖者奕新親賢樂利之化著孝弟仁讓之風行
===
以是而言法
天則
天心合而裁成輔相範圍彌綸賛化育之不及
以是而言法
祖則
祖德孚而長養培植開廣流行增創造於維新
玄化
鴻庥淳曜充溢其始也法
天既則克配乎
punctuated:
真機動盪而發之極其至粹，帝王之所授受、聖祖之所述作，固會其全而無遺，闡其妙而殆盡矣。則皇上所以得道統之傳者，又不於是而可見哉？
由是，大典微言昭如日星，鴻恩滋澤同乎天地，遵道者丕變，覩聖者奕新，親賢樂利之化著，孝弟仁讓之風行。
以是而言法天，則天心合，而裁成輔相、範圍彌綸，賛化育之不及；以是而言法祖，則祖德孚，而長養培植、開廣流行，增創造於維新。玄化鴻庥，淳曜充溢。其始也法天，既則克配乎
translation_en:
…the authentic animating impulse stirs, and its expression reaches the utmost purity. What the sage emperors and kings transmitted and received, and what the sagely ancestor expounded and composed, indeed encompass the whole without omission and elucidate its subtleties almost completely. Is it not also evident from this how His Majesty has received the transmission of the Way?
Thus, the subtle words of the great canon shine as brightly as the sun and stars; the nourishing bounty of imperial grace equals that of Heaven and Earth. Those who follow the Way are profoundly transformed, and those who behold the sage are splendidly renewed. The transforming influence that leads people to cherish the worthy, rejoice in happiness, and enjoy its benefits becomes manifest; customs of filial devotion, brotherly respect, benevolence, and deference prevail.
Speaking on this basis of taking Heaven as a model, one accords with Heaven’s mind: ordering and assisting, encompassing and comprehensively coordinating, one supplements what remains unfulfilled in its transforming and nourishing work. Speaking on this basis of taking the ancestor as a model, one accords with the ancestor’s virtue: nurturing and cultivating, expanding and spreading, one augments his founding achievement through renewal. Mysterious transformation and abundant blessings, pure radiance, fill all things. At first, he took Heaven as his model; thereafter, he became worthy to stand as the counterpart of…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
天矣其始也法
祖既則有光乎
祖矣可見
聖祖之學舉其大而
皇上之學會其精信乎作述一道後先一揆者
與雖然周公頌文王之德而作清廟於頌
著孔子贊周監於二代郁郁乎文而願從
之臣子逢時之幸固如是也愚也生際
昌時涵泳
===
聖化鋪張揚厲之心雖激於中然聞簫韶者知
舜德之難名覩河洛者知禹功之莫及果
何以塞明問也惟執事進而教之
第二問
王家卿
同考試官教諭吳　批〔華以明時豫以作樂乃古人制作之精意竊乎天地者也子能集以理氣數而不蔓不〕
〔贅殆觀其深者耶〕
考試官教諭胡　批〔此策場中頗襲浮套應問〕
punctuated:
天矣。其始也法祖，既則有光乎祖矣。可見聖祖之學舉其大，而皇上之學會其精。信乎作述一道、後先一揆者與！雖然，周公頌文王之德而作《清廟》，於《頌》著；孔子贊周監於二代，郁郁乎文，而願從之。臣子逢時之幸，固如是也。愚也生際昌時，涵泳聖化，鋪張揚厲之心雖激於中，然聞《簫韶》者知舜德之難名，覩河洛者知禹功之莫及，果何以塞明問也？惟執事進而教之。
第二問
王家卿
同考試官教諭吳批〔華以明時，豫以作樂，乃古人制作之精意，竊乎天地者也。子能集以理氣數，而不蔓不〕〔贅，殆觀其深者耶？〕
考試官教諭胡批〔此策場中頗襲浮套應問〕
translation_en:
…Heaven. At the outset he took the ancestors as his models; thereafter he brought glory to them. We can thus see that the learning of the sagely ancestor grasped its broad essentials, while His Majesty’s learning comprehends its finest subtleties. Truly, founding and carrying forward follow one Way, and predecessor and successor conform to a single standard!
Yet the Duke of Zhou praised King Wen’s virtue by composing “The Pure Temple” (Qingmiao), preserved among the Hymns. Confucius praised Zhou for looking to the two preceding dynasties—“How splendid its culture!”—and wished to follow it. Such indeed is the good fortune of a subject who encounters a favorable age. Born in this flourishing time and steeped in the sage ruler’s transforming influence, I, in my ignorance, feel within me an ardent desire to expound and extol it. Yet those who hear the Shao music know how difficult it is to name Shun’s virtue, and those who behold the Yellow and Luo rivers know that Yu’s achievements cannot be equaled. How, then, can I adequately answer your discerning question? I ask only that you favor me with further instruction.
Second Policy Question
Wang Jiaqing
Associate Examiner Wu, Instructor, comments: 〔“Splendor makes the seasons manifest” [?], and “Enthusiasm gives rise to music”: these express the subtle intent of the ancients in establishing institutions, appropriating the workings of Heaven and Earth. You can bring these together through principle, vital force, and number, without rambling or〕〔redundancy. Surely you have perceived their depths?〕
Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: 〔In this policy-essay examination, candidates have frequently relied on empty stock formulas to answer the questions…〕

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
〔殊無心得之論知曆樂本原而文更藻潤者僅見此〕
〔作是用錄之〕
考試官學正史　批〔以律起曆以曆驗律此律曆合一之理場中知者絶少子能合而一之歸于自然可與語制作矣〕
明於天地自然之數與氣而後可以窺制
作之原察於天地自然之理而後可以達
制作之妙盈天地間氣與數而已而理實
主宰之得其數與氣而不得其理則所謂
===
數者不過推測占步之遺術而已爾所謂
氣者不過聲響節奏之繁音而已爾其何
以欽若乾象協和神人弼成雍熙泰和之
治哉知此則知治曆明時者固當知曆數
之運而曆之理尤所當明作樂崇德者固
當求聲氣之元而樂之理尤所當察矣執
事發策下詢承學之意或在于此且曆果
何始乎神農以前尚已黃帝考定星曆建
立五行起消息正閏餘于時撓成擅其術
punctuated:
〔殊無心得之論，知曆樂本原而文更藻潤者，僅見此〕〔作，是用錄之。〕
考試官學正史　批〔以律起曆，以曆驗律，此律曆合一之理。場中知者絶少，子能合而一之，歸于自然，可與語制作矣。〕
明於天地自然之數與氣，而後可以窺制作之原；察於天地自然之理，而後可以達制作之妙。盈天地間，氣與數而已，而理實主宰之。得其數與氣而不得其理，則所謂數者，不過推測占步之遺術而已爾；所謂氣者，不過聲響節奏之繁音而已爾。其何以欽若乾象、協和神人，弼成雍熙泰和之治哉？知此，則知治曆明時者，固當知曆數之運，而曆之理尤所當明；作樂崇德者，固當求聲氣之元，而樂之理尤所當察矣。執事發策下詢承學之意，或在于此。且曆果何始乎？神農以前尚已，黃帝考定星曆，建立五行，起消息，正閏餘，于時撓成擅其術
translation_en:
〔…there are hardly any discussions grounded in personal understanding. This is the only〕〔essay I have seen that understands the foundations of calendrical science and music and also displays polished, elegant writing; hence its inclusion.〕
Examiner Shi, Instructor, comments: 〔To derive the calendar from the pitch standards and to verify the pitch standards through the calendar: this is the principle that unites pitch standards and calendrical science. Very few in the examination hall understand it. You can bring the two into unity and ground them in the natural order; with you one may discuss the establishment of institutions.〕
Only after understanding the numbers and qi inherent in Heaven and Earth can one glimpse the source of the establishment of institutions; only after discerning the principles inherent in Heaven and Earth can one comprehend its subtleties. What fills the space between Heaven and Earth is simply qi and number, yet principle truly governs them. If one grasps their numbers and qi but fails to grasp their principles, then what is called number amounts merely to inherited techniques of calculation, prediction, and astronomical reckoning; and what is called qi amounts merely to a profusion of sounds and rhythms. How could these enable one reverently to follow the celestial patterns, bring spirits and human beings into harmony, and help achieve a flourishing government of concord and great peace? Understanding this, one knows that those who regulate the calendar and clarify the seasons must indeed understand the workings of calendrical numbers, but must above all illuminate the principles of the calendar. Those who create music to exalt virtue must indeed seek the source of sound and qi, but must above all discern the principles of music. Perhaps this is your intention, honored examiner, in setting this policy question and condescending to consult us students.
Where, then, did the calendar actually originate? Let us leave aside the time before Shennong. The Yellow Emperor investigated and established stellar and calendrical calculations, instituted the Five Phases, determined the waxing and waning, and corrected intercalations and residual fractions. At that time, Nao and Cheng [?] excelled in these techniques…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
羲和專其業神降嘉穀民物阜康天地之
數正也嗣是而後舜受堯禪首察璣衡是
即堯欽若昊天敬授民時意也唐虞之際
其慎重星曆也如此降自夏商率皆是重
至周則有馮相氏掌日月星辰之次辨其
敘事以會天位保章氏掌志五物之變動
以詔救政訪序事焉其所以步時序之常
占象緯之異本五行以敬五事而休徵咎
徵寓焉職任之重何如也秦不師古慢天
===
虐民而星曆之官遂廢乃緣鄒衍五德之
運而自爲水德以亥爲正以十爲紀怠棄
三正何其悖也漢興脩復古制改更正朔
曆凡五變張蒼用顓帝劉歆作三統李梵
造四分劉洪有乾象而唐都洛下閎鄧平
輩分部運筭術各不同惟司馬遷之太初
最稱精密志所謂日月如合璧五星如連
珠蓋有得于曆元也獨恨去古未遠而保
章馮相之職竟莫之復此馬遷所以有史
punctuated: 羲和專其業，神降嘉穀，民物阜康，天地之數正也。嗣是而後，舜受堯禪，首察璣衡，是即堯欽若昊天、敬授民時意也。唐虞之際，其慎重星曆也如此。降自夏商，率皆是重。至周，則有馮相氏掌日月星辰之次，辨其敘事，以會天位；保章氏掌志五物之變動，以詔救政，訪序事焉。其所以步時序之常，占象緯之異，本五行以敬五事，而休徵、咎徵寓焉。職任之重何如也！秦不師古，慢天虐民，而星曆之官遂廢，乃緣鄒衍五德之運而自爲水德，以亥爲正，以十爲紀，怠棄三正，何其悖也！漢興，脩復古制，改更正朔，曆凡五變：張蒼用顓帝，劉歆作三統，李梵造四分，劉洪有乾象，而唐都、洛下閎、鄧平輩分部運筭，術各不同。惟司馬遷之太初最稱精密，志所謂「日月如合璧，五星如連珠」，蓋有得于曆元也。獨恨去古未遠，而保章、馮相之職竟莫之復，此馬遷所以有史
translation_en:
…Xi and He devoted themselves to this work; the spirits sent down auspicious grain, and the people and other living things flourished in peace: the numerical order of Heaven and Earth was correctly established. Thereafter, when Shun received the throne through Yao’s abdication, his first concern was to examine the astronomical instruments. This embodied Yao’s intention of reverently following August Heaven and respectfully communicating the seasons to the people. Such was the care accorded to astronomy and calendrical calculation in the age of Tang and Yu. Under the Xia and Shang, these matters generally continued to receive such emphasis. In the Zhou, the Royal Astronomer was responsible for the positions of the sun, moon, and stars, distinguishing the sequence of their movements to correlate the celestial positions. The Royal Astrologer recorded changes in the five celestial bodies, thereby advising on remedial measures in government and investigating the ordering of affairs [?]. Through these duties they calculated the regular succession of seasons and divined the significance of anomalies in the celestial bodies. Taking the Five Phases as their basis, they attended reverently to the Five Conducts, in which auspicious and inauspicious signs were manifested. How weighty were these official responsibilities!

Qin did not take antiquity as its model: it slighted Heaven and oppressed the people, and the offices concerned with astronomy and calendrical calculation were consequently abolished. Instead, following Zou Yan’s cycle of the Five Virtues, it designated its own virtue as Water, made the month corresponding to hai the first month of the year, and took ten as its numerical standard [?]. How perverse it was to neglect and discard the Three Standards for the beginning of the year!

When the Han arose, it restored ancient institutions and changed the calendrical arrangements for the beginning of the year and the months. The calendar underwent five changes in all: Zhang Cang used the calendar of Emperor Zhuanxu; Liu Xin devised the Triple Concordance calendar; Li Fan [?] created the Quarter-Remainder calendar; and Liu Hong produced the Celestial Images calendar. Tang Du, Luoxia Hong, Deng Ping, and others divided the work of calculation among themselves, each employing different methods. Only Sima Qian’s Grand Inception calendar was acclaimed as exceptionally precise. As the treatise puts it, “The sun and moon were like paired jade discs; the five planets were like strung pearls.” Evidently, it had correctly determined the calendrical epoch. The sole regret is that, although antiquity was not yet far distant, no one ever restored the offices of Royal Astrologer and Royal Astronomer. This is why Sima Qian had the historian’s …

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
無一字不本諸古人已試之法如黃鍾徑
圍之數則漢斛之積分可考寸以九分爲
法則淮南太史小司馬之說可推五聲二
變之數半律半聲之例則杜氏通典具焉
變宮變徵之不得爲調則孔氏之禮疏可
見至于制作之精微又在于求聲氣之元
其言曰黃鍾者陽氣之動陽聲之始分寸
之數具于聲氣之元不可得而見及斷竹
爲管吹之而聲和候之而氣應而數始形
===
焉是爲律本十一律由之而損益似有得
于天地之氣之外者此新書所以爲至而
朱子有取之也何近世儒者乃有倡爲舍
少之說詆訾漢儒以爲誤用蕤賓之管其
言曰黃鍾非九寸之管而引通鑑外紀呂
氏春秋所載含少之說以爲證不知黃鍾
以八十一分之積吹三十九分以爲聲故
謂之含少而非指三十九分爲黃鍾之律
也若執含少以爲清管則十一律何所稟
punctuated: 無一字不本諸古人已試之法。如黃鍾徑圍之數，則漢斛之積分可考；寸以九分爲法，則淮南、太史、小司馬之說可推；五聲二變之數、半律半聲之例，則杜氏《通典》具焉；變宮、變徵之不得爲調，則孔氏之《禮疏》可見。至于制作之精微，又在于求聲氣之元。其言曰：「黃鍾者，陽氣之動，陽聲之始。分寸之數具于聲氣之元，不可得而見。及斷竹爲管，吹之而聲和，候之而氣應，而數始形焉。是爲律本，十一律由之而損益。」似有得于天地之氣之外者，此新書所以爲至，而朱子有取之也。何近世儒者乃有倡爲舍少之說，詆訾漢儒，以爲誤用蕤賓之管？其言曰：「黃鍾非九寸之管。」而引《通鑑外紀》《呂氏春秋》所載含少之說以爲證。不知黃鍾以八十一分之積，吹三十九分以爲聲，故謂之含少，而非指三十九分爲黃鍾之律也。若執含少以爲清管，則十一律何所稟
translation_en: …not a single word fails to rest upon methods already tested by the ancients. For example, the figures for the diameter and circumference of the Huangzhong pitch pipe can be checked against the cubic measure of the Han hu capacity standard. The rule that one cun comprises nine fen can be inferred from the accounts of Huainan, the Grand Scribe, and Junior Sima. The numerical relations of the five tones and two altered tones, and the precedents for half-length pitch pipes and their corresponding tones, are fully set out in Du’s Comprehensive Institutions (Tongdian). That the altered gong and altered zhi tones cannot serve as the basis of modes can be seen in Kong’s Commentary on the Rites. As for the subtleties of construction, these depend further upon seeking the source of sound and qi. The work says: “Huangzhong is the stirring of yang qi and the beginning of yang sound. The numerical measures in fen and cun are inherent in the source of sound and qi, but cannot be seen. Only when bamboo is cut into a pipe, blowing it produces a harmonious sound, and observing it reveals a response of qi, do the numbers first take visible form. This is the foundation of the pitch standards; the other eleven are derived from it by diminution and augmentation.” It seems to apprehend something beyond the qi of Heaven and Earth. This is why the New Book is considered consummate, and why Master Zhu approved of it. Why, then, have recent Confucian scholars advocated the theory of “discarding the lesser” (she shao) [?], disparaging Han scholars for supposedly having mistakenly used the Ruibin pipe? They say: “Huangzhong is not a pipe nine cun long.” As evidence, they cite the theory of “containing the lesser” (han shao) recorded in the Supplementary Account to the Comprehensive Mirror (Tongjian waiji) and Master Lü’s Spring and Autumn Annals (Lüshi chunqiu). They do not understand that Huangzhong has an accumulated measure of eighty-one fen and produces its sound by blowing thirty-nine fen [?]. It is therefore called “containing the lesser”; this does not mean that thirty-nine fen constitutes the Huangzhong pitch standard. If one insists on taking “containing the lesser” to mean a high-register pipe, then from what would the eleven other pitch standards derive…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
正是其好爲立異而未詳律呂本原徒資
談說而不可施之實用也抑曆者測候之
書其重存乎數律者作樂之具其重存乎
聲初若不相關涉者然究極其理則元氣
必發爲元聲而元數必本乎元運是以史
遷作記言律必兼曆而後世宗之朱子亦
謂治曆家用律呂候氣蓋此氣都由地中
透出如十一月冬至緹室布管距地飛葭
若非元氣之至其何以得元聲之數哉此
===
理也數也氣也三者渾融無間而制曆者
必先于協律作樂者必先于推曆二者交
相爲用者也我
國家
大統曆承用勝國之舊即許衡郭守敬所訂定
而
大祀樂章皆
皇祖所親製宴饗九奏贊以陶凱
皇祖謂其有和平廣大之意一切流俗諠澆淫
punctuated:
正。是其好爲立異而未詳律呂本原，徒資談說而不可施之實用也。抑曆者，測候之書，其重存乎數；律者，作樂之具，其重存乎聲。初若不相關涉者，然究極其理，則元氣必發爲元聲，而元數必本乎元運。是以史遷作記，言律必兼曆，而後世宗之。朱子亦謂治曆家用律呂候氣，蓋此氣都由地中透出。如十一月冬至，緹室布管，距地飛葭，若非元氣之至，其何以得元聲之數哉？此理也、數也、氣也，三者渾融無間，而制曆者必先于協律，作樂者必先于推曆，二者交相爲用者也。
我國家《大統曆》承用勝國之舊，即許衡、郭守敬所訂定。而大祀樂章皆皇祖所親製，宴饗九奏贊以陶凱。皇祖謂其有和平廣大之意，一切流俗諠澆淫
translation_en:
…their standard. This shows their fondness for advancing divergent views without having thoroughly understood the origins of the pitch standards: their claims merely furnish material for discussion and cannot be put to practical use. Now, a calendar is a book for measurement and observation, whose chief concern lies in numbers; pitch standards are instruments for making music, whose chief concern lies in sound. At first they seem unrelated. Yet, when their principles are investigated to the utmost, primordial qi must issue as primordial sound, and primordial numbers must be grounded in primordial cycles. Thus, when the historian Sima Qian composed his Records of the Historian, his discussion of pitch standards necessarily included calendrical science, and later generations followed his example. Master Zhu also said that calendrical specialists used pitch pipes to observe qi, for this qi emerges entirely from within the earth. For example, at the winter solstice in the eleventh month, pipes are arranged in a chamber lined with red silk, set at a distance from the ground [?], and reed ashes fly up. If primordial qi had not arrived, how could the numerical values of primordial sound be obtained? Principle, number, and qi: these three are completely integrated, with no separation between them. Those who construct calendars must therefore begin by harmonizing the pitch standards, while those who make music must begin with calendrical computation. The two serve each other reciprocally.
Our dynasty’s Grand Concordance Calendar (Datong li) continues the system of the preceding dynasty, namely that established by Xu Heng and Guo Shoujing. The musical texts for the great sacrifices were all personally composed by our imperial ancestor, while Tao Kai assisted with the nine musical performances for court banquets. Our imperial ancestor said that they conveyed a spirit of peace, harmony, breadth, and grandeur. All that was vulgar, clamorous, frivolous, and licentious …

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
家之樂悉屏去之二百年來遵行已久而
海宇乂安民物和同
列聖相承丕歷泰運肆我
皇上中和
建極
敬一承天三辰順序而不忒六樂和同而盡善
和氣致祥而天不愛道順氣感人而物無
札厲
欽天有監而星官專其業
===
神樂有觀而春卿掌其事制度一定萬世仰成
以締
宗社之福以享
亨嘉之會執事謂欲開局求人毋乃過慮乎
愚生管窺蠡測之見獻芹炙背之忱惟願
聖天子和德于上賢公卿和職于朝萬物咸和
于野則聲和氣和形和而
天地之泰和應億萬載無疆之休實在乎此矣
愚也何幸躬逢其盛
punctuated:
家之樂，悉屏去之。二百年來，遵行已久，而海宇乂安，民物和同。列聖相承，丕歷泰運。肆我皇上中和建極，敬一承天，三辰順序而不忒，六樂和同而盡善。和氣致祥，而天不愛道；順氣感人，而物無札厲。欽天有監，而星官專其業；神樂有觀，而春卿掌其事。制度一定，萬世仰成，以締宗社之福，以享亨嘉之會。執事謂欲開局求人，毋乃過慮乎？

愚生管窺蠡測之見，獻芹炙背之忱，惟願聖天子和德于上，賢公卿和職于朝，萬物咸和于野，則聲和、氣和、形和，而天地之泰和應。億萬載無疆之休，實在乎此矣。愚也何幸，躬逢其盛！
translation_en:
…such music [?] was entirely banished. For two hundred years these prescriptions have long been observed, and the realm has enjoyed peace and good order, its people and all living things dwelling in harmony. Successive sage sovereigns have inherited the throne and presided over an age of great peace. Now our Emperor establishes the supreme standard through equilibrium and harmony, and reverently serves Heaven with singleness of purpose. The sun, moon, and stars follow their proper courses without deviation; the Six Music Traditions are harmonious and perfectly good. Harmonious vital forces bring auspicious signs, and Heaven does not withhold its Way [?]; concordant vital forces move people, and living things suffer no pestilence. For observing Heaven there is the Directorate of Astronomy, whose astronomical officials devote themselves to their specialty; for divine music there is the Abbey of Divine Music, whose affairs the Minister of Rites oversees. Once these institutions and regulations are fixed, ten thousand generations may rely upon their accomplishments, securing blessings for the ancestral temples and altars of state and enjoying a convergence of prosperity and excellence. When you, honored sir, propose establishing a bureau and seeking qualified men, might this not be excessive concern?

The views of this humble student are as limited as looking through a tube or measuring with a ladle; my sincerity is that of one who offers celery or recommends warming one’s back in the sun. I wish only that the sage Son of Heaven harmonize his virtue above, that worthy dukes and ministers harmonize their duties at court, and that all things throughout the land dwell in harmony. Then sounds, vital forces, and forms will be harmonious, and the great harmony of Heaven and Earth will respond. The boundless blessings of countless ages truly depend upon this. How fortunate I am, in my ignorance, to witness this flourishing age in person!

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
第三問
許份
同考試官學正袁　批〔策士以人物一觀考古之學一祭許生智中銖兩非漫然博喿而策雖之也子〕
〔能考核詳盡品藻明當非尚友有素者能之乎〕
考試官教諭胡　批〔敘斷鄉先哲抑揚有體錄之〕
考試官學正史　批〔評苓精當人物策無踰此作〕
君子之所以自立而流聲實于無窮者有
本焉有末焉明于本末之義者可與論世
===
矣夫天下之道出于一原君子之學初無
二致本立而末隨之則其被天下傳後世
者莫非養盛自致而君子無心焉外此而
性資之暗合智力之圖成非不足以表見
于時而與君子之一貫者異矣是故道德
者士之上也合本與末而爲言者也德之
不足而功業焉次也文章焉又其次也觀
此則百代之士與一方之才胥以辨矣執
事以中土人才下詢承學愚也敢方人乎
punctuated:
第三問

許份

同考試官學正袁　批〔策士以人物一觀，考古之學一祭，許生智中銖兩，非漫然博喿而策雖之也子〕〔能考核詳盡，品藻明當，非尚友有素者能之乎？〕

考試官教諭胡　批〔敘斷鄉先哲，抑揚有體，錄之。〕

考試官學正史　批〔評苓精當，人物策無踰此作。〕

君子之所以自立而流聲實于無窮者，有本焉，有末焉。明于本末之義者，可與論世矣。夫天下之道出于一原，君子之學初無二致。本立而末隨之，則其被天下、傳後世者，莫非養盛自致，而君子無心焉。外此而性資之暗合、智力之圖成，非不足以表見于時，而與君子之一貫者異矣。是故道德者，士之上也，合本與末而爲言者也。德之不足而功業焉，次也；文章焉，又其次也。觀此，則百代之士與一方之才，胥以辨矣。執事以中土人才下詢承學，愚也敢方人乎
translation_en:
Third Policy Question

Xu Fen 許份

Associate Examiner Yuan, Instructor, comments: 〔Questioning candidates about historical figures provides a view of their learning concerning antiquity [?]. Candidate Xu weighs matters down to the smallest measures in his judgment [?], rather than merely displaying indiscriminate erudition in his policy essay [remainder garbled].〕〔His examination of the evidence is thorough, and his assessments are clear and appropriate. Could anyone accomplish this without long practice in befriending the worthy of the past?〕

Examiner Hu, Instructor, comments: 〔He recounts and judges the earlier worthies of his home region, with due proportion in praise and censure. Accept this essay.〕

Examiner Shi, Instructor, comments: 〔The assessments [?] are precise and appropriate. No policy essay on historical figures surpasses this work.〕

There are roots and branches to the means by which a gentleman establishes himself and perpetuates his reputation and substantive achievements without end. With someone who understands the significance of roots and branches, one may discuss the men of past ages. The Way throughout the world issues from a single source, and the gentleman’s learning has never had two divergent aims. Once the root is established, the branches follow. Thus, whatever extends throughout the world and is transmitted to later generations arises naturally from the fullness of his cultivation; the gentleman has no deliberate intention of securing such results. Apart from this, an unconscious conformity arising from natural disposition, or an accomplishment contrived through intelligence and effort, may indeed suffice to bring someone to prominence in his own time. Yet these differ from the single principle that runs through the gentleman’s life.

Thus, moral attainment ranks highest among scholars: it embraces both root and branches. Where virtue falls short, meritorious achievement comes next; literary accomplishment ranks next again. Viewed in this light, the scholars of a hundred generations and the talented men of any one region can all be distinguished. You, honored examiners, have condescended to ask us students about the talented men of the Central Lands. Could an ignorant person such as I presume to compare men…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
哉雖然居是鄉而不能道其鄉先正恥也
吾河南昔爲梁豫境嵩行盤峙河洛匯流
孕秀鍾賢不爲無自而況虞夏甫還敎隆
經正士咸自立而奮起者乎是故伊尹之
在商啓格帝之功于奕葉申甫之在周翊
中興之業于重光功業則盛矣而以功業
盡之可乎卜商告往知來大啓二毛之派
子貢多學能識竟聞一貫之傳文章則著
矣而以文章槩之可乎是皆聖賢之學豫
===
養者深愚之所謂本立而末隨之者也漢
而降人才未易縷數姑舉其著者言之張
良爲韓報讎而赤松之遊有得保身之哲
黃霸寬明有體而潁川之治允服士民之
心丰采凝峻聞者解綬李膺所以係登龍
之望也脩德清淨遺絹化盜陳寔所以有
文範之謚也謝安之舉謝玄不避親矣捷
傳淝水其鎮靜之效乎張方平之器三蘇
能知人矣不屈安石其凝定之操乎要說
punctuated:
哉！雖然，居是鄉而不能道其鄉先正，恥也。吾河南昔爲梁豫境，嵩行盤峙，河洛匯流，孕秀鍾賢，不爲無自。而況虞夏甫還，敎隆經正，士咸自立而奮起者乎？是故伊尹之在商，啓格帝之功于奕葉；申甫之在周，翊中興之業于重光。功業則盛矣，而以功業盡之可乎？卜商告往知來，大啓二毛之派；子貢多學能識，竟聞一貫之傳。文章則著矣，而以文章槩之可乎？是皆聖賢之學豫養者深，愚之所謂本立而末隨之者也。
漢而降，人才未易縷數，姑舉其著者言之。張良爲韓報讎，而赤松之遊，有得保身之哲；黃霸寬明有體，而潁川之治，允服士民之心。丰采凝峻，聞者解綬，李膺所以係登龍之望也；脩德清淨，遺絹化盜，陳寔所以有文範之謚也。謝安之舉謝玄，不避親矣；捷傳淝水，其鎮靜之效乎？張方平之器三蘇，能知人矣；不屈安石，其凝定之操乎？要說
translation_en:
…indeed! Nevertheless, to live in this province yet be unable to speak of its worthy predecessors is shameful. Our Henan formerly lay within the territories of Liang and Yu. The Song and Taihang mountains stand massed together, and the He and Luo rivers converge. That this land nurtures exceptional talent and brings forth worthy men is not without cause. How much more so when the ways of Yu and Xia had just returned [?], teaching flourished, the classics were correctly understood, and scholars all established themselves and rose to action!
Thus Yi Yin, serving the Shang, inaugurated achievements that reached the Supreme Lord and extended through successive generations; Shen and Fu, serving the Zhou, assisted the work of restoration as the dynasty shone anew. Their achievements were magnificent, but can achievements alone encompass them? Bu Shang, when told of what had gone before, understood what would follow, greatly opening the way for the lineage of the “two Mao” [?]. Zigong studied widely and could retain what he learned, and ultimately heard the teaching of the single thread running through all. Their literary accomplishments were distinguished, but can literary accomplishments alone sum them up? All these men had deeply nurtured themselves beforehand in the learning of sages and worthies. They exemplify what I humbly call establishing the root so that the branches follow.
From the Han onward, talented men cannot readily be enumerated one by one; let me mention only some of the most distinguished. Zhang Liang avenged the state of Han, yet in his intention to roam with Chisong he grasped the wisdom of preserving himself. Huang Ba was generous, discerning, and guided by sound principles; his administration of Yingchuan truly won the allegiance of scholars and commoners. Li Ying’s bearing was so grave and stern that men who heard of him untied their official seals: this was why men pinned on him their hopes of ‘ascending the dragon gate’ through his recognition. Chen Shi cultivated virtue and remained pure and tranquil; by giving silk to a thief, he reformed him. This was why he received the posthumous title Wenfan, ‘Model of Cultured Virtue.’ When Xie An recommended Xie Xuan, he did not avoid appointing a relative. Was the victory reported from the Fei River not the effect of his composure? Zhang Fangping recognized the capacities of the three Su: he truly knew how to judge men. Was his refusal to yield to Wang Anshi not evidence of his steadfast integrity? As for setting out the essentials …

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
十事而應變不窮則姚元之之捄時有賴
身經百戰而東京幾復則岳武穆之報國
略酬錢若水善決疑獄四十致仕殆二疏
之儔乎韓魏公擁英立神聲色不動貞社
稷之臣乎富弼再使彊虜和議以成人以
富文並稱當矣鄧禹杖策軍門大計遂定
卒爲東京元功宜矣忠義如巡遠則雖以
睢陽之小克保江淮德量如叔度則雖以
林宗之賢推爲顏子茲數子者功業雖有
顯晦均之有裨于當時者也賈山陳言于
文帝借秦爲喻有憂時致主之忠丁寬受
學于田何載易而東啓施孟梁丘之學治
安一書試無不驗賈誼所以爲通國體也
隷書六經人爭傳習蔡邕所以爲時儒宗
也漢政方移曹氏而荀悅作申鑒奏之寓
憫時之意焉張說許謚元忠而吳兢于唐
史書之有董狐之筆焉陳摶隱臥于華山
乃有指玄之作得于沉潛者久矣韓愈抒
punctuated: 十事而應變不窮，則姚元之之捄時有賴；身經百戰而東京幾復，則岳武穆之報國略酬。錢若水善決疑獄，四十致仕，殆二疏之儔乎？韓魏公擁英立神，聲色不動，貞社稷之臣乎？富弼再使彊虜，和議以成，人以富文並稱，當矣。鄧禹杖策軍門，大計遂定，卒爲東京元功，宜矣。忠義如巡遠，則雖以睢陽之小，克保江淮；德量如叔度，則雖以林宗之賢，推爲顏子。茲數子者，功業雖有顯晦，均之有裨于當時者也。賈山陳言于文帝，借秦爲喻，有憂時致主之忠；丁寬受學于田何，載易而東，啓施孟梁丘之學。《治安》一書，試無不驗，賈誼所以爲通國體也；隷書六經，人爭傳習，蔡邕所以爲時儒宗也。漢政方移曹氏，而荀悅作《申鑒》奏之，寓憫時之意焉；張說許謚元忠，而吳兢于唐史書之，有董狐之筆焉。陳摶隱臥于華山，乃有《指玄》之作，得于沉潛者久矣；韓愈抒
translation_en:
…ten proposals, responding inexhaustibly to changing circumstances: thus Yao Yuanzhi’s efforts to rescue his age provided something upon which to rely. Having fought a hundred battles and nearly recovered the Eastern Capital, Yue Wumu had partly fulfilled his wish to repay his country. Qian Ruoshui excelled at deciding doubtful criminal cases and retired at forty: was he perhaps a peer of the two Shu? Duke Han of Wei supported Yingzong and enthroned Shenzong, without any change in voice or countenance: was he not a steadfast servant of the state? Fu Bi twice went as envoy to the powerful northern enemy and successfully concluded peace negotiations. People were right to speak of Fu and Wen together. Deng Yu came, staff in hand, to the army’s gates, whereupon the grand strategy was settled. It was fitting that he ultimately became a leading founding contributor to the Eastern Han.

With loyalty and righteousness such as those of Zhang Xun and Xu Yuan, even a place as small as Suiyang could safeguard the Jiang and Huai regions. With virtue and magnanimity such as those of Huang Shudu, even someone as worthy as Guo Linzong acclaimed him as another Master Yan. Although these men’s achievements varied in prominence, all benefited their times.

Jia Shan presented his views to Emperor Wen, using Qin as an admonitory example; his loyalty lay in concern for his age and in seeking to guide his ruler to good government. Ding Kuan studied under Tian He and carried the Changes eastward, opening the way for the traditions of Shi, Meng, and Liangqiu. Every proposal in the work On Good Government and Security proved sound when tested: this was why Jia Yi was considered to understand the principles of governing a state. People competed to copy and study the Six Classics written in clerical script: this was why Cai Yong became the leading Confucian scholar of his age.

Just as Han’s governing power was passing to the Cao family, Xun Yue composed and submitted the Extended Reflections, conveying his sorrow over the times. Wu Jing recorded in his history of the Tang the affair involving Zhang Yue and Yuanzhong [?], displaying the historical integrity of Dong Hu’s brush. Chen Tuan lived in secluded repose on Mount Hua and produced Pointing to the Mystery: long had he gained understanding through profound contemplation. Han Yu gave expression…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
文于三變遂起八代之衰助于聖經者多
矣韋應物之詩一藝之工也而高潔之趣
故近風雅之餘音張衡之賦十年之思也
而曆筭之精似得璣衡之遺意宋庠之兄
弟聯舉榮矣而建白著述均之不媿科名
應劭之著風俗通末矣而物類名號亦足
以資多識玆數子者文章雖有高下均之
有助于道藝者也夫惟數子者徒以其性
資之合乎道才力之偶于時而于聖賢之
===
學本之閒也故智如子房而淪鴻溝之約
正如太丘而從宦者之喪濮議之非魏公
猶見違于君實仲約之議鄭公猶重忤于
希文四子且然餘可知矣此其功業果皆
殷周之功業乎賈太傅之志乃發憤于長
沙蔡中郎之賢至失身于董卓學遺格致
昌黎原道之踈也請誅仲淹雍丘謀國之
陋也四子且然餘可知矣此其文章果皆
聖門之文章乎道德之儒合本末而一之
punctuated:
文于三變，遂起八代之衰，助于聖經者多矣。韋應物之詩，一藝之工也，而高潔之趣，故近風雅之餘音。張衡之賦，十年之思也，而曆筭之精，似得璣衡之遺意。宋庠之兄弟聯舉，榮矣，而建白著述，均之不媿科名。應劭之著《風俗通》，末矣，而物類名號，亦足以資多識。玆數子者，文章雖有高下，均之有助于道藝者也。
夫惟數子者，徒以其性資之合乎道、才力之偶于時，而于聖賢之學，本之閒也。故智如子房，而淪鴻溝之約；正如太丘，而從宦者之喪。濮議之非，魏公猶見違于君實；仲約之議，鄭公猶重忤于希文。四子且然，餘可知矣。此其功業，果皆殷周之功業乎？賈太傅之志，乃發憤于長沙；蔡中郎之賢，至失身于董卓。學遺格致，昌黎《原道》之踈也；請誅仲淹，雍丘謀國之陋也。四子且然，餘可知矣。此其文章，果皆聖門之文章乎？道德之儒，合本末而一之
translation_en:
…his writing through three transformations, and thus reversed the decline of eight dynasties, contributing greatly to the elucidation of the sacred classics. Wei Yingwu’s poetry was mastery of a single art, yet its lofty and pure sensibility approached the lingering strains of the Airs and Odes. Zhang Heng’s rhapsodies embodied ten years of reflection, while his mastery of calendrical calculation seemed to capture the surviving intent of the celestial measuring instruments described in antiquity. Song Xiang and his brother won examination distinction together—a great honor—and their proposals to the throne and their writings alike did credit to their examination reputations. Ying Shao’s Comprehensive Account of Customs (Fengsu tong) concerned lesser matters, yet its treatment of categories of things and their names could also broaden knowledge. Though these men’s literary accomplishments varied in quality, all contributed to the Way and the arts of learning.
Yet these men relied merely on natural dispositions that accorded with the Way and talents that happened to suit their times; their grounding in the learning of the sages and worthies was deficient [?]. Thus even someone as wise as Zifang became implicated in the covenant at Honggou [?], and someone as upright as the magistrate of Taiqiu attended a eunuch’s funeral. Over the errors of the Pu succession controversy, even the Duke of Wei encountered opposition from Junshi; in the deliberations concerning Zhongyue, even the Duke of Zheng gravely crossed Xiwen. If even these four were like this, one can infer how the others fared. Were their achievements, then, truly all comparable to those of the Yin and Zhou dynasties? Grand Mentor Jia, for all his aspirations, gave vent to his indignation in Changsha; Court Gentleman Cai, for all his worthiness, went so far as to compromise himself by serving Dong Zhuo. Omitting the investigation of things and the extension of knowledge from learning was the deficiency of Changli’s Inquiry into the Way (Yuan dao); requesting Zhongyan’s execution was the narrowness of Yongqiu’s counsel on affairs of state. If even these four were like this, one can infer how the others fared. Were their writings, then, truly all writings of the Confucian school? The scholar of the Way and virtue joins root and branches into one…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
陽技巧四種後世皆不復存宋元豐中以
孫子吳子司馬法李衛公問對尉繚子三
略六韜號稱七書至今襲用焉由觀其義
類多眞贋相半而得失因之去非存是以
取其長固武之善經也然古之善用兵以
制敵者率不外於是矣以今考之三晉之
兵以齊號爲怯也孫臏因勢利導日減竈
以見弱焉卒之火舉弩發遂斃魏將此審
於料敵者也若虞詡之羌遮崤谷增竈兼
===
行以疑虜追逼不得不示强矣詡固善法
臏也孫子曰勇怯勢也强弱形也其以是
夫濰水之陣以信爲易與也韓信囊沙壅
流還走以誘之焉因之決壅半渡急擊殺
且此巧於覆人者也若檀道濟之轉戰濟
上唱籌量沙以降者告竭非是故不免矣
道濟固善自全也吳子曰涉水半渡可擊
善戰者以形其以是夫百里而趨利者蹶
上將此軍志也龐涓固以輿輕銳倍進而
punctuated: 陽、技巧四種，後世皆不復存。宋元豐中，以《孫子》《吳子》《司馬法》《李衛公問對》《尉繚子》《三略》《六韜》號稱七書，至今襲用焉。由觀其義，類多眞贋相半，而得失因之。去非存是，以取其長，固武之善經也。然古之善用兵以制敵者，率不外於是矣。以今考之，三晉之兵以齊號爲怯也，孫臏因勢利導，日減竈以見弱焉。卒之火舉弩發，遂斃魏將，此審於料敵者也。若虞詡之羌遮崤谷，增竈兼行以疑虜，追逼不得不示强矣。詡固善法臏也。《孫子》曰：「勇怯，勢也；强弱，形也。」其以是夫！濰水之陣，以信爲易與也，韓信囊沙壅流，還走以誘之焉。因之決壅，半渡急擊，殺且，此巧於覆人者也。若檀道濟之轉戰濟上，唱籌量沙，以降者告竭，非是故不免矣。道濟固善自全也。《吳子》曰：「涉水半渡可擊。」善戰者以形，其以是夫！「百里而趨利者蹶上將」，此《軍志》也。龐涓固以輿輕銳倍進而
translation_en:
…yang and technical skills, four categories in all, none of which survived into later ages. During the Yuanfeng era of the Song, the Sunzi (Master Sun), Wuzi (Master Wu), Methods of the Minister of War (Sima fa), Questions and Answers of Duke Li of Wei, Weiliaozi (Master Wei Liao), Three Strategies, and Six Secret Teachings were collectively designated the Seven Military Classics. They have continued in use down to the present. Examining their meaning [?], one finds that authentic and spurious material generally occur in equal measure, with corresponding merits and shortcomings. To discard what is wrong, preserve what is right, and draw upon their strengths is assuredly a sound guiding principle for military affairs. Indeed, the methods of those in antiquity who excelled at employing troops to overcome their enemies generally did not fall outside these teachings.

Considering the matter now, among the troops of the Three Jin, those of Qi had a reputation for cowardice. Sun Bin turned this disposition to his advantage, reducing the number of cooking hearths each day to display weakness. Finally, when the fire was raised and the crossbows discharged, he brought about the death of the Wei commander. This was a case of discerning judgment in assessing the enemy. As for Yu Xu, when the Qiang blocked him at Xiao Valley [?], he increased his cooking hearths and marched double stages to bewilder the enemy. Under close pursuit, he had no choice but to display strength. Xu was indeed skilled at applying Bin’s methods. The Sunzi says: “Courage and cowardice depend on the configuration of circumstances; strength and weakness depend on dispositions.” Surely this is what it means!

At the battle of the Wei River, Han Xin was regarded as an easy opponent. He dammed the current with bags of sand and then turned and fled to lure the enemy onward. Taking advantage of this, he breached the dam and struck swiftly when the enemy was halfway across, killing [Long] Ju. This was skill in overthrowing an opponent. As for Tan Daoji, who fought successive engagements in the region of the Ji River, he called out tallies while measuring sand. Since a deserter had reported that his supplies were exhausted, without this stratagem he would not have escaped. Daoji was indeed skilled at preserving his own forces. The Wuzi says: “When crossing water, troops may be attacked halfway across.” Those skilled in warfare employ dispositions [?]; surely this is what it means!

“To race a hundred li for an advantage brings down the chief commander”: this is from the Military Records. Pang Juan indeed advanced at double speed with his light, picked troops [?], and…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
後可曰泰山覆於前而色不變麋鹿興於
左而目不瞬然後可以制利害可以持敵
不然敵未交而心已怵矣雖有利害其孰
知之然則欲成天下之將材者亦於治心
養氣中求之乎此非老生之常談也
廟堂之上宜留神焉
第五問
陳加命
同考試官教諭吳　批〔條列弭盜之方援古酌今〕
===
曲盡籌畫蓋抱經世之蘊者與
同考試官教諭何　批〔採本銷萌其說良是非識〕
時務者不能道此
考試官教諭胡　批〔詳明切當鑿鑿可行〕
考試官學正史　批〔文古而慮周策之佳者〕
治盜之法必探其本而後可與慮始必銷
其萌而後可與圖成夫盜之所由生也有
本焉昧者爲之則標末是務譬之揚湯以
止沸夫是之謂悖盜之所由盛也有萌焉
punctuated:
後可曰：「泰山覆於前而色不變，麋鹿興於左而目不瞬。」然後可以制利害，可以持敵。不然，敵未交而心已怵矣，雖有利害，其孰知之？然則欲成天下之將材者，亦於治心養氣中求之乎？此非老生之常談也，廟堂之上宜留神焉。

第五問
陳加命

同考試官教諭吳　批〔條列弭盜之方，援古酌今〕，曲盡籌畫，蓋抱經世之蘊者與！
同考試官教諭何　批〔採本銷萌，其說良是，非識〕時務者不能道此。
考試官教諭胡　批〔詳明切當，鑿鑿可行。〕
考試官學正史　批〔文古而慮周，策之佳者。〕

治盜之法，必探其本而後可與慮始，必銷其萌而後可與圖成。夫盜之所由生也，有本焉。昧者爲之，則標末是務，譬之揚湯以止沸，夫是之謂悖。盜之所由盛也，有萌焉。
translation_en:
…only then may it be said: “Though Mount Tai collapse before him, his expression does not change; though deer spring up at his left, his eyes do not blink.” Only then can he control advantage and disadvantage and hold his own against the enemy. Otherwise, before the enemy has even engaged him, his heart is already seized with fear. Though advantages and dangers present themselves, how could he recognize them? Should those who wish to develop military commanders for the realm therefore seek them through the cultivation of the mind and the nurturing of vital energy? This is no mere commonplace of old scholars. Those at court should give it their attention.

Fifth Policy Question
Chen Jiaming

Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Wu: “He sets out methods for suppressing banditry point by point, drawing on antiquity and weighing present circumstances. His planning encompasses every detail. Surely he possesses a deep store of knowledge for ordering the world!”

Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor He: “Addressing the root [?] and extinguishing the first stirrings: his argument is indeed sound. No one without an understanding of current affairs could say this.”

Comment by Examiner and Instructor Hu: “Detailed, clear, pertinent, and sound; every proposal is practicable.”

Comment by Examiner and Instructor Shi: “The writing has an antique quality, and the thinking is comprehensive. An excellent policy essay.”

In dealing with banditry, one must investigate its roots before one can discuss how to begin, and extinguish its first stirrings before one can plan for success. For the emergence of banditry has its roots. Those who act without understanding concern themselves only with superficial symptoms. This is like lifting hot water out of a pot to stop it boiling: such conduct is contrary to reason. The growth of banditry likewise has its first stirrings…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
國不興政民得寡過焉猶懼其流而莫之
防也而士師掌士之八成聯民之什伍以
比追胥之事於是有司厲氏以辨盜物有
野廬氏以聚㰐賓客達道路有司寤氏以
詔夜禁有脩閭氏以禁徑踰馳騁國中者
其所以防民之慝者至備也雖有凶獷之
衆詐計亦銷沮矣况其時中原之地田以
井授疆理其畝而川涂溝澮止水浚坊民
之經徃循途旅進莫有鷔心後世阡陌旣
===
廢民失常業兼并恣睢征斂無藝乃教化
陵夷風俗頽敗而所在四馳無爲限隔旣
損德心又長跂扈卽水旱歲仍盜賊繁興
矣此大較也今欲令盜不興發莫若脩其
本周人之教固難幾企也而九職任民可
容失所乎欲令盜不延蔓莫若折其萌周
人之政迹亦今事也而備舉不𫏐豈不在
人乎是故其未形也探其本而制之則理
道豫得民莫與爲姦也其始形也銷其萌
punctuated:
國不興政，民得寡過焉，猶懼其流而莫之防也。而士師掌士之八成，聯民之什伍，以比追胥之事。於是有司厲氏以辨盜物，有野廬氏以聚㰐賓客、達道路，有司寤氏以詔夜禁，有脩閭氏以禁徑踰馳騁國中者。其所以防民之慝者至備也，雖有凶獷之衆，詐計亦銷沮矣。况其時中原之地，田以井授，疆理其畝，而川涂溝澮，止水浚坊，民之經徃循途旅進，莫有鷔心。後世阡陌旣廢，民失常業，兼并恣睢，征斂無藝，乃教化陵夷，風俗頽敗，而所在四馳，無爲限隔。旣損德心，又長跂扈，卽水旱歲仍，盜賊繁興矣。此大較也。

今欲令盜不興發，莫若脩其本。周人之教固難幾企也，而九職任民，可容失所乎？欲令盜不延蔓，莫若折其萌。周人之政迹亦今事也，而備舉不𫏐，豈不在人乎？是故其未形也，探其本而制之，則理道豫得，民莫與爲姦也；其始形也，銷其萌
translation_en:
…the state did not resort to punitive measures, and the people were able to commit few transgressions. Yet there remained a fear that their misconduct might spread unchecked. The Director of Justice administered the eight established judicial procedures and organized the people into groups of ten and five to coordinate the pursuit and apprehension of offenders. There were thus the Sili officials to distinguish stolen goods; the Yelu officials to assemble and inspect guests [?] and keep the roads open; the Siwu officials to proclaim nighttime prohibitions; and the Xiulü officials to prohibit those who took shortcuts, climbed over barriers, or raced about within the capital. Their means of preventing wrongdoing among the people were exceedingly thorough. Even among violent and unruly groups, fraudulent schemes would be frustrated and dispelled. Moreover, in those days, land in the Central Plains was allotted according to the well-field system, with field boundaries laid out; waterways, roads, ditches, and channels were arranged, waters contained, and embankments maintained [?]. In their movements, the people followed the roads and proceeded in groups, none harboring unruly intentions [?]. In later ages, once the field boundaries had been abolished, the people lost their settled livelihoods. Those engrossing land acted without restraint, and taxation knew no bounds. Moral instruction consequently declined and customs deteriorated. Everywhere people rushed about in all directions, with nothing to restrict or separate them. Their moral dispositions were impaired, while their arrogance and insubordination grew [?]. When floods and droughts then recurred year after year, banditry proliferated. Such is the broad outline.

Now, if we wish to prevent banditry from arising, nothing is better than putting its underlying foundations in order. The instruction practiced by the people of Zhou is admittedly difficult to approach, but can we allow the people to lack a place when assigning them to the nine occupations? If we wish to prevent banditry from spreading, nothing is better than cutting off its first shoots. The administrative practices of Zhou are also relevant to affairs today. Does it not depend on those responsible to make every provision without failure [?]? Thus, before banditry takes shape, if we investigate its roots and bring it under control, sound governance will be secured in advance, and none of the people will join in wrongdoing. When it first takes shape, extinguish its first shoots…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
焉善乎楊賜之言曰宜敕州縣簡別流民
以孤其黨然後誅其渠帥可不勞而定此
達權之通計其則於遏盜之機矣自宋以
來人異其議無非弭盜之遠猷也乃所以
當厥機宜可更僕而數焉富弼之言曰兇
險之徒自負圖大結煽民間亦能始禍要
在得而縻之使其謀不成則鼠輩爲羣不
足慮矣此唐人失之於黃巢者也蘇軾之
言曰德不足而才有餘者困於無門無所
===
不至願召豪猾而籠用之使歆利進身則
縱有嘯聚亦自無徒矣亦弭之慮於慶曆
者也至於歐陽修所謂四事則州郡置兵
爲備也選捕盜之官也明賞罰之法也用
良吏以撫疲民也而用良吏之一言尤爲
首務其諸龔遂之已事乎秦觀所謂二弊
則以惠莫大於招降禍莫深於窮治招降
則誘民爲盜窮治則驅民爲盜而傷惠損
威之論尤爲明備其諸殲渠之深意乎善
punctuated: 焉。善乎楊賜之言曰：「宜敕州縣簡別流民，以孤其黨，然後誅其渠帥，可不勞而定。」此達權之通計，其則於遏盜之機矣。自宋以來，人異其議，無非弭盜之遠猷也。乃所以當厥機宜，可更僕而數焉。富弼之言曰：「兇險之徒，自負圖大，結煽民間，亦能始禍。要在得而縻之，使其謀不成，則鼠輩爲羣，不足慮矣。」此唐人失之於黃巢者也。蘇軾之言曰：「德不足而才有餘者，困於無門，無所不至。願召豪猾而籠用之，使歆利進身，則縱有嘯聚，亦自無徒矣。」亦弭之慮於慶曆者也。至於歐陽修所謂四事，則州郡置兵爲備也，選捕盜之官也，明賞罰之法也，用良吏以撫疲民也。而用良吏之一言，尤爲首務，其諸龔遂之已事乎？秦觀所謂二弊，則以惠莫大於招降，禍莫深於窮治。招降則誘民爲盜，窮治則驅民爲盜。而傷惠損威之論，尤爲明備，其諸殲渠之深意乎？善
translation_en:
…How sound are Yang Ci’s words: “The prefectures and counties should be ordered to distinguish and separate out the displaced people, thereby isolating the rebels’ following. Then execute their leaders, and the disturbance can be settled without toil.” This is a comprehensive strategy grounded in an understanding of expedient action, a model for grasping the critical moment in suppressing banditry [?]. Since the Song dynasty, people have offered differing proposals, all of them far-reaching plans for ending banditry. As for the ways these suited the exigencies of their circumstances, one could go on enumerating them until the attendants needed replacing.

Fu Bi said: “Violent and treacherous men, conceited and harboring grand designs, form connections and stir up the populace; they too can initiate disorder. The essential thing is to secure them and keep them in check, preventing their schemes from succeeding. Then, even if these rat-like fellows gather in bands, they need cause no concern.” This is what the men of the Tang failed to do in the case of Huang Chao. Su Shi said: “Those whose virtue is insufficient but whose talents are abundant, when frustrated by the lack of an avenue for advancement, will stop at nothing. I ask that powerful and cunning men be summoned, brought under control, and employed, so that they are drawn by the prospect of gain and advancement. Then, even if someone calls for a band to assemble, he will find himself without followers.” This too was a consideration for quelling disorder in the Qingli era [?].

As for Ouyang Xiu’s four measures, they were to station troops in prefectures and commanderies for defense; select officials responsible for apprehending bandits; make the rules of reward and punishment clear; and employ good officials to comfort the exhausted people. Of these, employing good officials is especially the foremost task. Is this not exemplified by what Gong Sui accomplished? As for Qin Guan’s two abuses, his premise was that no act of clemency is greater than inviting surrender, and no calamity deeper than pursuing investigations to the utmost. Yet inviting surrender entices the people to become bandits, while exhaustive prosecution drives them to become bandits. His discussion of the impairment of clemency and the diminution of authority is particularly lucid and comprehensive. Does it not convey the deeper significance of eliminating the ringleaders? Excellent…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
由是而聯州縣之交也苟有事焉必同心
捕獲無論彼此盜固無所容也又由是而
嚴差捕之詐欺苟有犯焉必重罰以懲無
及平民盜固無由縱也若夫嚴保甲之什
伍謹覘諜之期會申告賞之明規舉連坐
之重罰皆踵行之故事惟良有司作之以
精明持之於悠久耳易曰神而明之存乎
其人君子可以觀矣
punctuated: 由是而聯州縣之交也。苟有事焉，必同心捕獲，無論彼此，盜固無所容也。又由是而嚴差捕之詐欺，苟有犯焉，必重罰以懲，無及平民，盜固無由縱也。若夫嚴保甲之什伍，謹覘諜之期會，申告賞之明規，舉連坐之重罰，皆踵行之故事，惟良有司作之以精明，持之於悠久耳。《易》曰：「神而明之，存乎其人。」君子可以觀矣。
translation_en: …thereby strengthening cooperation among the subprefectures and counties. Whenever an incident occurs, they must work together to capture the offenders, without distinguishing between their respective jurisdictions; bandits will then surely have nowhere to hide. This will also impose strict restraints on deceit by runners charged with making arrests. Any offender must be severely punished as a deterrent, without implicating innocent commoners; bandits will then surely have no means of escaping apprehension. As for tightening the organization of households into groups of ten and five under the baojia system, carefully observing the appointed times for reconnaissance and intelligence reports, reiterating clear rules for reporting crimes and granting rewards, and enforcing severe penalties for collective liability—all these are established practices handed down and followed. They require only capable local officials to implement them with discernment and maintain them over the long term. The Book of Changes says: “Making it wondrously effective and illuminating it rests with the person.” From this, the gentleman may perceive the lesson.

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
河南鄉試錄後序
嘉靖乙卯河南鄉試事竣〔直〕
以執事當告成於末簡乃作
而颺言曰人材之興裨乎治
道而其生也關乎氣運之盛
道化之隆蓋自昔然矣豫當
寰宇中央陰陽冲會固天地
===
之奧區也粵自洪濛始判天
乃出圖書於河洛肇洩靈祕
授之聖神性道之玄機經世
之鴻猷於此乎闢緘啓鑰邈
焉爲萬世宗仰玆非天所特
厚而眞元之氣所獨鍾者乎
故奕代發祥伊傅接軫周道
punctuated:
河南鄉試錄後序

嘉靖乙卯，河南鄉試事竣，〔直〕以執事，當告成於末簡，乃作而颺言曰：「人材之興，裨乎治道，而其生也，關乎氣運之盛、道化之隆，蓋自昔然矣。豫當寰宇中央，陰陽冲會，固天地之奧區也。粵自洪濛始判，天乃出圖書於河洛，肇洩靈祕，授之聖神。性道之玄機、經世之鴻猷，於此乎闢緘啓鑰，邈焉爲萬世宗仰。玆非天所特厚，而眞元之氣所獨鍾者乎？故奕代發祥，伊傅接軫，周道
translation_en:
Postscript to the Record of the Henan Provincial Examination

When the Henan Provincial Examination of the yimao year of Jiajing [1555] was completed, I, 〔Zhi〕, having served in its administration, was obliged to report its completion on the final pages. I therefore rose and proclaimed:

“The emergence of talented men contributes to the art of governance, while their birth depends upon the flourishing of cosmic forces and the fullness of moral transformation through the Way. This has been so since antiquity. Yu [Henan] occupies the center of the world, where yin and yang blend and converge; it is indeed a region harboring the deepest mysteries of Heaven and Earth. When primordial chaos first divided, Heaven brought forth the Chart and the Writing from the Yellow and Luo Rivers, first revealing its divine secrets and imparting them to the sages. The profound workings of human nature and the Way, and the grand designs for ordering the world, were here unsealed and unlocked, to become objects of reverence and emulation for countless generations. Is this not a place especially favored by Heaven, where the true primordial vital force is uniquely concentrated? Thus, through successive ages, auspicious manifestations appeared, and men such as Yi Yin and Fu Yue followed one another in succession. The Way of Zhou …”

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
中興申甫降嶽至宋伊洛眞
儒倡明道學斯文賴以不墜
往牒昭然休哉遐矣
國朝奄有四海
祖宗
列聖統一聖眞
湛恩汪濊
===
聲敎旁孚兹惟近藩漸被獨先
焉至我
皇上道契先天
德侔祇台
臨宇以來
建極錫福籲俊右文
皇極敷言之訓布列黌宮昭回雲
punctuated:
中興，申甫降嶽。至宋，伊洛眞儒倡明道學，斯文賴以不墜。往牒昭然，休哉，遐矣！
國朝奄有四海，祖宗列聖統一聖眞，湛恩汪濊，聲敎旁孚。兹惟近藩，漸被獨先焉。至我皇上，道契先天，德侔祇台，臨宇以來，建極錫福，籲俊右文。皇極敷言之訓，布列黌宮，昭回雲
translation_en:
…was restored to flourishing, and the sacred mountain brought forth Shen and Fu. By the Song dynasty, the true Confucian scholars of the Yi and Luo rivers proclaimed and elucidated the Learning of the Way; through them, this cultural tradition was preserved from decline. The records of the past make this plain. How glorious, and how far-reaching!
Our dynasty possesses all within the Four Seas. Its founding ancestors and successive sage sovereigns have united the authentic teachings of the sages. Their profound beneficence flows abundantly, and their civilizing influence extends in every direction. This province, close to the imperial center, has been foremost in receiving that influence. Now our emperor accords in his Way with primordial Heaven, and his virtue equals that of the earth [?; the transcription 祇台 is doubtful]. Since assuming rule over the realm, he has established the supreme standard and bestowed blessings, summoned men of outstanding talent, and honored literary cultivation. His instructions expounding the Sovereign's Supreme Standard have been displayed throughout the schools, their radiance illuminating the clouds …

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
之中果無伊傅申甫諸賢其
人焉豈理也哉爾多士進矣
不可必者遇也不可負者時
也士生斯時孰無
帝臣之願而皓首窮經不沾一命
者何限也多士拔茅彙征登
名兹選旣遇而獲時矣盍思
===
所以報稱者哉以用世則思
爲四輔以明道則思爲二賢
功業未必同而同其志道德
未必同而同其學則本諸身
而達諸政矢其心以圖報於
國者當無愧於爾鄉之先�People
雖山川且藉以增重賓興大
punctuated: 之中，果無伊傅申甫諸賢其人焉，豈理也哉？爾多士進矣！不可必者，遇也；不可負者，時也。士生斯時，孰無帝臣之願？而皓首窮經，不沾一命者，何限也！多士拔茅彙征，登名兹選，旣遇而獲時矣，盍思所以報稱者哉？以用世，則思爲四輔；以明道，則思爲二賢。功業未必同，而同其志；道德未必同，而同其學。則本諸身而達諸政，矢其心以圖報於國者，當無愧於爾鄉之先�People。雖山川，且藉以增重，賓興大
translation_en:
…among them, could there truly be no worthy men like Yi Yin, Fu Yue, Shen Bo, and Zhongshan Fu? How could that be reasonable? You assembled scholars have now advanced! What cannot be assured is an opportunity; what must not be failed is the time in which one lives. What scholar born in this age does not aspire to serve the Emperor? Yet how many study the Classics until their hair turns white without receiving even a single appointment! You scholars, like clumps of thatch pulled up together, have advanced in company and had your names entered among those selected here. Having encountered opportunity and found your moment, should you not consider how to repay this favor fittingly?
In serving the world, aspire to emulate the Four Aides; in illuminating the Way, aspire to emulate the Two Worthies. Your achievements may not equal theirs, but let your aspirations be the same; your moral attainment may not equal theirs, but let your learning be the same. Then, grounding yourselves in personal cultivation and extending it to government, pledging your hearts to repay the state, you should stand without shame before the earlier worthies of your native region [?]. Even its mountains and rivers will thereby gain in stature. The ceremonial honoring and selection of worthies is great…

title: 嘉靖三十四年河南鄉試錄
text:
與不亦休有烈光耶是舉也
巡按御史李〔初元〕殫精瘁力
務獲眞材以對揚
明命而〔直〕謬叨斯役敢攄御史之
意用申玆告多士其懋敬之
哉
應天府句容縣儒學教諭胡
〔直〕謹序
punctuated:
與，不亦休有烈光耶？是舉也，巡按御史李〔初元〕殫精瘁力，務獲眞材，以對揚明命。而〔直〕謬叨斯役，敢攄御史之意，用申玆告，多士其懋敬之哉！
應天府句容縣儒學教諭胡〔直〕謹序。
translation_en:
…would it not be splendid and shine with brilliant glory? [?] For this examination, Regional Inspector Li Chuyuan 李初元 exhausted his energies and strength, striving to obtain men of genuine talent and thereby honor and carry out the imperial command. I, Zhi, have undeservedly been entrusted with this duty and venture to express the Regional Inspector’s intentions, setting forth this admonition. May you, assembled scholars, earnestly heed it!
Respectfully prefaced by Hu Zhi 胡直, Instructor in the Confucian School of Jurong County, Yingtian Prefecture.
